Basilithe raises the Crystal's stiffness until its resonance simply will not be driven off, which is a defence against every technique that works by imposing an external rhythm.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md
why: The register's Basilithe is a resonance-stability current: natural frequency, stiffness-to-mass ratio, quartz oscillator stability. It contains no growth law. The page attributes a crystal-growth law to it and builds the Obelisk's lattice on that attribution. The register's actual law would serve the working better, since holding a configuration against forcing is what the Obelisk does for its whole duration and a quartz habit is a prism, but it also imports a failure the page does not carry: 'Resonant catastrophe. A frequency that cannot be shifted also cannot be detuned away from a forcing that happens to match it.'

options.option: Rewrite the Mechanism to use Basilithe's stated resonance-stability law, with resonant catastrophe as the named failure.
options.changes: One paragraph; gives the Obelisk a precise, findable counter (match its locked frequency) and explains the prism habit; makes the Weakness line about radiance secondary.

options.option: Add a growth current to the Codex line and keep Basilithe for the holding, e.g. a Materia crystallisation Wellspring from the register.
options.changes: Adds a sixth or seventh Wellspring to a working that already runs six; raises the Tempering Capacity problem (SA-GAP-OPALIS-TEMPERING-CAPACITY) further.

options.option: Amend the Basilithe register entry to include a growth law.
options.changes: Changes a Core Law, which affects every Basilithe page including Harmonic Null-Ascension; the Families page's physical readings are built to be one law each.

options.option: Record the attribution as loose language and rule that 'crystal-growth' is shorthand for the metastable lattice the resonance law holds.
options.changes: No content change; leaves the resonant-catastrophe counter unwritten.

quote_a: Tarturon's entropy law is throttled to run backward across the Obelisk's own surface, a local, temporary entropy inversion
quote_b: Below yield a material returns to shape and the load leaves no record. Above it, behaviour changes kind, and the response scales with the load applied rather than with anything the material chose. Tarturon couples output to moral weight through exactly that curve, and like thermite it supplies its own oxidiser, which is the mechanical reason the reaction cannot be smothered once initiated.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md
why: The register's Tarturon is a yield-criterion and self-oxidising-reaction current coupled to moral weight. It is not an entropy current. Entropy of mixing belongs to Dissolution, The Unbinding Stream, in Limina: 'a solid dissolves not because the solvent attacks it but because the mixed state has higher entropy than the separated one'. The page uses Tarturon for the entropy inversion and then names 'raw Tarturon or a comparable Dissolution-aligned field' as the counter, treating the two as interchangeable. Tarturon's actual failure line is meanwhile the best available explanation of the page's own four-instance cap and goes unused: 'Runaway. The load that drives the reaction is generated by the reaction, and nothing in the mechanism provides a stopping condition.'

options.option: Swap Dissolution in for the entropy inversion and keep Tarturon for the load-driven escalation and the fifth-instance runaway.
options.changes: Changes the Codex line's secondary list; adds a Limina current to a Materia working, which is the canonical hard cross-Family case and would raise the Stage's justification rather than lower it.

options.option: Keep Tarturon and rewrite the Mechanism to use its yield curve rather than an entropy law.
options.changes: Re-reads the Obelisk as a post-yield structure rather than an entropy inverter; loses the reversal modes' current justification and needs a new one for Oneiric Reversal.

options.option: Amend the Tarturon register entry to include an entropy law.
options.changes: Changes a Core Law; affects every Tarturon page and blurs the line with Dissolution, which the Families page's Discrepancies section is at pains to keep sharp.

options.option: Record the attribution as loose and rule that 'entropy' here means the post-yield irreversibility of Tarturon's curve.
options.changes: No content change; the counter line's conflation of Tarturon with Dissolution stays on the page.

quote_a: dissolving what she marks as an ending and rebuilding what she marks as a beginning, over an area up to 800 m across
quote_b: Basilithe's crystal-growth law is pushed into a metastable high-order lattice while Tarturon's entropy law is throttled to run backward across the Obelisk's own surface, a local, temporary entropy inversion held open by the other four Wellsprings acting as boundary conditions (Petralon's mass anchor, Oneirion's conceptual template, Tenebra's radiance suppression, Fractura's mirrored load-sharing across up to four instances).
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Obelisk of the Eclipsed Dawn.md
why: The Effect turns on Opalis marking a thing as an ending or a beginning, and the Target Response distinguishes hostile constructs, allies and damaged Essence by category. The Mechanism lists six currents and not one of them performs a recognition: Basilithe is stiffness, Tarturon is yield, Petralon is compressive load path, Oneirion is configuration space, Tenebra is absorption, Fractura is fracture mechanics. None can tell an ending from a beginning or a friend from an enemy. Judicium is the system's recognition current and is not on the Codex line; the Bastion Imperium precedent for adding one is already in this set.

options.option: Add a recognition current to the Codex line and name which Sub-Stat performs the marking.
options.changes: Adds a seventh Wellspring and a Fulguria current to a Materia working; raises the Tempering Capacity question further; gives a counter a target.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: the Obelisk runs one mode over its whole area indiscriminately, and Opalis chooses the mode, not the objects.
options.changes: Makes the working a field rather than a discriminator; allies inside a Fracture Cascade unwind too, which gives the 800 m radius a real tactical cost.

options.option: Rule that Oneirion's 'conceptual template' is the marking, and state how a coordinate in configuration space encodes 'ending' or 'beginning'.
options.changes: Keeps the current list; needs a sentence that makes an abstract state coordinate carry a categorical judgement, which is a claim with consequences on every Oneirion page.

options.option: Rule that the marking is a pre-cast declaration and the field then applies it by pre-authorised list, as on Archivium Locus.
options.changes: No new law; turns the marking into pre-battle planning a player can attack, and makes the locked mode's consequence heavier.

quote_a: Opalis collapses six orbiting Wellspring sigils into a point of infinite density and a colossal prism rises from it
quote_b: Aetheric Density · The concentration of Aether present in a given volume. Sets the ceiling on the AU/s output a practitioner can achieve in that location
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: Infinite density is not a quantity and is not a system term. The system's density vocabulary is Aetheric Density (a concentration with a named, if unnumbered, scale) and Flux Density (EU per gram of Crystal mass). A point of infinite density is either gravitational-singularity language imported from outside the system or a figure of speech; as written it is the only place in this batch where a mechanic is stated in a unit the system does not carry.

options.option: Replace with a stated Aetheric Density condition, e.g. the six sigils are brought to Wellspring Core density at a point.
options.changes: Uses the system's own four-step density scale; needs SA-GAP-AETHERIC-DENSITY settled before it can be checked numerically.

options.option: State it as a Flux Density figure in EU/g at the convergence point.
options.changes: Gives the working its first hard number; requires an EU/g figure for Opalis, who has no card.

options.option: Keep 'infinite density' as in-world rhetoric and mark it as such on the page.
options.changes: No mechanical change; the phrase stops reading as a measurement.

options.option: Delete the clause; the six sigils converge and the prism rises, with no density claim.
options.changes: Smallest change; loses nothing mechanical, since no later line depends on the density.

quote_a: Governing Sub-Stats: Density (whether the Obelisk is a participant or a suggestion), Compression (how cleanly six Wellspring signatures refine into one stable lattice), Depth (how many Wellspring qualities the working holds without resonance conflict)
quote_b: Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B, with inscription and glyph-chain durability requiring Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Ardency Density above B-Grade requires Body Path at Stage IV, and the page's declared Path gate is Attraction Path only. The working requires SSS-Grade, far above B. The other two named Sub-Stats close cleanly: Compression is open to any Path, and Depth's multi-Wellspring clause ('Stage VI to exceed A where two Wellspring qualities are held in one working') is met by Attraction Path at Stage XII and is in fact the clause the page's own gloss restates. Separately, the working layers six Wellsprings and does not name Harmonics Breadth, which is the Sub-Stat Part Seven writes for that case.

options.option: Add Body as a secondary Path gate.
options.changes: One line; implies a physical practice for a practitioner otherwise described entirely through Attraction and standing.

options.option: Replace Density with Harmonics Breadth, whose multi-Wellspring gate the declared Attraction Path carries.
options.changes: Re-reads the Obelisk's solidity as layered-harmonisation breadth rather than raw density; closes the gate and names the Sub-Stat the working actually needs.

options.option: Rule that only the first-named governing Sub-Stat binds.
options.changes: Settles many pathgate rows at once; weakens Part Seven's stated strict reading.

options.option: Rule that Opalis has recognised Body Path commitment and record it on a card.
options.changes: Requires a card for her (SA-GAP-OPALIS-NO-CARD) and fixes three other Opalis pages at the same time.

quote_a: The Obelisk records what she was feeling when she raised it and plays it back to her; sustaining it long enough leaves hairline stress in her own Temperance layers that only stillness closes.
quote_b: No more than four Obelisks stand at once; a fifth does not fail to appear, it brings the others down with it.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Obelisk of the Eclipsed Dawn.md
why: A working that lowers entropy inside a boundary must hold a record of what it sorted, and Landauer's principle prices clearing that record at k_B T ln2 per bit, 2.87x10^-21 J at 300 K. Reversing even 1 J/(kg K) across the 1.34x10^8 m^3 hemisphere the page claims needs about 1.7x10^31 bits of record and dissipates about 49 GJ when cleared, which is four orders of magnitude below the SSS floor of 418 TJ the page assigns the modes. So the binding constraint on the reversal modes is storage rather than power, and the four-instance cap is most naturally a capacity limit. The system has no quantity anywhere for how much record a Soul Crystal can hold: Continuum Retention is a duration, Tempering Capacity is a harmonisation ceiling, and neither is a store of bits.

options.option: Rule that the four-instance cap is a record-capacity limit and give the capacity a system quantity.
options.changes: Adds a new resource to the system; makes every recording or reversing working checkable against it; gives the fifth-instance punishment a derivation.

options.option: Rule the cap is Fractura's load-sharing avalanche and leave record capacity unquantified.
options.changes: No new resource; uses the current the page already names for the cap; the reversal modes stay unpriced.

options.option: Price the reversal modes at the Landauer figure rather than at the SSS ceiling.
options.changes: Makes Ecliptic Aegis and Oneiric Reversal cheap and Fracture Cascade expensive, which is a large tactical change and a defensible one.

options.option: Record the gap and leave the cap as stated.
options.changes: No change; the working's most interesting limit stays an assertion.

quote_a: It does not move her through the room; it moves her through configuration space, the coordinate space in which every arrangement a system could take is a point with no physical location of its own.
quote_b: A mechanical system's every possible arrangement is a coordinate in a space that has no physical location, and the system's evolution is a trajectory through it. Oneirion lets a working act on that manifold rather than on the room.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: The coordinates of a mechanical configuration space are the generalised positions, so a continuous curve in that space is by construction a continuous motion in the room; that is what makes it a configuration space rather than an abstract label set. Liouville's theorem adds that trajectories under Hamiltonian flow do not jump and phase-space volume is conserved. Read strictly against its own stated analogue, Oneirion's manifold therefore cannot deliver the page's central claim of 'no line of travel between the two points'. Either the manifold is not the mechanical configuration space, in which case the register's analogue is being stretched past the law it names, or the crossing is continuous in the room.

options.option: Rule that Oneirion's manifold is an abstract state space not coordinatised by positions, and say so in the register.
options.changes: Keeps every Oneirion teleport and reach effect; costs the register its clean physical analogue, which is the Families page's whole method.

options.option: Rule the crossing continuous in the room and very fast, and make 'no line of travel' an observational claim rather than a physical one.
options.changes: Preserves the analogue; requires a speed, which at 50 m in 0.25 s is trivial and audible, and the acoustic arithmetic on this page already supports a quarter-second crossing.

options.option: Restrict Oneirion to addressing and reach, and source displacement from a Spatium current instead.
options.changes: Splits the working across two Families, which the Families page says is the harder architecture; changes the Codex line and adds a gate.

options.option: Record the tension and keep both sentences as written.
options.changes: No change; the strongest physical objection in the batch stays unanswered.

quote_a: Aeldoris forces that reorganisation open for a half-second rather than a night.
quote_b: The reorganisation happens during genuine rest and cannot be forced, which is why Hypnather practitioners sleep like the dead and wake structurally different.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: The register states flatly that Hypnather's reorganisation cannot be forced. This page forces it twice: the Trigger has Aeldoris 'let her own Crystal drop toward sleep on command rather than waiting on fatigue', and the Mechanism has him force the reorganisation open for half a second. This is the register-side sibling of SA-GAP-DESCENT-FORCED-FAILURE, which records the same problem page-against-itself on Hypnather Descent Rite; here it is page-against-register, and on his own Crystal rather than a target's. Note that Oneiron Parasite and Oneiron Phantasm Court both use Hypnather without forcing it, so the contradiction is not uniform across the Aeldoris pages.

options.option: Amend the register: the reorganisation cannot be forced in a target, but a practitioner harmonised with Hypnather can open it in themselves at a cost.
options.changes: Distinguishes self from target across every Hypnather page; makes the Descent Rite the real problem and this page legal; needs the cost named.

options.option: Rewrite the page so he waits for a natural drop rather than commanding one, e.g. the step is only available in the moments after genuine fatigue.
options.changes: Makes the step situational and much more interesting tactically; removes it as an at-will mobility option.

options.option: Rule that a stretched-exponential relaxation makes a fraction of the ordering available immediately without force, and rewrite 'forces' accordingly.
options.changes: Keeps the register intact and the working intact; uses the real physics (a KWW relaxation with low beta has a fast early portion) and only changes a verb.

options.option: Record both and leave the register and the page as written.
options.changes: No change; two of the four Aeldoris pages contradict a Core Law they cite.

quote_a: Aeldoris drops into half-sleep for an instant and steps out again from the dream-shadow of another mind nearby, arriving up to fifty metres away
quote_b: He was a boy when a sleep took him that nobody in the house could break.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Aeldoris Vanthryx · The Ruthless.md
why: Oblivion-Step uses she/her for Aeldoris throughout ('she is removed from where she stood', 'her own Crystal', 'she cannot step to a point that is merely empty'). The character card uses he/him throughout, as do Oneiron Parasite ('a fragment of him') and Oneiron Phantasm Court ('mirrored back at Aeldoris himself'). One page against a card and two sibling pages. Recorded rather than resolved; this account quotes the page as written and follows the card in its own sentences.

options.option: Correct Oblivion-Step to he/him to match the card and the two sibling pages.
options.changes: Editorial only; one page changed, nothing mechanical.

options.option: Correct the card and the other pages to she/her.
options.changes: Larger editorial pass; the card's Lore section and four pages change.

options.option: Rule the pronouns deliberately mixed and state why in canon.
options.changes: Becomes a characterisation fact requiring support elsewhere; no mechanical effect.

options.option: Record the discrepancy and leave both as written pending Isaac's word on the character.
options.changes: No change; the volume reads inconsistently.

page: (4 Aeldoris pages, and the Francis card)
quote_a: Gnosis Dual Sight 475 (at ceiling) · Gnosis Fracture Reading 445 · Harmonics Fear-Reading 440 · Dexterity Dream-Blink 420 · Harmonics Empathic Bleed 400 · Tempering Descent Control 385 · Ardency Falseface Mass 355 · Dominion Court Authority 315 · Resilience Identity Anchor 270 · Vitality Waking Stability 245.
path_a: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Aeldoris Vanthryx · The Ruthless.md
quote_b: Every Sub-Stat name in the system is now unique, which means a Sub-Stat can be cited in a diagnostic reading without naming its Primary.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md
why: None of the ten Sub-Stat peak names on the Aeldoris card appears among the sixty-four, and none is a retired name on the Merge Ledger either, so they cannot be read through it. Part Twelve's closing note assumes every Sub-Stat name in play is one of the sixty-four. The Francis card is mostly canonical by contrast (Dominion Sovereignty, Ardency Cascade, Gnosis Cognition, Harmonics Attunement) but carries two that are not: 'Dominion Authority' and 'Ardency Inscription', the second of which is a retired name that reads as Density. Four technique pages in this batch take their Sub-Stat readings from the Aeldoris card.

options.option: Map each card name onto one of the sixty-four and restate the card's section V.
options.changes: One card edited; the four technique pages become checkable against Part Seven's gates; loses the flavour names.

options.option: Keep the flavour names and add the canonical Sub-Stat in brackets after each.
options.changes: Keeps the card's voice and makes it auditable; sets a pattern for every other card.

options.option: Rule that card Sub-Stat peaks are descriptive labels for specialised expressions of a canonical Sub-Stat, and state the convention.
options.changes: No card edits needed now; requires the convention to be written somewhere a drafter will find it.

options.option: Record the discrepancy and leave the cards as written.
options.changes: No change; no Path gate can be checked against any Aeldoris Sub-Stat figure.

quote_a: A fragment of him takes root behind a target's ribs, watches what they feel, and can be made to unmake their composure from inside.
quote_b: Eidolyn gives the planted fragment enough Ardency Density to hold a shape and survive inside another Crystal's territory rather than dissolving on arrival. Oneirion routes it through the target's own configuration space so it can move and act there instead of sitting inert. Hypnather anchors it to the target's own rest cycles
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Oneiron Parasite · Nightmare Warden.md
why: Detonation appears in the Effect, the Function ('watches, distorts and can be made to detonate'), the Numerical Effect ('Grade A, on detonation') and the Target Response ('a psychic stagger on detonation'). The Mechanism names three laws and none of them releases anything: templated nucleation gives shape, configuration-space routing gives mobility, structural relaxation gives a growth schedule. There is no combustion, no stored elastic energy, no phase transition, no oxidiser and no discharge in the working anywhere. Under the ruling that the mechanism is the effect, the detonation has no law behind it.

options.option: Name the law that detonates, e.g. add a Caloria or Vectoria current, or state that the release is the graft's stored surface energy returning.
options.changes: Adds a current or a clause to the Codex line and a gate to check; gives the detonation a derivable yield instead of a Grade band.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: the Warden watches and distorts and cannot be detonated; its removal is what staggers the host.
options.changes: Removes the burst entirely; makes the working pure surveillance and sabotage, which its Sub-Stats (Gnosis Cognition, Gnosis Retention) already fit; strengthens the purge counter.

options.option: Rule the detonation is the graft crossing back below its critical radius and dissolving, so the stagger is the host's own structure losing a load-bearing member.
options.changes: No new current; uses the nucleation physics already in play; the yield becomes small and the effect stays psychic, which matches 'a psychic stagger'.

options.option: Rule that Ostwald coarsening reversed is the release: the Warden gives its accumulated order back to the host all at once.
options.changes: Elegant and cheap; makes the burst scale with how long it was implanted, which gives the page's 'left too long' cost a second edge.

quote_a: Bounded by Stage VII's 475 ceiling, Grade A, on detonation.
quote_b: A | 276–400 | 20–100 GN | 46 GJ – 4.184 TJ | 11–1,000 t | City Block to Multi-City Block
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md
why: Two numeric faults in one clause. First, 475 is not A-Grade: Part Four puts A at 276-400 and S at 401-550, and Part Five calls 401-475 Stage VII's instability band, reachable under strain only. So the sentence names two different Grades. Second, if the detonation is bounded at A-Grade then Part Eleven's A row makes it 46 GJ to 4.184 TJ, 20-100 GN, eleven to a thousand tonnes of TNT, released inside a thorax at an implantation range of thirty metres. The page's stated effect is 'a psychic stagger' and the host 'loses composure at the worst possible moment'. Eleven tonnes of TNT would kill the host, the surrounding street and Aeldoris.

options.option: State the detonation's yield directly in joules at a scale consistent with 'a psychic stagger', and detach it from the Strike Force table.
options.changes: The Grade requirement becomes a gate on implantation and control rather than on output; the working stops reading as a suicide device.

options.option: Rule that the detonation is not a Strike Force event at all, because nothing mechanical is delivered.
options.changes: Cleanest reading of 'psychic stagger'; needs a statement about how non-kinetic workings are measured, which the system currently lacks.

options.option: Correct '475, Grade A' to 'Grade A, ceiling 400' or to 'Grade S under strain', and pick one.
options.changes: Editorial; fixes the internal contradiction without settling the yield question.

options.option: Keep the A-Grade bound and rewrite the Target Response to match it, making the Warden a lethal implanted charge.
options.changes: Changes the working's character completely and makes the thirty-metre range a hazard to the caster; would need a new cost and a new counter.

quote_a: Sub-Stats · Gnosis Cognition, Gnosis Retention, Dominion Sovereignty, Ardency Density
quote_b: Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B ... Sovereignty requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Two of the four named Sub-Stats fail their Part Seven gates against the card. Ardency Density above B-Grade requires Body Path at Stage IV; the working requires A-Grade and the card reads 'Spirit dominant, Attraction secondary, Body tertiary, Fate untouched', and Part Seven is explicit that commitment is recognised from behavioural pattern rather than declared. Dominion Sovereignty closes at exactly A but the page's stated late push toward S-Grade crosses its Fate gate, and the card's Fate Path is untouched. Gnosis Cognition and Gnosis Retention both close cleanly.

options.option: Drop the late push toward S-Grade from the page and keep the working at A.
options.changes: One clause; Sovereignty closes; the Warden becomes a Stage VII working with no upward option, which suits a technique whose limit is the host rather than the caster.

options.option: Replace Ardency Density with Harmonics Breadth or Ardency Depth, whose gates the card's Attraction Path carries.
options.changes: Re-reads the graft's solidity as layered harmonisation rather than raw density; closes the gate; changes what a counter targets.

options.option: Record Body Path commitment for Aeldoris on the card.
options.changes: Fixes this and the Falseface Lattice's identical gate at once; contradicts the card's own reading of him as a man whose body was never the instrument.

options.option: Rule that a secondary Sub-Stat's gates do not bind a technique page.
options.changes: Settles many pathgate rows across the volume; weakens Part Seven's stated strict reading.

quote_a: Hypnather anchors it to the target's own rest cycles, drawing on the same recovery window the Sleep Crown strengthens, which is why it grows stronger the longer the host sleeps near it undisturbed.
quote_b: Efficiency · Eta · η · The ratio of Essence spent to Essence that arrives as intended effect.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: After implantation the Warden is sustained out of the host's recovery rather than the caster's reserve. The system has no rule for a working fed by a third party's Essence: it does not say whose efficiency applies, whose EU is drawn down, whether the host's Starvation line can be reached by carrying one, or whether the host's own recovery figures should be reduced. Every other cost in the system is charged to the practitioner. This is the only working in the batch whose running cost is charged to the target, and the ledger cannot record it.

options.option: Rule that a host-fed working runs on the host's eta and draws the host's EU, and state the Starvation consequence.
options.changes: Gives the Warden a second, quantifiable cost borne by the victim; makes prolonged implantation a medical emergency a physician could detect; needs an EU figure to be checkable at all.

options.option: Rule that the caster's eta always applies and the host supplies only the recovery window, not Essence.
options.changes: Keeps the accounting with the practitioner; makes 'grows stronger while the host sleeps' a schedule rather than a transfer.

options.option: Rule host-fed sustain impossible and have the Warden draw on Aeldoris continuously.
options.changes: Caps how many he can hold and for how long; makes the working far more expensive and the 'left too long' cost his rather than the host's.

options.option: Record the gap and leave the sustain unaccounted.
options.changes: No change; the working's running cost sits outside the ledger entirely.

quote_a: Trigger · Declared, by gaze or touch, against a target with a subconscious to implant into, at up to 30 meters.
quote_b: A strong mental shield refuses the implantation outright.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Oneiron Parasite · Nightmare Warden.md
why: The working has five good counters and no tell. Implantation is by gaze at up to thirty metres and the host's first indication is disturbed sleep, which is a symptom arriving after the working has taken. Every counter listed requires already knowing: a shield must be up in advance, a purging rite must be sought, a shared-dream ritual must be convened, the line must be found and cut. The only real tell in the record is on the character card rather than this page, and it announces the practitioner and not the act: Sleepfall Presence, a passive wave causing micro-sleeps in everyone nearby.

options.option: Give the implantation a tell at the moment it lands, e.g. a cold point behind the sternum or a single missed heartbeat.
options.changes: Cheapest fix; makes every existing counter reachable without changing any number; costs the working its ambush value, which may be the point of it.

options.option: Make the tell diagnostic rather than perceptual and state it: a Judicium or Gnosis Analysis read finds it, and say at what Grade.
options.changes: Keeps the ambush; makes screening a real institutional practice and a scene a player can play; ties the counter to an existing current.

options.option: Require touch rather than gaze, so the host knows they were touched.
options.changes: Removes the thirty-metre standoff and makes the working far riskier to use; changes its tactical role completely.

options.option: Import Sleepfall Presence onto the page as the working's stated tell.
options.changes: No new mechanic; makes the counter findable by anyone who reads the card, which is the fair-play standard, and ties the technique to the man.

quote_a: Only takes hold on a mind with an active subconscious and an actual unresolved contradiction in it. A mind at peace with itself, or with nothing behind the waking self, gives the working nothing to find.
quote_b: The target must be guilty of something they know and have not admitted. A target without guilt or deception gives the Phantasm Court nothing to convene about.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Aeldoris Vanthryx · The Ruthless.md
why: The technique page's precondition is an unresolved contradiction between the waking and equilibrium selves. The character card's precondition is guilt the target knows and has not admitted, and the card's Relationships section makes it load-bearing: 'Anyone without guilt · The one target he has no working against.' Those are different target sets. A person can hold an unresolved contradiction without any guilt attached to it, and a guilty person can be entirely consistent about it. The distinction decides who he can and cannot work on, which is the character's whole premise.

options.option: Rule guilt the condition and rewrite the page's Limitation to match the card.
options.changes: Narrows the working sharply and sharpens the character; makes 'a man with nothing hidden' a complete defence, which is the fairest counter in the batch.

options.option: Rule unresolved contradiction the condition and rewrite the card.
options.changes: Widens the working to anyone self-divided, guilty or not; weakens the card's 'anyone without guilt' line and the Broken Tribunal's moral shape.

options.option: Rule them two requirements that must both hold.
options.changes: Narrowest reading; the target must be both self-divided and guilty, which makes the reconnaissance prerequisite heavier and the technique rarer.

options.option: Rule that guilt is the common case of an unresolved contradiction and say so on both.
options.changes: No mechanical change; keeps both texts and makes the relationship explicit.

quote_a: Sub-Stats · Gnosis Cognition and Dominion Reach (Oneirion's documented Stat Effect), Ardency Density and Gnosis Memorium (Eidolyn's), Gnosis Retention (Hypnather's); all estimates, no sheet exists to confirm exact figures
quote_b: Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B ... Sovereignty requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Ardency Density above B-Grade requires Body Path at Stage IV; the working requires A-Grade and the card's Path line reads 'Body tertiary'. Dominion Reach reads as Sovereignty under the Merge Ledger and closes at exactly A, but the page's stated late push toward S-Grade crosses its Fate gate, and the card reads 'Fate untouched'. Gnosis Cognition and Gnosis Retention close cleanly. The page also lists Retention and Memorium as two Sub-Stats where the Merge Ledger makes them one, so the FOW line carries the same stat twice, and the page reads its ceiling off 'Band C', a retired lettered Coherence Band.

options.option: Drop the late push toward S-Grade and replace Ardency Density with Ardency Depth or Harmonics Breadth.
options.changes: Closes both failing gates; Depth's multi-Wellspring clause is the one this three-current working actually needs and the card's Attraction Path carries it.

options.option: Record Body Path commitment for Aeldoris on the card.
options.changes: Fixes this, the Warden and the Falseface Lattice together; contradicts the card's reading of him.

options.option: Collapse Retention and Memorium into one entry and restate the FOW line against the sixty-four.
options.changes: Editorial; removes the duplication and makes the gates checkable.

options.option: Rule that estimated FOW lines are not bound by Part Seven until a sheet exists.
options.changes: Settles every 'all estimates' page at once; leaves the gates unchecked wherever a page says it is estimating.

quote_a: A resisted edit's paradox shockwave falls in the EX-Grade Strike Force band: 5 to 50 exanewtons peak force, Moon to Large Planet scale energy release, the ceiling set by Francis's own Stage XIV Grade rather than by the Principle itself.
quote_b: EX | 1,201–1,500 | 5–50 EN | 1.24×10²⁹ J – 6.9×10³⁷ J | 29.6 Et – 16.5 Rt | Moon to Large Planet
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md
why: The working's radius is five kilometres, so the bubble volume is 5.24x10^11 m^3 and the air inside it masses 6.41x10^11 kg, whose complete mass-energy is 5.76x10^28 J. The EX band's floor is 1.24x10^29 J, which is 2.15 times that figure, and reaching it would require converting about 1.38x10^12 kg of mass. Two Sets of Books III says the energy was in the room; here it cannot have been, even counting every atom of the atmosphere. The physics the page's own Mechanism invokes would supply a derivable number instead: a held false-vacuum bubble releases its wall energy 4 pi R^2 sigma plus its interior pressure work (4/3) pi R^3 epsilon, and at R_c = 5 km the relation sigma/epsilon = 1,667 m fixes the ratio.

options.option: Derive the discharge from the wall tension and the energy-density difference and state it in joules.
options.changes: Gives the working its first physically closed number; the yield scales with radius squared rather than with the caster's Grade, which changes how the technique is used.

options.option: Reduce the stated band to one whose floor fits inside the field's mass-energy, e.g. SS or S.
options.changes: One line; the discharge becomes a survivable local event and the five-kilometre radius stops implying a planetary figure.

options.option: Rule the discharge non-kinetic, a law-shock rather than a Strike Force event, and say how such things are measured.
options.changes: Removes the arithmetic problem and creates a new measurement category the system currently lacks; would apply to several Francis pages.

options.option: Keep the band and rule that a paradox discharge draws on the Aether stratum without limit, suspending the in-the-room constraint.
options.changes: Settles it by ruling; sets a precedent that would let any sufficiently graded working exceed its field's mass-energy.

quote_a: Resistance from a comparably graded source is what converts the edit into a shockwave instead of a quiet change.
quote_b: Catharsis forces the release, the old state discharging the way a collapsing bubble wall dumps its surface tension outward.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Principle Overwrite.md
why: The Mechanism's own analogue makes the discharge unconditional. A false vacuum nucleated inside a true one is held against an inward pressure difference and a wall tension; releasing the boundary releases both, whether or not anyone resisted. The page's Mechanism describes exactly that collapse and its Target Response then makes the collapse contingent on opposition, leaving a 'quiet change' option the physics does not offer. Catharsis's register failure points the same way and is unused: 'Supercooling. The transition fails to nucleate, the load accumulates past the point where it should have released, and when it finally goes it goes all at once.'

options.option: Rule the discharge unconditional and state its magnitude once, with resistance changing only how early it arrives.
options.changes: Makes every use of the working a district-scale event, which is a very large change to how it can be deployed and a much more frightening technique.

options.option: Rewrite the Mechanism so an unresisted edit is released rather than collapsed, and name the law that lets the boundary be let down gently.
options.changes: Preserves the quiet option; needs a mechanism for a controlled release, which Catharsis's constant-temperature phase change could supply.

options.option: Rule that resistance raises epsilon, so the discharge scales with opposition rather than switching on with it.
options.changes: Keeps both sentences roughly intact and makes the shockwave a magnitude rather than a mode; gives an opponent a reason not to push.

options.option: Rule that a failed Seal is the shockwave and a clean Seal is the quiet change, and price the Seal.
options.changes: Ties the outcome to the Four Glyph Roles the Craft page already defines, and makes 'Force the Seal early' a live counter with a stated consequence.

quote_a: Francis runs pure Spirit Path here, so every Principle Overwrite fights his own Crystal's gate as much as any external counter, which is a plausible source of the memory cost.
quote_b: Path · Spirit dominant, Fate secondary, Body tertiary. No Choir carries Fate Path at any weight, because a Celestial's Crystal is anchored to somebody else's Throne. His opened when the anchor was cut. It is the one thing about him the Host's registers cannot explain.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Francis Alexander · The Crimson Dirge of Atonement.md
why: The page's Weakness is built on Francis having no Fate Path, and offers that as the source of the memory cost. The card gives him Fate Path as his secondary and makes it a central fact about the character. Dominion Sovereignty's gate is 'Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A, and Stage IX to exceed SSS where the imposed law encodes abstract conceptual truths'; rewriting a Principle is that case, EX exceeds SSS, and at Stage XIV with Fate secondary the gate closes. So the page's stated weakness dissolves, and the memory cost loses the explanation the page offers for it. Meanwhile the gate that does fail on this working, Dominion Radius's Attraction requirement, is not mentioned.

options.option: Correct the page's Weakness to match the card and find the memory cost's source elsewhere, e.g. in the record a boundary-holding working must keep.
options.changes: One paragraph; the working stops fighting an imaginary gate; the cost needs a new derivation, and the false-vacuum record is available.

options.option: Correct the card to remove Fate Path.
options.changes: Removes the card's most distinctive claim about him and the Severance's one unexplained consequence; several Francis pages would need checking.

options.option: Keep both and rule that Fate Path opened after the events this technique page describes.
options.changes: Makes the page a historical record rather than a current one; needs a date on both and affects the other Francis pages' timelines.

options.option: Rewrite the Weakness around Dominion Radius's Attraction gate, which does fail.
options.changes: Keeps a real structural weakness on the page and makes it checkable; implies the five-kilometre projection is the strained part, not the law-claim.

quote_a: Governing Primary: Dominion (Sovereignty, Radius), primary, gated as above
quote_b: Radius requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed A, Stage VI to exceed A for partial projection outward, and Stage VII to exceed S for boundary expansion speed.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The working projects a five-kilometre field at EX-Grade, which crosses all three of Dominion Radius's Attraction Path thresholds. The card's Path line is 'Spirit dominant, Fate secondary, Body tertiary' with no Attraction Path at any weight, and Part Seven is explicit that commitment is recognised from behavioural pattern rather than declared. The page's own FOW line names Dominion Radius as a governing Sub-Stat and its Weakness paragraph argues at length about a different gate, Sovereignty's, which in fact closes.

options.option: Record Attraction Path for Francis on the card.
options.changes: Closes the gate and would settle the other Francis pages that project fields; contradicts the card's 'every bond pointing inward, nothing points back', which is an Attraction-Layer statement rather than a Path one and may already support it.

options.option: Drop Dominion Radius from the FOW line and carry the extent on Sovereignty alone.
options.changes: One line; needs a statement that a law-claim's reach is Sovereignty rather than Radius, which would apply to every Domain Weaving page.

options.option: Reduce the radius to a figure the ungated Grade supports.
options.changes: Changes the working's scale substantially and its tactical role with it.

options.option: Rule that Domain Weaving reach is gated by Sovereignty alone and Radius applies only to a formal Domain.
options.changes: Settles a class of pages at once; requires the distinction between a Domain and a law field to be written down.

quote_a: Multi-inversion chains are refused by the Crystal rather than merely risky. One Principle per activation, without exception.
quote_b: Principle Collapse. Multi-inversion chains cause paradox recoil that fractures selfhood and destabilises local reality; the card gives an eighteen percent chance of self-erasure at high inversion depth
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Francis Alexander · The Crimson Dirge of Atonement.md
why: Three documents give three answers to one question. The technique page's Summary card says chaining 'risks paradox rather than compounding the effect'; its own Limitation says chains are 'refused by the Crystal rather than merely risky ... without exception'; and the character card says chains happen and carry an eighteen percent chance of self-erasure at depth. A fourth data point cuts against 'without exception' as well: Judgment Manifest has Francis call 'up to three Hermetic Principles' at once across a two-kilometre field.

options.option: Rule chaining possible at the card's eighteen percent self-erasure risk and rewrite the Limitation.
options.changes: Gives Francis his most dangerous option back with a stated price; makes the eighteen percent a number a player can plan around; needs a definition of 'inversion depth'.

options.option: Rule chaining impossible within one activation and reconcile Judgment Manifest as three separate simultaneous activations.
options.changes: Keeps the Limitation; needs a rule for how many activations can be held at once, which the system does not have.

options.option: Distinguish chaining within one working (refused) from holding several workings at once (permitted at a cost).
options.changes: Resolves all four texts with one distinction; the cost of concurrency needs stating.

options.option: Record the three positions and leave them as written.
options.changes: No change; the working's central limit is unresolved across its own page.

page: (3 Francis pages in 29–56, plus Judgment Manifest)
quote_a: Francis isolates one Hermetic Principle within a five-kilometre radius and rewrites its behavior for roughly fifteen seconds of sustained declaration (cause running as effect, rhythm running as stillness, opposed polarities merging)
quote_b: Eastern and Western Hermetic traditions · Jabir's Shaneni-origin synthesis and the Herald-aligned curriculum. The philosophical bridge is the principle of correspondence. Both describe the same Wellspring-soul relationship in different grammars.
path_b: wiki/The Alftian Codex/Volume the First.md
why: The operand of this mechanic is a Hermetic Principle, and no register of Principles exists anywhere in the system: no page lists them, counts them, or states which are editable. The three named on the page (cause and effect, rhythm, polarity) are three of the seven Principles of the Kybalion, a real-world text. Canon does carry Hermeticism, but as an in-world school and a grammar for describing Wellspring-soul relations, which the Alftian Codex says explicitly. The system's own word for the stratum is on the character card instead: 'Edits and fuses operational principles at the Archonic Law stratum', and the Archonic Law stratum is likewise not a register anywhere. The system does use 'Principle' as a term at the top of the ladder, in Apex ('Holding a Principle in the Soul Crystal without fracturing') and in the EX-Grade note, without ever enumerating them.

options.option: Publish a register of Principles with a count, the Archon or Titan each answers to, and which are editable at which Stage.
options.changes: Gives four Francis pages a checkable operand and the top of the ladder a spine; large new reference page; must not simply reprint the Kybalion's seven.

options.option: Rename the operand to the system's own term, the Archonic Law stratum, and define that stratum without enumerating its contents.
options.changes: Smaller; removes the out-of-world citation and keeps the mystery; a counter still has nothing specific to target.

options.option: Keep 'Hermetic Principle' as the in-world school's name for the operand and state that the Accord has no register of its own, which is itself a political fact.
options.changes: Costs nothing, fits The Four Crafts' 'the taxonomy is political' lever, and turns the gap into a hook; leaves the mechanic uncheckable.

options.option: Restrict the working to the three Principles the page names and treat the set as closed until ruled otherwise.
options.changes: Makes the technique concrete and immediately counterable; loses the open-ended reality-editing that the character is built on.

quote_a: Path gate · Spirit Path, drift toward Attraction Path
quote_b: Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B, with inscription and glyph-chain durability requiring Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page's own Sub-Stat list ("Sub-Stats · Gnosis Cognition, Dominion Sense, Dominion Sovereignty, Ardency Density") names two Sub-Stats whose Part Seven gates the declared Paths do not open. Ardency Density at A-Grade exceeds B and therefore requires Body Path, and Aeldoris's card reads "Path · Spirit dominant, Attraction secondary, Body tertiary, Fate untouched" (wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Aeldoris Vanthryx · The Ruthless.md:43). Ardency Density is the Sub-Stat the page assigns the load-bearing job to: "Eidolyn gives that imagined motion enough Ardency Density to press outward into real muscle." Separately, the page's stated S-Grade push crosses Dominion Sovereignty, which "requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A" (Part Seven), and the same card line reads Fate untouched. Two of the four listed Sub-Stats fail their gate; the working as written cannot be run by the practitioner the page credits it to. The Four Paths page forecloses the easy fix: "Path commitment is not declared. It is recognized by the Crystal based on behavioural pattern."

options.option: Drop Ardency Density from the Sub-Stat list and rewrite the Eidolyn clause so the motion is released rather than pressed, since the physical account shows the working delivers no mechanical work at all (the target's own ATP moves the limb).
options.changes: Removes the failing gate and matches the mechanism the account derives; changes one Mechanism sentence and the FOW line; makes the working cheaper and reframes Eidolyn's role as thresholding rather than force.

options.option: Raise the page's Path gate to include Body, and reconcile the card.
options.changes: Contradicts Aeldoris's card (Body tertiary) and the Four Paths rule that commitment is recognised, not declared; would need a card edit and a stated behavioural reason.

options.option: Cap the working at A-Grade and delete the "late-Stage practitioners can push toward S-Grade" clause.
options.changes: Closes the Dominion Sovereignty failure only; leaves Ardency Density failing; removes the page's stated ceiling headroom.

options.option: Reassign the working to a practitioner whose card carries Body or Fate.
options.changes: Breaks the Origin line ("Derived by Aeldoris") and the three sibling Aeldoris pages that share its Wellspring set.

quote_a: Weakness · Letheveil clarity dissolves the thread, since a mind that has just had its recent fear-memory shaken loose leaves Oneirion no coordinate to lock onto. Non-humanoid targets respond inconsistently, their configuration space mapping differently.
quote_b: Failure · Ensemble collapse. The spread is mistaken for a single reading, and the practitioner acts on a branch that carried eleven percent of the weight.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Fluxia — Fluid Dynamics.md
why: The working's primary current is Somnalis, and Somnalis's register failure is ensemble collapse: reading a distribution as a single answer. That is the failure mode this working is built to suffer, because the whole mechanic is picking one branch out of the target's spread and then driving the body down it. The page carries neither the failure nor its consequence, and the system states no rule for what happens when the seeded motion is a branch the target was eleven percent committed to — whether the limb still moves, moves wrongly, or the thread simply fails. The page's FOW line also omits Gnosis Forecast, which is the Sub-Stat Somnalis actually strengthens ("Stat Effect · Strengthens Gnosis Forecast, Dominion Sense"), so the ensemble-reading stat is off the sheet entirely.

options.option: Add the register failure to the page as its own line: a misread spread seeds a low-weight branch, and state what the target's body then does.
options.changes: Gives the working a failure mode a player can bait; needs one ruling on what a low-weight seed produces (nothing, a wrong motion, or a motion the target can claim as their own).

options.option: Publish a general rule for Fluxia ensemble collapse (a weight threshold below which a read does not license an action) in the Families page, and let every Fluxia working inherit it.
options.changes: One reference addition serving every Somnalis, Thaloré and Fluxia working; sets a number the system currently has nowhere.

options.option: Add Gnosis Forecast to the page's Sub-Stats and let its Part Seven gate carry the read.
options.changes: Puts the governing stat on the sheet; Forecast requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed S, which at A-Grade closes, so it costs nothing in gates — but it makes the Attraction drift load-bearing rather than incidental.

options.option: Leave it as a Wellspring-level hazard the page need not restate.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; the gap stays and each scene decides for itself.

quote_a: Oneirion locks onto that possibility's coordinate in the target's own configuration space rather than in the room, which is why Aeldoris needs no line of sight to the limb he moves, only to the fear-image forming behind the target's eyes.
quote_b: Trigger · Declared, against a target within 60 meters who is already feeling fear or panic.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Puppet-Dream Marionette.md
why: "Line of sight to the fear-image forming behind the target's eyes" is not a sensing act the system defines: Dominion Sense's Part Seven clauses cover topology, higher-order phenomena and Archon-tier pressures, and no page states whether reading a mind at 60 m requires the target to be visible, audible, merely present, or known. The question decides whether cover counters the working, which is the difference between a counter a player can act on and none at all. It also decides whether the working has any tell: the page gives none — declaration, then somebody's leg moves — and if no line of sight is required, there is no moment at which a target could know they are being read.

options.option: Rule that mind-reading at range requires an unobstructed sense line to the target's face, so cover, a mask or a turned back denies the read.
options.changes: Makes cover a counter to this and to every other Limina reading working; adds a tell (he must be looking at you); narrows the working sharply indoors.

options.option: Rule that configuration-space coordinates need no physical line, and give the working a compensating tell instead (a perceptible pressure at the moment of seeding).
options.changes: Keeps the page's stated reach; the counter moves from cover to noticing the seed; needs a new tell written into the page.

options.option: Publish a general sensing-requirement clause in the Dominion Sense entry covering range, obstruction and target awareness.
options.changes: One reference addition governing every Sense-based working; large scope, settles many pages at once.

options.option: Leave undecided and resolve per scene.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; the working keeps a failed fairness check for tell and findability.

quote_a: At Stage VI's A-Grade ceiling, peak force runs 20 to 100 GN and energy yield 46 GJ to 4.184 TJ, an 11 to 1,000-tonne TNT equivalent, City Block to Multi-City Block scale at the sustainable maximum. The burst itself is instantaneous, under a second, matching the source's "1 turn (instant burst)."
quote_b: Cataclysm makes that transition available to Essence expression, and blast radius thereafter scales with the cube root of yield, which is why the Wellspring's area effects widen coherently rather than merely spilling.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Caloria — Thermodynamics.md
why: The page states a 20-metre radius and an 11–1,000 tonne TNT yield, and the cube-root scaling law that the page's own secondary Wellspring writes into canon makes those two numbers incompatible. Taking the standard scaled distance for 34 kPa (Z ≈ 4 m·kg^(−1/3), the overpressure that knocks bodies down and breaks weak structures, which is what the page's Effect describes), 11 tonnes reaches 89 m and 1,000 tonnes reaches about 400 m: four to twenty times the stated radius. Inverted, a 20 m radius corresponds to W = (20/4)³ = 125 kg TNT = 5.2×10⁸ J, which is C-Grade on the same table, two Grades below the page's stated requirement. The thermal half closes cleanly — heating the 4.1×10⁴ kg of air in a 20 m sphere by 1,500 K takes about 62 GJ, just inside the A-Grade floor of 46 GJ — so it is specifically the blast half that does not fit. Either the radius is a C-Grade radius or the yield is an A-Grade yield.

options.option: Keep the 20 m radius and drop the yield to C-Grade (about 125 kg TNT, 5.2×10⁸ J), lowering the Stage floor and Grade requirement to match.
options.changes: Makes the working a Stage IV–V area attack rather than a Stage VI one; the fire (62 GJ for the sphere) would then exceed the concussive budget, so the Effect becomes fire-primary with a knockdown, not a city-block blast.

options.option: Keep the A-Grade yield and raise the radius to what the cube-root law gives (89 m at the floor).
options.changes: Quadruples the danger zone, puts the caster inside their own lethal radius at the origin, and turns an area-denial working into a battlefield-scale one; the page's Counterplay (get behind a ward) stops being survivable at range.

options.option: Keep both and state a confinement clause: the burst is bounded at 20 m by the working itself, so the yield is spent inside a held boundary rather than propagating freely.
options.changes: Adds a containment mechanic the system does not currently have; the reflected-overpressure failure in Cataclysm's register would then apply to the caster on every use, at up to 8× incident overpressure, which would be the largest cost on any page in this batch.

options.option: Treat the 46 GJ – 4.184 TJ band as the Grade's headroom rather than this working's output, and give the page its own figure.
options.changes: Decouples every technique page from the Grade table's full range; needs a stated rule for how much of a Grade band a given working draws.

quote_a: A spiralling gale of fire detonates outward to a 20-metre radius, burning everything caught inside and following the burn with a blunt shockwave that knocks bodies back or down and overloads weak shields on contact.
quote_b: A subsonic flame front that meets sufficient confinement and turbulence accelerates until the reaction couples to a shock wave and begins propagating faster than sound in the unreacted medium. The mechanism is a change of kind, not degree.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Caloria — Thermodynamics.md
why: The Effect asserts a detonation in the open, and the Mechanism that Cataclysm supplies requires confinement and turbulence to reach one — the register says so in the same sentence that grants the transition. An unconfined outward burst is the one geometry that does not run deflagration-to-detonation: a laminar burning velocity of roughly 0.4 m/s has to accelerate to a CJ velocity of about 1,800 m/s, and in free air there is nothing to do the accelerating. The page's Mechanism line never claims the transition either; it describes Cascade and Radius widening a jet into a coherent burst, which is a deflagration. The page's own open question — "Why the shockwave sometimes outruns the flame it came from instead of arriving with it" — is the signature of the two halves being separate events rather than one: a shock crosses 20 m in 58 ms, a flame front takes seconds.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: a deflagration that pushes a pressure front ahead of a slower flame, with the shock always arriving first and the burn following.
options.changes: Resolves the open question by making the separation the rule rather than an anomaly; removes the word detonates; the knockdown and the burn become two arrivals a target can react between, which gives the working a mid-flight counter it does not have now.

options.option: Add the confinement clause to the Mechanism: the working supplies its own boundary (a held shell) so the flame front accelerates against it and the transition runs.
options.changes: Justifies the detonation and the shock; invokes Cataclysm's reflected-overpressure failure on the caster at the origin, at up to about 8× incident; would need the boundary to be a stated component with a Grade cost.

options.option: Split the working into two declared modes, an open deflagration and a confined detonation, with different Stage floors.
options.changes: Two entries where there is one; the Limitation line ("cannot be aimed finer than its full radius, throttled mid-release, or interrupted once declared") would need a mode-choice exception.

options.option: Leave the Effect and mark the transition as unexplained.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; the working keeps an off-mechanism effect and the physical account does not close.

quote_a: Craft · Spellcraft (Ars Vocis; declared, with a chant carrying the working when the caster wants the extra output a release call buys)
quote_b: What nothing else can do · It scales with throats. Everything above trivial requires more than one voice, which makes Chantcraft the only craft that cannot be practised alone.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: The page buys extra output with a chant, and The Four Crafts ratifies chanting as its own craft that a single practitioner cannot perform above the trivial. The Accord Latin page is more specific still: "The sustained vowel has to be carried continuously while the line advances, which one set of lungs cannot do, so the voices overlap and hand the vowel between them. Three is the working minimum" (wiki/The Tongues of the Realms/Accord Latin — The Formulary and the Two Spoken Registers.md:91). A solo caster's release call is therefore a shout inside Ars Vocis, not Ars Cantus, and cannot draw the scaling the page credits it with. As written the page is either claiming a Chantcraft benefit for a Spellcraft act, or quietly requiring a choir the Trigger line does not mention.

options.option: Delete the chant clause and keep Ars Vocis declaration only.
options.changes: Removes the unearned output bonus; the working becomes strictly solo; the spoken tell stays, which is the page's best fairness feature.

options.option: Keep the chant and state the choir: three voices minimum, per the Accord Latin working minimum, with the extra output priced to the throats.
options.changes: Turns a solo burst into a ritual with a visible, interruptible setup — a large change to how the working plays, and a strong new counter (take one voice out).

options.option: Publish a rule for a solo release call as a named Ars Vocis intensity step distinct from Chantcraft.
options.changes: Adds a general mechanic serving every declared working; needs a stated magnitude and a stated cost so it does not become free output.

options.option: Rule that the extra output comes from the declaration's Law V closure rather than from chanting, and rename it.
options.changes: Keeps the number, moves the source; no choir; requires the Law V clause to actually state an output effect.

quote_a: Counter · Thaloré-worked water blunts the blast outright; Cinerion rust-barriers redirect the force rather than absorb it; Verdantia wards muffle how far the flame spreads.
quote_b: Pressure at depth depends on nothing but how dense the fluid is and how far down you are. Not on the vessel, not on the volume, not on the surface. Thaloré gives emotional content that same constitutive relation: density times depth, expressed as literal metaphysical weight, which is why a Thaloré practitioner's grief has a measurable pressure field and why standing near one is physically tiring.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Fluxia — Fluid Dynamics.md
why: Both named counters use their Wellspring as an element rather than as the law the register gives it. Thaloré is hydrostatic pressure and emotional weight, not water: nothing in its entry produces or commands water, and "Thaloré-worked water" is an elemental reading of a pressure Wellspring. Cinerion is char and ash — "Char is a high-surface-area carbon scaffold that catalyses further reaction, and settled ash returns potassium and phosphorus to the ground that fed the fire" (wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Caloria — Thermodynamics.md) — and a "rust-barrier" is neither, rust being oxidised iron and Cinerion's residue being carbon and mineral ash. Cinerion is also a Caloria Wellspring, so a Cinerion barrier is a fire Wellspring countering a fire working, which the page does not explain. The physics of the real counter is available and unstated: about 25 tonnes of water boiled absorbs the 62 GJ thermal load, and the Field Manual's Caloria line already states what to do with the blast half.

options.option: Rewrite both counters from the registers: Thaloré opposes the blast as a standing pressure field (density times depth against overpressure), and Cinerion's ash veil scatters the radiant component.
options.changes: Makes both counters derivable from pages a player can find; loses the vivid water and rust imagery; the Thaloré counter becomes about weight rather than wetness.

options.option: Name water-bearing Wellsprings and materials explicitly instead of Thaloré, and iron-bearing ones instead of Cinerion.
options.changes: Keeps the intended counters and fixes the attribution; requires checking which Wellspring in the sixty actually commands water, and stating it.

options.option: Publish an elemental-reading note in the Families page saying that field usage names Wellsprings by their apparent element, and that the register's law governs.
options.changes: Legitimises the page's language as in-world shorthand across many pages at once; risks every page citing elements instead of laws.

options.option: Replace the named counters with the Family terrain answer the register already gives (thermal equilibrium, saturated cold, oxygen-poor air).
options.changes: A fully attested counter with no new rules; removes three named counters and makes the working harder to beat with a working rather than with ground.

quote_a: Path gate · Spirit, Body
quote_b: Cascade requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B for spread, Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed S for range.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Ardency Cascade is the Sub-Stat the page relies on for the burst — "Cataclysm strengthens Ardency Cascade, Ardency Overchannel and Dominion Radius. That is what turns a single flame into a coherent 20-metre burst instead of a narrow jet" — and spreading it past B-Grade requires Attraction Path. The page declares Spirit and Body and no Attraction. At A-Grade the working is two brackets past B and the whole working is spread, so the gate fails on the Sub-Stat that makes it an area effect at all. Dominion Radius closes only by a single bracket (Part Seven: "Radius requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed A, Stage VI to exceed A for partial projection outward" — at exactly A neither threshold is crossed), so there is no headroom anywhere in the spread half of this working.

options.option: Add Attraction to the page's Path gate.
options.changes: One line; opens Cascade's spread and leaves Radius one bracket from its own gate; no practitioner is named on this page, so no card contradicts it.

options.option: Drop the Grade requirement to B so Cascade's spread gate is not crossed.
options.changes: Lowers the Stage floor and the yield band with it; combines with the radius-versus-yield conflict, since a B or C-Grade yield is what the 20 m radius actually implies.

options.option: Recast the burst as Dominion Radius alone and drop Cascade from the Design Chain.
options.changes: Keeps Spirit and Body; makes the working a projected boundary rather than a cascading spread; changes what Cataclysm is contributing and may leave the secondary Wellspring doing nothing.

options.option: Rule that a Wellspring's Stat Effect satisfies its own Sub-Stat's Path gate.
options.changes: A system-wide rule that would close gates on many pages at once; substantially weakens Part Seven as a constraint.

quote_a: Cut severs textile and rope at 3-5 metres and scores light plate at 2-3.
quote_b: This runs on real acoustic phase-locking, laminar versus turbulent airflow, the same physics that lets a trained voice cut through noise an untrained one cannot.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Radiant Ribbon Shell.md
why: The Mechanism cites a voice cutting through noise, which is audibility — the singer's formant at 2.5–3 kHz — and the Effect asks for a cutting edge that severs rope and scores plate. Sound in air cannot deliver it. Acoustic radiation pressure at 160 dB is about 28 Pa, giving 2.8×10⁻⁵ N over a 1 mm² focus against the 20–60 N needed to part a rope; even at air's shock-forming ceiling near 194 dB, a 4 mm focus delivers roughly 0.4 N, two orders short, and air cannot carry more without ceasing to be a linear medium. The Mechanism as written produces no force at all, and the Effect's own cut-cloth-not-flesh selectivity has no mechanism behind it either. The page's Target Response repeats the claim: "a bound target's textile or rope parts cleanly at the Cut Lamina's edge."

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism and delete the Cut: the working hushes, carries and reads coherence, and the cutting mode becomes a separate technique with a force-bearing Wellspring behind it.
options.changes: Removes one of the page's three modes and its Cost clause ("cutting against conscience costs voice"); the remaining working is coherent and the account closes.

options.option: Keep the Cut and supply a mechanism that can deliver newtons — a cavitation or shock-front clause, a solid or liquid coupling medium, or a Wellspring that supplies the force directly.
options.changes: Needs a new Wellspring or component on the Codex line and a reason the edge spares flesh; likely raises the Stage floor; the cut-cloth-not-flesh selectivity still needs a stated basis.

options.option: Reinterpret the Cut as resonant failure rather than pressure — severing a cord at its characteristic mode, as Celestial Harmonic Shear does — with a stated dwell time.
options.changes: Attested precedent exists on another page; makes the Cut slow rather than instant, which is a large play change and a genuine counter (move); explains cloth over flesh, since flesh is damped.

options.option: Treat the Cut's figures as an in-world exaggeration recorded by the source and mark them unverified.
options.changes: Nothing mechanical; the numbers stay on the page with a caveat and the working keeps a mode nobody can adjudicate.

quote_a: Hush runs roughly -9 dB at 8 metres and holds through gusts to about 30 knots.
quote_b: The voice entrains nearby air into laminar bands that can damp ambient noise, carry a phrase intact, or thin into a cutting edge.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Radiant Ribbon Shell.md
why: Laminar entrainment does not attenuate sound. Air's own absorption over 8 m is about 0.04 dB, four orders below the stated 9 dB, and ordered flow is if anything a cleaner medium for sound than turbulent flow, so making the air laminar should improve transmission rather than damp it — which is exactly what the page's Carry mode claims for the same bands. Active cancellation is the only real route to broadband −9 dB over an 8 m region, and cancelling over a region that size requires a wavelength longer than about 48 m, which caps it below roughly 7 Hz — infrasound, not speech. The stratal account has a route the page does not use: the working's primary Wellspring is Judicium in Fulguria (Electromagnetism), and phase-locking is a real mechanism, but it must be stated as destructive interference with a stated bandwidth, not as flow order. As written the physical account and the stratal account describe different phenomena and do not balance.

options.option: Restate Hush as narrowband destructive interference with a stated frequency range and a stated failure outside it.
options.changes: Makes the mode physical and gives it a limit a player can exploit (speak outside the band, or at the wrong pitch); the -9 dB figure survives only inside the stated band.

options.option: Restate Hush as absorption by an impedance boundary the working holds at the field's rim, which the Consequence line already gestures at ("Panic and ambient clamor fold outward and thin at the field's rim").
options.changes: Changes the geometry from a volume to a surface; the hush becomes directional, so sound from inside still travels inside; consistent with the page's Consequence and with the Carry mode.

options.option: Keep the laminar-bands language as the in-world description and publish the real mechanism separately.
options.changes: Preserves the page's voice; the account and the page diverge, which is what this pass exists to prevent.

options.option: Drop the Hush figure and state the effect qualitatively.
options.changes: Removes a checkable number; the mode stops failing the physical account by being unmeasurable rather than by being wrong.

quote_a: Air-Step bursts run 30-60 m/s with a two-beat recovery.
quote_b: Ballast with lower vowels and reset cadence against Ribbon Fray; a calm ally widens the laminar stability of Choir mode against turbulence caused by anger.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Radiant Ribbon Shell.md
why: The page names eight components — Hushfield, Cut Lamina, Carry, Choir mode, Ribbon Fray, Feather Vows, Air-Step, and the four gates Set, Place, Speak, Recover — and defines two. Air-Step is the sharpest case: it appears only in the Numerical Effect, carries a speed and a recovery time, and no Effect, Function, Mechanism, Target Response or Consequence line mentions movement at all, so the page grants a 30–60 m/s displacement with no mechanism, no cost and no Wellspring behind it. Choir mode implies more than one voice, which touches Chantcraft's scaling rule, and the page never states how many. Feather Vows are the subject of the page's own open question ("Why the Feather Vows chime true and dull false") while never being defined as objects, and the Anamnesis register says reading can reset the record being read — which would mean testing a vow erases it, a cost nobody has charged.

options.option: Define each named component on the page: what it is, which mode produces it, its numbers and its cost.
options.changes: Large page rewrite; makes every mode adjudicable; Air-Step in particular needs a mechanism and a Path gate it currently fails.

options.option: Cut the undefined components, keeping Hush, Carry and the coherence read.
options.changes: A short, coherent page; loses Air-Step, Choir mode and the Feather Vows, and with them the page's own open question.

options.option: Split the Feather Vows out as their own artefact entry, with the Anamnesis reset priced as the cost of testing one.
options.changes: Gives the vows a mechanism and a real cost; adds an artefact page; answers the page's open question, which may be worth keeping open instead.

options.option: Keep the names as in-world jargon from the class-template the source records, with a note that the record does not define them.
options.changes: Nothing mechanical; the numbers attached to undefined components (Air-Step's 30–60 m/s) stay unadjudicable.

quote_a: a bound target's textile or rope parts cleanly at the Cut Lamina's edge
quote_b: Convert accumulated strain, impact, and moral load into stored radiant weight (the Strain Lamina); amplify sharply in the presence of banners, seals, or spoken oaths (the Oath Lamina); hold that store behind a restraint that favours mercy until judgment is deliberately chosen (the Mercy Lamina)
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Solarbound Aegoric Knight.md
why: Two technique pages in different Families use "Lamina" as a named structural component — a Cut Lamina in an airflow working, three Laminae in a stored-radiance working — and no system page defines the term. It is not in the Core Vocabulary, not in the Lexicon of Magic, and not in the Master Glyph Index. A reader cannot tell whether a Lamina is a layer of a working, a stored quantity, a boundary, or only a house word two authors reached for independently. Because both pages hang numbers and behaviour on their Laminae, the term is load-bearing in at least two places without a definition anywhere.

options.option: Publish a Lamina entry in the Core Vocabulary: a bounded layer of a working that holds one property and can be shed or breached independently.
options.changes: One reference addition; makes both pages checkable and gives Laminae a stated way to be broken, which is a counter route for every working that uses one.

options.option: Rename the components on both pages to terms the Lexicon already carries.
options.changes: No new vocabulary; two page edits; loses a usefully specific word that two authors reached for independently.

options.option: Rule that Lamina is in-world craft jargon with no mechanical weight, and strip the numbers attached to it.
options.changes: Keeps the flavour and removes the adjudication problem; the Cut Lamina's distances and the Strain Lamina's storage would need to be restated on some other component.

options.option: Leave it undefined and treat each page's usage locally.
options.changes: Nothing; the gap remains and grows with each new page that reaches for the word.

quote_a: Governing Primary Harmonics (Fidelity, Attunement) and Dexterity (Burst, Finesse). Stage floor VII, Refraction, ascending to VIII, Transcendence. Grade required A-Grade at floor, S-Grade at apex. Path gate Attraction Path.
quote_b: Celerity requires Body Path at Stage II to exceed D, and Stage IV to exceed B for standing acceleration.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page's "Burst" resolves through the Merge Ledger to Dexterity Celerity, whose Part Seven gate requires Body Path to exceed B for standing acceleration. The working runs at A-Grade, which exceeds B; the Air-Step's 30–60 m/s from a standing position is standing acceleration by the plainest reading; and the page's declared Path gate is Attraction Path only. The same FOW line also lists one Sub-Stat twice: the Merge Ledger resolves "Fidelity" to Attunement, so "Harmonics (Fidelity, Attunement)" names Attunement and Attunement. Attunement's own gate closes (it requires Attraction Path at Stage II to exceed D, and Attraction is declared), so the failure is confined to the movement mode — which is the same mode that has no mechanism written for it anywhere on the page.

options.option: Delete Air-Step from the page, which removes the failing gate and the undefined component in one edit.
options.changes: The working loses a mobility mode it never described outside one number; the Path gate then stands as written and every remaining Sub-Stat closes.

options.option: Add Body to the Path gate and keep Air-Step.
options.changes: One line; opens Celerity; makes a voice working require Body commitment, which sits oddly against a Harmonia category and an Attraction-Path class-template.

options.option: Restate Air-Step as an assisted displacement driven by the laminar bands rather than by the practitioner's own acceleration, so Celerity is not the governing Sub-Stat.
