options.changes: Needs a stated mechanism (a pressure boundary the practitioner pushes against) and its own Sub-Stat and gate; keeps the mode.

options.option: Correct the doubled Sub-Stat and cap the working at B-Grade so no gate is exceeded.
options.changes: Fixes the Merge Ledger duplication and the gate at once; contradicts the page's stated A-Grade floor and S-Grade apex and would lower the Stage floor.

quote_a: Path gate · Spirit, Fate
quote_b: Empathy requires Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page's primary Wellspring strengthens three Sub-Stats and all three are Attraction-gated, while the page declares Spirit and Fate. Benediction's register line is "Strengthens Harmonics Empathy, Axis, Resilience Oath" (wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vitalia — Biochemistry.md), and the page carries the same three in its FOW line. At the required B-Grade, Empathy's gate is crossed outright — B exceeds C, so Attraction Path is required and no Attraction is declared. Axis and Oath both "require Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B" (Part Seven) and therefore close only because B-Grade sits exactly at B and does not exceed it: one point of allocation past 275 fails all three at once, and Stage V's own instability zone runs to 350. So the working stands on a knife-edge for two of its Sub-Stats and is already over the line on the third.

options.option: Add Attraction to the page's Path gate.
options.changes: One line; opens all three Benediction Sub-Stats with headroom; no practitioner is named on this page, so no card contradicts it. Makes a healing working Attraction-committed, which fits a bond Wellspring.

options.option: Drop Empathy from the FOW line and run the working on Axis and Oath alone, both of which close at exactly B.
options.changes: Keeps Spirit and Fate; removes the passive-sensing component, so the caster must be told where the wound is rather than feeling it; the knife-edge on the other two remains.

options.option: Lower the Grade requirement to C so Empathy's gate is not crossed.
options.changes: At exactly C-Grade the C threshold is not exceeded, so Empathy's gate does not engage and the page's Spirit-and-Fate gate stands. Lowers the working's output band and its Stage floor with it, and contradicts the page's 'near 350' figure in the other direction.

options.option: Rule that a Wellspring's own Stat Effect satisfies its Sub-Stats' Path gates.
options.changes: A system-wide rule closing gates on many pages at once; substantially weakens Part Seven as a constraint.

quote_a: Operates within the B-Grade output ceiling that Stage V, Splintering permits, proportionate to what a stat total near 350 can move rather than to a destructive-yield table, since nothing here is discharged outward.
quote_b: At Stages V, VII, IX and XI the Sub-Stat ceiling sits above that bracket, and the band between them, 276 to 350, 401 to 475, 551 to 625, 726 to 750, is the instability zone, reachable only under strain, never by allocation.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The figure 350 is out of band on either reading. Read as a Sub-Stat, 350 is the top of Stage V's instability zone, two Grade brackets above the B-Grade the page itself requires (176-275) and reachable "only under strain, never by allocation" - so the sentence prices a routine healing working at a value the Crystal can only touch under strain, in the same breath as naming the B ceiling. Read as a Primary total, Part Four is explicit that "A Primary is the combined total of its eight Sub-Stats, and its Grade is read off the mean", and 350 ÷ 8 = 43.75, which is E-Grade. Nothing on the page says which reading is meant, and the two differ by five Grade brackets.

options.option: Restate the output as a B-Grade Sub-Stat figure in the 176-275 range and delete 350.
options.changes: Puts the working in its own declared band; loses nothing else on the page; makes the healing ceiling checkable against Part Eleven's B row.

options.option: Keep 350 and state that the working is a strain expression, with the instability-zone consequences Part Five attaches (Crystal Fracture Events at an exponentially increasing rate).
options.changes: Turns a routine blessing into a dangerous one and gives it a real cost, which the page currently lacks; contradicts the 'mild drain' Cost line.

options.option: Declare the figure a Primary total and correct the Grade to what the mean gives.
options.changes: Makes the working E-Grade, far below its stated B requirement and its Stage V floor; would need the Stage floor lowered too.

options.option: Publish a conversion note for non-destructive workings, since the page is right that a healing working should not be priced off a destructive-yield table.
options.changes: A genuinely missing rule that would serve every Harmonia and healing page; needs a stated scale for restorative output that the system does not currently have anywhere.

quote_a: The caster reaches along an existing or newly formed bond.
quote_b: III to IV, Flourishing. Formation of the first genuine Spirit Axis, a bond with another soul that carries mechanical weight in the Harmonics system.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The working creates a Spirit Axis in the moment of casting, on a wounded ally who may be a stranger, and the system states no rule for how an Axis is formed. The only formation the system describes is a Temperance Threshold Event - the first Axis is the Catalyst Condition for the III-to-IV transition, which is a Crystal-authorised event rather than a thing done in a second - and Part Twelve defines Axis as the structural integrity of "established" Spirit Axes, with no procedure for establishing one. Three questions follow that no page answers: whether the ally must consent (a bond is the one structure that cannot be formed unilaterally, and the Consent Doctrine is one of the Four Theories); how long formation takes; and whether the bond persists after the six seconds, which decides whether a battlefield healer accumulates permanent Axes at a rate nobody has priced. Benediction's own law says the bond carries an affinity figure the Continuum reads, so a formed Axis is a durable, readable object, not a gesture.

options.option: Publish an Axis formation rule in Part Twelve or the Harmonics entry: what forms one, whether consent is required, how long it takes, and whether it persists.
options.changes: One reference addition governing every bond-based working, Benediction Wellspring and oath in the system; large and load-bearing.

options.option: Restrict the working to an existing Axis and delete 'or newly formed'.
options.changes: The healer can only bless people they are already bonded to, which is a strong limit and a strong story constraint; makes the technique useless on strangers, including most casualties.

options.option: Rule that the working forms a transient channel rather than an Axis, distinct from and weaker than a true Spirit Axis.
options.changes: Keeps the technique usable on strangers; introduces a second, lesser class of bond the system does not currently have, which would need its own durability rule.

options.option: Leave undecided and resolve per scene.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; the working's central prerequisite stays unadjudicable and the consent question stays open.

quote_a: Cost · The caster feels a trace of the wound they just closed; a mild, lingering emotional drain that fades once the ally's Crystal has stabilised.
quote_b: Failure · Competitive inhibition. A rival ligand with higher affinity displaces the existing bond, and the displacement is silent, complete, and not felt until the bond is called on.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vitalia — Biochemistry.md
why: The only cost the page states is explicitly mild, explicitly temporary and explicitly self-clearing, it is unpriced in EU, and nothing on the page limits repetition: a caster may bless every casualty in a company in sequence at no cumulative price. A restorative working with no accumulating cost fails the fairness check that every ability must cost something that hurts. The costs that would hurt are already in the register and unused. An Axis conducts in both directions, which is why the caster feels the wound at all, so every blessing leaves the caster with a durable readable bond carrying an affinity figure; and Benediction's own failure means any of those bonds can be silently outbid by a rival with higher affinity, with the caster not finding out until the bond is called on. Neither is priced anywhere.

options.option: Make the cost cumulative: each active blessing is a standing Axis, and a caster carrying several is measurably degraded until they close.
options.changes: Caps mass healing without a hard number; gives Resilience Oath something to do; makes a field healer's caseload a resource.

options.option: Price the cost in the register's own failure: every bond formed is a bond that can be outbid, and an opponent who does so acquires a channel into the patient.
options.changes: Turns the cost into a risk rather than a fee, and hands opponents a counter the page currently lacks; needs a rule for what an outbid bond does.

options.option: Price it in EU as a fraction of reserve, so repeated casting drives the healer toward Essence Starvation below ten percent.
options.changes: Uses the one cost mechanic the system already defines; blocked until SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA is ruled, since no formula converts a Stage into an EU reserve.

options.option: Add a stated cooldown or a cap on concurrent blessings.
options.changes: The bluntest fix and the least interesting; caps the abuse without explaining anything.

quote_a: A struck body stops moving, stops healing, and stops taking new damage easily.
quote_b: Fixatio performs that cure on the target's present configuration. What it holds is not held by force. It is held because the alternative configuration has stopped being a reachable state.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Sigillum Fixatio.md
why: The Mechanism describes kinetic trapping: raising the barrier out of the present configuration so that spontaneous transitions stop occurring. That produces exactly one of the Effect's three clauses. "Stops healing" follows perfectly, because biological repair is enzymatic catalysis and catalysis is barrier lowering - remove it and the chemistry does not break, it simply stops happening. "Stops moving" does not follow, because movement is driven by muscle at kilonewton scale rather than by thermal agitation, and a barrier height is not a restraint against a driven process. "Stops taking new damage easily" does not follow either: a barrier of the height the page's nine-second duration implies is about 83 kJ/mol, roughly 32 RT, while a sword blow delivers on the order of 100 J to a limb, which is enormous against any per-bond barrier. Barrier heights govern what happens spontaneously; they say nothing about what happens when an opponent does work on the target. The thermoset reading would give mechanical strength, but it is a different claim from the reachability one the Mechanism actually makes.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: the target stops changing of its own accord - no healing, no bleeding out, no decay, no drift, and an active working's parameters frozen - while remaining exactly as vulnerable to an external blow as before.
options.changes: Makes the working a control and denial tool rather than a defensive one; a held ally can still be killed, which is a large tactical change and a much sharper piece of design.

options.option: Add the thermoset's mechanical half explicitly: the cure forms a spanning covalent-analogue network, so damage must break bonds rather than displace them, at a stated strength.
options.changes: Justifies the damage resistance and the immobilisation; needs a strength figure that is not an attack-output row, and inherits the brittleness the page already states.

options.option: Split the effect: physical targets get the network, metaphysical targets (workings, wards) get the reachability lock.
options.changes: Two mechanisms on one page, each internally coherent; doubles the page's rules surface and needs both priced.

options.option: Delete 'stops taking new damage easily' and keep immobilisation as an asserted effect.
options.changes: Smallest edit; leaves the movement clause unexplained and the Mechanism still over-claiming.

quote_a: At the required C-Grade output, the lock resists roughly 0.1 to 0.3 gigantonewtons of applied peak force, on the order of 7 megajoules to 1.046 gigajoules, before the bond parts, comparable to a small-building-level structural failure.
quote_b: Vitality (Fortitude) governs how much force the locked target's frame can take before the bond parts
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Sigillum Fixatio.md
why: The page states the constraint correctly in its FOW line and incorrectly in its Numerical Effect, two sections apart. A human femur fails in compression at 4-10 kN and a 5 cm² section of cortical bone parts at roughly 65 kN, so a lock rated at 0.1 GN is rated four orders of magnitude above the failure load of the body it is holding: long before the bond parts, the target has been torn apart and the lock is holding pieces. The figures themselves are Part Eleven's C row, which is a table of attack output - "Peak Force (N)" and "Energy Yield (J)" for a practitioner's expression - not a restraint rating, and the working performs no work on its target at all by its own Mechanism. The FOW line's reading is the physical one: what breaks is the frame, not the hold.

options.option: Delete the gigantonewton figure and state the FOW line's rule as the mechanic: the lock ends when the held frame fails, so its effective strength is the target's own Vitality Fortitude.
options.changes: Internally consistent and self-scaling - holding a stone pillar is stronger than holding a man; removes a number and replaces it with a stat reference the sheet already carries.

options.option: Keep a strength rating but derive it from something other than the attack-output table, with a stated basis.
options.changes: Needs a restraint or hold table the system does not have; would serve every binding working if written.

options.option: State that the lock also raises the target's frame strength for the duration, which is what Fixatio's Stat Effect on Vitality Fortitude would suggest.
options.changes: Makes the held target genuinely hard to damage and justifies the big number; contradicts SA-EM-FIXATIO-BARRIER-VS-ARMOUR's mechanism question rather than answering it, and makes the working a defensive buff.

options.option: Leave both readings on the page as a recorded disagreement in the source.
options.changes: Nothing mechanical; the page keeps two incompatible constraints and neither can be adjudicated.

quote_a: Path gate · None (the source's "Mind Path" is not a Path; it reads as Gnosis weighting)
quote_b: Fluency requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D and Stage III to exceed C, with its Command Weight component requiring Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page's reconciliation is right that Mind is not one of the Four Paths and wrong that the answer is None. Its own FOW line makes Gnosis Fluency load-bearing - "Gnosis (Fluency) governs the precision of the command that authorises the working" - and Fluency's Part Seven gate requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D. The working is C-Grade, which exceeds D, so a Path is required and the page declares none. The Command Weight clause happens to close, since at exactly C-Grade the C threshold is not exceeded, which means one Grade bracket of growth would fail a second gate on the same Sub-Stat. Resilience Anchoring is open and Vitality Fortitude closes at exactly C, so Fluency is the single failing gate.

options.option: Set the Path gate to Spirit.
options.changes: One line; opens Fluency at C and leaves Command Weight one bracket from its Attraction gate; consistent with a spoken command being the authorising act.

options.option: Drop Fluency from the FOW line and let Resilience Anchoring alone govern, since Anchoring is open to any Path.
options.changes: Keeps Path gate None; removes the command-precision component, so the working would need another account of what the spoken word does.

options.option: Lower the Grade requirement to D so Fluency's D threshold is not exceeded.
options.changes: Takes the working well below its stated force and energy band and below the Stage IV floor's usefulness; contradicts the Numerical Effect entirely.

options.option: Publish a rule for workings with no Path commitment at all, if the system intends such a category to exist.
options.changes: A general addition; the Four Paths page is explicit that commitment is recognised by the Crystal from behaviour rather than declared, so a genuine None may not be a possible state.

quote_a: on the order of 7 megajoules to 1.046 gigajoules
quote_b: | C | 101–175 | 0.1–0.3 GN | 20.92 MJ – 1.046 GJ | 0.005–0.25 t | Small Building to low Building |
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md
why: The page is quoting Part Eleven's C row and gets the ceiling, the force band and the real-world comparison exactly right while putting the floor at 7 MJ where the table says 20.92 MJ. The discrepancy is a factor of three and it matters at the bottom of the band, which is where a Stage IV working actually operates: 7 MJ sits inside the D row (15 kJ - 20.92 MJ), so as written the page's floor claims a D-Grade output for a C-Grade requirement. It is most likely a transcription slip rather than a design choice, but the rule is that a number is quoted or derived, and this one is neither.

options.option: Correct the floor to 20.92 MJ to match Part Eleven's C row.
options.changes: One number; the page then quotes the table exactly and the band is checkable.

options.option: Keep 7 MJ and state that the working spans the D-C boundary, with a reason.
options.changes: Requires the Grade requirement to read D-C rather than C; lowers the floor of what the lock can hold.

options.option: Delete the energy figure and keep the force figure, since the working performs no work on its target.
options.changes: Consistent with the Mechanism; removes a number that the account argues should not be there at all.

quote_a: A physical target is immobilised, its wounds stop worsening and stop healing, and it gains marked resistance to further physical alteration, not invincibility.
quote_b: Fixatio performs that cure on the target's present configuration. What it holds is not held by force. It is held because the alternative configuration has stopped being a reachable state.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Sigillum Fixatio.md
why: The stated mechanism raises the barrier to transitions out of the present configuration, and a barrier does not distinguish between kinds of chemistry. Everything a living target does is enzymatic catalysis - myosin ATPase, the sodium-potassium pump, oxidative phosphorylation, clotting cascades - and a cure that stops healing on those grounds stops circulation and respiration on the same grounds. The physical account therefore does not balance against a stratal account that describes a selective hold: either the barrier is universal, in which case a nine-second lock puts the target at the edge of the 6-10 second syncope interval without cerebral perfusion and a longer one is asphyxia rather than stasis, or the hold is selective, and the system states no rule anywhere for a barrier that rises for repair and not for heartbeat. The page names neither consequence.

options.option: Rule the hold universal and state the consequence: a held body is a body not breathing, so duration is bounded by physiology and a long hold is lethal.
options.changes: Makes the working far darker and gives its nine seconds a reason; adds a real moral weight to using it on an ally, which the Counter line's 'in the rare case a caster invites it' hints at.

options.option: Rule the hold selective and publish the basis: the cure fixes configuration at the structural layer and leaves metabolic cycles running, with a stated boundary between the two.
options.changes: Keeps the working clean; requires a system-level distinction between structural and metabolic state that no page currently draws, and that would apply to every stasis working.

options.option: Restrict the working to non-living targets and active workings, which is where its mechanism is unambiguous.
options.changes: Removes the immobilisation-of-a-person use entirely; the technique becomes an anti-working and anti-ward tool, which its Lock-form reading already suits.

options.option: Leave undecided.
options.changes: Nothing; the physical and stratal accounts stay unbalanced on a working whose whole content is what it stops.

quote_a: They absorb strain, moral weight, and impact, hold it under Fixatio's cure until intention and conviction align, and then release it once, as a single act that does not reverse
quote_b: Efficiency is the ratio of Essence spent to effect that arrives. The remainder leaves as heat, sound, and structural bleed, which is why a low-efficiency practitioner is loud, warm, and easy to find, and why the highest Bands run quiet.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md:35
why: The system prices efficiency at the moment of spending and states no rule for a working that HOLDS a charge between the spend and the effect. This discipline is defined by that interval. At Stage VII the eta band is 0.60-0.70 (Part Nineteen's Tier 5 row as corrected by R44-4), so filling a store to the bottom of the Stage's own A-Grade output band (46 GJ, Part Eleven) puts roughly 25 GJ of waste heat somewhere, and the physical account cannot be closed until the system says where and when. If the bleed is paid once at the fill, an 80 kg practitioner absorbs 25 GJ against a body whose whole margin to a lethal core temperature is about 1.2 MJ, which is still four orders of magnitude fatal. If it is paid continuously while held, the store is a beacon and a long hold is self-cooking, and the page's central image of a knight bearing weight undramatically for hours cannot happen. If it is paid at the release, the store is a lossless battery, which no other working in the corpus is allowed to be. The page's own stealth logic needs the third answer and its physiology needs none of them.

options.option: Rule that a held store bleeds nothing and the (1 - eta) loss is charged in full at the release, making a Fixatio-cured store the one lossless reservoir the system allows, with the cure itself as the stated reason.
options.changes: Keeps the discipline's silent hold and its stealth, and makes the release the loud event; creates a general precedent that any Fixatio-anchored store is loss-free, which every barrier working in the corpus could then claim.

options.option: Rule that a held store bleeds at a stated rate per unit time, so capacity is bounded by how long a man can carry it rather than by the Mercy Lamina alone.
options.changes: Gives the page the duration figure it is missing and makes the Strain Lamina a race; makes the knight thermally visible while charged, which turns the account's real tell (a man taking blows without reacting) into a detectable signature and weakens the ambush use.

options.option: Rule the fill-time bleed vented into the anchor rather than the body: the gesture-keys (shield, brand, ground) are the heat sink, and the anchor degrades.
options.changes: Explains why a Stage VII working keeps an external anchor it had earned the right to drop, and makes a cracked brand or a warped shield the tell; requires a rule for anchor failure that the system does not currently have.

options.option: Leave it open and mark the discipline unpriceable until the Essence Ledger settles the general storage case, since no working in the corpus states one.
options.changes: Blocks any numeric statement about this discipline and about every other store-then-release working; keeps the corpus honest at the cost of leaving a whole family of workings uncosted.

quote_a: **Temperance Signature** · Stage VII, Refraction, through Stage X, Realization (Bands C through A).
quote_b: **Grade range** · A-Grade at Stage VII's ceiling to S-Grade at Stage X's, tracking the Stage range directly rather than a separately invented tier label.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Solarbound Aegoric Knight.md:25
why: A Stage range and a Grade letter are the only quantities the page states. It gives no range, no duration, no store capacity, no release figure, no EU cost, no Flux Density and no AU/s, and it names no practitioner, so no card can supply them either. Every figure in this account's ledger is therefore derived from the Grade letter through Part Eleven and nothing else: the implied output band 46 GJ to 4.184 TJ at A rising to 4.184 to 24.3 TJ at S, and an implied store density of 575 MJ/kg to 304 GJ/kg in an 80 kg frame. That derivation exposes the gap rather than filling it, because it also shows the absorbed side is about 1e5 J in a hard day, six orders below the release. The system has no rule that converts a Stage into EU, so the store cannot be priced even in principle, and the page's Cannot list (one release per cycle, no partial spend) governs a quantity that has never been stated.

options.option: State the four missing figures on the page: store capacity, fill time, hold duration and release yield, chosen inside the A-to-S band Part Eleven already implies.
options.changes: Makes the discipline costable and its Cannot list enforceable; fixes the output at a number that then has to survive the storage-bleed ruling, since the two questions are the same arithmetic.

options.option: Rule that the release yield is not a free figure but equals what was absorbed times a stated multiplier, so the Strain Lamina's input governs the output.
options.changes: Closes the six-order gap between absorbed strain (about 1e5 J) and Grade-band release (1e10 J and up) by making the multiplier the thing under scrutiny; reframes the discipline as an amplifier rather than a battery and puts the energy question onto the Oath Lamina.

options.option: Rule that Grade letters alone are a sufficient statement for a discipline page and that Part Eleven's band IS the number, with no page-level figures required.
options.changes: Legitimises every other technique page that states only a Grade, and makes Part Eleven load-bearing for costing across the corpus; leaves duration and capacity still unstated because Part Eleven prices output, not storage.

options.option: Mark the page incomplete and hold it out of the costed set until a practitioner card exists to anchor the figures.
options.changes: Keeps the ledger clean and makes the discipline unusable in a scene with numbers in it; defers the work to whenever a knight of this discipline is written.

quote_a: **Category** · Domain Weaving is the discipline's apex expression, the deliberate reshaping of local Continuum behaviour so a chosen law (here: things that are sworn, do not break) becomes easier to sustain.
quote_b: **Breadth** requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B, and Stage V to exceed A where several Wellsprings are layered inside one working.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:134
why: The page states no Path anywhere, and three separate system gates require one. Domain Weaving's alignment is Attraction (the row '| **Domain Weaving** | Attraction |' at wiki/Disciplines/The Disciplines.md:61), and the page calls Domain Weaving the discipline's apex expression. Part Seven's Breadth clause gates a working that layers several Wellsprings on Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B and Stage V to exceed A, and this working layers three - Fixatio, Benediction and Judicium - at A rising to S. The seated-Domain clause runs into Dominion Radius and Gravity, both Attraction-gated at Stage V-VI. So a practitioner without Attraction Path cannot reach the page's own stated Grade range, and the system gives no default Path for a discipline page that omits one: it does not say the alignment is implied, and it does not say an unstated Path is any Path.

options.option: State Attraction Path on the page, at the Stage the highest of the three gates demands, and let the Grade range follow from it.
options.changes: Makes the page consistent with Part Seven, The Disciplines and Dominion at once, and narrows who can run the discipline; adds a real gate a player can look up and a real disqualification for a knight built on Spirit or Fate.

options.option: Rule generally that a discipline page's Category implies its Path alignment from The Disciplines table unless it says otherwise.
options.changes: Fills this gap and the same gap on every other technique page that omits a Path, at the cost of silently assigning Paths to workings nobody has reviewed.

options.option: Reduce the claim: drop Domain Weaving as the apex expression and keep the discipline purely Traitus, so no Attraction gate applies.
options.changes: Removes the seated-Domain clause and the socially-binding ground with it, which is the page's most distinctive claim; leaves the Breadth clause still biting on three layered Wellsprings.

options.option: Rule that the Breadth clause counts harmonized Families rather than Wellsprings, so a three-Wellspring working inside three Families is gated differently.
options.changes: Changes how every multi-Wellspring working in the corpus is gated, not just this one; needs Part Seven rewritten and the Tempering Capacity ceiling restated.

quote_a: once a full Domain is seated, make the surrounding ground resist breaking, structurally and socially, for as long as the practitioner's pulse holds it
quote_b: Deliberate reshaping of local Continuum behaviour so that a chosen law becomes easier to sustain within a defined space.
path_b: wiki/Disciplines/The Disciplines.md:61
why: Structural resistance is a physical claim and the system can price it: a raised barrier to fracture, in joules per square metre of new crack surface, against a stated area. The social half has no referent anywhere in the system. Domain Weaving reshapes local Continuum behaviour so a chosen law is easier to sustain, and the page's chosen law is 'things that are sworn, do not break' - but the system states no rule for whether a promise, a truce or a line of soldiers is a law the Continuum tracks, no quantity that would be raised, no resistance for a mind inside the Domain, and no tell that a person is being held. The Nightglass Seal account found that purpose IS tracked (Attraction Force, the Authorization glyph role, the warrant), which makes this the nearer question rather than a settled one: those three price a practitioner's own intent, not a bystander's. Without a rule, 'resist breaking socially' reads either as mind control with no stated counter, which the fairness check cannot pass, or as flavour on a structural effect, in which case the page's most distinctive clause does nothing.

options.option: Rule the social half real and price it, with the quantity raised, who gets to resist, the resistance route and the tell all stated.
options.changes: Creates the system's first rule for a Domain acting on choices rather than matter, which every Attraction working could then reach for; needs a Counterplay route written at the same time or the discipline fails the fairness check.

options.option: Rule the social half descriptive: the Domain raises the structural barrier only, and men hold because the ground holds and they can see it holding.
options.changes: Keeps the imagery, costs nothing new, and makes the effect entirely physical and entirely counterable; removes the page's boldest claim and with it the reason the discipline is Judicium-tertiary at all.

options.option: Route the social half through the existing vow machinery: it binds only those who have sworn to the practitioner's cause, and binds them to terms they chose.
options.changes: Makes the effect consensual and therefore fair without a new resistance rule, and makes the Oath Lamina the gate on both halves; means the Domain does nothing to an enemy, which changes how the discipline is used in a line of battle.

options.option: Leave it open and mark the seated-Domain clause unpriced pending a general ruling on whether the Continuum tracks obligations between persons.
options.changes: Blocks the discipline's apex tier from appearing in a scene with stakes; leaves the same question standing for every working that claims a social effect.

quote_a: which frays the Crownforge spiral symmetry the working depends on and must be re-centred by hand rather than shrugged off
quote_b: **Counter**  [Uur] Disruption breaks the lattice mid-formation. The sudden phase change back to soft tissue is its own kind of trauma, and the reversal is frequently worse than the completed conversion would have been.
path_b: wiki/The Fourteen Titans/The Physical Order — Atla'zon and Gaia.md:85
why: The line makes the Crownforge spiral symmetry the thing the working depends on, and names [Uur] Disruption as the discipline's one unanswerable counter precisely because it frays that symmetry. The counter is attested: [Uur] Disruption is Root - Uurgath (wiki/Artifacts/Banisher - Writ-Spear of Exile.md:42), it is an Associated Glyph of Chaos (wiki/The Fourteen Archons/The Primordial Dyad - Order and Chaos.md:48), and the quoted line shows what it does to a lattice mid-formation. The thing it acts on is not attested at all. 'Crownforge' and 'spiral symmetry' each occur exactly once in the corpus, both in this one sentence: no entry in the Master Glyph Index, none among the sixty Wellsprings, none in the Eight Families, no Trait, no place, no school. So the page's only stated weakness is anchored on an unfindable proper noun, and a player told to look it up finds this sentence and stops. Either the symmetry is a real structure with a real geometry, in which case it is load-bearing for the mechanism and needs a register entry, or it is this Shell's name for its own lattice, in which case the counter should be stated against the lattice - where the Titans page already states it - and not against a word with no entry.

options.option: Register Crownforge as a named lattice geometry, with its symmetry stated, and let [Uur] Disruption's effect on it follow from the geometry.
options.changes: Gives the page's one named counter something a player can actually look up and reason about, and creates a structure other Materia workings can reference; adds a register entry that then has to be consistent with Fixatio's anchoring.

options.option: Drop the proper noun and state the counter against the Shell's lattice directly: Disruption frays any anchored lattice mid-formation, and this one must be re-centred by hand.
options.changes: Removes an unattested term at no cost to the mechanism and keeps the counter findable through [Uur] Disruption's own entry; loses a piece of flavour that reads as if it belonged to a school.

options.option: Attach Crownforge to an existing in-world school or smithing tradition and make the term that school's name for the geometry, correct or not.
options.changes: Turns an orphan term into a lookup trail through a culture page, which is the kind of hook the addendum asks for; requires naming or using a culture, which this pass is not allowed to invent.

options.option: Leave the term and log it as flavour with no mechanical weight, stating that the counter operates on the lattice regardless of what it is called.
options.changes: Costs nothing and keeps the line; leaves the page's stated weakness resting on a word with no entry, which is the thing a player would try hardest to look up.

quote_a: **Path gate** · Spirit Path.
quote_b: **Cascade** requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B for spread, Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed S for range. **Overchannel** open, carrying inherent Overflow risk above D-Grade and Backlash risk above C, with no Path providing structural protection; recovery of rebound as usable output requires Body Path at Stage V to exceed B. **Density** requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B, with inscription and glyph-chain durability requiring Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:123
why: The page declares Spirit Path and nothing else, and its own four Sub-Stats are 'Gnosis Cognition, Gnosis Retention, Ardency Cascade, Ardency Density'. Two of the four are gated on Paths the page does not declare. Ardency Cascade requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B; Ardency Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B. The page's stated Grade is 'A-Grade, with a late push toward S-Grade', which exceeds B on both, so both gates bite. The two Gnosis Sub-Stats close cleanly on Spirit - Retention requires Spirit at Stage II to exceed D and Stage VI to exceed A, and Cognition is open with a Spirit clause at Stage IV - so the page's Path declaration is correct for half its architecture and silent about the other half. The Claustra register adds a third request for the same Path the page omits: Claustra 'sits between Spirit and Attraction because the seal's syntax is Soul Plane precision while its duration is a Fate-side claim that must be renewed by something'. Either the working runs at B and below, or it needs Attraction and Body declared, or two of its Sub-Stats are the wrong ones.

options.option: Declare Attraction and Body alongside Spirit at the Stages Part Seven demands, and state which Path carries which Sub-Stat.
options.changes: Makes the page legal at A and S and makes it a three-Path working, which is a heavy build and narrows who can run it to almost nobody; collides immediately with the author's own card, which carries neither Path (see SA-CROSS-SOMNIUM-SERENYRA-PATH).

options.option: Cap the working at B-Grade, where neither Attraction nor Body is required, and restate its range and duration for B.
options.changes: Keeps the single Spirit Path gate and the author's card intact; drops the working two Grades, which means the 200 m range and the three-exchange hold both have to come down, and removes the 'late push toward S' the page is built around.

options.option: Replace the two Ardency Sub-Stats with Sub-Stats that are Spirit-gated or open, and rebuild the construct's solidity on those.
options.changes: Preserves Grade and Path together, but breaks the clean derivation from the two Wellspring registers - Ardency Cascade and Density are exactly what Oneirion and Eidolyn strengthen once the Merge Ledger is applied - so the page would state Sub-Stats its own Wellsprings do not support.

options.option: Rule that a Sub-Stat strengthened by a harmonized Wellspring is exempt from its Part Seven Path gate.
options.changes: Fixes this page and roughly a dozen others in the batch at a stroke, and guts Part Seven: every Path gate in the system becomes optional for anyone harmonized to the right Wellspring, which is most practitioners.

quote_a: **Grade required** · A-Grade, with a late push toward S-Grade.
quote_b: **Path** · **Spirit dominant, Fate secondary.** *The card's own progression is Spirit → Mind → Fate; Mind is struck as Choir vocabulary and not one of the four, and the stated destination, Fate, is committed as her secondary — memory and emotional signature used to forecast the state of Wellsprings.*
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Serenyra Vaelith · The Archmagus of the Grove-Spired Crown.md:73
why: Somnium Scriptorium is Serenyra Vaelith's own working - the page says the source gives 'no date or founding problem beyond Serenyra's own authorship'. Her card commits her to Spirit dominant and Fate secondary, and to nothing else: 'The Fate Path routes no force here; it is a reading, not a weapon.' She therefore has neither Attraction Path nor Body Path at any weight. Ardency Cascade needs Attraction at Stage IV to exceed B and Ardency Density needs Body at Stage IV to exceed B (Part Seven), so on the system's own arithmetic the author of this technique cannot run it above B-Grade, while the page requires A with a push to S. This is not a marginal miss: it is two of the four Sub-Stats the working is built on, gated on the two Paths she does not have, on a sheet that says so explicitly. Nothing else on her sheet fails - Stage VIII, Grade S ceiling 550, eta ~0.70 inside the Tier 6 band, Crystal State Refined all check clean - which makes the Path line the single load-bearing contradiction.

options.option: Add Attraction or Body to her card at the weight the gates need.
options.changes: Legalises her signature working and changes her character: the card's whole Path note argues she is a reader rather than a projector, and 'the Fate Path routes no force here' is written as characterisation, not bookkeeping.

options.option: Rebuild the technique on Spirit-gated and open Sub-Stats only, so its author can run it.
options.changes: Keeps her card and her voice; costs the page its derivation from the Oneirion and Eidolyn registers, and probably costs the construct its stated solidity, which is the Ardency Density clause.

options.option: Cap the working at B-Grade and treat the A-to-S line as a later practitioner's extension rather than hers.
options.changes: Resolves the contradiction without touching either sheet and gives the discipline a history - a stronger, differently-Pathed successor - but means the page's own numbers describe a working its author never performed.

options.option: Rule that a practitioner running a self-authored working is gated on their own Path only where the working's governing Wellspring names that Sub-Stat.
options.changes: Narrow enough to fix this page, and sets a precedent that self-derived techniques are cheaper to gate than taught ones, which inverts the Counterplay register's position that self-derived techniques are the harder problem.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Effective to 200 metres, line-of-sight required.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · A mechanical system's every possible arrangement is a coordinate in a space that has no physical location, and the system's evolution is a trajectory through it. Oneirion lets a working act on that manifold rather than on the room. This is the mechanical reason Oneirion techniques reach targets no line of sight connects, and the reason they are so difficult to describe afterward.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:50
why: The governing Wellspring's Core Law states line-of-sight independence as the mechanical consequence of its own analogue, and names it as such: a configuration-space trajectory has no physical location, so there is nothing for a sightline to be a condition on. The technique page requires line of sight outright. Both cannot be read literally. The page's own Trigger suggests where the real constraint might live - 'an inscribed glyph that successfully anchors to a target's psyche, usually accompanied by speaking the target's name or true title' - because a spoken name needs the target to be within earshot, which is a far tighter and more interesting condition than sight and produces different counters (a wall does not stop it, a loud room does). As written, the page imports a physical-space restriction into a working whose Wellspring exists specifically to escape physical space.

options.option: Drop line-of-sight and keep the 200 m as an addressing range, consistent with Oneirion's stated law.
options.changes: Makes the working far stronger and much harder to hide from - it reaches through walls - and shifts every counter onto the anchor rather than onto cover; the Counterplay 'Deny the Field' and 'Knot and Lock' routes carry the load instead of a sightline.

options.option: Replace line-of-sight with earshot, on the page's own Trigger: the anchor is a spoken name, so the target must be able to be named at him.
options.changes: Keeps a real limit and makes it the right one, so noise becomes a counter and cover does not; sharpens the tell, since the working must announce its target aloud; leaves the 200 m figure needing a reason, because 200 m is not an earshot.

options.option: Keep line-of-sight and state the reason it applies here when the register says it should not - the anchor is inscribed in the air and must be inscribed where he is.
options.changes: Preserves the page and makes this working a stated exception to its own Wellspring's law, which needs the exception written into the register or it reads as an error.

options.option: Amend the Oneirion register instead, if line-of-sight independence is not meant to be general.
options.changes: Touches every Oneirion working in the corpus rather than this one page; the clause is currently the register's explanation for why Oneirion techniques are hard to describe afterward, so removing it costs the amnesia its stated cause.

quote_a: **Craft** · Spellcraft, spoken (a glyph inscribed in the air, anchored by naming the target).
quote_b: **Law V, the Law of Material Anchor, is a Stage gate rather than a universal.** Below **Stage VII, Refraction**, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary. At Refraction the practitioner can hold the Crystal as an object of study, and the Glyph Roles compress into an internal chain that needs no material anchor at all. *This is why internalised Spellcraft reads as a mark of rank rather than a technique, and why a man who casts silently in a room has told everyone present his Stage without saying a number*
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md:201
why: The working's stage floor is Stage VII, Refraction, and its practitioner is Stage VIII, so by Law V neither of them needs an external anchor at all - and the page gives it two, a spoken name and a glyph inscribed in the air. The consequence is a counter the system says should not exist at this Stage. The Counterplay register: 'Take the anchor and the sentence does not complete. Break his wrist and a gestured chain is finished. Put a hand over his mouth and a spoken one is. Above Refraction the chain is internal and none of this applies, which is the practical reason Stage VII is the line every soldier is taught to fear.' So the cheapest counter in the register is supposed to stop working at exactly this working's floor, and this page hands it back. The Four Crafts clause also makes it a status claim in reverse: silent casting is the mark of rank, so a Stage VIII practitioner casting aloud is either concealing her Stage or has not internalised a working she is entitled to internalise. Either reading is a fact about her worth stating, and the page states neither.

options.option: Internalise the working: no spoken name, no air-inscription, an internal chain as Law V allows at her Stage.
options.changes: Removes the 'hand over the mouth' counter and the loudest tell at once, making the working much more dangerous and much harder to detect; leaves the anchor question open, since a Claustra seal still needs something to renew against.

options.option: Keep the spoken anchor and state why she chooses it - precision on the target, or a deliberate warning she is unwilling to drop.
options.changes: Turns a rules mismatch into characterisation and keeps the counter findable, which is the fair-play outcome; needs one line on the page, and makes the choice itself a thing an opponent can rely on.

options.option: Lower the stage floor below Refraction so the external anchor is required rather than retained.
options.changes: Makes the Craft line correct by construction and puts the working within reach of far more practitioners; contradicts the Grade range and the Sub-Stat ceilings the page depends on.

options.option: Rule that a Claustra working keeps an external anchor at every Stage, because a seal's duration is a claim that must be renewed against something outside the practitioner.
options.changes: Gives Law V a stated exception with a reason, and applies to every Claustra working in the corpus - Sigillum Fixatio, Bastion Imperium, Archivium Locus, The Aether Bastion - each of which would then carry the anchor counter permanently.

quote_a: Holds up to roughly three exchanges of real time; subjective time inside the construct can run far longer, though the source gives no ratio and none is invented here.
quote_b: **What nobody knows** · Why some targets remember every page of what happened inside and others wake with no memory the dream occurred at all.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Somnium Scriptorium.md:27
why: The page is correct to refuse to invent a ratio, and the refusal leaves a quantity the working cannot function without: how much can actually be said and done inside nine or fifteen seconds. The two quoted lines are one question. Real temporal psychology does not permit subjective dilation as a change of clock rate - the free-fall chronometer result is that reported duration stretches by about a third while temporal resolution does not improve at all, so the dilation is a duration judgement reconstructed from how much was encoded. On that reading total recall and total amnesia are the two ends of one dial, which answers the page's 'What nobody knows' from its own physics, and it also means the ratio is not a free parameter: it is whatever the encoding rate was. The system has no rule for either quantity. Compounding it, the three exchanges are themselves ambiguous by 1.67x under the two live turn conventions (SA-GAP-TURN-LENGTH), so the working's real duration is indeterminate twice over.

options.option: State a ratio on the page and let the memory outcome follow from it, with a stated range rather than a single figure.
options.changes: Makes an interrogation scene writable and bounds what a confession can contain; fixes the amnesia as a consequence rather than a mystery, which closes the page's own open question and removes a hook.

options.option: Rule that subjective duration is not a ratio but a function of encoding, so a target who remembers everything experienced a long dream and a target who remembers nothing experienced no duration at all.
options.changes: Answers both quoted lines with one mechanic and ties the working's usefulness to a variable the practitioner cannot fully control; means she cannot know in advance whether the interrogation will be recoverable, which cuts both ways and is the more interesting version.

options.option: Set no ratio and bound the working by content instead: a stated maximum of what can be established inside one use, in questions rather than seconds.
options.changes: Sidesteps the physics and gives the table something usable; leaves the system without a general rule for subjective time, which the next dream working will need.

options.option: Leave it open and mark every dream-space duration in the corpus unpriced until a general ruling lands.
options.changes: Keeps the corpus honest and blocks the Oneirion workings from appearing with numbers; the turn-length ambiguity would still have to be settled separately.

quote_a: **Stat Affinity** · *Gnosis (Warding, Retention, Cognition, Memorium, Diagnosis) · Resilience (Coherence, Severance, Nullity, Persistence, Continuity) · Harmonics (Recovery, Fidelity, Suppression, Stability, Memory) · Dominion (Reach, Sovereignty, Sense, Gravity)*
path_a: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:15
quote_b: **Stat Effect** · Strengthens Gnosis Cognition, Dominion Reach, Ardency Spectral. Workings operate through conceptual space, not only physical space.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:51
why: Limina's Family-level Stat Affinity names four Primaries and Ardency is not among them. Two of Limina's own Wellsprings strengthen Ardency Sub-Stats in their Stat Effect lines on the same page: Oneirion strengthens 'Ardency Spectral' and Eidolyn strengthens 'Ardency Density in summoned constructs, Ardency Inscription'. Applying the Merge Ledger those are Ardency Cascade and Ardency Density, which are two of the four Sub-Stats Somnium Scriptorium runs on, and the page's FOW line makes Ardency its secondary Primary outright: 'Governing Primary - Gnosis, with Ardency secondary.' So a technique built correctly from two Limina registers ends up with a Primary the Family says it does not have an affinity for. This matters beyond one page, because the affinity line is what a player would consult to work out whether a build is coherent, and here it contradicts the Wellspring entries three dozen lines below it.

options.option: Add Ardency to Limina's Stat Affinity, naming the Sub-Stats its own Wellsprings strengthen.
options.changes: Makes the Family line agree with its entries and legitimises Ardency-secondary Limina builds; widens the largest Family further, which the page already calls the largest.

options.option: Rule that Stat Affinity lists a Family's characteristic Primaries rather than an exhaustive set, and that a Wellspring's own Stat Effect governs.
options.changes: Fixes this and any similar mismatch across all eight Families without editing them, and makes the affinity lines advisory, so they stop being usable as a build check.

options.option: Amend the two Wellspring Stat Effect lines to name Sub-Stats inside Limina's stated affinity.
options.changes: Keeps the Family line authoritative; removes the register basis for this page's Ardency Sub-Stats and therefore for the construct's stated solidity, and would ripple into every technique built on Oneirion or Eidolyn.

options.option: Leave both and log the affinity lines as a known approximation across the Families pages.
options.changes: Costs nothing now; leaves a contradiction on the page a player is most likely to use for build-checking, which is the worst place to leave one.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Effective to 200 metres, line-of-sight required.
quote_b: Physical Force is the umbrella measurement for every form of mechanically expressed destructive, resistive, or manipulative output a character can produce through bodily action, Essence-reinforced technique, or Aetheric projection converted into kinetic effect. Five facets: **Strike Force**, destructive energy delivered per attack; **Durability**, capacity to absorb, deflect or endure incoming energy without structural failure; **Lifting Strength**, sustained force applied against gravitational or structural resistance; **Range**, the spatial envelope across which force remains coherent; and **Aura Pressure**, the passive force a character's presence exerts on their environment.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md:17
why: Part Eleven does ladder range against Grade, in 'Range and Force Coherence': Projected Force Range at 50% yield runs 100-200 m at C, 0.5-1 km at B, 3-8 km at A, 20-50 km at S, 300-800 km at SS and 'Planetary' at SSS. So there is a ladder, and any working that states a range in metres can be checked against it - provided the ladder governs that working. The quoted definition is the limit: the table prices Physical Force, 'every form of mechanically expressed destructive, resistive, or manipulative output', and Range is defined inside it as 'the spatial envelope across which force remains coherent'. A great many technique pages state a reach that is not an envelope of force at all: Somnium Scriptorium's 200 m is an addressing range for a working whose whole physical account is that it expends no energy and moves nothing; an Edict's 200 m is an authority radius; a dream anchor's reach is a claim on a psyche. For those the system supplies no ladder, and reading Part Eleven onto them produces a false failure - a working that expresses no force is not 'below band' for force. The gap is therefore narrower and more awkward than a missing table: the one ladder that exists is the wrong instrument for the pages that most often state a range, and nothing says so.

options.option: Rule that Part Eleven's Range ladder governs every stated range regardless of whether the working expresses force.
options.changes: Makes every range figure in the corpus immediately checkable and puts a great many of them far out of band - Somnium's 200 m becomes a C-Grade range on an A-to-S working - so the ruling would be followed by a large number of number conflicts.

options.option: Publish a second ladder for non-force reach: addressing range, authority radius, and anchor reach, laddered against Grade or against the Sub-Stat that carries it.
options.changes: Closes the gap properly and gives players a lookup for 'can he reach me' on the many workings that are not attacks; a real writing job, and the new ladder's numbers would then have to be reconciled with the ranges pages already state.

options.option: Rule that the reach of a non-force working is governed by the Sub-Stat carrying it - Dominion Radius, Dominion Sovereignty, Ardency Cascade's range clause - and price it per Sub-Stat rather than per Grade.
options.changes: Most faithful to how the pages actually work, since different workings reach by different means; leaves any page that names no reaching Sub-Stat still unpriceable, and Ardency Cascade currently gates range without quantifying it.

options.option: State explicitly that non-force reach is a free narrative parameter outside the band checks.
options.changes: Legitimises the current spread at no cost and permanently removes one of the five fairness tests from most non-attack workings, so a 15 m working and a 5 km one are equally in band by definition.

quote_a: **Cost** · Empathic residue clings to her after use, carrying fragments of the target's fear or grief home with her. Sustaining both the real-world and dream-space presence simultaneously exhausts her faster than single-space work.
quote_b: **Waiting for the cost.** Costs are real and they are rarely due inside a scene. *A plan that consists of surviving until he tires is a plan to be killed by a tired man.*
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md:68
why: Both stated costs settle after the fighting. Empathic residue 'clings to her after use' and carries home with her; faster exhaustion is a rate, not a price, and the working lasts nine or fifteen seconds. The Counterplay register files that pattern under What Does Not Work by name, so as written this working's cost is one an opponent cannot use, which is the fairness test the brief asks about. The physics supplies the cost the page is missing and it is a better one. Two tasks that both need a central decision stage are not run in parallel; the second is postponed by roughly the duration of the first's central stage, on the order of 200-500 ms. A practitioner holding a room and a construct at once is therefore not tiring, she is interleaving - a few hundred milliseconds late to everything in front of her, at every switch. That is due immediately, it is visible, and it is exploitable by somebody standing next to her, which is exactly what a cost is supposed to be. The page does not state it. Every other fairness test on this page passes, and two of them handsomely: the tells are enormous (she must say his name aloud, and he stands still upright and breathing), and the limits are stated honestly including two the page admits it cannot answer.

options.option: State the in-scene cost as reaction lag: while the construct is held she is a stated fraction of a beat late to everything in the room.
options.changes: Gives an opponent a usable opening and gives an ally a reason to guard her, which is how the working should read at a table; makes solo use genuinely dangerous and turns the technique into a two-person move.

options.option: Keep the stated costs and add a hard concurrency limit instead: she cannot act in the room at all while the chamber is held.
options.changes: Blunter and cleaner than a lag figure, and makes the Counter line ('breaking her concentration ejects both of them, violently') the central risk rather than a footnote; removes any version of the working used mid-fight.

options.option: Price the empathic residue so it bites within the scene - a stated penalty on the next working, not just a mood carried home.
options.changes: Converts existing flavour into a real cost without inventing a new mechanic; needs a quantity, which means it runs into the absence of an EU formula.

options.option: Leave the cost as written and accept that this working's price is narrative rather than tactical.
options.changes: Costs nothing and leaves one of the five fairness checks failed on a working whose tells and limits otherwise pass well; the Counterplay register's own text then reads as a criticism of this page.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · The real phenomenon underneath is measurement collapse: a system genuinely undetermined among several outcomes resolves to exactly one only when read, and the working forces that read to happen at a moment and along a vector Opalis chooses, in the same way a prism decides which color exits toward the target while creating none of the colors it separates.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · Nothing fails at its theoretical strength. Everything fails at a pre-existing flaw, because stress concentrates at a crack tip in proportion to the square root of the crack's length, and once that intensity exceeds the material's toughness the crack runs at a fraction of the speed of sound and does not stop. Fractura gives the practitioner sight of those flaws and the precision to load exactly one of them.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vectoria — Mechanics.md:22
why: The page names measurement collapse as 'the real phenomenon underneath', and measurement collapse does not apply: a body is not in a superposition of burned, crushed and dissolved, and macroscopic decoherence forecloses one on timescales far below any of the page's. Meanwhile the working's own primary Wellspring supplies the correct mechanism, quantitatively, and it describes the Lance better than the Lance's own Mechanism line does - 'sight of those flaws and the precision to load exactly one of them' is the technique in a clause. The physics is linear elastic fracture mechanics: K_I = sigma*sqrt(pi*a), failure when K_I reaches K_IC, so among a flaw population under one remote stress the longest crack reaches toughness first and the body fails there. The spread of competing failures is Weibull, P_f = 1 - exp[-(sigma/sigma_0)^m], and the effect is large and real: bulk soda-lime glass fails near 50 MPa while pristine fibre of the same composition reaches 3-7 GPa, two orders of magnitude from flaw population alone. That also makes the page's own stated Weakness correct - 'a structure anchored in pure Basilithe rejects the contradiction outright' is what a defect-free lattice does, and Basilithe's register is quartz-oscillator stiffness. Most tellingly the page states the right mechanism in the same sentence as the wrong one: a prism collapses nothing, every wavelength was already present, and dispersion selects by angle - which is exactly what the Master Glyph Index says a boundary condition may do.

options.option: Rewrite the Mechanism on Fractura's Core Law: the working selects the flaw with the highest stress intensity and loads it, and the prism analogy stands as selection rather than collapse.
options.changes: Makes the page's physics correct, quantitative and checkable, and hands players a real counter chain through Weibull scatter and the Basilithe anchor; costs the working its quantum framing, which is where its name and its mystique come from.

options.option: Keep measurement collapse and state what is genuinely superposed, so the claim has a referent.
options.changes: Preserves the page's language and requires the system to say what quantum state a body's manner of failure is in, and why decoherence does not resolve it; would be a new metaphysical commitment with consequences for every Fate-side working.

options.option: Split the two: Fractura's fault-reading is classical selection, and the Fate-side contribution is a separate claim about outcome weight, priced separately.
options.changes: Keeps both halves honest and makes the working two mechanisms rather than one, which the ten-Wellspring stack already suggests; needs the Fate-side half given its own limits and counters, since only the classical half currently has any.

options.option: Leave the page and record that its stated mechanism is a metaphor, with Fractura's law governing in any case where the two disagree.
options.changes: Cheapest, and leaves a page whose 'real phenomenon underneath' is explicitly not the real phenomenon, on a technique whose whole appeal is that it has one.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Range up to 900 m, single-target with a fractured echo along a line up to 40 m; at the required SSS-Grade the strike sits at the conservative low end of that Grade's benchmark, on the order of 1 PN of peak force and roughly 400 TJ of yield (low hundred-kiloton TNT-equivalent), an estimate chosen per Law Two since the card gives no force figure of its own. Resolution is instantaneous, with the harmonic disturbance it leaves lingering a few seconds afterward.
quote_b: **Mechanism** · A subsonic flame front that meets sufficient confinement and turbulence accelerates until the reaction couples to a shock wave and begins propagating faster than sound in the unreacted medium. The mechanism is a change of kind, not degree. Cataclysm makes that transition available to Essence expression, and blast radius thereafter scales with the cube root of yield, which is why the Wellspring's area effects widen coherently rather than merely spilling.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Caloria — Thermodynamics.md:64
why: The page delivers 400 TJ and confines the consequences to a 40 m line, and the two figures are not reconcilable. 400 TJ is 95.6 kt TNT-equivalent. Vaporising a 70 kg target outright costs roughly 1.5e8 J - about 15 MJ to bring it to boiling plus about 95 MJ of latent heat for its water - so the stated yield is around 2.7 million times the energy the stated effect requires, and the surplus cannot remain in a target that no longer exists. Cataclysm is one of the ten Wellsprings the page invokes, and its register forbids the containment in its own words: blast radius scales with the cube root of yield. Hopkinson-Cranz scaling puts severe overpressure near 7 km at 1 Mt, so at 0.0956 Mt it reaches about 3.2 km - eighty times the page's 40 m in radius, and roughly half a million times in enclosed volume. The conflict is sharpest because it is self-inflicted: the whole claim of this working is precision, one selected wound driven home, and 95 kt is the least precise quantity in the corpus. The system does offer a route the page never takes. Part Eleven's Essence-Typed Damage clause prices a Fractura strike on a pre-identified fault at 'thirty to fifty percent below the Shell's rated ceiling', which is the one clause that would let a selection working deliver far less raw yield than its Grade and still do the work.

options.option: Drop the yield by orders of magnitude and price the working on the Essence-Typed Damage discount instead: a small delivered force at exactly the right flaw, doing SSS work at SS or S energies.
options.changes: Makes the containment honest and the precision real, and makes the working genuinely distinct from every other SSS strike rather than a nuclear device with a story; puts the raw figure below the Grade's floor deliberately, so it needs the Part Eleven clause cited on the page to be legal.

options.option: Keep 400 TJ and state the real collateral: a multi-kilometre blast, and a practitioner at 900 m standing inside her own Cataclysm register's Reflected overpressure failure.
options.changes: Makes the page physically consistent and makes the working nearly unusable anywhere anyone lives, which is a strong characterisation; the 900 m range becomes suicidal, so range would have to rise toward the SSS band the page is already five Grades short of.

options.option: Route the working through Dissolution as its default rather than Cataclysm, since a dissolution runs downhill and releases no shock.
options.changes: Solves the containment at a stroke and keeps the yield figure as stored potential rather than delivered blast; changes what the working looks like in a scene from an explosion to a quiet coming-apart, and makes the Verdantia counter the primary one.

options.option: Rule that a selected-failure working deposits its yield entirely into the selected flaw with no coupling to the surrounding medium, and state that as a general exception.
options.changes: Preserves every number on the page and creates a general rule that fracture-selection workings do not obey blast scaling, which every Fractura and Cataclysm page could then invoke; needs a stated reason, because the register currently says the opposite.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Range up to 900 m, single-target with a fractured echo along a line up to 40 m; at the required SSS-Grade the strike sits at the conservative low end of that Grade's benchmark, on the order of 1 PN of peak force and roughly 400 TJ of yield (low hundred-kiloton TNT-equivalent), an estimate chosen per Law Two since the card gives no force figure of its own. Resolution is instantaneous, with the harmonic disturbance it leaves lingering a few seconds afterward.
quote_b: | SSS | 726–950 | 1–5 PN | 418 TJ – 4.184 ZJ | 100 kt – 1 Tt | Large Town to Small Country |
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md:43
why: The page requires SSS-Grade and states roughly 400 TJ of yield, describing it as 'the conservative low end of that Grade's benchmark'. The SSS floor is 418 TJ in Part Eleven's Strike Force table and 4.184e14 J in Part Four's attack-output column, which is the same figure. 400 TJ is 4.00e14 J, so it sits 4.3% below the floor, inside the SS band, and the working's stated Grade cannot produce it. The page's TNT figure has the same 4.3% error: it says 'low hundred-kiloton' while 400 TJ is 95.6 kt and the floor figure 418 TJ is 99.9 kt, which is where Part Eleven's '100 kt - 1 Tt' begins. The peak force figure by contrast is correct and at the floor: 1 PN is the bottom of the SSS row's 1-5 PN. This is the third page in the batch carrying the identical figure - Celestial Harmonic Shear and Harmonic Null-Ascension state 'on the order of 1 PN peak force and roughly 400 TJ yield' in the same sentence shape, citing the same nonexistent Law Two - so the number is copied boilerplate rather than a derivation, and correcting it once should correct it three times.

options.option: Raise the figure to 418 TJ on all three pages, the actual SSS floor, and keep the 'conservative low end' framing which then becomes true.
options.changes: An 18 TJ change that makes three pages legal at their stated Grade and costs nothing narratively; leaves the containment problem untouched and very slightly worse.

options.option: Cite Part Eleven's Essence-Typed Damage clause on the page and keep 400 TJ as raw yield with an effective yield 1.4x to 2x higher.
options.changes: Turns the defect into the page's best mechanic - a selection working legitimately under-delivers energy because it is aimed - and requires the clause quoted on the page; applies to Celestial Harmonic Shear too, which is also a fault-selection cut.

options.option: Lower the working's required Grade to SS, where 400 TJ sits comfortably inside 4.184e13 - 4.184e14 J.
options.changes: Makes the number correct by moving the Grade instead, and drops the Stage floor with it, which contradicts the page's Stage XII requirement and the Stage XII immunity clause built on it.

options.option: Rule that 'on the order of' language permits a stated figure within some tolerance of a band edge.
options.changes: Legalises all three pages and any other near-miss at a stroke; makes every band edge soft, which removes the band edges' function as the thing a Grade means.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Range up to 900 m, single-target with a fractured echo along a line up to 40 m; at the required SSS-Grade the strike sits at the conservative low end of that Grade's benchmark, on the order of 1 PN of peak force and roughly 400 TJ of yield (low hundred-kiloton TNT-equivalent), an estimate chosen per Law Two since the card gives no force figure of its own. Resolution is instantaneous, with the harmonic disturbance it leaves lingering a few seconds afterward.
quote_b: | SSS | 5–30 m | Planetary | Metaphysical law within 50 km |
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md:121
why: Part Eleven ladders Projected Force Range against Grade, at the distance where at least fifty percent of peak Strike Force is delivered: 100-200 m at C, 0.5-1 km at B, 3-8 km at A, 20-50 km at S, 300-800 km at SS, and Planetary at SSS. This working states 900 m. That is a B-Grade reach on an SSS-Grade working, five Grades below its own band, and the ladder unambiguously governs here because the page states a peak force in newtons and declares Family Vectoria with Physics Domain Mechanics - this is an expression of Physical Force by the table's own definition. The gap is not marginal: SSS Projected Force Range is not a number at all but the word 'Planetary', so the page is short by something like five orders of magnitude. It matters for counterplay rather than for flavour, because the Counterplay register's advice that 'Vectoria has to close' and that 'most practitioners are a threat about closing range and are written as though they were not' is true of this working as written and would be false of it in band.

options.option: Raise the range into the SSS band, or state it as unbounded by line of sight in the way Part Eleven's 'Planetary' implies.
options.changes: Makes the page consistent and makes Opalis a strategic rather than a tactical threat, which changes how any scene containing her is framed; removes distance as a counter entirely and throws the whole counterplay load onto the Basilithe and probability routes.

options.option: Keep 900 m and state why this working is range-limited when its Grade is not - the selection needs a resolved reading of the target's flaw population, which degrades with distance.
options.changes: Preserves the scene-scale working and gives the limit a mechanism worth looking up; makes fault-reading resolution a quantity the system would then need for other Fractura workings.

options.option: Rule Part Eleven's Range ladder a ceiling rather than a benchmark, so a working may state any range up to its Grade's figure.
options.changes: Legalises this page and most other stated ranges in the corpus at once; removes range from the band checks in the upward direction, so an SSS working with a 5 m reach would also be in band.

options.option: Reclassify the working as something other than an expression of Physical Force, so the ladder does not govern.
options.changes: Sidesteps the comparison and is hard to sustain, since the page states 1 PN of peak force and sits in Vectoria under Mechanics; would also remove the Strike Force table's authority over its yield, which is the only thing currently pricing it.

quote_a: - **Path gate** · Spirit Path
quote_b: **Penetration** requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed C. **Compression** open to any Path, scaling exponentially with Temperance Stage rather than Path commitment; concealment of a working's signature requires Attraction Path at Stage VII to exceed S. **Cascade** requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B for spread, Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed S for range.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:123
why: The page declares Spirit Path, and four independent parts of the system ask for Attraction or Body. Its own FOW line gives 'Ardency (Flux, Penetration, Cascade)': Flux is open to any Path, Penetration requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed C, and Cascade requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B for spread - and the 40 m echo line is spread. Part Seven's Harmonics Breadth clause requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed A 'where several Wellsprings are layered inside one working', and ten are layered here at SSS. The Vectra category sits 'Body <-> Attraction' and is described as 'fundamentally about where force goes'. The declaration is not simply wrong, which is what makes it worth ruling rather than correcting: Part Eleven's Path bonuses vindicate Spirit for delivery, since Spirit Path gives '+5% to +25%' to projected Strike Force and 'they hit hardest at range', which is exactly what a 900 m beam needs. So Spirit is the right Path for one of the working's five requirements and insufficient for the other four, and Opalis has no card against which any of it can be checked.

options.option: Declare all three Paths at the Stages the gates demand and accept that this is a three-Path working at the top of the register.
options.changes: Makes the page legal and makes the working nearly unique, which suits a Stage XII signature technique; cannot be verified against a practitioner until Opalis has a card, and a three-Path build may not be something the system intends to exist.

options.option: Reduce the working to what Spirit alone supports: drop the spread echo, drop the penetration claim, and reduce the Wellspring stack below the Breadth clause's threshold.
options.changes: Keeps a single clean Path gate and removes the 40 m echo, the penetration and most of the ten Wellsprings - which is most of what distinguishes the page.

options.option: Rule that a technique's Path gate names the Path that delivers the working, with the Sub-Stat gates governing the practitioner's sheet rather than the page.
options.changes: Reconciles this page and most other Path-gate conflicts in the batch by making the two statements answer different questions; requires the sheet-side check to be written somewhere, or the gates stop being checked at all.

options.option: Rule the Harmonics Breadth clause counts Families rather than Wellsprings, so five Families rather than ten Wellsprings is the quantity gated.
options.changes: Reduces one of the four requests and leaves three standing; changes how every multi-Wellspring working in the corpus is gated, and five Families would still cross the threshold here.

quote_a: **Effect** · A thrust or gesture sends a beam of black-gold refracted light out to 900 m; where it lands, it collapses every way the target could be hurt into the one that does the most damage and forces that wound to be the one that happens.
quote_b: | SSS | 2,997,925–29,979,246 m/s | entirely Essence-mediated | 1–5% c |
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:102
why: The page calls the working a beam of light and says 'Resolution is instantaneous'.
