Both are explicitly flagged by the page as estimates rather than derivations, which is honest and is also precisely what the batch may not carry forward: no formula anywhere in the system converts a Stage into an EU figure, so 5,000 is not conservative or unconservative, it is unanchored. The duration has two separate problems on top of that - no turn length is fixed anywhere in the corpus (SA-GAP-TURN-LENGTH), and 'Law Two' is cited on this page and three others as the authority for the only numbers they give and is defined nowhere in the corpus (SA-UNATT-LAW-TWO). The practical consequence is that the one cost this working states and the one duration it states both rest on nothing, on a page whose other numbers - radius, peak force, Grade - are quoted correctly from Part Eleven and Part Four.

options.option: Replace the figure with null and state the cost qualitatively until an EU formula exists.
options.changes: Consistent with the rest of the batch and with the page's own honesty; leaves the working with no quantified resource cost, so the fairness test rests entirely on the intent-divergence condition.

options.option: Publish an EU-by-Stage table, even a coarse one, and derive the figure from it.
options.changes: Closes SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA across the whole corpus and is the single highest-value missing table in this batch; every page that has estimated an EU cost would then have to be rechecked against it.

options.option: Price standing workings as a rate (EU per second) rather than a total, and state the rate.
options.changes: Correct for a working that is explicitly 'held open rather than fired' and makes duration and cost one decision instead of two; still needs an anchor for the rate.

options.option: Define Law Two, wherever it belongs, so the four pages citing it have an authority to cite.
options.changes: Closes SA-UNATT-LAW-TWO and whatever it settles here; does not by itself anchor the EU number, since Law Two is invoked on this page for the duration rather than the cost.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Incoming force below the S-Grade energy-yield ceiling (up to roughly 24.3 terajoules, per the Strike Force benchmarks for that Grade) is absorbed as a glancing structural event rather than a wound; force above that ceiling still gets through, since the hardening raises the failure threshold and does not remove one.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Four; and III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md, S row
why: The citation is correct and the consequence is not. Part Eleven's S-Grade ceiling is 2.42672x10^13 J, which the page quotes accurately as roughly 24.3 terajoules, and then asks a human body to receive it 'as a glancing structural event rather than a wound'. 24.3 TJ is 5,808 tonnes of TNT, 5.8 kilotons. Vaporising the practitioner outright costs about 2.5x10^8 J - heating 100 kg of water-like tissue from 310 K to 373 K is 2.6x10^7 J and the latent heat of vaporisation is 2.26x10^8 J - so the stated ceiling is about ninety-seven thousand times the energy needed to boil him away entirely. Taken as heat at a specific heat of 3,500 J/(kg K) it is a temperature rise of 6.9x10^7 K, the interior of a star. Taken as momentum, sqrt(2E/m) for 100 kg gives 6.97x10^5 m/s: Mach 2,030, or 0.23 percent of light speed. Note what is not wrong here: the page's framing is honest ('the hardening raises the failure threshold and does not remove one'), the Grade citation is exact, and the qualitative claim - that blunt force below some threshold becomes a structural event rather than a wound - is sound material physics. What fails is the location of the threshold, which the page inherits from Part Eleven's Grade band rather than choosing. This is the same failure as SA-PHYS-REPRISAL-YIELD-VS-STAGGER on the same practitioner, and it recurs wherever a page takes a Grade band's energy figure and describes a person surviving it.

options.option: State the absorption ceiling as a stress or a force rather than an energy, since a body fails at a stress: a figure in the hundreds of megapascals distributed is defensible, and an energy is not.
options.changes: Makes the working checkable against any described blow and brings it into line with what the material table actually supports; requires a convention for converting Part Eleven's joule bands into stresses, which the corpus does not have.

options.option: Lower the stated ceiling to what a stone-curve body can plausibly take and accept that it does not cover the top of S-Grade.
options.changes: Honest and costs the working its headline claim; the working becomes a defence against everything up to a point rather than against a Grade, which is arguably what a failure threshold is.

options.option: Rule generally that Part Eleven's energy bands are notional scale markers rather than joule figures to be conserved against.
options.changes: Would close a large class of rows across this batch at once - the Obelisk, the Lance, the Reprisal and this page all fail the same way - and would remove the corpus's only quantitative link between Grade and real force, which is the thing that makes any of these checks possible.

options.option: Keep the figure and state where the energy goes, naming a sink.
options.changes: Preserves the claim and requires the page to answer the question it currently skips; at 24.3 TJ no sink that leaves the practitioner in the scene is available, so this option is stated mainly so the ruling can say so.

quote_a: **Weakness** · Entropy fields and dissolution-type magics unmake the coagulated coherence directly rather than testing its failure threshold, which routes around the technique's entire premise; Sublimatio-adjacent workings that convert matter to a higher state without an intermediate stage are named on the card as a specific hazard for the same reason.
quote_b: **Effect** · Drakvor's own flesh stops behaving like flesh. Skin, bone, and the Essence running under both take on the failure curve of stone rather than the failure curve of a body, and blows that would open him instead ring off him.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/The Last Monolith.md:17
why: The Mechanism and Effect agree that the body takes on 'the failure curve of stone rather than the failure curve of a body'. That is a real and specific constitutive change, and it has a direction. Cortical bone runs roughly 170-200 MPa in compression and 120-150 MPa in tension, with a fracture toughness around 2-12 MPa*m^0.5 and a strain to failure of 1-3 percent. Granite runs roughly 130-250 MPa in compression - an even trade - and 7-25 MPa in tension, with a toughness of 0.5-2 MPa*m^0.5 and a strain to failure of 0.1-0.3 percent. So the exchange is: compression, no change; tension, about ten times weaker; toughness, about five times lower; strain to failure, about ten to twenty times lower. And a brittle solid has no plastic reserve, so it does not bruise or deform, it cracks, and a crack runs at 0.4-0.6 of the shear wave speed, 1,200-1,800 m/s in rock, which is faster than any reaction. The page's stated Weakness line names only entropy fields, dissolution magics and Sublimatio-adjacent workings. Every one of those is exotic. The weakness the stated mechanism actually produces is available to anyone holding a spear, a pick, a hook or a lever, because a thrust that wedges, a pull, a twist and a joint lock are all tension or shear. The register two files away states the principle without being asked: 'Masonry is enormously strong in compression and nearly worthless in tension, which is why the arch exists' (Petralon, Vectoria). The Effect line's 'blows that would open him instead ring off him' is correct and is a statement about crushing only.

options.option: Add tensile and shear loading to the Weakness line: thrusts, levers, joint locks and hooked weapons, with the material reason stated.
options.changes: Gives the working a counter an ordinary soldier can use and makes the state a real trade rather than a strict upgrade; substantially lowers the technique's power against mundane opposition, which is where it currently has none.

options.option: Narrow the Effect line so the hardening is explicitly compressive-only and says so.
options.changes: Same outcome by the other door and keeps the Weakness line short; makes the working read as armour rather than as transformation, which may be the more accurate description of it.

options.option: Add a second current whose register supplies tensile toughness, so the state is not purely brittle.
options.changes: Keeps the working strong and requires naming a current the page does not carry; the Materia register's options each bring their own Failure line, and the harmonisation count is already flagged on the card.

options.option: Rule that a Coagula hardening is isotropic in the system's terms and that the real-material tension asymmetry does not carry over.
options.changes: Closes the row by declaring the physical account out of scope for this working; conflicts with the standard the batch is written to, since the page's own Mechanism is stated in materials language and invites the comparison.

quote_a: **Wellspring** · Coagula (primary) · Judicium (secondary)
quote_b: **Monolithion**, the Enduring Monument. Strengthens Vitality Tolerance, Resilience Persistence, Dominion Gravity. Presence becomes geological.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/V. Wellsprings, Attraction and Obsession, Magic Integration (Parts Thirteen–Fifteen).md, Part Thirteen, Materia
why: The technique is called The Last Monolith. The Materia register contains a Wellspring called Monolithion, the Enduring Monument, whose entire gloss is 'Presence becomes geological' and which strengthens Vitality Tolerance, Resilience Persistence and Dominion Gravity - which is what a sustained held state costs and what it is for. The page declares Coagula and Judicium and not Monolithion. This is not automatically an error: the page's two declared currents supply its four governing Sub-Stats exactly and clear every Path gate, which makes this the best-derived FOW line in the batch, and adding a third current would raise a harmonisation count the practitioner's own card already flags ('Six Wellsprings claimed woven into it... Fifty-four of the Sixty remain untouched'). But the omission is conspicuous enough to need a ruling rather than a shrug, because the page's stated duration limit and its release cost are both endurance questions and neither declared current addresses endurance at all. Basilithe sits in the same register and is the next nearest - 'Resilience Hardening, Harmonics Stability. The soul's frequency locks and refuses retuning' - with a Failure that would be a real liability here: 'A frequency that cannot be shifted also cannot be detuned away from a forcing that happens to match it.'

options.option: Add Monolithion as a third current and take Vitality Tolerance and Resilience Persistence into the FOW line.
options.changes: Gives the working Sub-Stats for the thing it is actually limited by (how long he can hold it) and matches its name; raises the harmonisation count and dilutes what is currently an exactly-derived Sub-Stat list.

options.option: Leave the currents alone and note on the page that the name is descriptive rather than a Codex assignment.
options.changes: Costs nothing, keeps the clean derivation, and closes the question by saying the name points at an image rather than at a register entry.

options.option: Replace Judicium with Monolithion and drop the predictive-bracing layer.
options.changes: Simplifies the working to a pure endurance state and loses the Gnosis half, which is the half that makes the hardening selective rather than uniform - and which SA-GAP-MONOLITH-READ-STANDOFF shows is the harder engineering problem.

options.option: Rule generally that a technique's name carries no Codex weight and that assignment is decided only by the phenomenon.
options.changes: Consistent with the Glyph Index's own Standing Note ('Assignment is decided after the phenomenon, never before') and would settle a class of name-versus-register questions across the corpus at once.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · At the Wellspring stratum, Coagula's Core Law, "the personal, Soul Plane unifying force; a soul gathering itself back together," is run inward rather than projected outward, which is the Wellspring's native direction and the one thing this technique shares with ordinary Coagula use. Where an ordinary harmonisation makes a Crystal harder to split, sustained and pushed to saturation it does the same thing to the tissue the Crystal sits inside: Resilience Integrity climbs until the body's own failure curve reads closer to stone's than to flesh's, exactly as the current registers d
quote_b: | S | 401-550 | ... | Mach 25-200 | (Part Four travel speed); | S | 5-15 m | 20-50 km | (Part Eleven Contact Range and Projected Force Range)
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Four; III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md, Range and Force Coherence
why: The page has Judicium 'reading the geometry and force of an incoming blow closely enough that the hardening can present its density exactly where the blow will land rather than uniformly and too late'. That is a reactive defence, and a reactive defence has a latency floor. A mechanical redistribution inside a hardened body propagates at the speed of sound in that body; longitudinal wave speed in granite is about 5,500 m/s, so across a 2 m body the news takes 2/5500 = 0.36 ms. Part Four puts S-Grade travel speed at Mach 25 to 200, which is 8,575 to 68,600 m/s, and in 0.36 ms such an attack covers 3.1 m to 25 m. So the Judicium read must precede contact by at least the body's own acoustic transit time, which sets a minimum detection standoff of roughly 3 m at the bottom of S-Grade and roughly 25 m at the top - against a Part Eleven S-Grade Contact Range of 5-15 m. The requirement brackets the engagement distance, which means the working is viable at the low end of its own Grade and not at the high end. The gap is that nothing in the system ladders how far a Gnosis read reaches, or how early. Part Eleven ladders Projected Force Range but defines Range as 'the spatial envelope across which force remains coherent', which is not a sensing distance (see SA-GAP-RANGE-LADDER), and Part Twelve's Gnosis entries describe what a read resolves rather than at what distance. Without that ladder, every reactive defence in the corpus is unpriceable in the one variable that decides whether it works.

options.option: Publish a detection-range ladder for Gnosis, by Grade or by the Sub-Stat that carries the read.
options.changes: Closes this row and makes every reactive working in the corpus checkable; a real writing job, and the new numbers would have to be reconciled with the reaches pages already state.

options.option: State a standoff requirement on this page - the read must precede contact by the body's own acoustic transit - and let the attacker's speed decide whether it is met.
options.changes: Local fix that adds a genuinely interesting limit: fast attackers beat the bracing not by being strong but by being early, which is a different counter from everything else on the page.

options.option: Rule that a Judicium read is not bounded by mechanical propagation because the densification gradient is set by the working rather than transmitted through tissue.
options.changes: Removes the latency floor and requires the system to say how fast a working's own internal state propagates, which it currently says nowhere; that number would govern every reactive defence.

options.option: Make the bracing uniform rather than directed, and drop the predictive clause.
options.changes: Removes the problem entirely and costs the working the thing its Judicium half is for; the page's own phrase 'rather than uniformly and too late' shows it considered and rejected this.

quote_a: ### Summary card
quote_b: **Analogue** · Latent heat of phase change. Enthalpy absorbed at constant temperature. **Mechanism** · Melting ice at zero degrees absorbs three hundred and thirty-four joules per gram and the temperature does not move a fraction. The energy goes entirely into breaking the ordered structure. Catharsis routes accumulated emotional load into a phase transition instead of into output, so enormous internal pressure is consumed by the change of state itself and the practitioner arrives on the other side measurably calmer and structurally different.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Caloria — Thermodynamics.md, Catharsis
why: The page picks a real law and uses it correctly in one direction, then runs it backwards. Catharsis's Analogue is latent heat of phase change: melting ice absorbs 334 J/g at constant temperature, which is as much energy as heating the same water by 80 K (c_p 4.18 J/(g K)). That is a genuine, quantitative buffer and it is exactly right for absorbing an unbounded load without the reading variable moving. But a latent-heat buffer stores; it does not generate. Recovering the stored 334 J/g requires refreezing, which requires rejecting that heat to a colder reservoir, and the recoverable work fraction is then capped by Carnot at 1 - T_c/T_h, going to zero as the two temperatures approach. The page names no cold reservoir anywhere. Its Effect line is 'what should have been damage becomes reserve' and its Numerical Effect is 'Recovered reserve scales with how deep the paradox runs' - net output from an absorber with nothing to reject into, which is a perpetual motion machine of the second kind. The practitioner's own sheet makes it sharper rather than softer: his card gives eta 0.93, and eta is defined as 'the ratio of Essence spent to Essence that arrives as intended effect', so seven percent of everything he routes leaves as heat, sound and structural bleed before any question of gain arises. Note also that the Wellspring register is more conservative than the technique page: Catharsis's own text says the practitioner arrives 'measurably calmer and structurally different', which is disposal, not income.

options.option: Restate the Engine as a disposal mechanism rather than a resource engine: it converts a load that would have destroyed him into a change of structure, and returns nothing.
options.changes: Matches Catharsis's own register text exactly and closes the physics; costs the page its Effect line and its 'Resource Engine' function, and removes the reason Francis would seek contradictions rather than avoid them.

options.option: Name the cold reservoir - state what the heat is rejected into, and price the recovery by Carnot against the stated temperatures.
options.changes: Keeps the gain and makes it bounded, findable and attackable, since a reservoir is a thing an opponent can saturate or deny; requires the system to say what a Crystal's thermal reservoir is, which it currently does not.

options.option: Rule that Essence recovery is not a thermodynamic transaction and that the latent-heat analogue describes only the absorption half.
options.changes: Closes the row by declaring the analogue partial; weakens the standard the batch is written to, since the page's whole mechanism is borrowed from the analogue and cannot be half-borrowed without saying which half.

options.option: Make the returned reserve come from the contradiction's own source rather than from the transition - the Engine bills whoever created the paradox.
options.changes: Gives the surplus a stated provenance and turns the working into a transfer rather than a conversion, which fits the Debt theory the page already leans on; it also makes creating a contradiction near Francis a bad idea, which changes how opponents fight him.

quote_a: **Cost** · Micro-fissures across the Soul Crystal, accumulating with use and not healing between uses, at a rate his own private count can outrun if he lets it.
quote_b: **Failure** · Supercooling. The transition fails to nucleate, the load accumulates past the point where it should have released, and when it finally goes it goes all at once.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Caloria — Thermodynamics.md, Catharsis
why: The page's Limitation describes a valve: 'The valve has a throughput ceiling. Past it, the load is not rejected, it is redirected back into the Essence Core, unrouted, aimed at continuity rather than at output.' A valve fails at the moment it is overloaded and the overload is the signal. Catharsis's own Failure line describes something else entirely: 'Supercooling. The transition fails to nucleate, the load accumulates past the point where it should have released, and when it finally goes it goes all at once.' A supercooled system gives no signal at all. It sits below its transition point, metastable, with the driving force building and nothing happening, until something nucleates it somewhere and the whole stored load releases at once. The difference is the entire counterplay: a valve warns, metastability does not, and a practitioner running a valve knows when he is near the ceiling while a practitioner running a supercooled store believes he is fine right up until he is not. The numbers are real. Water supercools to about -38 C before homogeneous nucleation forces the issue, and the fraction that freezes instantly on nucleation is about (T_m - T)*c_p/L = 38*4.18/334, roughly 47 percent of the mass in milliseconds. And classical nucleation theory puts the barrier at dG* = 16*pi*gamma^3/(3*dG_v^2), which diverges as the driving force goes to zero - so the loads least likely ever to resolve are the small, gentle ones, which is the opposite of what a throughput ceiling would predict.

options.option: Replace the valve framing with the register's: the ceiling is a nucleation failure, silent, with the release arriving late and all at once.
options.changes: Brings the page into line with its own Wellspring and makes the limit far more dangerous and far more interesting, because the practitioner cannot feel it coming; it also removes the page's implied ability to stop short of the ceiling.

options.option: Keep both as two distinct failures - an immediate overflow at the instantaneous ceiling and a slow metastable accumulation - and say which is which.
options.changes: Most faithful to both texts and gives the working two failure modes with different tells; requires stating what distinguishes a load that overflows from one that fails to nucleate.

options.option: State that Judicium's diagnostic count measures stored metastability rather than fissure density, so the practitioner does have a gauge.
options.changes: Reconciles the page's 'his own diagnostic count tracks closely' with the register's silence and makes the gauge the thing an opponent wants to spoil; Judicium's Failure line (spectral overload) then becomes a way to spoil it.

options.option: Amend Catharsis's Failure line to a throughput failure rather than a nucleation one.
options.changes: Changes one register entry instead of one technique page and would propagate to every other Catharsis working in the corpus; supercooling is also the more distinctive of the two failures and the reason the entry reads as physics rather than as flavour.

quote_a: **Stage floor** · Stage XIV, Zenith.
quote_b: **Empathy** requires Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Seven, Harmonics Gates
why: The page's FOW line governs on Tempering Processing, Harmonics Empathy and Resilience Insulation, correctly identified as Catharsis's own Stat Effect carried over unchanged. Two of the three clear their gates cleanly under their current names. Tempering Processing reads as Maturity under the Merge Ledger, and Part Seven says 'Maturity open ... its fracture-metabolism component Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed A' - Francis is Spirit dominant at Stage XIV, so it passes, and the gate is named for the technique. Resilience Insulation reads as Fortification: 'Fortification requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B; resistance to self-generated blowback is open' - his card gives Body tertiary and the relevant clause is open anyway, so it passes. Harmonics Empathy does not: 'Empathy requires Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C', the working is EX-Grade and far above C, and his card commits him to 'Spirit dominant, Fate secondary, Body tertiary' with no Attraction at any weight. The page's declared Path gate is Spirit. So one of the three Sub-Stats the working is built on is gated on the one Path the practitioner does not carry, and it is the sensing half - the Sub-Stat the page assigns to 'sensing the paradox as load before it becomes damage', which is the step the whole machine depends on.

options.option: Add Attraction to Francis's Path line at the weight the gate needs.
options.changes: Clears the gate and gives him all four Paths in some measure; his card's Path note is written as an argument about what a Celestial's Crystal is anchored to, so a fourth Path is a characterisation change as well as a bookkeeping one.

options.option: Replace Harmonics Empathy with a Gnosis Sub-Stat for the sensing step, since Judicium supplies Gnosis and currently governs nothing on this page.
options.changes: Fixes the gate and the odd fact that the declared primary current contributes no Sub-Stat at all; costs the page its exact derivation from Catharsis's Stat Effect, which is currently one of its virtues.

options.option: Rule that a Wellspring harmonisation supplies the Path commitment for the Sub-Stats that Wellspring strengthens.
options.changes: Would close this row and a large class of others across the batch at once; a substantial change to Part Seven, which says Path commitment 'is not declared. It is recognised.'

options.option: Drop the sensing clause and have the Engine run without detection, triggering on contact with a contradiction rather than on anticipation of one.
options.changes: Removes the gated Sub-Stat and matches the page's own 'continuous, with no activation act' framing more closely; loses the distinction between a real contradiction and an apparent one at the intake, which is the safeguard the page is careful about.

page: (batch-wide; bites hardest on The Principle Engine)
quote_a: **η · efficiency** — the ratio of Essence spent to Essence that arrives as intended effect.
path_a: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md, section V
quote_b: | XIV | Zenith | EX | 1,500 | 8 · Archmaster | 0.95–1.2 | Crystallized Soul |
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VII. Aether Class, Essence Typology, Aether Flow (Parts Seventeen–Nineteen).md, Part Nineteen
why: Part Nineteen's efficiency band for Tier of Standing 8, Archmaster, runs from 0.95 to 1.2. The Core Vocabulary defines eta as 'the ratio of Essence spent to Essence that arrives as intended effect', and Two Sets of Books states the complement: 'The remainder leaves as heat, sound, and structural bleed.' An eta above 1.0 therefore means more Essence arrives as effect than was spent, and the system names no source for the surplus anywhere. This is not a rounding matter at the top of the ladder: at 1.2 the surplus is twenty percent of everything an Archmaster does. Three readings are available and the system does not choose between them. It may be that eta above unity is deliberate and the surplus is drawn from the Aether stratum rather than the Essence one, which Two Sets of Books would support in principle ('a working's energy budget balances at the Aether stratum and not at the Essence one') but does not say. It may be that the band's upper figure is a typographical or scale artefact. Or eta may be defined differently at the top of the ladder from the way the Core Vocabulary defines it. The gap is logged here because The Principle Engine is the page where it becomes load-bearing rather than decorative: that working's entire claimed effect is a net return of reserve, and the question of whether the system permits net return at all is exactly this row (see SA-PHYS-ENGINE-NO-COLD-SINK).

options.option: Rule that eta above 1.0 is real and that the surplus is drawn from the Aether stratum, and say so in the Core Vocabulary.
options.changes: Legitimises the band, gives every Archmaster a stated free lunch with a stated provenance, and would close the Principle Engine's physics row in the same stroke; it also makes Aetheric Density a much more important constraint than it currently is, and that scale does not exist (SA-GAP-AETHERIC-DENSITY).

options.option: Cap the band at 1.0 and rewrite Tier 8 as 0.95-1.0.
options.changes: Smallest edit, restores the definition, and removes the only place the system currently hints that net gain is possible - which several high-Stage pages appear to be leaning on.

options.option: Define a second efficiency measure for the top Tiers, distinct from the Core Vocabulary's ratio, and name it.
options.changes: Lets both texts stand and adds a term the corpus must then use consistently; every eta figure on every card would need to say which measure it is.

options.option: Leave the band and state explicitly that the surplus is unexplained.
options.changes: Costs nothing and makes it a known open question rather than an apparent error; leaves every working whose effect is net return resting on it.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · Judicium reads the contradiction the way it reads any interface: a truth-value comparison against a reference, the same diagnostic operation attested elsewhere for the Wellspring. Where the comparison returns a genuine incompatibility rather than an error of perception, Catharsis takes the load. Catharsis's documented law is latent heat of phase change: energy absorbed at constant apparent temperature goes entirely into breaking an ordered structure rather than into raising output. Francis's Crystal runs the same operation on the contradiction itself. The paradox becomes the ice, and the phase transition consumes the destructive pressure the paradox would otherwise apply directly to his Core, leaving him structurally different and measurably stocked with reserve on the other side, exactly as Catharsis's own failure mode already describes for anyone using it under load.
quote_b: **Read him.** Taught techniques are documented and counterable by anyone who studied. Self-derived techniques must be read live, in the two or three exchanges before they kill you. Every thaumaturge has a pattern, because single-axis fluency produces one, and a pattern learned is a pattern interruptible.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md, IV. Break the Man
why: The working has no observable signature of any kind. Its Trigger is 'Continuous, with no activation act'; its Range is Self; its Craft is 'Spellcraft (Internalised: the chain held silently in the Crystal, never spoken)'; it produces no field, no sound and no visible change. The Counterplay register's whole Break the Man route depends on a technique being readable - 'self-derived techniques must be read live, in the two or three exchanges before they kill you' - and this one cannot be read live because it does nothing an observer can point at. Its Origin line says it is self-derived and 'undocumented anywhere Isaac's index can currently check', so the taught-technique route is closed too. The practical consequence is specific: an opponent cannot know whether putting Francis in a genuine bind is a trap for Francis or a gift to him, and that is the single decision the Engine turns on. Two partial mitigations exist and neither belongs to this working. Part Eleven puts an EX-Grade Passive Pressure Field at 'Planetary presence', and his card's Dirge Pulse 'runs continuously. It is the sound the lock makes.' Both announce Francis. Neither announces the Engine. The account's section 3 proposes a negative tell that a player could reach - a paraconsistent reasoner cannot use disjunctive syllogism, so he will not take a remainder after an alternative is denied - but that is derived from outside the corpus and is not currently anything the pages would let a player look up.

options.option: Give the working a stated tell on conversion - a visible or audible sign at the moment a contradiction is metabolised, however brief.
options.changes: Closes the fairness gap and makes the key decision (bind him or not) readable in one exchange; costs the working its silence, which is part of why it reads as a property of the man rather than a technique.

options.option: State the behavioural tell: a Crystal that holds contradictions does not narrow by elimination, and that is observable across two exchanges.
options.changes: Keeps the working silent and gives a player something to find, at the cost of requiring the system to state what a paradox-holding Crystal can and cannot infer - a new and quite abstract mechanic.

options.option: Make the fissure count externally readable by a Judicium-class diagnostic, so an opponent with the right current can see the damage even if not the operation.
options.changes: Ties the tell to the cost, which is elegant, and gives Judicium practitioners a specific reason to be in the scene; it tells an opponent how much he has spent rather than whether he is running.

options.option: Accept that the working is unreadable and state that its counter is environmental rather than observational - you deny the field rather than read the man.
options.changes: Consistent with the page's own two counters, which are both field denials; formally concedes that one of the five fairness tests is failed by design, which should then be on the record rather than implicit.

quote_a: **Weakness** · Anti-growth Wellsprings, Exuroth's dehydration and Nihiloth's null field, are not inputs the dome can metabolise and pass through it largely undiminished.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md, Part Four
why: The page prices what the dome absorbs and never prices what it costs to build. Its own geometry is a dome over a five-metre radius closing in one second. A 5 m hemisphere has a surface of 2*pi*r^2 = 157 m^2. At a wood density of 600 kg/m^3 a shell of thickness t masses 94,200*t kg, and the energy cost of building biomass is bounded below by its heat of combustion, about 17.5 MJ/kg for dry wood. Impose the page's own Grade: Part Four puts the B-Grade ceiling at 4.6024x10^10 J, 46.0 GJ. Spend all of it on wood and you get 2,630 kg, which is 4.38 m^3, which over 157 m^2 is a shell 2.8 cm thick - and the build is a 46 GW event sustained for one second, roughly fifteen large reactors' thermal output. Every additional centimetre costs another 16 GJ, so a 10 cm shell is 165 GJ, 39 tonnes of TNT, 3.6 times the page's own Grade ceiling before anything has struck it. The consequence is not that the working is impossible; it is that the Grade band silently fixes a dimension the page treats as free, and that dimension decides whether the Veil is a bunker or a screen. Note what does close: the page's stated 1-5 GN peak force spreads over 157 m^2 to 6.4-31.8 MPa, and wood takes 40-60 MPa parallel to the grain, so the absorption figure is a genuine pass. It is only the construction that is unpriced.

options.option: State the shell thickness on the page and let it follow from the Grade, at roughly 3 cm at B.
options.changes: Makes the dome checkable and honest about what it is - a thin living shell that survives by converting rather than by mass; changes how it reads in a scene, since 3 cm of wood is a thing a determined man can get through given time the page does not give him.

options.option: Lengthen the closure time so the build power falls, and keep the thickness.
options.changes: Power scales inversely with closure time, so a five-second build at the same energy is 9 GW; costs the page its one-second lag, which is currently its best-calibrated limit (5 m/s, a sprinting man).

options.option: Rule that the dome's mass is re-latticed from Essence and ambient matter already present rather than synthesised, so the heat-of-combustion floor does not apply.
options.changes: Consistent with Materia Primordia's register, whose Analogue is allotropy and whose language is 'the same Essence, re-latticed'; requires a stated cost for re-latticing, which the system does not currently supply, and would make the growth law decorative.

options.option: Raise the working's Grade to cover the construction it describes.
options.changes: Clears the arithmetic and takes the ward away from the Stage V practitioners the page is written for; the page's Stage and ceiling citations are otherwise correct, so this moves the one thing that currently checks out.

quote_a: **Governing Primary** · Ardency (Density, the Sub-Stat governing whether a ward outlasts what hits it), secondary Vitality (Regeneration, Hemostasis).
quote_b: Verdantia: **Stat Effect** · Strengthens Vitality Regeneration, Tempering Yield, Harmonics Synergy. || Materia Primordia: **Stat Effect** · Strengthens Vitality Ossification, Dominion Density.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vitalia — Biochemistry.md and Materia — Material Science.md
why: The page governs on 'Ardency (Density, the Sub-Stat governing whether a ward outlasts what hits it), secondary Vitality (Regeneration, Hemostasis)'. Of the three, only Vitality Regeneration is strengthened by either declared current. Verdantia gives Vitality Regeneration, Tempering Yield and Harmonics Synergy. Materia Primordia gives Vitality Ossification and Dominion Density, which read as Fortitude and Gravity under the Merge Ledger, and neither appears in the FOW line at all. Ardency Density and Vitality Hemostasis are strengthened by neither. Ardency Density is at least defensible on function - Part Twelve's entry does say 'Whether your ward outlasts the siege' - but the omission on the other side is the sharper one: Part Twelve defines Vitality Fortitude as 'Resistance to blunt trauma, impact force and structural breakdown, across bone, joint and connective tissue... The first number consulted when a clean hit lands and the question is whether the recipient is still standing.' That is the Sub-Stat a structure is rated on when something hits it, the page's own secondary Wellspring strengthens it, and the page does not name it. Note that none of this breaks a gate: at B-Grade every one of the three listed Sub-Stats passes Part Seven cleanly, and so would Fortitude ('requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed C, and Stage IV to exceed B'), which at B-Grade does not bind.

options.option: Add Vitality Fortitude and Dominion Gravity to the FOW line, taking them from Materia Primordia.
options.changes: Makes the secondary current contribute something and gives the ward the Sub-Stat Part Twelve names for surviving a clean hit; at B-Grade both pass their gates, so nothing else has to move.

options.option: Drop Ardency Density and Vitality Hemostasis and govern only on what the two currents strengthen.
options.changes: Strictest derivation; costs the page the Sub-Stat whose Part Twelve definition explicitly covers whether a ward outlasts a siege, which is the thing the page most wants to claim.

options.option: Add a third current that strengthens the two orphan Sub-Stats.
options.changes: Keeps the FOW line and raises the harmonisation count on a working with no named practitioner to carry it; would also bring a third Failure line onto a page that is already not carrying the two it has.

options.option: Rule that a working's Sub-Stats may be chosen by function rather than by Wellspring provenance.
options.changes: Closes a recurring class of rows across the batch in one move and severs the link the registers currently carry between a current and what it strengthens, which is how most technique pages derive their FOW lines.

quote_a: **Counterplay** · Strike inside the one-second closure window, or bring a working the dome cannot metabolise; heavy-metal toxins outright weaken the roots rather than feeding them, by the source's own account.
quote_b: **Failure** · Phase locking. Under sufficient pressure the lattice commits to one allotrope permanently, and the practitioner keeps whichever form they were wearing when the pressure came.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md, Materia Primordia
why: The page takes its frame from Materia Primordia and uses that register's own phrase to do it: 'the same Essence re-latticed as living wood on the outside and dense mineral bracing on the inside'. It does not carry the register's stated price. Materia Primordia's Failure is 'Phase locking. Under sufficient pressure the lattice commits to one allotrope permanently, and the practitioner keeps whichever form they were wearing when the pressure came.' This working exists to be hit, is rated to absorb 1 to 5 GN, and is held by a caster whose own body is the routing path for every injury it converts ('The ward routes injury through the caster's own body before it routes it into growth'). If 5 GN is not 'sufficient pressure', nothing in the B-Grade band is, and the page's Cost line prices only the transient sensation and the healing debt - both of which clear. The register supplies a permanent one and it is the kind a player can be told about in advance and still not avoid. Note the page's Cost is otherwise one of the strongest in the batch, which is why this is filed as a missing consequence rather than as a fairness failure.

options.option: Add phase locking to the Cost line: a heavy enough strike absorbed by the dome commits the caster's lattice permanently.
options.changes: Gives the working a catastrophic outcome proportional to how well it is working, which is unusual and good; needs a stated pressure threshold, which the system does not currently supply for any working.

options.option: Rule that phase locking applies only to a lattice the practitioner is wearing, not to one they have projected, so a dome does not risk it.
options.changes: Closes the row by reading the register narrowly and matches its wording ('whichever form they were wearing'); makes projected Materia Primordia workings strictly safer than worn ones, which is a general rule with consequences elsewhere.

options.option: Replace Materia Primordia with a Materia current whose Failure the page is willing to carry.
options.changes: Keeps the cost profile and costs the page the allotropy analogue, which is the only thing that explains how the dome closes in a second (see SA-PHYS-VERDANT-CLOSURE-ENERGY); Coagulatio and Monolithion are the nearest alternatives and neither supplies a re-latticing rate.

options.option: Keep the omission and state on the page that the pact's terms exclude the caster from phase locking.
options.changes: Turns a gap into a piece of lore about what a 'pact' is, which the page's title invites and its body never explains; requires saying who the pact is with, which no page currently does.

quote_a: **Effect** · A living dome of grown matter closes over the caster and every ally within five metres, and for as long as it holds, wounds taken inside it lag behind whatever caused them. *Fire arrives and the char becomes new bark. Frost arrives and the numbness becomes sap-slow warmth.*
quote_b: **Consequence** · Every unit of force the dome converts is logged against the caster's own capacity to heal the way a debt is logged against a ledger; the dome closes hairline Soul Crystal fractures on the same principle, far more slowly, while it stands.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Veil of Verdant Pact.md:41
why: The Effect line and the Mechanism line describe two different objects. The Effect says 'a living dome of grown matter closes over the caster and every ally within five metres, and for as long as it holds, wounds taken inside it lag behind whatever caused them' - wounds are taken inside the dome, by people, and the working delays them. The Mechanism describes a structure absorbing energy into its own tissue: 'ambient energy delivered to it, heat, kinetic shock, electrical discharge, corrosive chemistry, is absorbed the way a plant absorbs sunlight, as fuel for continuous structural addition rather than as damage taken.' That is a barrier: it intercepts at its surface and converts there. The Function line tries to hold both - 'Converts destructive force arriving inside the radius into accelerated tissue growth in the dome's own structure, and at a far smaller rate, in the caster's and allies' bodies' - and the Cost line commits to a third reading in which injuries route through the caster before reaching the wood. The three are not the same working. A barrier answers the question 'did it get through' and nothing else; a field answers 'what happens to a wound that was inflicted anyway'; a routing answers 'who holds it in the interval'. Which one is running decides several practical things: whether an attack that originates inside the radius is converted at all, whether an ally struck by a blade already inside the dome benefits, and whether the caster's stated cost applies to injuries the dome never touched.

options.option: Commit to the barrier reading: the dome converts what crosses its surface and does nothing for a wound inflicted inside it.
options.changes: Simplest and matches the Mechanism line and the physics; costs the Effect line's best image and means an enemy who gets inside the closure window is not merely inside the ward, he is immune to it.

options.option: Commit to the field reading: anything destructive inside the radius is converted wherever it happens, with the caster as the routing point.
options.changes: Matches the Effect and Cost lines and makes the dome a volume rather than a surface; raises the question of why the dome's own tissue is where the growth appears, and makes the one-second closure lag much less important.

options.option: Keep both explicitly, as a barrier at the surface and a slower conversion inside it, and give the two different rates.
options.changes: Closest to what the Function line already says and the most work: it needs two stated conversion rates and a rule for which applies to what.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism, per the standing ruling that the mechanism is the effect.
options.changes: Applies Isaac's 2026-09-24 ruling directly and settles the row without a new decision; the Effect line's imagery would have to be rebuilt around the dome's surface rather than around the people under it.

quote_a: > **What nobody knows** · Whether the dome draws on Verdantia's law alone, or on something older that Verdantia only resembles, since ancient Materia Primordia mineral seams have turned up threaded through its root system on every occasion anyone has checked.
quote_b: **Wellspring** · Verdantia, The Green Pulse (primary). Materia Primordia, The First Substance (secondary).
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Veil of Verdant Pact.md:25
why: The page's 'What nobody knows' presents the presence of Materia Primordia in the ward's root system as an unexplained anomaly suggesting an older law: 'Whether the dome draws on Verdantia's law alone, or on something older that Verdantia only resembles, since ancient Materia Primordia mineral seams have turned up threaded through its root system on every occasion anyone has checked.' Four lines below, the page's own Codex line declares 'Materia Primordia, The First Substance (secondary)', and its Mechanism line makes that current the ward's structural frame: 'Materia Primordia supplies the frame: the same Essence re-latticed as living wood on the outside and dense mineral bracing on the inside.' So the mineral seams are not an anomaly, an older law, or evidence of anything; they are the second declared Wellspring doing the job the page assigns it. A page cannot be mystified by a current it has already named as its own secondary. What is genuinely open underneath the question is more interesting than the question and is not asked: Materia Primordia is called The First Substance, so a ward whose frame is the first substance really is older in some sense than the growth that expresses on it, and whether the pact is with the green or with the stone is a question the page's own title raises and never addresses.

options.option: Strike the 'What nobody knows' as written, since its premise is answered by the page's own Codex line.
options.changes: A factual correction; leaves the page without an open question, which most technique pages in this section carry.

options.option: Rewrite the question as the one underneath it: whether the pact is with Verdantia's green or with the First Substance the frame is made of.
options.changes: Keeps an open question, makes it genuinely open, and hooks the page's title to its Wellspring line for the first time; invites a ruling about what a 'pact' is in this working, which no page currently states.

options.option: Keep the question and remove Materia Primordia from the Codex line, so the seams really are unexplained.
options.changes: Makes the mystery honest and removes the current that supplies the frame, the re-latticing rate and the mineral bracing - i.e. most of the mechanism.

options.option: Rule that a technique page's 'What nobody knows' is in-world ignorance rather than authorial ignorance, so a documented folk ward may not know its own Codex line.
options.changes: Resolves this row and a class of others by reading those blocks as in-fiction rather than editorial; would need stating somewhere, because several pages in this batch use the block both ways.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · Vohrin's law is heat's absence held as discipline rather than suffered as a condition. The cold is not summoned; it is a controlled, directional heat-sink running through Draven's own ignited musculature. At the instant of contact, that sink pulls thermal energy out of the target's tissue far faster than the tissue's own conduction can redistribute it, and the same ice-lattice-through-tissue mechanism already documented for Vohrin elsewhere in current canon, ordered crystallisation blocking Essence pathways at the wound, locks the local muscle chains and the Essence trying to move through them in the same instant. Cinerion compounds the effect same-Family, densifying the cold past what Vohrin alone would produce.
quote_b: **Numerical Effect** · Strike Force is Draven's own attested Ardency 320, A-Grade: 20 to 100 GN peak, 46 GJ to 4.184 TJ yield, city-block scale, with this technique run near the top of that sustainable range rather than an Overchannel spike. The freeze itself holds for 1 to 2 seconds, kept from the card as given.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Vorynn Execution Strike.md:45
why: The page states its own limiting condition correctly and then asks for an effect the condition forbids. Its Mechanism says the sink 'pulls thermal energy out of the target's tissue far faster than the tissue's own conduction can redistribute it' - true, and it is the constraint rather than the achievement, because a surface sink can only cool what conduction brings to it. The thermal diffusivity of soft tissue is about 1.4x10^-7 m^2/s and a thermal front reaches a depth L = sqrt(alpha*t): 0.37 mm in 1 s, 0.53 mm in 2 s, 2.9 mm in a minute. Inverted, reaching a muscle belly 5 cm down takes L^2/alpha = 0.0025/1.4e-7, about 17,900 seconds, five hours. This is the operating constraint of clinical cryoablation, where a probe at -180 C takes ten to fifteen minutes to grow an iceball a few centimetres across for exactly this reason, with radius going as sqrt(t). So within the page's own stated 1-to-2-second lock the cold reaches roughly half a millimetre, and 'locks the local muscle chains' is out by two orders of magnitude in depth. Pulling harder does not help: a sink faster than conduction freezes the surface harder and leaves the interior warm, because the bottleneck is the target's tissue and not the sink. Note what the physiology does supply at a reachable depth, because the page's stated sign is correct and the account for it is available: peripheral nerve conduction fails below about 7-10 C and many nerves run 3-5 mm deep, and cooled muscle locks rather than going limp because relaxation is SERCA-dependent with a Q10 near 3, so the pump slows faster than activation does. The page's 'seize rigid rather than absorbing' is the right outcome; only the stated route to it is too slow.

options.option: Restate the mechanism as nerve block and cold contracture at reachable depth rather than as freezing muscle chains.
options.changes: Keeps every stated outcome including the rigidity, closes the physics, and gives the working an anatomy - it works where nerves run shallow and less well where they do not, which is a real tactical texture the page does not have.

options.option: Keep the freeze and lengthen the contact to what diffusion needs.
options.changes: Physically honest and destroys the technique: five hours of contact is not a strike, and the 1-to-2-second lock is the whole of its tactical value.

options.option: Route the cold through Essence pathways rather than through tissue, so diffusion in tissue does not govern.
options.changes: The page already half-claims this ('ordered crystallisation blocking Essence pathways at the wound') and it would need a stated propagation rate for Essence-borne cold, which the system supplies nowhere; it also detaches the working from the thermodynamics its Family is built on.

options.option: Reduce the claimed scope from muscle chains to surface and superficial structures, and say so.
options.changes: Smallest edit and matches the arithmetic; the lock becomes local rather than whole-limb, which changes what a follow-through can assume.

quote_a: **Effect** · The strike does not need to be hard to be final. Contact alone collapses the target's momentum on the spot. Muscle chains lock, kinetic defence goes rigid, and the follow-through does the rest.
quote_b: **Numerical Effect** · Strike Force is Draven's own attested Ardency 320, A-Grade: 20 to 100 GN peak, 46 GJ to 4.184 TJ yield, city-block scale, with this technique run near the top of that sustainable range rather than an Overchannel spike. The freeze itself holds for 1 to 2 seconds, kept from the card as given.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Vorynn Execution Strike.md:45
why: Two lines on one page, a factor of about 2.5 billion apart. The Effect line opens 'The strike does not need to be hard to be final. Contact alone collapses the target's momentum on the spot.' The Numerical Effect gives it Draven's attested Ardency 320 at A-Grade - '20 to 100 GN peak, 46 GJ to 4.184 TJ yield, city-block scale, with this technique run near the top of that sustainable range'. 4.184 TJ is one kiloton of TNT. Delivered by a fist, to one person, in order to hold him still for one to two seconds. Meanwhile the cold the page describes, priced honestly against what a contact sink can reach in that time (a fist-sized 100 cm^2 patch to a depth of 0.5 mm, about 5 g, at roughly 340 J/g for sensible plus latent heat), costs about 1.7 kJ. The two claims are not merely different in scale; they are different techniques. A kiloton arriving at a target makes the lock, the 1-to-2-second window, the Essence-pathway crystallisation and the entire counterplay section irrelevant, because there is nothing left to lock. And the Effect line's claim is the more interesting one and is defensible on its own: removing a defender's compliance multiplies the force of an unchanged blow by two to four times, since F = E/d and a guard that yields 30 cm halves what a guard yielding 15 cm takes. The page has the good mechanism in its first sentence and contradicts it four lines later by reaching for its practitioner's Grade band.

options.option: Drop the Strike Force claim and let the working be what its first line says: a small blow made final by removing the target's ability to yield.
options.changes: Makes the page internally consistent, keeps the mechanism that is actually interesting, and removes the technique from the kiloton problem that recurs across this batch; costs the page its 'city-block scale' line.

options.option: State the force multiplier explicitly - compliance lost, F = E/d, two to four times - instead of a yield figure.
options.changes: Gives a checkable number that scales with the target rather than with the practitioner, which is unusual and good; requires a convention for how much a given defender yields, which the system does not have.

options.option: Keep the yield and rewrite the Effect line to match, making this a maximal strike with a cold rider.
options.changes: Consistent, and it makes the working redundant with an ordinary A-Grade punch plus a flourish; also inherits the standing problem that Part Eleven's A-Grade ceiling applied to one person is not survivable by anyone.

options.option: Rule that quoting a practitioner's Grade band on a technique page states a ceiling rather than the working's output.
options.changes: Would settle a recurring pattern across the batch in one move, since many pages quote a band and then describe a much smaller effect; requires every such page to state its actual output separately.

quote_a: **Effect** · The strike does not need to be hard to be final. Contact alone collapses the target's momentum on the spot. Muscle chains lock, kinetic defence goes rigid, and the follow-through does the rest.
quote_b: **Target Response** · Kinetic defences seize rigid rather than absorbing or redirecting the blow; a non-practitioner shows frost on the wound, a practitioner's Essence pathway crystallises at the point of contact.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Vorynn Execution Strike.md:46
why: The Effect and Function lines both say the working stops the target's momentum: 'Contact alone collapses the target's momentum on the spot' and 'A single compressed strike that stops the target's momentum rather than merely damaging the target carrying it.' The Mechanism supplies a heat sink and an ice lattice. A heat sink does not collapse momentum. Momentum is conserved and cooling a body does not change it; a frozen man travelling at 5 m/s is a frozen man travelling at 5 m/s. What cooling genuinely removes is the target's ability to generate new momentum (a locked muscle cannot contract usefully) and, more importantly, the ability to absorb - and the page's own Target Response says so in better words than its Effect line does: 'Kinetic defences seize rigid rather than absorbing or redirecting the blow.' That is the real and large effect: a defence works by yielding, since mean impact force is F = E/d and lengthening the deceleration distance is the only free variable, so a guard that yields 30 cm halves the force of one yielding 15 cm. Removing compliance multiplies the force of an unchanged blow by two to four. So the page contains the correct statement of its own effect in its Target Response and a physically wrong statement of it in its Effect and Function lines, using a vocabulary ('collapses momentum', 'kinetic collapse') that names a quantity the mechanism does not touch.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect and Function lines from the Target Response: the working removes the target's ability to yield and to answer, not his momentum.
options.changes: Applies the standing mechanism-is-the-effect ruling, makes the page internally consistent, and gives it a mechanism that is both correct and more interesting than momentum removal.

options.option: Keep 'kinetic collapse' as an in-world term of art and gloss it on the page as the loss of compliance.
options.changes: Preserves the page's Function heading and the Category framing while fixing the physics; adds a term the corpus would then use elsewhere.

options.option: Add a genuine momentum mechanism - an anchoring or grounding clause - so the Effect line becomes true.
options.changes: Requires a second current or a second boundary condition and makes the working a much bigger thing; nothing on the page or the card currently supplies a momentum-arresting law.

options.option: Narrow the claim to a practitioner's kinetic defences only, where 'momentum' means the Essence flow driving them rather than the body's.
options.changes: Salvages the phrase by redefining it and matches the crystallisation clause ('blocking Essence pathways at the wound'); leaves the working with little effect on a non-practitioner, which the page's own Target Response contradicts.

quote_a: **Cost** · **Every use tears fibre along the ignition path.** *Chained further, the tear compounds; his own count puts the Essence toll near a fifth of what he is carrying per use.*
quote_b: **Essence Starvation** — "Below ten percent EU a practitioner suffers Essence Starvation: reduced stat expression, Shell degradation, Trait flickering."
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md, section V
why: This is the only page in the twenty-eight that prices a cost as a fraction of reserve, which is the one condition under which the system's Essence Starvation threshold becomes computable at all (every other page states an absolute EU figure or nothing, and no formula converts a Stage into an EU total). So the page has, uniquely, given the ledger something to work with - and then left the arithmetic ambiguous in a way that changes the answer by a factor of two. 'A fifth of what he is carrying per use' reads most naturally as a fifth of current reserve, which is multiplicative: 0.8^n gives 80, 64, 51, 41, 33, 26, 21, 17, 13, 10.7, 8.6 percent, so Starvation arrives on the eleventh use. Read as a fifth of maximum reserve it is linear: 80, 60, 40, 20, 0, so Starvation arrives during the fifth. Eleven uses and five uses are very different techniques, and the difference decides whether Counterplay's 'Exhaustion' route is a plan for one engagement or for three. The gap is general rather than local: the system states a Starvation threshold as a percentage and never says whether a cost expressed as a fraction is taken against the current balance or the ceiling, so the first page in the corpus to state one cannot be resolved.

options.option: Rule that fractional costs are taken against current reserve (multiplicative) and say so in the Core Vocabulary.
options.changes: Gives this working eleven uses before Starvation and makes fractional costs asymptotic - a practitioner never quite runs out, which softens the Exhaustion counter across the corpus.

options.option: Rule that fractional costs are taken against maximum reserve (linear).
options.changes: Gives five uses, makes the clock countable by an opponent, and makes fractional costs behave like absolute ones once the maximum is known - which it is not, for anybody (SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA).

options.option: Restate this page's cost as an absolute EU figure once an EU-by-Stage table exists.
options.changes: Defers to the batch's largest gap and loses the one page that currently makes a Starvation margin computable.

options.option: Leave it to the page and require any page stating a fractional cost to say which denominator it means.
options.changes: Closes the ambiguity per page without a general rule; means the same phrase can mean different things on different sheets, which is how the turn-length question already went (SA-CROSS-TURN-CONVERSION-RATES).

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Heat extraction and impact force both land at Draven's A-Grade Ardency band (20–100 GN peak force, 46 GJ–4 TJ yield, city-block scale, per the FOW Physical Benchmarks table), delivered instantaneously across the arc rather than sustained.
quote_b: **Target Response** · Flesh loses heat sharply along the arc's path; armor not built to insulate against a genuine thermal gradient cracks under the sudden contraction.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Winter Rend.md:40
why: The page states that 'Heat extraction and impact force both land at Draven's A-Grade Ardency band (20-100 GN peak force, 46 GJ-4 TJ yield, city-block scale)'. The band is quoted correctly from Part Eleven and the card, and it may well be right for the impact. For the heat extraction it is out by six to eight orders of magnitude. Take the page's own geometry: a two-metre arc, swept at a realistic tip speed of about 30 m/s, so angular velocity 15 rad/s and a 120-degree sweep takes 0.14 s, with any one point on the target inside the cold for roughly 0.05-0.1 s. Thermal diffusion in soft tissue follows L = sqrt(alpha*t) with alpha about 1.4x10^-7 m^2/s, so at 0.1 s the cold reaches 0.12 mm. A target presenting 0.5 m^2 to the arc, cooled 0.12 mm deep, is about 6x10^-5 m^3, roughly 63 g of tissue, and taking tissue to freezing costs about 340 J/g in sensible plus latent heat. Total: about 21 kJ. Against 46 GJ that is a factor of 2.2x10^6, and against 4.184 TJ it is 2x10^8. Note what does close on the same page and by the same shallowness: the armour claim. Thermal shock resistance R = sigma(1-nu)/(E*alpha) puts structural steel at about 117 K, and the induced stress at a 120 K surface drop is E*alpha*dT/(1-nu) = 411 MPa, which is at yield - so 'armor not built to insulate against a genuine thermal gradient cracks under the sudden contraction' is correct, and it is correct precisely because the cooling is shallow and steep, which is the worst case for a stiff solid. The page has one target response whose physics closes exactly and one whose energy figure is astronomically overstated, in the same sentence pair.

options.option: Split the Numerical Effect: keep the Ardency band for the impact and state the thermal component separately in joules or in surface temperature drop.
options.changes: Makes both halves checkable and lets the armour claim keep the number that already works (a surface drop near 120 K); costs the page its single-band framing.

options.option: State the working's thermal output as a surface temperature drop rather than as an energy, since that is the quantity both stated target responses actually depend on.
options.changes: The cleanest fix - thermal shock and nerve block are both threshold-in-temperature effects, not energy effects - and it would set a convention other cold pages could follow.

options.option: Keep the energy figure and extend the contact time so the cooling reaches a depth that could absorb it.
options.changes: Destroys the technique: reaching even 5 cm needs about five hours by L^2/alpha, and this is a sweeping melee strike.

options.option: Rule generally that a practitioner's Grade band states a ceiling rather than a working's output.
options.changes: Would settle a recurring pattern across this batch in one move, since several pages quote a band and describe a much smaller effect; requires every such page to state its own output.

quote_a: **Consequence** · The arc lingers a moment as pale afterimage, the Tenebra-thinned residue of the strike's own path; a faint chime carries where ice forms and fractures in the same instant.
quote_b: **Analogue** · Signal-to-noise reduction. Absorptive coating and faceted return geometry. **Mechanism** · Something is undetectable when its return falls below the noise floor of whatever is looking, which is achieved by absorbing incident energy and by shaping surfaces so the little that reflects goes anywhere except back at the observer.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md, Tenebra
why: The page credits its visible residue to Tenebra: 'The arc lingers a moment as pale afterimage, the Tenebra-thinned residue of the strike's own path', and its Mechanism has Tenebra 'rid[ing] the same arc as afterimage - the same signal-to-noise reduction already documented on Draven's sheet, applied to the visible strike-path rather than to his own body'. Tenebra's register law is the reduction of return: absorbing incident energy and shaping surfaces so what little reflects goes away from the observer. An afterimage is return. A pale afterimage is bright return - added signal, and the most conspicuous possible thing to leave hanging in the air, on a practitioner whose other discipline on the same sheet is not being seen. The effect the page describes has a correct and much simpler mechanism already present in its primary current: cooling humid air below its dew point precipitates water, and below freezing it nucleates ice crystals, producing exactly the white trail that hangs and disperses - the same physics as a contrail or the fog off liquid nitrogen. No second Wellspring is needed to produce it. The page's accompanying detail is also correct and also Vohrin's: 'a faint chime carries where ice forms and fractures in the same instant' is differential thermal contraction cracking a thin ice layer as fast as it forms. So Tenebra on this page is credited with an effect its law forbids, while the effect itself is already explained by the current the page has declared primary.

options.option: Credit the pale arc to condensation under Vohrin and reassign Tenebra to the approach, as the sister page does.
options.changes: Makes both currents do what their registers say; costs the page the phrase 'Tenebra-thinned residue', and moves Tenebra's contribution from the visible aftermath to the closing, where the Ambush Art already places it.

options.option: Keep Tenebra on the arc and invert the effect: the strike-path is harder to see rather than easier, a dark line rather than a pale one.
options.changes: Consistent with the register and genuinely eerie; loses the condensation trail, which is the physically correct observation, and removes the page's best tell.

options.option: Drop Tenebra from this page entirely and run it as a single-current working.
options.changes: Simplest, and reduces a harmonisation count the card already flags as above his Tempering Capacity; costs the page its Limina half and the cross-link to his ambush discipline.

options.option: Rule that Tenebra may be run in reverse - as deliberate signature projection rather than suppression - and say so in the register.
options.changes: Would legitimise this page and give the corpus a named use for inverted currents, which it does not currently have; it also weakens Tenebra's counterplay profile everywhere, since a practitioner who can project is harder to locate by absence.

page: (all Vohrin workings; stated here from Winter Rend and Vorynn Execution Strike)
quote_a: **Cost** · Mild numbness through his own arms after the strike.
quote_b: **Vohrin** · Caloria. **The cold law.** *Heat's absence, held as a discipline rather than suffered as a condition.*
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Draven Kael Vorrick · The Beast Slayer.md:45
why: Cold is not a substance and cannot be emitted; a cold working is the acceptance of heat, which the card's own gloss states precisely ('heat's absence, held as a discipline rather than suffered as a condition'). A heat sink therefore has two ends, and every joule taken out of a target has to arrive somewhere. The corpus prices the cold end and never locates the hot one. This page: 'Mild numbness through his own arms after the strike' - which is physiologically the right symptom for a limb held cold, since peripheral nerve conduction falls about 1.5-2 m/s per degree and fails below roughly 7-10 C. The sister page: 'a controlled, directional heat-sink running through Draven's own ignited musculature', which names the conduit and not the reservoir. No register, no card and no technique page anywhere says where the accepted heat is rejected. At the scale a sweep can actually reach the question is academic - about 21 kJ into a 100 kg man is 0.06 K - but it becomes a hard ceiling as soon as a working claims anything larger: freezing 1 kg of another person deposits about 340 kJ, which is roughly 1 K of core temperature, and 3 kg is about 3 K, taking a practitioner from 37 C to 40 C and heat illness. That is a real, derivable limit on every cold working in the corpus and nothing states it. Cinerion, already on this practitioner's card, is the nearest thing to an answer - 'retunes the Shell to metabolize its own combustion products, harvesting from expenditure what other practitioners simply vent' - but it is used on these pages for remnants and for compounding the cold, not for the waste-heat problem.

options.option: State a rejection path for cold workings - into the Shell, into the ground, into the Aether stratum - and price it.
options.changes: Closes the gap for every Vohrin and Caloria cold page at once and introduces a real ceiling on how much a practitioner can freeze in an engagement, which is a counterplay route (make him take a lot) that does not currently exist.

options.option: Rule that Cinerion's metabolisation clause covers waste heat, making a Cinerion harmonisation the prerequisite for sustained cold work.
options.changes: Uses a current already on the card, explains why these two currents keep appearing together, and would make any cold practitioner without Cinerion sharply limited - a large change to several sheets.

options.option: Rule that the balance closes at the Aether stratum and the practitioner never receives the heat at all.
options.changes: Consistent with Two Sets of Books ('a working's energy budget balances at the Aether stratum and not at the Essence one') and removes the limit entirely; also removes the reason this page's own stated cost - numbness in his arms - would exist.

options.option: Leave it unstated and note on the pages that the rejection path is not recorded.
options.changes: Costs nothing and makes it a known open question; leaves every cold working in the corpus unpriceable in the one variable that bounds it.

quote_a: **Cost** · **Mild numbness in his own arms afterward.** *The discipline exacts its toll on the hand that drew the cold through.*
quote_b: **Cost** · **Every use tears fibre along the ignition path.** *Chained further, the tear compounds; his own count puts the Essence toll near a fifth of what he is carrying per use.*
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Vorynn Execution Strike.md:20
why: The working is an A-Grade area attack across a two-metre arc that cracks armour by thermal shock and cools flesh along its path, delivered instantaneously, with no stated usage cap and no resource figure. Its entire cost is 'Mild numbness in his own arms afterward. The discipline exacts its toll on the hand that drew the cold through.' That is a sensation that clears, and under the standing drawback rule a strain alone is not treated as a cost. The comparison that makes it a fairness failure rather than an oversight is on the same practitioner and the same primary current: Vorynn Execution Strike charges 'Every use tears fibre along the ignition path. Chained further, the tear compounds; his own count puts the Essence toll near a fifth of what he is carrying per use' - a structural cost that compounds and a stated fraction of reserve that makes Essence Starvation computable. The corpus demonstrably knows how to price a Vohrin working on this man, on a page written for the same card, and this page does not. There is also a cost available that would be specific to this working rather than borrowed: the heat taken out of the target has to arrive somewhere, and nothing states where (SA-GAP-WINTER-HOT-END), which at any scale above the trivial is a hard limit on how many times the arc can be drawn in an enclosed space.

options.option: Price the cost as its sister page does - a stated fraction of reserve per use, plus a compounding structural cost when chained.
options.changes: Brings two pages on one practitioner into line, makes Essence Starvation computable for this working too, and gives an opponent a clock; costs nothing in mechanism.

options.option: Make the cost thermal and specific: each sweep deposits the heat it removed, with a stated ceiling on sweeps before the practitioner is overheating.
options.changes: Closes the fairness gap and SA-GAP-WINTER-HOT-END with one decision, and produces an unusual and very playable limit - the working gets weaker the longer the fight and the smaller the room.

options.option: Cap the working at a stated number of uses per engagement.
options.changes: Crude but immediate; introduces a usage-cap mechanic the system does not state in general terms.

options.option: Accept the numbness as the cost on the grounds that the working's real limit is its two-metre reach.
options.changes: No edit, and leaves an area attack that cracks armour freely repeatable at no price; the reach limit is real but it is a positioning constraint rather than a cost, and the register is explicit that those are different things.

quote_a: **Radius** requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed A, Stage VI to exceed A for partial projection outward, and Stage VII to exceed S for boundary expansion speed.
path_a: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:146
quote_b: **Path** · Spirit dominant, Fate secondary, Body tertiary.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Francis Alexander · The Crimson Dirge of Atonement.md:43
why: Three of the five Sub-Stats this working's own FOW line names as governing gate on Attraction Path at Part Seven, and Francis's card carries no Attraction Path at any weight. The FOW line is 'Governing Primary: Dominion (Radius, Sovereignty, Command), primary; Harmonics (Empathy, Suppression), secondary' (World Echelon.md:49). Part Seven: Radius 'requires Attraction Path at Stage V to exceed A, Stage VI to exceed A for partial projection outward, and Stage VII to exceed S for boundary expansion speed' (:146); Command 'requires Attraction Path at Stage VIII to exceed SS' (:146); Empathy 'requires Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C' (:134). The page is EX-Grade at Stage XIV and the card puts Dominion at 1,480 of a 1,500 ceiling, so he is far past A, SS and C, and all three thresholds bind rather than sitting unreached. The card's Path line is 'Spirit dominant, Fate secondary, Body tertiary'. The two gates he does meet are exactly the two that do not want Attraction: Sovereignty 'requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A, and Stage IX to exceed SSS' (:146), Fate secondary, and Suppression 'requires Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed A' (:134), Spirit dominant - which is a pattern rather than a coincidence, and is what makes the absence look structural. Two unrelated pages derive the same requirement independently. The taxonomy makes the working's own category, Concordia, need 'Attraction-side reach to hold that alignment as a lasting Domain' (Unified Taxonom.md:206). And the plane the card says is merged with is organised 'By bond' and lit by 'Recognition' (The Crossing:31 table), while the Four Paths register says 'Attraction Path routes through bond and recognition' (Four Paths:18). Three derivations from three unrelated pages that World Echelon is an Attraction Path working, against a card that carries none. Note what is NOT in doubt: Grade and Stage agree with each other and with the page (EX, 1,201-1,500, Dominion 1,480).

options.option: Give Francis's card an Attraction Path weight.
options.changes: Satisfies all three gates at a stroke and matches what three unrelated pages already derive; costs the card its 'Spirit dominant, Fate secondary, Body tertiary' line, and complicates the rough-seat framing the page's 'What nobody knows' leans on, since a three-Path seat is a different object from a two-Path one.

options.option: Re-file the working's Governing Primary to the Sub-Stats he can carry - Dominion Sovereignty and Harmonics Suppression - and drop Radius, Command and Empathy.
