options.changes: Keeps the card untouched and leaves the page internally consistent; costs the working its five kilometres as a stated Dominion reach, so something else on the page has to state where the radius comes from, and Empathy was the Sub-Stat doing the emotional weighing.

options.option: Rule that a Domain merged onto the Soul Plane is not measured by Dominion Radius at all, because that plane is organised by bond rather than distance.
options.changes: Closes this and SA-CROSS-ECHELON-DISTANCE-VS-BOND with one decision and is faithful to the cosmology; requires a bond-count measure the system does not currently have, though the card supplies a candidate figure in 'four thousand subjugated spiritual dominions'.

options.option: Rule that Part Seven's Path gates state certification requirements rather than capability requirements.
options.changes: Would legitimise this page and several others in the batch at once, and has textual support in the page's own 'Whether he has ever actually been assayed for a certificate that would say so ... is not on record'; it also removes the Path system's only teeth everywhere in the corpus, which is a very large change to make from one technique page.

quote_a: **Mechanism** · The merger behaves like forcing a phase transition across a coupled oscillator network, the Kuramoto model for synchronisation. Judicium reads which beings and Wellsprings in range are out of phase with the court's verdict-rhythm; the Domain then drives the whole field toward one synchronised phase, and what would be ordinary variance in emotion becomes, once everything shares one reference phase, a measurable deviation the court reads as evidence.
quote_b: The Soul Plane does not speak in vibration. It does not carry pressure or temperature or the acoustic signatures a Physical Plane sensory Wellspring is built to catalogue.
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:21
why: The mechanism needs vibration and the plane it is run on does not carry any. A Kuramoto network is defined over units that each have a phase and a natural frequency: the state variable IS an oscillation, and without one there is nothing for sin(theta_j - theta_i) to act on. The page declares 'Physics Domain: Electromagnetism, primary' (:27) and merges the Domain with the plane the card names as the Soul Plane (card:106). The cosmology says of that plane, in the same sentence pair, that it 'does not speak in vibration' and that what light is there is not radiation but 'Recognition. ... It does not illuminate from outside. It recognises from inside' (The Crossing:21, :31 table). So the working's carrier (electromagnetic), its state variable (phase of an oscillation) and its coupling law (symmetric sinusoidal) are all Physical Plane objects asserted across a boundary the same cosmology page exists to describe. This is not a small mismatch to be waved through: it is the difference between a field that has a frequency spectrum and one that has a bond graph, and every derived figure on the page - the 16.7 microsecond crossing time at c, the 2.4 million crossings in the window, the lock threshold K_c = 2/(pi g(0)) - is computed in the first of those and spent in the second.

options.option: Keep the mechanism and move the field: the Tribunal reads the Soul Plane from the Physical Plane rather than merging with it.
options.changes: Every physical figure on the page becomes valid as written, and Judicium - a spectroscopic law of identification - is doing exactly what its register says it does; costs the page its 'merges' language, which the Codex line says matches the card 'exactly', and costs the working its claim on the records and entities there.

options.option: Restate the mechanism in the plane's own currency: a consensus process over a bond graph rather than phase-locking over a frequency population.
options.changes: Faithful to the cosmology and keeps the merge; the mathematics is still real (consensus dynamics on a graph has its own threshold in the graph's algebraic connectivity), so nothing is lost in rigour, but the page loses the Kuramoto name it gets right and the four physical figures that follow from it.

options.option: Rule that a merged Domain imports the Physical Plane's vibrational structure into the region for the duration, and that this importing is what the merge IS.
options.changes: Saves the page as written and gives the corpus a general account of what Domain merger means, which it does not have; it also makes every Domain-merge working a much larger metaphysical claim than its page states, and the cosmology page would need to say so.

options.option: Log it and leave the plane mismatch unexplained on the page.
options.changes: Costs nothing now and keeps the working's best-argued physics intact; leaves the single most load-bearing claim on the page - which plane this happens on - unadjudicable, and with it the radius, the propagation figures and the threshold.

quote_a: **Attraction Layer** · Vast and one-directional. Fifty-seven Wellsprings under partial siphon and four thousand subjugated spiritual dominions, every bond pointing inward. *Nothing on it points back.*
path_a: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Francis Alexander · The Crimson Dirge of Atonement.md:41

path_b: wiki/Techniques/World Echelon.md:38
why: Kuramoto coupling is symmetric and the layer it is run through is declared one-directional. In the model, oscillator i pulls on j through sin(theta_j - theta_i) and j pulls back on i through sin(theta_i - theta_j): the same coefficient, opposite sign. There is no one-way phase coupling in the model, and there is none in linear physics generally - the same objection is already on record in this batch against Symphonia Ascendant, that there is no one-way resonant coupling. The card's Attraction Layer is 'Vast and one-directional. ... every bond pointing inward. Nothing on it points back.' A synchronisation law run over bonds on which nothing points back is asking a bidirectional law to behave unidirectionally, and the two sentences cannot both be true as written. Note the consequence the page does not draw: under a symmetric law the caster is a node like any other, so the court synchronises him too, and there is no clause on the page excluding him - which is a genuine and interesting cost, and it is precisely what the card's one-directional layer denies. There is also a reading that saves both, which the corpus does not state anywhere: that one-directionality is a claim about net TRANSFER (the siphon) and not about coupling, so bonds may carry phase both ways while value flows one way. Physically that reading is clean - a phase coupling moves no energy on average - and it is the reading this page needs.

options.option: Rule that the Attraction Layer's one-directionality governs net transfer, not coupling: bonds carry phase both ways, value flows inward only.
options.changes: Saves both sentences at once, is physically correct because phase coupling is nearly energy-free, and explains why a five-kilometre phase working is affordable for a man whose layer is a siphon; it also concedes that anything he couples to can read him, which is a new Counterplay route on every Attraction-Layer practitioner.

options.option: Replace Kuramoto with master-slave entrainment: a single strong drive that oscillators lock to, which genuinely is one-directional.
options.changes: Matches the card exactly and hands the reader the Arnold tongue detuning counter in plain sight; costs the page the population-coupling and the K_c threshold theorem, and a drive strong enough to entrain a district is no longer the cheap phase-setting working that made five kilometres plausible.

options.option: State on the page that Francis is inside his own court and synchronised with it.
options.changes: Free, honest to the mechanism, and gives an opponent the court's reference phase by watching the man; it contradicts the card's 'Nothing on it points back' unless that line is narrowed first.

options.option: Log it and leave both sentences standing.
options.changes: No edit; leaves the corpus with a second instance of the same physics error it has already logged once, which makes it a pattern rather than a slip.

quote_a: **Effect** · Francis merges his personal Tribunal Domain with the local Spirit World across a five-kilometre radius for roughly forty seconds, folding the space into court geometry and converting every emotion caught inside into weighed evidence.
quote_b: | **Organisation** | By distance | **By bond** |
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand.md:35
why: The page states a distance for a field on a plane the cosmology organises by bond. The Effect line gives 'a five-kilometre radius'; the Crossing's property table gives Organisation as 'By distance' on the Physical Plane and 'By bond' on the Soul Plane, and Movement likewise as 'Arrival at the point of connection rather than travel toward it'. A sphere of radius 5,000 m therefore does not name a well-formed region on the far side of the merge: it is a boundary specified in a coordinate the target plane does not use, which under the standard's own failure taxonomy is a Boundary fault rather than a flavour problem. What makes this worth logging rather than shrugging at is that the corpus already holds the figure a bond-organised reach would need: the card's Attraction Layer carries 'four thousand subjugated spiritual dominions' (card:41), a count of bonds, and the card's own scale line for the Tribunal is stated in kilometres beside it. So the page had both currencies available and chose the one that does not apply. Note this conflict and SA-PHYS-ECHELON-SOUL-PLANE-VIBRATION are the same boundary read two ways, and any ruling on which plane hosts the field disposes of both.

options.option: State the working's reach in bonds - a number of dominions, entities or records held - and let the physical footprint follow from wherever those bonds land.
options.changes: Faithful to the cosmology, uses a figure the card already carries, and produces a much more interesting working whose reach is a function of whom he has already bound; costs the page its clean five kilometres and makes the area unpredictable to a reader, which cuts against stating limits plainly.

options.option: Rule that a merged Domain imposes the Physical Plane's metric on the merged region, so a radius is well-formed inside it.
options.changes: Saves the page as written and settles a question every Domain-merge working will raise; it is a large cosmological claim to make from a technique page, and it partly undoes the Crossing page's central distinction.

options.option: State both: a physical footprint in metres and a bond reach, with the smaller of the two binding.
options.changes: Rigorous, gives an opponent two things to attack instead of one, and makes the working weaker in exactly the places it should be weak; costs the page a second figure that nothing in the source supports, so the bond number would have to be ruled rather than found.

options.option: Log it and leave the radius as a physical-plane approximation.
options.changes: No edit, and the figure remains usable at the table; leaves the boundary formally ill-specified, which is the one thing the glyph standard says a working cannot afford.

quote_a: **Effect** · Francis merges his personal Tribunal Domain with the local Spirit World across a five-kilometre radius for roughly forty seconds, folding the space into court geometry and converting every emotion caught inside into weighed evidence.
quote_b: With World Echelon the Tribunal merges with the Soul Plane and he holds the spiritual entities and the records there.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Francis Alexander · The Crimson Dirge of Atonement.md:106
why: The page and the card name different places. The page merges the Tribunal with 'the local Spirit World', twice (:17 and :36); the card, describing this working by name, says 'With World Echelon the Tribunal merges with the Soul Plane and he holds the spiritual entities and the records there', and sizes the Tribunal as 'a Verdict Domain layered over the Soul Plane'. 'Spirit World' occurs in exactly one file in the mirror, which is this page: grep -rl 'Spirit World' wiki/ returns wiki/Techniques/World Echelon.md and nothing else. Per CONTINUE.md's staleness protocol the absence is canon's and not the mirror's - wiki/ last committed 2026-09-25 18:40, after this page's last_edited of 2026-09-12 and after the card's of 2026-09-24. The choice is not cosmetic. 'Soul Plane' has a cosmology page that states three properties this working's mechanism has to survive (no vibration, light as recognition, organisation by bond), which is what SA-PHYS-ECHELON-SOUL-PLANE-VIBRATION and SA-CROSS-ECHELON-DISTANCE-VS-BOND turn on. If 'Spirit World' is instead a third place, then nothing in canon describes it, and the working becomes unadjudicable in the friendliest possible way: no page can contradict it because no page mentions it.

options.option: Correct the page to 'Soul Plane', the card's term and the attested one.
options.changes: Costs one word twice and puts the working inside a described cosmology; it also immediately brings the Crossing page's three properties to bear, which is where the page's real trouble is, so this option makes two other conflicts sharper rather than softer.

options.option: Establish 'Spirit World' in the register as a distinct layer, with its own properties.
options.changes: Keeps the page's wording and could be genuinely useful if the cosmology wants a near-side layer between the Physical Plane and the Soul Plane; it is a new cosmological object created to resolve a technique page's word choice, and every other page that says 'Soul Plane' would need checking against it.

options.option: Rule 'Spirit World' a colloquial synonym for the Soul Plane and say so once in the register.
options.changes: Cheapest fix, keeps both texts as written, and is plausible in-world as the way practitioners talk; it means the Crossing page's constraints apply in full, so it is option one's consequence without option one's edit.

options.option: Log it and leave the two terms standing.
options.changes: No edit; leaves the page's governing plane a matter of which document a reader picks up first, and leaves two other conflicts on this page formally unresolvable because their premise is which plane this is.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Five-kilometre radius, as given. Roughly forty seconds sustained (8 turns at 5 seconds per turn).
quote_b: *Within a fifty-kilometre law field, fifteen kilometres of which is the Crimson Tribunal itself, a Verdict Domain layered over the Soul Plane that determines guilt and converts emotion, Aether and sin into destructive law matrices.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Francis Alexander · The Crimson Dirge of Atonement.md:106
why: The card sizes the Crimson Tribunal at fifteen kilometres standing; the technique that merges that same Tribunal with the plane states five. The card: 'Within a fifty-kilometre law field, fifteen kilometres of which is the Crimson Tribunal itself, a Verdict Domain layered over the Soul Plane'. The page: 'Five-kilometre radius, as given.' Three readings are available and the page states none of them: that the working projects a fraction of the standing Tribunal; that the five kilometres is a merged core inside a fifteen-kilometre Tribunal; or that the figures simply disagree. The discrepancy is larger than it looks, because these are radii and the working is a volume claim: (15/5)^3 = 27, so the card's Tribunal is twenty-seven times the volume of the page's field, and the page's own comparison figure - 125 times Dirge Ascension's kilometre, by the cube of five - shows the account is already reasoning in volumes. Note this is a genuine two-source disagreement about a number, which is the one thing the standing rules say is never resolved inside an account.

options.option: Rule that the five kilometres is the merged core inside the standing fifteen-kilometre Tribunal, and say so on the page.
options.changes: Reconciles both figures with no number changed, and gives the working a shape worth having - a court within a court, with a mechanically distinct inner region; it needs the page to state what the outer twelve kilometres of Tribunal is doing during the forty seconds.

options.option: Correct the page to fifteen kilometres, matching the card.
options.changes: Card beats technique page as the older and more specific source; multiplies the field's volume by twenty-seven, which does not by itself break the physics because phase-setting is cheap and the propagation delay at 15 km is still only 50 microseconds, but it invalidates every derived figure in the account's ledger.

options.option: Correct the card to five kilometres.
options.changes: Keeps the technique page and the account's arithmetic intact; edits a character card on the authority of a technique page, and the card's figure is load-bearing for the fifty-kilometre law field it sits inside.

options.option: Log it and leave both figures standing, with the page's five used for this working.
options.changes: No edit and the table can still run the working; leaves the corpus stating two sizes for one Domain, which is exactly the kind of number a reader will look up.

quote_b: **Mechanism** · The merger behaves like forcing a phase transition across a coupled oscillator network, the Kuramoto model for synchronisation. Judicium reads which beings and Wellsprings in range are out of phase with the court's verdict-rhythm; the Domain then drives the whole field toward one synchronised phase, and what would be ordinary variance in emotion becomes, once everything shares one reference phase, a measurable deviation the court reads as evidence.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/World Echelon.md:38
why: The category's defining requirement and the working's mechanism are contradictory as worded. Concordia is 'The Spirit-Attraction Apex because it requires both: Spirit-side precision to align many Essence Cores WITHOUT FLATTENING ANY, and Attraction-side reach to hold that alignment as a lasting Domain'. The mechanism 'drives the whole field toward one synchronised phase'. For a phase population, flattening is the only thing that sentence can mean: the Kuramoto order parameter r running from 0 to 1 measures precisely the collapse of the phase distribution onto a single value, and a locked field has one phase where it had a spread. The page's Codex line asserts the opposite, that Concordia matches 'the card's own "merges" language exactly' (:28). There is a reading that saves it, and it is worth stating because the page does not: phases flatten while amplitudes and contents do not, and the taxonomy never says which quantity must survive. The page's own Target Response supports that reading - emotion 'becomes a synchronised, weighed quantity', keeping its content and losing its timing - so the material for the defence is on the page and the page does not make it. There is also a stronger physical form of the defence: r rises continuously above K_c, so a court could hold r = 0.4 and flatten nothing fully, which is also the only version that leaves variance left to measure.

options.option: Rule that Concordia's 'without flattening any' governs contents and amplitudes, not phase, and state that in the taxonomy.
options.changes: Saves this page and gives the category a test a reader can actually apply to the next Concordia working; it narrows a line that currently reads as a promise about preserving individuality, which is part of why the category reads as a healing one.

options.option: State the working as partial synchronisation - an order parameter held below full lock, a phase band rather than a phase.
options.changes: The best fit to both texts: it is real Kuramoto behaviour above the threshold, it literally does not flatten any oscillator, and it is the only version that leaves the deviation the court needs to read as evidence; costs the page its all-or-nothing framing.

options.option: Re-file the working out of Concordia into a domination-side category and drop the Apex claim.
options.changes: Honest to what the mechanism does and consistent with the Heresiology's 'transformation of review into domination' already logged against this page; costs the page its category line and the Attraction-side reach the taxonomy was supplying, which is one of the three independent derivations in SA-NUM-ECHELON-ATTRACTION-GATE.

options.option: Log it and leave the category claim standing.
options.changes: No edit; leaves the corpus's healing-and-alignment Apex category exemplified by a non-consensual mass-weighing working, which will read as the category's meaning to anyone who finds this page first.

quote_a: **Wellspring** · Judicium (primary); fifty-seven of the Sixty Wellsprings, injured per the Heresiology's Wellspring Injury framework, secondary and unspecified
quote_b: | **Judicium** *order, measure, and consequence* | **Moralization of extermination** · transformation of review into domination · **reclassification of cruelty as cleansing** | **Law without mercy becomes burnished sadism. Mercy without law becomes indulgent chaos.** Judicium injury is most visible **where either side is used to excuse the other's absence** |
path_b: wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md:172
why: The page cites the Heresiology as its authority for fifty-seven injured secondary Wellsprings while its PRIMARY performs, unremarked, the one corruption that same document names for that primary. The Heresiology's table Wellsprings Most Frequently Injured (:166) names five, and Judicium is one of them, with its common corruptions given as 'Moralization of extermination - transformation of review into domination - reclassification of cruelty as cleansing' and its doctrine as 'Law without mercy becomes burnished sadism. ... Judicium injury is most visible where either side is used to excuse the other's absence' (:172). World Echelon's own Effect line is review made into domination in the most literal available sense: it converts 'every emotion caught inside into weighed evidence' across five kilometres, with nobody inside it party to the proceeding, which is also the Accord's consent position breached (Two Sets of Books, section IV). Judicium's register law is a law of identification, not of compulsion - 'the practitioner reads the characteristic lines of a Crystal, a technique, or a lie, and identifies composition from signature alone' (Fulguria:22) - so the compulsion half of this working has no support in the Wellspring it names. This may well be deliberate characterisation rather than an error: the card's trajectory is 'toward the Law of Final Mercy, a cosmic force that defines atonement as annihilation' (card:125), which is the Heresiology's doctrine line almost word for word. What is missing is any statement anywhere that this Judicium is itself injured.

options.option: State on the page that Francis's Judicium is injured under the Heresiology's own framework - the primary being one of the fifty-eight, not an intact current.
options.changes: Costs nothing mechanically, turns the page's strongest theme into something a reader can look up, and makes the Heresiology's doctrine line a live Counterplay hook (mercy as the seam in a court held without it); it does commit the character's central current to a corrupted state, which other pages about him would need to agree with.

options.option: Rule that a Wellspring can be used in its corrupted mode without being injured, and state the difference.
options.changes: Preserves an intact primary and gives the corpus a distinction it currently lacks between doing the corrupt thing and being the corrupted practitioner; it weakens the Heresiology's diagnostic value, since the doctrine column reads as a test and this makes it a tendency.

options.option: Attach a mechanical consequence to injured-primary use and price it here.
options.changes: Gives the working the hard cost its Cost line lacks and connects two documents that currently only gesture at each other; it is a new system-wide mechanic introduced from a single technique page, which is a large scope for one ruling.

options.option: Log it and leave the page's Wellspring line as written.
options.changes: No edit; leaves a page that cites the Heresiology in one clause and contradicts its Judicium row in the next, which is the kind of seam the corpus exists to catch.

path_b: wiki/Techniques/World Echelon.md:38
why: Two clauses on the same page describe two different instruments, and only one of them can be built out of the stated mechanism. The Effect line converts 'every emotion caught inside into weighed evidence'. The Mechanism says the evidence is 'a measurable deviation' from a shared reference phase. Evidence-as-deviation is a differential measure, and a differential measure has a blind spot at each end of its own scale. A mind whose phase already sits at the court's reference has deviation zero and yields no evidence at all. A mind whose natural frequency lies outside the lock range never couples in the first place - entrainment holds only inside the Arnold tongue, whose width is set by the coupling strength - so it registers no deviation either, and is conspicuous only by absence. Under the page's own mechanism, therefore, exactly the middle band of the population is legible: close enough to be caught, far enough to read. 'Every emotion' is false by the mechanism the page itself supplies, and the Target Response line (:40) repeats the error ('Anyone caught inside'). The cheap fix is that the Effect line is the wrong one, not the Mechanism: the Mechanism is the best-argued clause on the page, and the blind spots it implies are the working's most playable feature and the source of a real sub-peer counter (see SA-FAIR-ECHELON-NO-SUB-PEER-ROUTE).

options.option: Correct the Effect and Target Response lines to state what the Mechanism states: emotion becomes legible as deviation from the court's phase, blind at both ends of the scale.
options.changes: Makes the page self-consistent, costs no mechanism, and hands a reader a counter the mathematics already implies; the working stops being a guaranteed mass-read, which is a real reduction in power at Zenith.

options.option: Rule that failing to couple is itself evidence - contumacy - as a real court treats a refusal to appear.
options.changes: Elegant, in register, and closes the blind spot at the far end while leaving the near end open; it also makes the detuning counter costly rather than free, which is better play than either extreme.

options.option: Keep 'every' and add an absolute reading pass alongside the differential one, priced separately.
options.changes: Preserves the page's scope and is defensible, since Judicium's register law is absolute spectroscopy ('no substance can present another's spectrum') rather than differential; it makes the working two workings, and the second one has no stated cost, no threshold and no counter.

options.option: Log it and leave both clauses standing.
options.changes: No edit; leaves the page's headline claim contradicted by its own mechanism section four lines later, and leaves the table with no answer to a player who asks what the court reads off a perfectly calm man.

quote_a: **Numerical Effect** · Five-kilometre radius, as given. Roughly forty seconds sustained (8 turns at 5 seconds per turn).
quote_b: **Effect** · Francis steps into a proto-Archonic state for 45 seconds, shedding his mortal ceiling; local physics inside a one-kilometre radius run on rewritten equations for the duration, and his Aether output spikes to 2,800,000 AU/s.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Dirge Ascension.md:17
why: The working has no AU/s figure, and the only figure the batch holds for this practitioner is measured in the one state this working forbids. Dirge Ascension states 'his Aether output spikes to 2,800,000 AU/s' for a proto-Archonic state in which, in the same sentence, he is 'shedding his mortal ceiling'. World Echelon's Limit is 'Cannot be run alongside Dirge Ascension; the two Domains do not coexist' (:19), so the number cannot be borrowed: it belongs to a state this page excludes by its own text. The consequences run down the whole ledger. Flux Density for this working is null (see SA-NUM-FRANCIS-ASCENDED-FLUX), EU spent is null, the starvation margin is null, and R44-2's relation AU/s = Flux Density x eta cannot be checked here in either direction, because two of its three terms are missing and the third, eta 0.93, is itself out of band. Note that borrowing an area-scaled figure from another page would be wrong even if one existed: a synchronisation working sets phases and not amplitudes, so its cost does not scale with the volume it covers, which is the entire reason a five-kilometre field is affordable at all. The real cost driver the physics names is the population's emotional variance through K_c = 2/(pi g(0)), and the system has no measure of that.

options.option: State a resting AU/s for Francis on his card, distinct from the ascended figure.
options.changes: Closes this gap and SA-NUM-FRANCIS-ASCENDED-FLUX together, and gives the corpus its first stated resting/ascended pair, which several other pages will want; it is a new number and must be ruled rather than derived, since nothing in the source implies a ratio.

options.option: State the working's own output on the page.
options.changes: Narrowest fix, makes this page checkable, and leaves the card alone; it does not help the other Francis workings, and an AU/s for a working whose joules come from the population is a slightly odd quantity to state.

options.option: Rule that phase-setting workings are priced by population and variance rather than by AU/s, and give the ledger a field for it.
options.changes: The honest answer to the physics, and it would make a divided district genuinely harder to convene a court over, which is excellent play; it needs a crowd-variance measure the system does not have, so it is the largest of the four options.

options.option: Log it and leave the working unpriced.
options.changes: No edit; the largest-area working in the batch stays with no output, no expenditure and no starvation margin, so nothing about its cost can be adjudicated at the table.

quote_a: **Consequence** · The synchronisation does not release cleanly, hence the local Principle drift once the working ends; the field takes time to de-phase back to ordinary variance.
quote_b: **Cost** · High soul-heating and a local Principle drift that outlasts the working itself.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/World Echelon.md:18
why: The page's after-effect is correct physics and carries no number. 'The synchronisation does not release cleanly ... the field takes time to de-phase back to ordinary variance' is critical slowing down: near a synchronisation transition the leading eigenvalue goes to zero and the relaxation time diverges, and the same divergence has been measured at abrupt desynchronisation as well. It is the one clause on the page a physicist would have predicted from the mechanism before reading it. What is missing is both time constants: the lock time tau, and the de-phase time, which is of order tau. Without them the stated cost has no duration, no persistence radius and no consequence - and note that this half of the invoice is billed to the district and not to the caster, since 'high soul-heating' is his and 'a local Principle drift that outlasts the working itself' is the quarter's. It is also the number an opponent most needs, because the drift window is the only interval in which the court's reference phase is still readable off the population after Francis has stopped paying for it, and the register's general prohibition on waiting a practitioner out ('a plan that consists of surviving until he tires is a plan to be killed by a tired man') does not apply to a window the page itself states.

options.option: State the de-phase time as a multiple of the lock time, and let the lock time follow from the population's variance.
options.changes: One figure gives the page a real aftermath, a real cost and a Counterplay window, and it is the form the physics actually takes; it depends on the crowd-variance measure the system does not have, so in practice the multiple would be stated and the base assumed.

options.option: State a flat drift duration on the page.
options.changes: Cheapest and immediately usable at the table; loses the property that makes the effect interesting, namely that a harder court drifts longer.

options.option: Rule that Principle drift resolves at a stated event rather than after a stated time.
options.changes: Fits a world that already thinks in tides and thresholds, and gives the drift a narrative shape instead of a stopwatch; it makes the aftermath's length a scheduling question, which may be better or worse play depending on the scene.

options.option: Log it and leave the drift undurated.
options.changes: No edit; the page keeps its best line and the district keeps an aftermath nobody can adjudicate, including the people inside it, who by the page's own account cannot tell the drift from their own mood.

page: (batch-wide for Francis Alexander; stated here from World Echelon)
quote_a: | Francis Alexander | XIV Zenith | 470 | EX, ceiling 1,500 | 0.93 | 0.95–1.2 ✗ | "Absolute Crystal" | 2,800,000 (`Dirge Ascension`) | 2,800,000 ÷ 0.93 = **3,010,753 EU/g** |
quote_b: **Effect** · Francis steps into a proto-Archonic state for 45 seconds, shedding his mortal ceiling; local physics inside a one-kilometre radius run on rewritten equations for the duration, and his Aether output spikes to 2,800,000 AU/s.
path_b: wiki/Techniques/Dirge Ascension.md:17
why: The batch's Flux Density for Francis is derived from an ascended output and then used as a baseline Crystal property. The method table carries 2,800,000 / 0.93 = 3,010,753 EU/g, and the 2,800,000 is stated by Dirge Ascension for a proto-Archonic state in which the same sentence has him 'shedding his mortal ceiling'. A Flux Density is a property of the Crystal; derived from an ascended output it is the ASCENDED Flux Density, and his resting figure is unknown. Every downstream use of 3,010,753 EU/g for a non-ascended working therefore overstates him by whatever Dirge Ascension multiplies - a factor nothing in the corpus states. World Echelon is where it bites hardest, because its Limit forbids the ascended state outright (:19), so the page is priced with a figure its own text excludes. Note precisely what this does NOT touch: R44-2's AU/s = Flux Density x eta is an identity among the three quantities and is satisfied by these numbers as they stand. The claim here is only that all three belong to the ascended state together, and that the corpus holds no resting member of the triple for this practitioner.

options.option: Mark 3,010,753 EU/g as the ascended figure in the method table and leave his resting Flux Density null until a source states one.
options.changes: Accurate, costs no number and stops the figure propagating into workings that exclude the ascended state; it leaves every non-Dirge Francis page unpriceable, which is the honest position but a wide one.

options.option: State a resting AU/s on the card and recompute Flux Density from it.
options.changes: Closes this and SA-GAP-ECHELON-AUS with one figure and restores pricing across all his workings; the resting AU/s has to be ruled, since nothing in the source implies a ratio between resting and ascended output.

options.option: Rule that Dirge Ascension raises output without changing Flux Density - the spike coming from eta or from the environment co-authoring above eta 1.0 - so 3,010,753 EU/g is his baseline after all.
options.changes: Saves every downstream figure at a stroke and is mechanically coherent with Part Nineteen's statement that above eta 1.0 the environment becomes a co-author; it requires Dirge Ascension to say where the spike comes from, and an eta above 1.0 sits oddly with a card that states 0.93.

options.option: Log it and keep using 3,010,753 EU/g as his baseline.
options.changes: No edit and the batch's arithmetic stays uniform; every figure derived for a non-ascended Francis working is then an ascended figure wearing a resting label, which is the sort of error that compounds silently across a corpus.

quote_a: **Counter** · A Sovereign-tier Spirit Path practitioner, or a transcendent-grade Harmonics Empathy field (Catharsis- or Benediction-class), can refuse to be weighed at all.
quote_b: Fulguria fails against boiled leather, fired clay, dense fog and a shielded interior. Materia has opinions and no tools on open water. Fluxia cannot act without a medium, so a dry vault is a Fluxia prison. **The counter-Fulguria kit has been leather and ceramic for four centuries and it is not a secret; it is simply cheaper to ignore until somebody dies of it.**
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md:25
why: Both counters the page names sit at or above the caster's own register, so the working offers nothing to anyone below Zenith: 'A Sovereign-tier Spirit Path practitioner, or a transcendent-grade Harmonics Empathy field (Catharsis- or Benediction-class), can refuse to be weighed at all.' That fails the standing requirement that a Counterplay route be findable by a player who reads the right pages, and it fails it unnecessarily, because the mechanism hands over at least three sub-peer routes the page does not name. (i) Terrain: Judicium is a Fulguria Wellspring and the page's own Physics Domain is electromagnetism, and the register says 'Fulguria fails against boiled leather, fired clay, dense fog and a shielded interior. The counter-Fulguria kit has been leather and ceramic for four centuries and it is not a secret' - so the cheapest counter to a five-kilometre tribunal is the quarter it is held over, at a tanner's prices. (ii) Detuning: entrainment holds only inside the Arnold tongue, and an oscillator whose frequency sits outside the lock range never couples however long the drive runs - which against this court means no deviation, and therefore no evidence at all (SA-EM-ECHELON-EVERY-VS-DEVIATION). (iii) Lock: the register's own counter-form 'occupies a limit so no other limit can be set there' (Counterplay:36), and this working's entire boundary is a single scalar limit on how much variance a field may carry, which makes it the textbook target. And a fourth, against the man rather than the field: his card carries Paradox Stasis, 'Every Celestial, regardless of Choir, freezes when presented with two contradictory Oaths of equal metaphysical weight' (card:89), and a court is a machine for surfacing contradictory oaths. None of these requires peer tier. What the page does well, for the record: it states a real opportunity cost (it cannot run with his better working), a real duration, and a real structural weakness in the rough seat.

options.option: Add the three mechanism-level routes - terrain, detuning, Lock - to the page's Counterplay line.
options.changes: Takes the page from failing the fairness test to being one of the better-countered workings in the batch, and costs the working nothing it does not already imply; it does make a Zenith Domain beatable by a well-prepared non-peer, which is the point but is a real reduction in threat.

options.option: Add only the detuning route, since it follows from the stated mechanism and needs no new canon.
options.changes: Minimal and rigorous, and it rewards exactly the player who read the mechanism; leaves the terrain and Lock routes undiscoverable from this page, though both are one hop away in the Counterplay register.

options.option: Keep only the peer counters and rule the working peer-tier-only by design.
options.changes: Internally consistent for a Stage XIV Domain and preserves the character's menace; leaves a five-kilometre non-consensual field with no answer below Sovereign tier, which is the shape of encounter the fairness standard exists to prevent.

options.option: Leave the counters as written and make the working's own cost the lever an opponent pulls (see SA-GAP-ECHELON-DEPHASE-TIME).
options.changes: Turns a fairness gap into a resource fight, which suits a court scene; it depends on a cost figure the page does not currently have, so it cannot be used until that gap is closed.

quote_a: He conducted his sessions during lunar Aether tides, when ambient Resonance naturally quiets
quote_b: Aetheric Density · The concentration of Aether present in a given volume. Sets the ceiling on the AU/s output a practitioner can achieve in that location
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: All three Harmonic branches are limited by a field quantity the system does not name or scale: ambient tonal noise. It is not Aetheric Density, and it constrains the opposite way round — a loud room raises the floor and hides the signal rather than lowering a ceiling on output. The Core Vocabulary has a term and a scale for density and nothing at all for ambient Resonance, so no Harmonic working's field condition can be priced, compared between sites, or checked against a terrain modifier. Caelmorne's whole method is an exploitation of this quantity and the system cannot say by how much.

options.option: Add ambient Resonance to the Core Vocabulary as a named field quantity with a four-condition scale, mirroring the Aetheric Density scale in The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings.
options.changes: Gives every Harmonic working a terrain line and makes 'lunar Aether tide' a named condition; requires deciding what the four conditions are.

options.option: Rule that ambient Resonance is a facet of Aetheric Residue rather than a separate quantity.
options.changes: No new term; makes a district's working history the thing that deafens a Harmonist, which is evocative and makes battlefields the worst places to listen.

options.option: Rule that the constraint is entirely on the practitioner's own Shell output and there is no ambient term at all.
options.changes: Removes the terrain counter from the Harmonic tree and makes Suppression the only variable; the Thick Veil line on Resonant Divination would need rewriting.

options.option: Leave it unscaled and state on the Harmonic Arts page that ambient Resonance is read qualitatively by the practitioner and has never been instrumented.
options.changes: Nothing mechanical; converts the gap into an in-world admission and makes a Measurewright who could instrument it a plot.

quote_a: Therapeutic applications, at Stage VII for diagnostic listening, Stage IX for therapeutic projection, and Stage XI for Fell Chord surgery
quote_b: The Essence account, at all three strata, in diagnostic voice.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: The page states three Temperance Gates and seven named applications and not one number: no EU, no rate, no duration, no range, no Grade, no frequency. The Registry's standard for a proper entry requires the Essence account at all three strata, and the Essence stratum here is empty. Every figure in this account's ledger is therefore null, including for Microharmonic Recalibration and Fell Chord surgery, which are the branch's two most consequential operations.

options.option: Price the branch off the Harmonic Arts page's Temperance Gates, stating an EU band per application at each gate.
options.changes: Creates the first EU figures the Harmonic tree has ever carried; needs a basis, and no EU-by-Stage benchmark exists anywhere (SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA).

options.option: Bill the branch in output rate rather than reserve, as a standing share of AU/s for as long as the listen or the projection holds.
options.changes: Matches the shape of a sustained receptive working and follows the Lumen Dissecans precedent; requires an AU/s figure for at least one named practitioner, and none has a card.

options.option: Rule that receptive Harmonic work is genuinely free and only projection is billed, then price projection alone.
options.changes: Halves the problem and makes diagnosis lawfully unlimited, which fits the consent doctrine and makes the surveillance objection sharper rather than softer.

options.option: Give Caelmorne Halvrein a character card, and derive the branch's figures from it as the Techniques batch derives Serenyra's.
options.changes: One card fixes eta, Flux Density, AU/s and Crystal State for the whole branch; it is also a new character card, which needs its own authorisation.

quote_a: Microharmonic Recalibration — the foundational healing technique, projecting a clean reference tone the patient's own Crystal uses to re-align.
quote_b: It costs something that hurts. EU at a rate that reaches Starvation in a real fight, Harmonics, Coherence, the body, or a vow.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Fairness check 1 fails. The branch can read a stranger's Temperance Stage, Trait list and incipient Crystal collapse without touching them, and can retune a soul's emotional state without their knowledge, and the page bills nothing for any of it. The implied cost — a Shell held quiet as a standing precondition, which Counterplay prices under 'Make him hold Pressure in' — is real but is nowhere stated as an invoice, and the most dangerous application (a projection that can shatter a Crystal) has the emptiest ledger of all.

options.option: Bill diagnostic listening as a standing Harmonics toll rather than EU: the Shell held below its own noise floor costs Harmonics Suppression continuously and fails when the practitioner is tired.
options.changes: Gives the branch a cost that is exhaustible in a scene without inventing an EU figure, and makes a long surveillance shift a real expenditure.

options.option: Bill therapeutic projection in EU at a band per application, and leave diagnosis free.
options.changes: Puts a price on the half that can kill and leaves the surveillance problem untouched; needs an EU basis that does not exist.

options.option: Add a Coherence cost to nonconsensual projection specifically: a practitioner whose lived behaviour drifts from the Auricle Choir doctrine they were trained under degrades under Coherence fault.
options.changes: Turns the branch's ethics into a mechanic rather than a rule, and makes an unlawful Harmonist measurably worse at their own craft over time.

options.option: Leave it free and state that this is deliberate: Anima Harmonics is cheap, which is exactly why it is governed by sacred law rather than by cost.
options.changes: No mechanical change; makes the legal apparatus the only brake and raises the stakes on every jurisdiction question.

quote_a: a Harmonist with loud, undisciplined Shell output hears nothing but their own tone and cannot perform any of the above at all
quote_b: Tenebra · The Hidden Shadow — Strengthens Dexterity Silence, Harmonics Suppression, Dominion Sense. The practitioner becomes difficult to detect, read, or track by conventional or Aetheric means.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: Fairness check 4 is only a partial pass. Diagnostic Anima Harmonics has no tell at all: the working is the practitioner being quiet, and the practitioner must be quiet to perform it. The one observable a careful opponent could use — an abnormally suppressed Essence signature — is identical to what a Tenebra practitioner presents, so the countertell is ambiguous by construction. This may be the intended design rather than a defect, but it is not stated as a design anywhere.

options.option: State the ambiguity on the page as the branch's operational security: a Harmonist reads as a Tenebra practitioner to Gnosis Analysis and both professions rely on it.
options.changes: Nothing mechanical; turns the defect into a named piece of tradecraft and gives an in-world reason the Concord regulates by licence rather than by detection.

options.option: Give receptive mode a positive tell: gates open inward produce a characteristic absence in the practitioner's own tone that another Harmonist can hear.
options.changes: Makes Harmonists detectable to each other and nobody else, which is a strong scene shape and creates a counter-surveillance profession.

options.option: Rule that a diagnostic read is lawfully undetectable and that this is why the sacred-law prohibition is absolute rather than proportionate.
options.changes: Ties the ethics to the mechanism; consistent with the Auricle Choir's 'no middle ground' doctrine.

options.option: Add a tell only to deep and deepest reads, leaving shallow perception undetectable.
options.changes: Graduated risk: the reads worth doing are the ones that can be caught, which is a good pressure to put on a Diviner or a Harmonist in a room.

quote_a: Anima Harmonics | A therapeutic tone projected at the wrong frequency shatters the patient's Crystal instead of healing it
quote_b: a working with a stratal account whose physics does not close was recorded by someone who did not check
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: The two accounts do not meet. The physical account of a resonant projection closes fine and is genuinely cheap — injection locking captures an oscillator with a coupling far too weak to move it by force, and resonant forcing destroys structures cheaply for the same reason. But the stratal account bills nothing at any stratum for an operation whose documented failure is the destruction of a Soul Crystal. An effect of that magnitude with a null Essence stratum is a working recorded by someone who did not check.

options.option: State that the energy is the patient's own, released by their own resonance, and that the practitioner supplies only phase and frequency — then bill the practitioner for precision rather than for power.
options.changes: Closes both books on Two Sets of Books III ('they supply the boundary condition'); makes the cost a precision cost, which no page in the batch currently prices.

options.option: Bill the projection in EU proportional to the patient's own Stage, since a higher-Stage Crystal is a stiffer resonator and takes longer to capture.
options.changes: Makes treating a powerful patient expensive and treating a weak one cheap, which inverts the usual scaling and is interesting; needs an EU basis.

options.option: Rule that Echo Fracture's energy is the ambient field's, drawn through the practitioner as a conduit, and that the structural fault is therefore in the practitioner's Shell rather than in their reserve.
options.changes: Makes the cost a Shell injury rather than an expenditure, which fits Statute IX and explains why Izathen survived his own catastrophe.

options.option: Leave the physics open and mark the branch as devotional literature until a Measurewright entry exists.
options.changes: No mechanical change; the Archives' own politest insult, applied to a discipline the Accord relies on, which is a good institutional embarrassment.

quote_a: The Anima is not a single note but a chord, the Essence Core's emotional frequency layered with the Aether Shell's conductivity signature and the Attraction Layer's recognition hum
quote_b: Temperance Gate · Stage V (Splintering) for rudimentary perception · Stage VII (Refraction) for overtone differentiation · Stage IX (Invocation) for Attraction Force resonance.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Harmonic Arts.md
why: Diagnostic Anima listening is gated at Stage VII on both pages, but the Anima is defined as a three-part chord whose third component is the Attraction Layer's recognition hum — and Attraction Force resonance is not perceptible until Stage IX on the same page that sets the gate. A Stage VII Anima Harmonist is therefore defined as reading a chord one third of which they cannot hear. Either the gate is wrong, the definition is wrong, or the Attraction component of an Anima is a different thing from Attraction Force resonance and nothing says so.

options.option: Raise diagnostic Anima listening to Stage IX and move therapeutic projection to Stage XI, sliding the whole branch up two Stages.
options.changes: Makes the branch a Master-tier discipline and empties the Expert tier of soul-readers; every Stage VII Harmonist in the corpus moves.

options.option: Rule that a Crystal's own recognition hum radiates through its Shell and is audible at Stage VII, while reading Attraction Force currents between two presences requires Stage IX.
options.changes: Smallest change and the cleanest distinction: you can hear that a soul has bonds without being able to trace them, which is exactly the line between Anima Harmonics and Resonant Divination.

options.option: Redefine the Anima as a two-part chord (Core and Shell) and move the recognition hum into Resonant Divination's territory outright.
options.changes: Simplifies the branch and strengthens the boundary between branches; contradicts the card-derived definition the page is built on.

options.option: Keep both and state that Stage VII Harmonists routinely misread the third component, which is why field triage is 'less precise than a full Coherence Ladder measurement'.
options.changes: Nothing mechanical; converts the contradiction into an attested limitation the page already half-states.

quote_a: a philosopher-summoner of the early Reconstruction Age (the pre-Concordance register calls this the Age of Deliberation, an era name the Errata table withdraws)
quote_b: Mnirah Valein · A philosopher-summoner of the Age of Deliberation who codified the Twelve Stages of Spirit Infusion
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Summoning Arts.md
why: The Anima Harmonics page states that 'Age of Deliberation' is an era name the Errata table withdraws and uses 'early Reconstruction Age' instead. The Spirit Summoning Arts page, which is the governing entry for the same figure and the same work, still carries the withdrawn name. Two pages date the same person's career to two eras, one of which is declared retired by the other.

options.option: Correct the Spirit Summoning Arts page to 'early Reconstruction Age' to match.
options.changes: One word on a governing page; requires confirming the Errata table actually withdraws the name, which this account could not verify independently.

options.option: Correct the Anima Harmonics page instead, if the Errata table does not in fact withdraw it.
options.changes: Reverses the correction; the withdrawal claim is currently attested only on the page that makes it.

options.option: Rule that both names are live, one pre-Concordance and one current, and record the equivalence in the era table.
options.changes: No page changes; adds a synonym row and makes older documents readable, which is in keeping with how the corpus treats retired Sub-Stat names.

quote_a: Diagnostic applications, gated by Temperance Stage
quote_b: One full Tier Grade above an opponent in the relevant stat wins a direct exchange of that stat category without meaningful contest.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Neither this page nor The Harmonic Arts states a Grade requirement for any of the three Harmonic branches, only Temperance Stages. Every other technique and discipline in the corpus carries a Grade line, and contested exchanges are resolved first by Tier Grade differential. With no Grade, a contested Anima read — Harmonist against a subject actively suppressing — has no stated resolution procedure at all.

options.option: State a Grade floor per application, derived from the Stage ceilings in Part Five (A at Stage VII, S at IX, SS at XI).
options.changes: Gives every Harmonic application a contested-exchange procedure; the floors fall out of the Stage gates with no invention.

options.option: Rule that receptive disciplines are resolved on the relevant Sub-Stat (Harmonics Suppression against Gnosis Analysis) rather than on Grade, and state the opposed pair.
options.changes: Adds an opposed-roll rule the system does not currently have anywhere; more precise and a larger change.

options.option: Leave Grade unstated and rule that the Harmonic Arts are uncontested by design: a read either succeeds or is defeated by a named counter (Basilithe, Tenebra, Thick Veil), never by a contest.
options.changes: Nothing to add; makes the named counters the only answers and makes finding them the whole game, which suits the challenge doctrine.

quote_a: Caelmorne Halvrein is the branch's defining figure and is confirmed canon in full.
quote_b: Practitioner | Stage | Level | Grade | eta (card) | eta (Tier table) | Crystal State | AU/s | Flux Density derived
path_b: imports/system-accounts/_method.md
why: The branch's defining figure, confirmed canon, has no character card anywhere in Volume I through V. Neither does Thalos of Ira, Aurevia the Echowright or Izathen the Broken Lyre. Every eta, Flux Density, AU/s and Crystal State in all three Harmonic accounts is therefore a Tier band rather than a figure, and the system accounts for the entire Harmonic tree contain no card-sourced number of any kind.

options.option: Write a card for Caelmorne Halvrein and derive the branch's figures from it.
options.changes: Fixes eta, Flux Density, AU/s and Crystal State for Anima Harmonics; a new character card needs its own authorisation and its own issue.

options.option: Write one card for the Harmonic tree's founder generation (Thalos, Aurevia, Caelmorne) as a single historical-figures entry.
options.changes: Three figures at one cost, and the three branches each gain a reference practitioner; historical-figure entries are not a form the corpus currently uses.

options.option: Rule that the Harmonic Arts are documented at discipline level only and carry no exemplar figures, taking all numbers from the Tier bands.
options.changes: No new material; every Harmonic number in the corpus stays a band, and the accounts say so explicitly rather than reading as incomplete.

quote_a: Combat application, Stage VIII, Interference Lock: reading a hostile working's tonal structure during the casting process to identify its harmonic weak points
quote_b: The Essence account, at all three strata, in diagnostic voice.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: A combat application with its own Temperance Gate, a named originating practitioner and an assessed operational tempo carries no EU figure, no rate, no range, no duration and no Grade. The only number attached to the branch anywhere is Aurevia's 'read, analyse, and counter in under two seconds', which is a tempo rather than a cost. Interference Lock ends other practitioners' workings and appears in no ledger.

options.option: Bill Interference Lock in EU per counter at the Stage VIII gate, with a band.
options.changes: Gives the branch its first cost and makes a Harmonist's counter-count per engagement finite, which is the property the working most needs; requires an EU basis.

options.option: Bill it as a share of AU/s held for the read-and-counter window, following the Lumen Dissecans precedent for sustained diagnostic work.
options.changes: Matches the two-second window to a rate rather than a lump; needs an AU/s figure and no named practitioner has a card.

options.option: Rule that the counter's cost scales with the target working's Q — cheap against a sharply tuned working, expensive against a broadband one — and state the relation.
options.changes: Makes the branch's most interesting physical property into its cost curve; a new kind of cost rule the system does not currently have.

options.option: Leave the branch uncosted and rule that its limiter is the two-second window and the Echo Fracture risk, not expenditure.
options.changes: No numbers added; makes tempo and risk the whole brake and puts the entire weight of balance on the counters.

quote_a: The practitioner does not need to overpower the working; they need to find the one frequency that collapses its whole tonal structure.
quote_b: The honest answer is that a working's energy budget balances at the Aether stratum and not at the Essence one. The practitioner does not supply the joules. They supply the boundary condition
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: The physical account closes beautifully — a phase-only intervention costs nearly nothing in joules and the energy destroyed is the hostile caster's own, already committed, which is the purest case of Two Sets of Books III anywhere in the batch. The stratal account does not close, because it is empty. A working that cancels another practitioner's cast mid-flight, at range, in under two seconds, has no Essence stratum stated at all, so the two books cannot be compared, let alone balanced.

options.option: State the Essence stratum explicitly as precision rather than power: a small fixed expenditure per counter, independent of the target's magnitude.
options.changes: Closes both books and makes the branch flat-rate against anything, which is startling but is what the physics says; a Stage XII working costs the same to lock as a Stage VI one.

options.option: Bill the practitioner for the read rather than for the counter, on integration time.
options.changes: Moves the cost to the half that actually takes work, and makes a Harmonist who must counter many workings quickly run out of attention rather than reserve.

options.option: Rule that the counter's Essence cost scales inversely with how well the read went, so a confident lock is cheap and a guessed one is ruinous.
options.changes: Ties cost to skill and gives the Echo Fracture risk a gradient rather than a cliff; a new rule shape.

quote_a: a working with no exploitable harmonic signature (a silent or already-completed effect) offers Interference Lock nothing to grip
quote_b: Every working produces tonal output as a byproduct of its Wellspring process.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Harmonic Arts.md
why: The governing entry states without qualification that every working produces tonal output. The branch page states that some workings are silent and therefore ungrippable. Both cannot be true as written. The distinction the branch page needs — between a working still in progress and one already resolved — is present in the same sentence and does the work on its own; 'silent' is the word that contradicts, and it is doing real mechanical work, because it is one of only two stated ways out of Interference Lock.

options.option: Strike 'silent' and keep 'already-completed', so the only escape is finishing the cast first.
options.changes: Smallest change; makes the counter to Interference Lock purely a matter of tempo, which is clean and findable. Removes an escape route some techniques may be relying on.

options.option: Qualify the governing entry: every working produces tonal output, but some outputs fall below the noise floor of any receiver — Tenebra-suppressed and Luminalis-polarised workings in particular.
options.changes: Keeps both, names which Wellsprings buy silence, and makes suppression a purchasable counter to the Harmonic tree rather than a free one.

options.option: Rule that 'silent' means a working whose tone is uncorrelated with its effect, so the read returns a line that is no use, rather than no line.
options.changes: Preserves the universality of tonal output and makes a decoy signature a legitimate technique; the Knot counter then has a Thaumic-specific form.

quote_a: multiple practitioners project layered harmonic support around a central working, letting the primary caster achieve output beyond individual capacity, without increasing that caster's own Essence expenditure
quote_b: Temperance Stage functions as a hard ceiling on every Sub-Stat in the system, and a Primary's mean therefore cannot exceed it either. A character cannot allocate their way past a ceiling their Soul Crystal cannot structurally sustain.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Part Five states the Temperance ceiling without exception and adds that forcing a stat past it by 'external metaphysical imposition' generates Crystal Fracture Events at an exponentially increasing rate. Harmonic Amplification is external metaphysical imposition that raises a working's effective magnitude past the primary's individual capacity, and neither the branch page nor The Harmonic Arts mentions fracture risk. Either the Cantic Order's method is exempt from the system's hardest stated rule, or 'capacity' means something narrower than the ceiling and nothing says which.

options.option: Rule that amplification raises the working's output and not the caster's stat, so no ceiling is touched — the choir supplies amplitude the primary never holds.
options.changes: Preserves the hard ceiling and keeps the Order's method; requires accepting that a working's magnitude and its caster's Grade are separable quantities, which the corpus has not previously stated.

options.option: Apply Part Five's fracture clause and state that the primary takes Crystal Fracture risk rising with the number of supporting voices.
options.changes: Gives the Cantic Order a real and escalating price, explains why symphonic incantation is rare, and makes a large choir a threat to its own centre.

options.option: Cap amplification at the primary's own Stage ceiling, so the choir shortens the time to reach it rather than exceeding it.
options.changes: Removes the 'beyond individual capacity' claim entirely and makes the method an efficiency device, which is less dramatic and fully compliant.

options.option: Rule the Cantic Order a documented exception, licensed and registered, and state the exception in Part Five.
options.changes: Preserves both texts by naming one institution as the carve-out, which makes membership of the Order strategically decisive.

quote_a: projecting a precisely tuned counter-frequency at that weak point to overwrite the waveform and pin or unravel the spell mid-flight
quote_b: Nihiloth · The Hollow Law — Two waves in antiphase do not conceal one another. They sum to zero, and the region between them carries no energy at all.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: Interference Lock runs Nihiloth's Core Law exactly, and the branch is explicitly harmonised to no Wellspring at all: 'the discipline listens to the working's dialect rather than speaking one of its own.' The system does not say how a working invokes a Wellspring's law without harmonising with that Wellspring, and the Core Vocabulary makes harmonisation one of four conditions an Ability needs to develop. Either the branch is quietly Nihiloth-aligned, or the system permits unharmonised use of a Core Law and has never said so.

options.option: Name Nihiloth as Thaumic Harmonics' operative Wellspring for the combat application only, leaving the diagnostic half Family-free.
options.changes: Gives Interference Lock a Family (Limina), a failure terrain and a cost basis; contradicts the branch's stated Family-neutrality for half of itself.

options.option: Rule that destructive interference is a Material-Plane behaviour available to any Shell that can produce a tone, and that Nihiloth's Core Law is the Soul-Plane expression of the same regularity rather than its licence.
options.changes: Establishes a general principle with wide consequences: the Sixty describe laws rather than own them, which reframes every Wellspring entry in the corpus.

options.option: Rule that the Harmonist borrows the target working's own Wellspring and turns it, so the law invoked is always the enemy's.
options.changes: Elegant and specific to the branch; makes the counter's character change with every opponent and gives Echo Fracture a mechanism (you borrowed a law you cannot hold).

quote_a: Combat application, Stage VIII, Interference Lock
quote_b: When two characters clash, who wins a contested exchange is answered first by Tier Grade differential, then by technique and tactical intelligence, then by Soul Crystal architecture.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: Interference Lock is an explicitly contested working — one practitioner against another's live cast — and carries no Grade on either page. Part Four says a contested exchange is answered first by Tier Grade differential, which cannot be computed. The branch's own doctrine says magnitude is irrelevant, which may be the intended answer, but that would make it the only working in the corpus resolved without reference to Grade and no page says so.

options.option: State a Grade floor of S at the Stage VIII gate, matching Part Five's Stage VIII Max Grade.
options.changes: Gives the contested exchange a procedure; falls out of the Stage gate with no invention.

options.option: Rule Interference Lock explicitly exempt from Grade differential, resolved on Gnosis Analysis against the target working's Q or Coherence instead.
options.changes: Codifies the branch's 'outplay, not overpower' doctrine as a real mechanical exception; needs a stated opposed pair.

options.option: Resolve it on Harmonics Attunement against the target's Harmonics Stability, both of which already exist as Sub-Stats.
options.changes: Uses existing Sub-Stats, gives Basilithe practitioners (who raise Stability) their advantage numerically, and needs no new rule shape.

quote_a: Aurevia the Echowright is confirmed canon as the practitioner who proved Thaumic Harmonics could function as a combat discipline
quote_b: Guild assessors classified her operational speed as exceptional: read, analyse, and counter in under two seconds
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Harmonic Arts.md
why: The branch's combat originator is confirmed canon, carries an assessed operational figure, and has no character card. Her two-second tempo is the only attested number the branch holds, and there is nothing to anchor it to — no Stage, no Grade, no eta, no reserve. A tempo without a practitioner's architecture behind it cannot be checked against Part Six's reaction-speed table or against anything else.

options.option: Write a card for Aurevia the Echowright and anchor the two-second figure to her Stage and Dexterity Reflex.
options.changes: Makes the branch's only number checkable and gives the Harmonic tree a combat exemplar; a new card needs its own authorisation.

options.option: Restate the two-second figure as a guild assessment standard rather than a personal one: the certification threshold for combat Thaumic work.
options.changes: Turns a personal feat into an institutional benchmark any Harmonist can be measured against, which is more useful at a table and needs no card.

options.option: Leave it as attributed history and mark it unanchored.
options.changes: Nothing changes; the figure stays a story rather than a stat, and no account may derive from it.

quote_a: The practitioner does not need to overpower the working
quote_b: It costs something that hurts. EU at a rate that reaches Starvation in a real fight, Harmonics, Coherence, the body, or a vow.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Fairness check 1 fails. A working that can unravel a hostile cast mid-flight, that explicitly does not require a magnitude advantage, and that gets cheaper the better-built its target is, must have something it runs out of. As written it has nothing: no reserve cost, no rate, no toll, no per-engagement cap. The real limiters are the two-second window and the Echo Fracture risk, and neither is an expenditure, so a Harmonist never has to choose which working to answer.

options.option: Cap counters per engagement by attention rather than by EU: a Harmonist can hold one hostile working's line at a time, and switching costs the read.
options.changes: Forces target selection without inventing a number, and makes two simultaneous casters a genuine problem for a single Harmonist.

options.option: Bill each counter in EU at the Stage VIII gate.
options.changes: The conventional fix; needs an EU basis and makes the branch's cost independent of its own interesting physics.

options.option: Make Echo Fracture risk cumulative across an engagement, rising with each counter attempted, so the fifth lock of a fight is genuinely dangerous.
options.changes: Turns the stated catastrophic failure into a resource clock; fits Statute IX and the branch's own doctrine, and costs nothing to state.

options.option: Bill the counter in Harmonics: each lock spends Harmonics Stability, and a depleted Harmonist can no longer hold their own tone steady enough to project.
options.changes: Uses an existing Sub-Stat as the consumable and makes the branch self-limiting in the currency it actually works in.

quote_a: A Diviner's four attested applications, each gated by Temperance Stage exactly as the source page states them:
quote_b: Bond Reading (Stage VIII) ... Fate Entanglement Analysis ... Resonant Tracking ... Convergence Forecasting (Stage X) ... Dissonance Warning, the Sonochoral Conclave's civic specialty
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Resonant Divination.md
why: The page announces four attested applications and then lists five. It also says each is gated by Temperance Stage exactly as the source states, and two of the five carry no Stage on either page. The count and the gating claim are both wrong against the page's own list.

options.option: Correct the count to five and gate the two ungated applications.
options.changes: Largest fix and the most complete; requires deciding Stage floors for Fate Entanglement Analysis and Resonant Tracking, which The Harmonic Arts also omits.

options.option: Correct the count to five and state plainly that two applications are ungated in the source.
options.changes: Honest and minimal; leaves the gating gap open and visible rather than filled by invention.

options.option: Rule Dissonance Warning an institutional service rather than an application, restoring the count to four.
options.changes: The Conclave's civic work becomes a product built from the other four rather than a fifth capability; tidy, and consistent with how the page introduces it.

quote_a: Bond Reading (Stage VIII) — maps a subject's relational network: who they are connected to, how strongly, through what kind of recognition
quote_b: Temperance Gate · Stage V (Splintering) for rudimentary perception · Stage VII (Refraction) for overtone differentiation · Stage IX (Invocation) for Attraction Force resonance.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Harmonic Arts.md
why: Bond Reading is gated at Stage VIII and reads Attraction Force currents, which the same governing page says are not perceptible below Stage IX. A Stage VIII Diviner is therefore licensed to perform a reading whose input they cannot receive. This is the same shape of contradiction as SA-CROSS-ANIMA-CHORD-VS-GATE and the two should probably be ruled together, since one governing page sets both perception gates and both application gates.

options.option: Raise Bond Reading to Stage IX to match the perception gate.
options.changes: One number; makes the branch's floor Stage IX and aligns it with the deepest perceptual depth, which is where the page says bonds live.

options.option: Lower the Attraction Force resonance perception gate to Stage VIII.
options.changes: Also one number, but moves a gate that governs all three branches and would give Anima Harmonists the recognition hum a Stage earlier than currently stated.

options.option: Rule that Bond Reading at Stage VIII returns presence and strength only, and that tracing a current to its far end — Resonant Tracking — is the Stage IX capability.
options.changes: Keeps both numbers, gates the currently ungated application, and creates a clean progression: hear that a bond exists, then follow it.

quote_a: Fate Entanglement Analysis — identifies destiny-level convergences, trajectories locked together by currents too strong for ordinary intervention to deflect
quote_b: Temperance Gate · Stage VIII for basic Bond Reading · Stage X for Convergence Forecasting · Stage XII for Attraction Force resonance tracking.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Harmonic Arts.md
why: Neither the branch page nor the governing entry gates Fate Entanglement Analysis or Resonant Tracking, while gating the other three. As written, the application that reads destiny-level convergences and the application that locates a person from a severed bond are both available at the branch's floor, alongside basic Bond Reading. Resonant Tracking in particular is a manhunt tool and it is ungated.

options.option: Gate Fate Entanglement Analysis at Stage XII (it reads multiple Wellspring processes converging, which is Attraction Force resonance work) and Resonant Tracking at Stage IX.
options.changes: Fills both gaps from the existing ladder; makes the branch's most strategically dangerous application a Grandmaster capability.

options.option: Gate both at the branch floor explicitly, stating that they are variations on Bond Reading rather than separate capabilities.
options.changes: Minimal; makes a Stage VIII Diviner a complete manhunt asset, which raises the stakes on the branch's regulation and on its counters.

options.option: Gate Resonant Tracking at Stage IX and rule Fate Entanglement Analysis a reading that happens to a Diviner rather than one they perform — a convergence that loud cannot be missed at any Stage.
options.changes: Makes destiny-level entanglement an uncontrollable perception rather than a tool, which fits the page's account of it sounding louder than everything else.

quote_a: The recursive amplification produced an Echo Fracture that propagated through the local Aether field, shattering Crystal harmonization in every soul within the event's radius. The resulting zone of harmonic chaos persisted for decades.
quote_b: Both accounts are complete. Neither is a translation of the other. A working that has a good physical account and no stratal account was not a working, and a working with a stratal account whose physics does not close was recorded by someone who did not check.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: A purely receptive discipline produced a regional metaphysical event lasting decades, and no account of where the energy came from exists on any page. One practitioner's reserve cannot fund it; the physics of a feedback loop says the energy is the network's, released because the practitioner closed a loop with gain above unity. That is a coherent account and it is not written down, so the batch's largest single physical event has a null stratal account and an unstated physical one.

options.option: State that the energy was the local Aether field's, released by a loop Izathen closed, and that the Diviner supplied only the gain — the purest case of Two Sets of Books III in the corpus.
options.changes: Closes both books, explains the radius (it is a field event, not a personal one) and explains why Izathen survived what he caused.

options.option: Rule it an Aetheric Saturation event under the Core Vocabulary's existing definition, which already produces 'Crystal Fracture Events in everyone exposed, including the person who caused it'.
options.changes: Uses an existing named danger state rather than inventing an account; makes Echo Fracture a species of Saturation and links the Harmonic tree to the Counterplay register's 'Saturate it' route.
