options.option: Bill it to Izathen's own reserve and state the figure.
options.changes: Requires an EU figure vastly beyond anything in the corpus and a card for him; contradicts the branch being receptive.

options.option: Leave the physics open and record on the page that no Measurewright account of 8,000 AF has ever been taken, which is itself a scandal.
options.changes: No mechanical change; makes the missing account an in-world fact and a hook, and is honest about the state of the record.

quote_a: Convergence Forecasting (Stage X) — projects which presences are moving toward resonant convergence and what happens when they arrive at the same frequency, days or weeks in advance at skilled hands.
quote_b: EU · Essence Units — The raw reserve. Total volume of usable Essence stored in the Crystal at any given moment
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The branch states one quantity of any kind — 'days or weeks' — and it is a range with no basis, no units on the skill axis and no stated dependence on anything. There is no EU cost, no range, no duration, no Grade, no subject limit and no statement of how many bonds a single reading covers. A Bond Reading that maps an entire relational network is either bounded by something or it is unbounded, and the page does not say which.

options.option: Bound a reading by subject count and integration time: one subject per sustained reading, with the time to converge rising as the bond weakens.
options.changes: Makes the branch slow rather than expensive, which fits its physics and makes a Conclave's throughput a real logistical constraint.

options.option: Bill it in EU per reading with a band per application.
options.changes: Conventional; needs an EU basis and makes a purely receptive discipline cost reserve, which the physics does not support.

options.option: Tie forecast lead time to the rate at which the coupling is changing rather than to the Diviner's Stage, and state that.
options.changes: Replaces the vague 'days or weeks at skilled hands' with a rule a player can exploit: a fast-moving convergence is invisible, so acting quickly beats the instrument.

options.option: Leave it unnumbered and state that Concord regulation, not cost, is the branch's limiter.
options.changes: No numbers; puts the entire brake on institutions and makes an unlicensed Diviner a very serious problem.

quote_a: every one of the applications above degrades or misreads the instant a targeted connection is deliberately masked, severed cleanly, or run through a Thick Veil zone
quote_b: One full Tier Grade above an opponent in the relevant stat wins a direct exchange of that stat category without meaningful contest.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: A masked connection degrades a reading, which is a contest between a masker and a reader, and neither the branch page nor the governing entry states a Grade for either side. Part Four resolves contests on Tier Grade differential first. With no Grade on the branch and no stated opposed Sub-Stat pair, whether a Tenebra-suppressed subject defeats a Grandmaster Diviner is unanswerable from the rules.

options.option: Resolve masking on Harmonics Suppression against Gnosis Analysis and state the pair, leaving Grade out of it.
options.changes: Uses existing Sub-Stats, gives Tenebra practitioners a numeric route, and establishes an opposed-pair convention the corpus currently lacks.

options.option: State a Grade floor per application from Part Five's Stage ceilings (S at VIII, SS at X, SSS at XII).
options.changes: Gives Part Four something to compare; falls out of the Stage gates with no invention.

options.option: Rule the branch uncontested and defeated only by the three named conditions (masked, cleanly severed, Thick Veil), never by a Grade contest.
options.changes: Makes the counters absolute and the instrument otherwise perfect, which is a strong design but makes the three conditions load-bearing for the whole branch.

quote_a: Izathen the Broken Lyre is confirmed canon, unchanged from the card in substance
quote_b: Practitioner | Stage | Level | Grade | eta (card) | eta (Tier table) | Crystal State | AU/s | Flux Density derived
path_b: imports/system-accounts/_method.md
why: The branch's central cautionary figure, confirmed canon, author of the largest harmonic catastrophe in the record, has no character card. Neither does any member of the Sonochoral Conclave. Every eta, Flux Density, AU/s and Crystal State in this account is a Tier band. Shared with SA-GAP-ANIMA-NO-CARD and SA-GAP-THAUMIC-NO-CARD: the entire Harmonic tree has no card-sourced figure anywhere.

options.option: Write a card for Izathen the Broken Lyre in his post-Fracture state.
options.changes: Anchors the branch's numbers and gives the corpus a living consequence of Echo Fracture; a new card needs its own authorisation.

options.option: Write a card for a current Sonochoral Conclave reader instead, as the branch's working exemplar.
options.changes: More useful at a table than a historical casualty and gives the Conclave a face; a new character, which needs authorisation.

options.option: Rule the Harmonic tree documented at discipline level only and take every figure from the Tier bands.
options.changes: No new material; all three accounts state their numbers as bands and say why, which is honest and closes the gap by declaring it.

quote_a: Bond Reading (Stage VIII) — maps a subject's relational network: who they are connected to, how strongly, through what kind of recognition, and whether the bond is consonant or under strain. This is the diagnostic tool behind Concord soul forensics.
quote_b: It has a tell. A careful opponent can read it coming.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Fairness check 4 fails outright. The working takes nothing from the subject, leaves no residue on them, imposes no boundary on them, is performed at a distance and, being gated above Refraction, requires no voice, hand, ink or blood. There is no observable of any kind. A subject learns they were read only in the failure case, when the Diviner accidentally forms a bond. A surveillance instrument with no tell means an opponent cannot be careful, only lucky, and the three stated counters (mask, sever, Thick Veil) all require already suspecting.

options.option: Give a sustained reading a trace at the far end: a bond being integrated over hums faintly, and the other party to the bond — not the subject — can feel it.
options.changes: Creates a tell that reaches a third person, which is a superb scene shape: your ally feels that someone is reading your friendship.

options.option: Rule that a reading leaves Aetheric Residue on the bond itself, readable afterward by another Diviner, so surveillance is detectable retrospectively but not live.
options.changes: Keeps the branch undetectable in the moment and makes counter-surveillance a real profession; consistent with Residue being 'always readable by someone patient enough'.

options.option: Accept the absence and state it as the branch's defining property, with Concord licensing as the only brake, on the page itself.
options.changes: No mechanical change; makes the regulation the story and puts the whole weight of fairness on the three stated escapes.

options.option: Require the Diviner to be within some stated distance of one endpoint of the bond, giving a physical tell of presence.
options.changes: Adds a range limit the branch currently lacks and makes a Diviner a person who has to be somewhere, which restores every Counterplay route at once.

quote_a: EU · Essence Units — The raw reserve. Total volume of usable Essence stored in the Crystal at any given moment, also called Essence Volume. Scales with Temperance Stage.
quote_b: Essence Capacity · 92,000 EU · Flux Density 18,400 EU/g
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Dougou Ozumu Zettari.md
why: The five attested EU reserves in the corpus are not monotone in Temperance Stage and span eleven orders of magnitude: Karo Venrik Stage V 1,600 EU; Niran Yukari Stage VII 485,000 EU; Muken Moto Stage X 1,850,000 EU; Gimbzo Stage XII 4.8e14 EU; Dougou Ozumu Zettari Stage XIII 92,000 EU. Dougou at Stage XIII holds one fifth of Niran's reserve at Stage VII and one five-billionth of Gimbzo's at Stage XII. Read against the Spellcraft batch's stated costs and the ten-percent Starvation rule, the consequences are concrete and absurd: a Stage XIII practitioner cannot afford one domain-scale Edictum (Stage VII, 90,000 EU, needing 100,000 EU in reserve), and the only Stage V practitioner with a card cannot afford the batch's cheapest working (Imprinta, Stage IV, 8,000 EU floor, needing 8,889 EU). Karo's own card flags its figure as unsourceable for exactly this reason. Either the reserves are wrong, the costs are wrong, or 'scales with Temperance Stage' is not a claim about magnitude.

options.option: Publish an EU-by-Stage benchmark table in Part Nineteen and bring every card and every technique cost into band against it.
options.changes: Closes SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA as well, and is the root fix; it moves figures on dozens of cards and every technique page in the corpus, so it is a very large ruling.

options.option: Rule that 'scales with Temperance Stage' sets a ceiling rather than a value, and that a Crystal's actual reserve is set by Tempering Yield and by architecture — so a sealed, near-zero-leak build like Dougou's legitimately holds far less than an open one at a lower Stage.
options.changes: Preserves every card as written and makes reserve a build choice rather than a rank; requires accepting that a Stage XIII practitioner can genuinely be unable to cast a Stage VII working, which is a strong and interesting claim.

options.option: Rule that technique EU costs are absolute and reserves are not comparable across Aether Classes, and mark cross-card EU comparison as invalid.
options.changes: Stops the arithmetic being done at all; removes the Starvation-margin calculation from every system account and makes 'can X afford Y' unanswerable.

options.option: Hold the reserves and re-scale the Spellcraft batch's stated EU costs, which are all described on their own pages as estimates.
options.changes: Touches only the four Design Chain pages in this section rather than the cards; the costs are self-declared estimates, so the ground is softest here.

quote_a: binding a single named target to a stated condition costs an estimated 50,000-70,000 EU and takes effect the instant the sentence completes; binding a space or a domain-scale target runs toward 90,000 EU
quote_b: At Stage IX / S-Grade, cancelling a personal-scale oath costs an estimated 90,000-130,000 EU and completes in under a second once the counter-field locks
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Oathrend.md
why: Edictum at Stage VII and A-Grade binds a space or a domain for about 90,000 EU. Oathrend, two Stages and a full Grade higher, spends 90,000-130,000 EU to cancel a single personal oath. The lower-Stage, lower-Grade working therefore covers a domain for what the higher-Stage one spends on one person, and nothing on either page explains the inversion. The Stage floors, the Grades and the costs disagree about which of these workings is the larger act.

options.option: Raise Edictum's domain-scale figure so that scale costs more than a personal binding by an order rather than by a third.
options.changes: Restores a sane ladder and makes domain-scale Edicts a Bench-level expenditure rather than a routine one; Edictum's personal figure stays, so only one number moves.

options.option: Lower Oathrend's personal figure and reserve the 130,000 EU end for multi-party and divinely-witnessed pacts only.
options.changes: Makes the two workings comparable at personal scale and keeps Oathrend expensive where the physical account says it should be (one anti-field per anchor).

options.option: Rule that the two costs are not comparable because Edictum imposes a condition (cheap, boundary work) while Oathrend must supply a matched-amplitude anti-field (expensive, energy work), and state that principle so it governs future pricing.
options.changes: Keeps both numbers and gives the corpus a costing principle it currently lacks: boundary workings are cheap at any scale, cancellation workings scale with what they cancel.

options.option: Treat both figures as the estimates their own pages call them and re-derive after SA-CROSS-EU-STAGE-LADDER is ruled.
options.changes: Defers; nothing changes now and the inversion stays on record as a symptom of the larger ladder problem rather than a defect of either page.

quote_a: The named condition holds. A sentenced target cannot perform the forbidden act ... until the Edict is lifted by the same or greater authority that set it.
quote_b: A fist with combustion on it is Spellcraft with the body as the pen, and the sentence is still ephemeral - which is why the fist stops burning the moment attention lapses.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: The standing Craft durability rule makes Spellcraft ephemeral: it holds only while attention holds, which is the property every other Spellcraft page in this section cites to explain why its working lapses. Edictum is filed as Spellcraft and holds indefinitely with no attention and no upkeep, ending only when a superior authority lifts it or the caster's standing fails. The physical account supports the page (a boundary condition, once imposed, is lossless to maintain) and contradicts the Craft rule. Several other pages in this section note the same tension for their own workings: Anointing's Traitus mark, Imprinta's permanent deposit, Precept's inscription.

options.option: Rule that a Spellcraft working whose product is a standing condition rather than a sustained expression is durable, and state the exception in The Four Crafts.
options.changes: Covers Edictum, Anointing and Imprinta in one ruling and makes the Craft split about what the working leaves rather than about how it is delivered; a real change to a governing page.

options.option: Reassign Edictum to Runecraft on durability grounds.
options.changes: Contradicts the page's own 'explicitly a spoken working' and loses the Law V reading that makes the voice its largest vulnerability; tidy on durability and wrong on everything else.

options.option: Rule that the Edict lapses with the caster's attention and that what persists is the Continuum's record of it, enforced institutionally rather than metaphysically.
options.changes: Preserves the Craft rule exactly and turns a metaphysical binding into a legal one, which is a very different and much more Concord-flavoured working.

options.option: Keep both and state on The Four Crafts that the durability table describes the delivery and not the product, with Edictum as the worked example.
options.changes: No mechanical change; makes the apparent contradiction an explicit reading rule that the rest of the batch can cite.

quote_a: Path gate · None documented.
quote_b: Sovereignty requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A, and Stage IX to exceed SSS where the imposed law encodes abstract conceptual truths.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page names Dominion (Sovereignty, Command) as governing Primary and requires A-Grade at Stage VII. Part Seven gates Dominion Sovereignty on the Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A, and Dominion Command on the Attraction Path at Stage VIII to exceed SS. The Fate gate therefore binds at exactly this working's Stage and Grade, and the page's 'None documented' is wrong against the system's own gate table. The same error appears on Oathrend, Imprinta and Scission in this section, which suggests the four Design Chain pages were written without Part Seven open.

options.option: Correct all four Design Chain pages' Path gate lines from Part Seven, working from each page's own stated governing Primary and Grade.
options.changes: Four pages, no invention, and every gate falls out of an existing table; it also makes Path a real constraint on who can cast these workings, which it currently is not.

options.option: Rule that 'None documented' means the card did not state one and is not a claim that none applies, and add a standing note that Part Seven governs regardless.
options.changes: No page edits; makes Part Seven the default for every technique entry and closes the class of error rather than the instances.

options.option: Correct Edictum alone and leave the other three to their own rulings.
options.changes: Smallest change; leaves three known instances of the same defect on the shelf.

quote_a: the card gives three mortal derivations of the same working (Valen Dros, the Daughters of Concord, Lirae Ilmashai, and the historical Edictum of Silence attributed to Seraphiel Moto), all unattested individually
quote_b: Practitioner | Stage | Level | Grade | eta (card) | eta (Tier table) | Crystal State | AU/s | Flux Density derived
path_b: imports/system-accounts/_method.md
why: No Edictum caster has a character card, so eta, Flux Density, AU/s, Crystal State and reserve are all null and the Starvation margin cannot be computed for any named practitioner. This is true of all four Design Chain pages in this section (Edictum, Oathrend, Imprinta, Scission), which between them carry the only EU figures in the batch and not one practitioner to spend them.

options.option: Attach each of the four workings to an existing carded practitioner who could plausibly hold it, and derive the figures from those cards.
options.changes: No new characters; requires a ruling on who, and a wrong attachment is worse than none.

options.option: Write one card for a Concord Bench officer, covering Edictum and Scission as institutional workings.
options.changes: Gives the Accord a face and two of the four workings a practitioner; a new character needs its own authorisation.

options.option: Rule that these four are institutional workings documented without exemplars, and take every derived figure from the Tier bands.
options.changes: No new material; the accounts state their numbers as bands and say why.

quote_a: The vow's consequences unwind across every plane they were enforced on. What the oath was holding together ... is no longer held by anything
quote_b: Oathrend generates a field of equal magnitude and opposite phase across that same anchor point, and the two sum to zero the way two opposed waves cancel rather than fight. The seal does not weaken. It opens.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Oathrend.md
why: Destructive interference is not destruction. Nihiloth's own Core Law says the two fields 'sum to zero', which is a statement about the net in the overlap region while both are present; neither field is altered and the moment one stops the other is fully present again. An active noise control system switched off does not leave a quiet room. Yet the page has the cancellation complete in under a second and the consequences unwind permanently. Either the null must be sustained indefinitely, which contradicts the stated cast time and would make Oathrend a sustained working, or something other than destructive interference is destroying the bond and the page does not say what.

options.option: Rule that the null is momentary and that what ends the oath is the Claustra seal's own requirement of continuity: a claim that registers zero for any interval is a claim that has lapsed, and cannot re-establish itself.
options.changes: Closes the mechanism elegantly and makes Oathrend a timing attack on continuity rather than a destruction; it also makes any oath with a stated tolerance for interruption immune, which is a new and findable counter.

options.option: Make Oathrend a sustained working: the null must be held for a stated duration while the parties' claims decay, and releasing early restores the oath intact.
options.changes: Contradicts 'completes in under a second', gives the working a real window an opponent can contest, and makes multi-party pacts genuinely hard; a large rewrite of the Numerical Effect line.

options.option: Change the mechanism from destructive interference to something that does destroy - Dissolution's solvation, or Letheveil's lossy compression of the record - and rewrite the Wellspring line accordingly.
options.changes: Keeps the permanence and loses Nihiloth, which is the page's primary Wellspring and its Family anchor; the largest change.

options.option: Keep both and state that the unwinding is a consequence of the momentary null propagating outward - everything downstream fails during the zero and does not spontaneously re-form - while the seal itself is untouched and could in principle be re-sworn.
options.changes: Preserves both sentences and creates a meaningful distinction between the oath and its consequences: the vow can be renewed, the truce it was holding cannot be un-broken.

quote_a: Oathrend generates a field of equal magnitude and opposite phase across that same anchor point
quote_b: The practitioner does not supply the joules. They supply the boundary condition, and the boundary condition is cheap in absolute terms and expensive in the only currency a soul has.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: Every other working in this section moves a boundary and lets the ambient field pay. Destructive interference cannot: cancelling a field of energy U requires producing an anti-field of energy U in the overlap region, matched in amplitude. This is the one working in the batch whose physical account says the caster must supply as much as the target holds, which is precisely what Two Sets of Books says practitioners do not do. The page states no source for the anti-field.

options.option: State that the anti-field is drawn from the Aether stratum like any other expression and that the Crystal supplies only the phase, which is the cheap part and the hard part.
options.changes: Closes both books on the system's own principle, keeps the EU cost modest, and makes phase precision rather than magnitude the practitioner's skill - which the phase-error arithmetic (2 sin(phi/2)) then makes checkable.

options.option: Accept that Oathrend is an exception and that the caster genuinely supplies matched energy, then raise the EU cost to scale with the oath's own weight.
options.changes: Makes great pacts genuinely unaffordable and explains why the working is rare; requires an EU scale for oath weight, which does not exist.

options.option: Rule that the anti-field is drawn from the oath's own anchor - the claim is made to cancel itself - so no external energy is needed at all.
options.changes: The cheapest closure and the most elegant: the practitioner supplies a phase inversion at the anchor and the oath does the rest, which would also explain Nihiloth's symmetric-null failure.

quote_a: Weakness · A Mirrored-Scale-class working (Purganeth's own reciprocity law) turns the caster's own counter-field back on them in exact kind; this is the one documented case where the caster, not the oath, absorbs the working.
quote_b: Failure · The cancellation is symmetric. Everything the practitioner brought inside is subject to the same null, including the parts of themselves they were relying on.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: Nihiloth's documented Failure applies to every casting and the page does not carry it. Superposition does not know whose field is whose: an antiphase field placed across an anchor nulls whatever is at that anchor, so a caster whose own oaths, bonds or Domain touch the same anchor point loses them in the same instant. The page names only the Purganeth mirror as a weakness, which is a special case requiring the target to have prepared. The Wellspring's own general cost is missing, and it is the cost that would stop an Oathrend specialist from operating with impunity.

options.option: Add the symmetric null to the page as a standing cost: any bond of the caster's that shares an anchor with the target oath is nulled with it.
options.changes: Gives every casting a real risk that scales with how entangled the caster is with the parties, which makes liberating your own faction's oaths dangerous and outsiders the natural practitioners.

options.option: Rule that the counter-field is directional and nulls only along the claim it is matched to, exempting the caster.
options.changes: Preserves the page as written and requires stating why Nihiloth's documented symmetry does not apply here, which needs a mechanism.

options.option: Rule that the symmetry is why the working is cast by third parties with no stake, and state that as doctrine: the Ashblood Apostates break other people's oaths because they cannot safely break their own.
options.changes: No mechanical change; turns the Wellspring's failure into an institutional fact that explains the technique's sociology.

quote_a: Path gate · None documented.
quote_b: Persistence requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed S, and Stage VIII to exceed SS against Oblivion-class pressure. ... Oath requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page names Resilience (Oath, Persistence) as governing Primary and requires S-Grade at Stage IX. Part Seven gates Resilience Persistence on the Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed S, and Resilience Oath on the Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B. Both bite at this working's stated Grade, so 'None documented' is wrong against the system's own table. Same class of error as SA-CROSS-EDICTUM-PATH-GATE.

options.option: Correct the Path gate line from Part Seven: Fate Path primary (Persistence at S), Attraction Path secondary (Oath at B).
options.changes: No invention; makes Oathrend a Fate-Path working, which fits a technique that operates on Plane-of-Fate objects and narrows who can perform it.

options.option: Rule 'None documented' a statement about the source card rather than about the system, under a standing note that Part Seven always governs.
options.changes: No page edits; closes the whole class of error at once.

quote_a: the card gives it to three separate lineages of use (Zeven Halek's single battlefield invocation, Lysandra Velkaris's rejection of divine bondage, the Ashblood Apostates' standing liberation doctrine), all unattested in current canon
quote_b: Starvation margin | null | Needs a reserve figure the card does not carry.
path_b: imports/system-accounts/Techniques/Lumen Dissecans.md
why: No Oathrend caster has a card, so the working's stated 90,000-130,000 EU cost cannot be set against any practitioner's reserve and the Starvation margin is null. This matters more here than elsewhere in the batch because the derived reserve floor (144,444 EU at the ceiling) exceeds the stated capacity of two of the five carded practitioners in the corpus, including one four Stages above the working's floor.

options.option: Write a card for an Ashblood Apostate, the one lineage the page describes as standing doctrine rather than a single incident.
options.changes: Gives the working a practitioner, a faction and a motive; a new character needs its own authorisation.

options.option: Attach Oathrend to an existing carded practitioner with a Fate Path and an S-Grade Resilience.
options.changes: No new character; requires a ruling on who, and the working's politics make the choice consequential.

options.option: Leave it exemplar-free and take every figure from the Tier bands, as the Harmonic tree does.
options.changes: No new material; the account states its numbers as bands and says why.

quote_a: Craft · Spellcraft (a spoken renunciation).
quote_b: Below Stage VII, Refraction, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary. At Refraction the practitioner can hold the Crystal as an object of study and the Glyph Roles compress into an internal chain that needs no material anchor at all.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: Fairness check 4 is only a partial pass. Oathrend's floor is Stage IX, two full Stages above Refraction, so Law V does not require the voice and nothing on the page says the spoken renunciation is mandatory rather than customary. A silent Oathrend has no tell at all: the parties learn of it only afterwards, as a felt absence, and the stated counter (catch the counter-field before it locks) requires under a second of warning that nothing provides. Edictum, by contrast, sits exactly at Refraction and keeps its voice for stated institutional reasons; Oathrend keeps its voice for no stated reason.

options.option: State that the renunciation must be spoken and give the reason: a cancellation with no utterance leaves no record, and the Concord will not recognise an unrecorded unbinding.
options.changes: Mirrors Edictum's institutional logic, restores the 'interrupt the chain' counter at every Stage, and makes clandestine Oathrend an unrecognised act rather than an easy one.

options.option: Rule the voice optional above Refraction and add a different tell - the anchor points ring before they null, audible to a Harmonist or to any party to the oath.
options.changes: Keeps silent casting possible and gives the Harmonic tree a job; creates a cross-discipline dependency where Bond Reading and Oathrend meet.

options.option: Accept that a prepared, silent Oathrend is undetectable and state that this is why Purganeth-witnessed swearing exists: the counter is bought at the swearing because it cannot be bought later.
options.changes: No mechanical change; puts the whole weight of fairness on preparation, which is consistent with the challenge doctrine but leaves an unprepared target with nothing.

quote_a: Physics Domain · Remanence (a substrate retaining an imposed state after the imposing field is withdrawn).
quote_b: The fragment is still tethered to what it was cut from - sever that tether (kill the original, break the focus, or place it inside an active Silence field) and the echo stops being anything at all, the same failure mode Animatria suffers.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Imprinta.md
why: The page's stated Physics Domain and the page's stated Weakness are mutually exclusive. Remanence is defined on the page itself as retention after the imposing field is withdrawn: a magnetised bar is not connected to the magnet, basalt is not connected to the planetary field that wrote it, a fired potsherd is not connected to the radiation it recorded. An Animatria construct is the opposite by definition - 'It maintains continuity through a tether back to its source, which is why Animatria summoning fails completely inside Silence Realms' (The Spirit Summoning Arts). The page has chosen remanence as its mechanism and Animatria's counter as its weakness. The Cost line supports remanence ('spent outright and permanently, the way a limb is not on loan'); the Counter and Weakness lines support the tether. Only one can be true, and the difference decides whether a Silence Realm does anything at all to an Imprinta.

options.option: Keep remanence and rewrite the Weakness and Counter: an Imprinta has no tether, is unaffected by Silence and by the caster's death, and is beaten by damaging the substrate or by Anamnesis thermal resetting.
options.changes: Makes Imprinta genuinely permanent and genuinely dangerous, removes the cheapest counter in the register from it, and promotes a counter that is currently only in the Limina register. The Cost line already agrees.

options.option: Keep the tether and change the Physics Domain from remanence to something tethered - resonant coupling under Transference, or Animatria's own continuity - and refile the Category from Mnemata to Animatria.
options.changes: Makes the page internally consistent and makes Imprinta a species of Animatria, which also forces its Stage floor up to VI (SA-CROSS-IMPRINTA-ANIMATRIA-GATE) and contradicts the permanent-detachment Cost line.

options.option: Rule that both are true of different Imprinta: a fragment deposited with the tether cut is remanent and permanent, one deposited with the tether intact is an Animatria construct in a substrate, and the caster chooses at the write.
options.changes: Two workings under one name, two cost structures and two counters; the richest option and the largest, and it makes 'which kind is this' a question a player has to answer in play.

options.option: Rule that the tether is to the deposit's origin moment rather than to the living caster - Anamnesis's record, not a live line - so killing the original does nothing and destroying the record does.
options.changes: Preserves the word 'tether', keeps remanence physically honest, and invents a new target: the archive or the place the memory came from.

quote_a: Stage floor · Stage IV — Flourishing. Grade required · B-Grade.
quote_b: Temperance Gate · Stage VI (Glory) for basic eidolons · Stage VIII (Transcendence) for semi-autonomous forms · Stage X (Realization) for constructs capable of independent tactical action.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Summoning Arts.md
why: The page states that its deposit suffers 'the same failure mode Animatria suffers' and describes a detached Core fragment operating with limited independence, which is the Spirit Summoning Arts' definition of an Animatria construct. Animatria's own floor for a basic eidolon is Stage VI and for a semi-autonomous form Stage VIII. Imprinta produces a semi-independent echo at Stage IV, two Stages below the basic floor and four below the semi-autonomous one, for 8,000-15,000 EU against Animatria's stated 75,000-150,000 EU fabrication band. If the tether reading of SA-EM-IMPRINTA-REMANENCE-VERSUS-TETHER wins, Imprinta is a hugely cheaper Animatria available four Stages early.

options.option: Rule Imprinta remanent rather than Animatria (see SA-EM-IMPRINTA-REMANENCE-VERSUS-TETHER option one), which removes the comparison entirely.
options.changes: Resolves both conflicts at once; a remanent deposit is not a construct and is not gated by the Summoning ladder.

options.option: Raise Imprinta's floor to Stage VIII and its cost into the Animatria band.
options.changes: Makes it a rare and expensive working, which contradicts the page's account of imprints left by ordinary people at emotional moments.

options.option: Rule that an Imprinta's independence is genuinely lesser than an eidolon's - it reacts, it does not act - and state the line, keeping the low floor and low cost.
options.changes: Preserves the page and draws a distinction the Summoning Arts does not currently make: reaction is cheap and early, action is expensive and late.

quote_a: A piece of the caster's own Essence Core, paid and detached at the moment of casting - not drawn from reserve on an ongoing basis, but spent outright and permanently, the way a limb is not "on loan."
quote_b: Essence Core | The Soul-Plane layer. Holds identity, memory, and Traits. | Fracture into Shards
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The only permanent personal cost in the Spellcraft batch is stated in kind and never in quantity. No unit in the system measures a fraction of an Essence Core, so a practitioner's tenth Imprinta cannot be distinguished from their first, there is no threshold at which the subtraction becomes dangerous, and the cost cannot be tracked on a Ledger. The Core's own failure state is Fracture into Shards and the working performs a miniature version of it deliberately, with no stated accounting.

options.option: Measure the Core in Traits: an Imprinta costs a stated fraction of a Trait's worth of Core, and a practitioner who spends enough loses one outright.
options.changes: Uses an existing countable unit, gives the cost a visible threshold, and makes an Imprinta specialist someone whose Traits are measurably thinning - which the Flicker already describes.

options.option: Measure it as a permanent reduction in maximum EU, stated as a percentage per casting.
options.changes: Makes the cost fully numeric and trackable and ties it to the reserve ladder; requires a percentage, which would be an invented number until ruled.

options.option: Rule the Core unquantifiable by design and state that the cost is recorded narratively on the Ledger rather than numerically.
options.changes: No new units; keeps the cost real at a table and unavailable to arithmetic, which is consistent with how the corpus treats identity elsewhere.

quote_a: Anamnesis is the Wellspring version of that retained trace: the medium keeps the shape of what was pressed into it.
quote_b: Anamnesis is the instrument, not the miracle.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: Every line of Anamnesis's register describes an instrument for reading records that ordinary physical process laid down: the practitioner reads history through contact with objects, places and beings. Imprinta uses the same Wellspring to write one deliberately. The system states no rule about whether a Wellspring's law can be run in reverse, and this is not an isolated case - the Harmonic Arts' 'perception and manipulation are the same skill applied with different intent' makes the same move for a different discipline. A general ruling is available and none exists.

options.option: State a general principle: a Wellspring's law is symmetric and may be run receptively or projectively, with the projective direction carrying the register's Failure as its standing risk.
options.changes: Covers Imprinta, the whole Harmonic tree and any future reading discipline; makes Anamnesis's thermal resetting the price of writing as well as of reading.

options.option: Rule the reversal specific to Anamnesis and state why: remanence is intrinsically bidirectional because writing and reading a hysteretic medium are the same operation at different amplitudes.
options.changes: A narrow and physically honest ruling that does not commit the corpus to symmetry everywhere.

options.option: Rule that Imprinta does not reverse Anamnesis at all - the caster supplies the field and Anamnesis merely certifies that the record is genuine - so the Wellspring stays a reading one.
options.changes: Keeps the register consistent and moves the writing work to the Essence Core, which the Cost line already pays for.

quote_a: Path gate · None documented.
quote_b: Retention requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D, and Stage VI to exceed A for the number of complete workings held loaded. Analysis open, though diagnosis of external fields and living beings requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page names Gnosis (Retention, Analysis) as governing Primary, Harmonics (Attunement) as secondary, and requires B-Grade at Stage IV. Part Seven gates Gnosis Retention on the Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D and Gnosis Analysis on the Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B, and Harmonics Attunement on the Attraction Path at Stage II to exceed D. All three bite at or below this working's stated Grade, so 'None documented' is wrong. Same class as SA-CROSS-EDICTUM-PATH-GATE and SA-CROSS-OATHREND-PATH-GATE.

options.option: Correct the Path gate line from Part Seven: Spirit Path primary, Attraction Path secondary.
options.changes: No invention; makes Imprinta unavailable to a practitioner with neither Path, which meaningfully narrows who leaves echoes behind.

options.option: Rule 'None documented' a statement about the source card under a standing note that Part Seven always governs.
options.changes: No page edits; closes the class.

quote_a: The card's three mortal derivations — Soji the Dreamwalker, Caldran of Athame, the Choir of Vellsorea — are unattested individually
quote_b: Essence Capacity 1,600 EU and Flux Density 3.2 × 10² EU/g carry across from the legacy sheet. I have not been able to source EU benchmarks by Stage and cannot confirm these are in range. Flagged rather than restated.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Karo Venrik · The Foolish Magus.md
why: No Imprinta caster has a card. The nearest carded practitioner in Stage terms is Karo Venrik at Stage V with 1,600 EU, one Stage above this working's floor and unable to afford its cheapest casting by a factor of five - and his own card flags the reserve figure as unsourceable for the same reason this batch logs SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA. So the batch's cheapest working has no practitioner who can demonstrably pay for it.

options.option: Write a card for an Anamnesis practitioner at the working's own Stage floor.
options.changes: Gives the batch its only low-Stage exemplar and a reserve figure to check costs against; a new character needs its own authorisation.

options.option: Resolve Karo Venrik's flagged reserve figure first, since it is the only low-Stage datum in the corpus and is declared unverified on its own card.
options.changes: Fixes the datum every low-Stage cost comparison depends on; it is a card edit and belongs to whoever owns that card.

options.option: Leave it exemplar-free and take every figure from the Tier bands.
options.changes: No new material; the account says so.

quote_a: an imprint left with no emotional charge behind it tends to sit inert rather than awaken
quote_b: It has a tell. A careful opponent can read it coming.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Fairness check 4 fails. A dormant Imprinta has no emission, no upkeep, no draw and no signature, because it is a state of a substrate rather than a working in progress; the page's own word is that it 'tends to remain a dormant, undetected trace'. Nothing can be read coming, because the deposit was laid down years or centuries earlier and does nothing at all until its trigger condition is met, at which point it has already happened. Unlike Resonant Divination, which at least has institutional countertells, an Imprinta has no associated person to observe.

options.option: Give a dormant deposit a faint, findable Aetheric Residue signature readable by Gnosis Analysis or by an Anamnesis practitioner on contact.
options.changes: Creates a real counter-profession and makes sweeping a room for echoes a thing a careful party does; consistent with Residue being 'always readable by someone patient enough'.

options.option: Give the waking a tell instead of the dormancy: the deposit rings before it acts, giving one beat of warning.
options.changes: Keeps the deposit undetectable and makes the encounter survivable; smallest change and it preserves the working's character.

options.option: Accept the absence and state that an Imprinta is found by research rather than by perception - the maker, the moment and the place are a documentary trail.
options.changes: No mechanical change; makes the counter archival and rewards exactly the lookup behaviour the challenge doctrine wants.

options.option: Rule that a narrowly-triggered deposit is undetectable and a broadly-triggered one leaks, so the caster trades concealment against reach at the write.
options.changes: Turns the tell into a design decision the caster makes, which gives a player something to reason about in both directions.

quote_a: the rite raises the entropy of the mixed, bound configuration above the entropy of the two components held apart - once the separated state is thermodynamically preferred, the process completes on its own
quote_b: A solid dissolves not because the solvent attacks it but because the mixed state has higher entropy than the separated one, and the process therefore runs on its own once initiated.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: The page's sentence does not reach its own conclusion. If the rite raises the entropy of the bound configuration above that of the separated components, then the bound state is the preferred one and nothing separates. For separation to be spontaneous the separated state must have the lower free energy, which means raising the free energy of the bound configuration or lowering the separated pair's - typically by supplying a solvent, which is what a solvation analogue actually describes. The Dissolution register is self-consistent because there 'mixed' means dissolved-into-a-solvent; the technique page has carried the register's sentence across while reversing which state counts as mixed.

options.option: Rewrite the sentence in free-energy terms: the rite raises the free energy of the bound configuration relative to the separated pair, and the offering and catalyst are the solvent that does it.
options.changes: Closes the physics, gives the seven-step apparatus a mechanical function it currently lacks, and makes the Offering and Catalyst steps the reagents rather than the ceremony.

options.option: Keep the entropy framing and correct the direction: the rite raises the entropy of the separated state, by dispersing the freed component into a prepared medium.
options.changes: Smallest textual change, stays in the register's own vocabulary, and makes the circle the medium the freed half disperses into - which would also explain why the piece comes back fragmentary.

options.option: Rule that Soul-Plane entropy runs opposite to material entropy and state that as a system principle.
options.changes: Preserves the sentence and commits the corpus to an inverted thermodynamics on one Plane, with consequences for every entropy-based Wellspring in Limina.

quote_a: a full seven-step rite ... severs a bond of up to Stage VI density in roughly six to twelve minutes of ritual time, at an estimated 40,000-60,000 EU
quote_b: Aetheric Saturation · A danger state in which excessive Essence floods an area faster than it can disperse. Produces Crystal Fracture Events in everyone exposed, including the person who caused it.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: At Tier 5 efficiency (eta 0.60-0.70, Part Nineteen as corrected by R44-4) a ceiling-cost Scission wastes 18,000-24,000 EU as heat, sound and structural bleed, delivered over six to twelve minutes into one small fixed circle: roughly 25 to 67 EU per second, sustained, in a room nobody may leave. The Core Vocabulary's saturation danger state is the obvious hazard and neither the technique page nor the Counterplay register mentions it for any ritual working. The system has a named danger with no threshold, so whether a Scission chamber is dangerous to its own officiants cannot be determined.

options.option: State a saturation threshold in EU per second per unit volume in the Core Vocabulary, and apply it to every sustained working.
options.changes: Gives the corpus its first field-hazard number and makes ritual chamber design a real discipline; it is a new number and needs a basis.

options.option: Rule that the Space and Circle steps of a Ritus exist precisely to manage dispersal, and state that an improvised circle carries saturation risk.
options.changes: No numbers; gives two of the seven steps a mechanical purpose and makes a hasty rite dangerous to its officiants, which is a good pressure.

options.option: Rule that bleed disperses rather than accumulating for workings below some scale, and mark ritual saturation as a concern only for multi-caster work.
options.changes: Keeps ordinary rites safe and reserves the hazard for the Cantic Order and large ritual teams, where it also gives Thaumic Ritual Stabilization something to stabilise.

quote_a: Path gate · None documented.
quote_b: Ward requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C, with defence of the character's own Domain requiring Fate Path at Stage VIII to exceed SS. ... Analysis open, though diagnosis of external fields and living beings requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page names Resilience (Ward, Anchoring) as governing Primary with Gnosis (Analysis) secondary and requires A-Grade at Stage VI. Part Seven gates Resilience Ward on the Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed C and Gnosis Analysis on the Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed B for diagnosis of living beings, which is exactly what the rite's locating step does. Both bite below this working's stated Grade, so 'None documented' is wrong. Fourth instance of the same class in this section.

options.option: Correct the Path gate line from Part Seven: Spirit Path, required at Stage IV, for both the Ward toll and the diagnostic step.
options.changes: No invention; makes Scission a Spirit-Path rite and explains why it is guild work rather than something a Body-Path practitioner picks up.

options.option: Rule 'None documented' a statement about the source card under a standing note that Part Seven always governs.
options.changes: No page edits; closes all four instances in this section at once.

quote_a: the two named practitioners (Kujo Valorin, Zethyra the Veinwrought — both unattested in current canon and kept because the card's history does not make sense without them)
quote_b: three centuries of Concord casework has not found a fourth candidate
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Scission.md
why: A rite with three centuries of documented Concord casework has no carded practitioner and no carded patient. Every eta, Flux Density and Crystal State in the account is a Tier band, and the Starvation margin is null. This is the most institutionally documented working in the batch and the one least anchored to a person.

options.option: Write a card for a Concord Scission officiant, which would also serve Edictum as an institutional working.
options.changes: One card covers two workings and gives the Accord a working face; a new character needs authorisation.

options.option: Attach the rite to an existing carded practitioner with a Spirit Path and A-Grade Resilience.
options.changes: No new character; requires a ruling on who.

options.option: Rule it institutional and exemplar-free, with every figure from the Tier bands.
options.changes: No new material; the account says so.

quote_a: Stage floor · XI, Dissonance. Grade required · SS-Grade.
quote_b: Level / Stage | 195 / 500 · Band II — Disciplined Foundation · Stage VII — Emanation · Tier of Standing 5, Expert
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Niran Yukari.md
why: Antinomy and Kurotana both require Stage XI, Dissonance, at SS-Grade, and both name Niran Yukari (as Septarch) as the only bearer. His card places him at Stage VII with a highest Sub-Stat of 268, B-Grade; SS-Grade begins at 551. So the sole attested bearer is four Stages and three full Grades below his own signature techniques' stated floor, with his best statistic under half the minimum. The Kurotana page implies the card is an earlier state ('His sheet already records ... a partial Domain seed carrying the exact name Kurotana's completed form uses'), but no page states that Septarch is a future condition, and the Antinomy page writes him in the present tense throughout. A reader holding both documents cannot tell whether Antinomy has ever been performed.

options.option: State on both technique pages that Septarch is a projected apex condition of Niran Yukari and that no sheet for it exists yet, dating the card as the present state.
options.changes: Costs nothing, resolves the tense, and makes both pages design documents for a future rather than records of a present; every scene using Antinomy would then be flagged as out of sequence.

options.option: Write a Septarch sheet at Stage XI with SS-Grade Sub-Stats, a reserve, an eta and a Domain upkeep, as a second card for the same person.
options.changes: Gives both techniques a costable bearer and the batch its only Grandmaster figures; a second card for one character is a structure the corpus does not currently use.

options.option: Lower Antinomy's and Kurotana's Stage floor and Grade to something Niran's card can reach.
options.changes: Makes both techniques performable now and shrinks them considerably; Kurotana's whole account of a rebuilt vessel reads oddly at Stage VII, and Dissonance is Stage XI by definition.

options.option: Rule the card stale and advance Niran's Stage on it.
options.changes: One card edit, but it contradicts the card's own detailed account of a Stage VII Crystal with a partial Domain seed and proto-Ketsumyogan, which is internally coherent and recently written.

quote_a: Aether | Class III Resonant — Acoustic Consequence Architect · Thread-Lock Reader. 16,376 AU/s · η 0.89
quote_b: 5 · Expert | V–VII Splintering to Refraction | 0.50–0.60 | First genuine efficiency; the Crystal has learned to stop leaking.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VII. Aether Class, Essence Typology, Aether Flow (Parts Seventeen–Nineteen).md
why: Niran's card states eta 0.89 and Tier of Standing 5, Expert, at Stage VII. Part Nineteen puts Tier 5 at 0.50-0.60. The card's figure sits in the Tier 7 Grandmaster band (0.85-0.90), which is the band for Stages XI-XII, which is exactly where his two signature techniques (Antinomy, Kurotana) place him. So the eta matches the techniques' Stage and not the card's. Extends SA-NUM-ETA-TIER, which enumerates five other cards and does not include this one. Note that the card is otherwise arithmetically clean: 18,400 x 0.89 = 16,376, so R44-2 holds on it without correction.

options.option: Rule the eta correct and the Stage understated, advancing the card's Stage to match both the eta and the technique floors.
options.changes: Resolves this and SA-CROSS-SEPTARCH-STAGE-VERSUS-CARD together; contradicts the card's detailed Stage VII architecture, and the AU/s would have to be rechecked against the new Stage's ceilings.

options.option: Rule the Stage correct and the eta out of band, bringing it to 0.50-0.60 — which under R44-2 moves the AU/s as well, since Flux Density x eta governs.
options.changes: Drops his stated output from 16,376 AU/s to roughly 9,200-11,000; the card is currently one of the few that satisfies R44-2 exactly, and this would be the first correction applied to a card that was already consistent.

options.option: Rule that Tier of Standing bands are typical rather than binding, and that eta may sit outside its Tier where a card states a reason.
options.changes: Resolves this row and the five in SA-NUM-ETA-TIER at once, and makes eta a genuine diagnostic axis rather than a lookup — which Part Five's own note already half-says ('two practitioners at the same Tier with different eta are the same rank and not the same problem').

options.option: Hold the card and log it beside the other out-of-band etas pending a single ruling on the whole set.
options.changes: Defers; nothing moves, and the row stands with the five already recorded.

quote_a: Crystal State | Harmonic-Emergent. Settled and load-bearing; Ketsumyogan proto-expression stabilised into early active manifestation.
quote_b: Crystal States · The three conditions a Soul Crystal can occupy. Fractured (split by trauma or overload, producing erratic casting and identity leak), Refined (balanced and coherent, the baseline healthy state), and Overgrown (power exceeding architecture, producing involuntary discharge). Crystallized is not a State; self-as-law belongs to the Crystallized Soul tier alone.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The system states three Crystal States and names them. 'Harmonic-Emergent' is not one of them, and 'Harmonic' is a Developmental Tier (Part Twenty-One) rather than a State — the card has crossed the two axes. The Core Vocabulary already polices this exact error for a different term ('Crystallized is not a State'), so the distinction is one the corpus cares about. Every system account naming this practitioner must therefore record Crystal State as unattested rather than as stated.

options.option: Correct the card to Refined, which is what 'settled and load-bearing' describes in the system's own words.
options.changes: One field; the descriptive sentence after it survives unchanged and reads as a gloss on Refined.

options.option: Split the field on the card into Crystal State (Refined) and Developmental Tier (Resonant, per Part Twenty-One at Stage VII), which is what the card appears to be trying to say.
options.changes: Two fields where there was one; brings the card into line with the two-axis system and is the more complete fix.

options.option: Add 'Emergent' to the Core Vocabulary as a fourth State for Crystals mid-transition.
options.changes: A new mechanic, and the Core Vocabulary's own sentence about Crystallized suggests the list is deliberately closed.

quote_a: Weakness · Septarch's own unresolved contradiction, that he rejected Niran Yukari first, destabilizes the working back onto its caster whenever the target's situation mirrors that specific shape.
quote_b: Failure · The cancellation is symmetric. Everything the practitioner brought inside is subject to the same null, including the parts of themselves they were relying on.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: Antinomy runs three Wellsprings and carries none of their documented Failures. Nihiloth: the cancellation is symmetric, so whatever of Septarch's is inside the coupled system is nulled with the target's - and the page has him holding their fear, love, shame and contradiction inside his own lattice, which is inside. Oblivara: code exhaustion, past which the reconstruction is 'confident, complete, and wrong', so a read past the redundancy limit tunes with certainty to a mode the target does not have. Transference: reverse coupling, a gradient running both directions. The page carries only a personal-history weakness. The stratal account therefore describes a working with three standing hazards and the technique page prices none of them.

options.option: Add all three Wellspring Failures to the page as standing risks, each with the condition that triggers it.
options.changes: Gives the technique three failure modes an opponent can induce rather than one that depends on knowing his biography; makes repeated use genuinely dangerous to him.

options.option: Add Nihiloth's symmetric null only, as the cost of the transit: each lock nulls something of Septarch's for its duration.
options.changes: Smallest addition and the most thematic - he goes without something of his own for as long as he holds their contradiction - and it gives the transit a measurable shape.

options.option: Rule that Oblivara's redundancy is what protects him from the symmetric null, so the three Wellsprings are balanced against each other and no Failure fires unless one is absent.
options.changes: Turns the three-Wellspring stack into an interlocking design and makes disrupting any one of them the counter; the most elegant and the largest claim.

options.option: State on the page that the Wellspring Failures apply as written and need no restatement, with a standing note that every technique inherits its Wellsprings' failures.
options.changes: No page-by-page work; establishes a general reading rule that would apply across the corpus and close this class of omission everywhere.

quote_a: Every use requires Septarch to hold the target's fear, love, shame and contradiction inside his own Soul Crystal lattice for the duration of contact; this is a real transit, not observation, and it is the only genuine expense the technique carries.
quote_b: Efficiency · Eta · η · The ratio of Essence spent to Essence that arrives as intended effect.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The system measures expenditure: Essence spent, output rate, efficiency of conversion. Antinomy's sole stated cost is not an expenditure but a transit - another person's interior moving through the practitioner's lattice and being held there. The system has no unit for that, no capacity limit for it, no rate, and no rule for whether eta applies to it. Consequently there is no point at which Septarch is full, no count of how many locks he can hold, and no way to put the technique on a Ledger. The same shape appears on Kurotana via Vantabriel's retained load.

options.option: Define a lattice capacity in the Core Vocabulary: a stated number of concurrent transits or a saturation threshold, past which the held material begins acting on the holder.
options.changes: Creates a new resource with immediate consequences for Antinomy, Kurotana and any Vantabriel practitioner; needs a scale.

options.option: Price the transit in Harmonics or Resilience rather than EU: holding a foreign contradiction spends the Sub-Stat that keeps one's own coherent, and a depleted holder loses the lock.
options.changes: Uses existing Sub-Stats, makes the limit exhaustible in a scene, and makes the counter 'outlast him' available where it currently is not.

options.option: Rule that a transit is free but leaves permanent residue, so the cost is cumulative and biographical rather than per-scene.
options.changes: Fits the character and the Debt reading, and makes a career of Antinomy a slow ruin; unavailable to in-scene arithmetic.

options.option: Rule the transit unquantifiable by design and record it narratively on the Ledger.
options.changes: No new units; keeps the cost real at a table and outside arithmetic, consistent with how the corpus treats identity elsewhere.

quote_a: Path gate · Attraction, dominant.
quote_b: Persistence requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed S, and Stage VIII to exceed SS against Oblivion-class pressure. ... Suppression requires Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed A.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page's FOW line names Harmonics Suppression, Gnosis Cognition, Dominion Sense, Resilience Nullity and Warding among its Sub-Stats and requires SS-Grade. Part Seven gates Harmonics Suppression on the Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed A, and Resilience Persistence on the Fate Path at Stage VIII to exceed SS. At SS-Grade both bite, so a single Attraction gate is incomplete rather than wrong. Milder than the four Design Chain pages' 'None documented', but the same omission.

options.option: Extend the Path gate line to Attraction dominant, Spirit and Fate required, per Part Seven.
options.changes: No invention; narrows the technique to a three-Path practitioner, which at Stage XI is plausible and makes the requirement genuinely demanding.

options.option: Rule that a page's named dominant Path is the requirement and secondary gates are assumed met at the stated Stage.
options.changes: No page edits; establishes a reading convention that would also cover the four Design Chain pages.

quote_a: Derived by Septarch alone, as the technical expression of Kurotana's Black Mandate fused with the Recognition, Refusal and Redrafting doctrine unique to his own fate-state
quote_b: EU Reserve 485,000 · Flux Density 18,400 EU/g · AU/s 16,376 · Passive Recovery 28% EU/min · Active 8%
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Niran Yukari.md
why: Septarch, the bearer of both Stage XI techniques in this section, has no sheet. The only figures available are the pre-Kurotana card's, which describe a different Stage, a different Grade band and a Domain seed rather than the completed Domain. So neither Antinomy nor Kurotana can be costed, their Starvation margins are null, and the completed Murder of Crows carries no upkeep figure while its seed carries a precise one (8,400 EU/s).

options.option: Write a Septarch sheet at Stage XI, with reserve, Flux Density, eta, Domain upkeep and the SS-Grade Sub-Stat spread.
options.changes: Costs both techniques and gives the batch its only Grandmaster figures; a second sheet for one character needs a structural decision.

options.option: Extend Niran's existing card with a projected Septarch column, so one document carries both states.
options.changes: Keeps one card per character and makes the transformation legible as an arc; a new card format.

options.option: Leave Septarch uncosted and state on both technique pages that no sheet exists, so no scene may quote a figure.
options.changes: No new material; both accounts already say so, and it prevents invented numbers entering play.

quote_a: The bearer forfeits the original body's authority and lets fate rebuild them as an instrument of one forced outcome.
quote_b: The Essence account, at all three strata, in diagnostic voice.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: Kurotana permanently rebuilds all three layers of a Soul Crystal and enables five named capabilities including a Domain, and states no number anywhere: no EU for the Black Recognition, none for Soul Drafting, Consequence Architecture, Name Revision or the Black Mandate, no Domain upkeep, no radius, no reserve, no eta and no saturation threshold. It is the largest single transformation described in the Spellcraft section and the only one with an entirely empty Essence stratum. The physical account, by contrast, closes unusually well: the single-crystal reading explains the endurance, the self-repair, the terrain-like presence, the resistance to weapons and the death by clean contradiction as one material fact.

options.option: Bill the Black Recognition once, as the Three Witnesses and nothing else, and state explicitly that the vessel has no marginal cost - a state, not a working.
options.changes: Closes the books on the Edictum/Imprinta model (pay once, hold for nothing) and makes the entry price the whole price, which is defensible and makes the bearer genuinely tireless.

options.option: Bill the five capabilities individually in EU, with the Black Mandate scaling by abstraction as the page already implies.
options.changes: Gives the vessel a reserve to run down and restores the exhaustion counter; needs figures and a Septarch sheet to spend them from.

options.option: Bill it in Vantabriel's retained load rather than in EU: every use increases what the vessel is carrying, and saturation is the ceiling.
options.changes: Uses the Wellspring's own documented failure as the resource, makes patience a real counter, and needs one threshold rather than five costs.

options.option: Rule the vessel deliberately unpriced as a narrative state rather than a mechanical one, and record that on the page.
options.changes: No numbers; makes Kurotana a condition a Judger adjudicates rather than a loadout, and puts the whole weight of balance on the contradiction counter.

quote_a: Vantabriel (Limina, the Wellspring of Night) governs Witness Backlash: what strikes the vessel is kept rather than reflected, and its endurance is carried loss rather than replaced loss
quote_b: Failure · Thermal saturation. Absorption without emission has a limit, and past it the retained load has nowhere to go but into the structure holding it.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
why: The page takes Vantabriel's absorption and omits its limit. An absorber with no emission path has a finite capacity, and past it the retained load discharges into the structure holding it - which here is a Monolithion single crystal with, by its own register, nothing to arrest a crack. Saturation and brittle failure are the same catastrophe arriving from inside. Oblation's cavitation failure is similarly unstated and similarly apt: the Three Witnesses drop the pressure term to nearly nothing, and a collapsed pressure term boils and pits the conduit. Without a stated saturation threshold the exhaustion route in Counterplay III does not reach this vessel at all.

options.option: State a Vantabriel saturation threshold for the vessel, in absorbed load or in engagement time, past which the retained load discharges through the lattice.
options.changes: Restores 'outlast him' as a real counter and gives a long fight a clock; needs a scale, and would apply to every Vantabriel practitioner.

options.option: Rule that the completed Domain is the emission path - the crows carry the retained load outward - so saturation never occurs while the Domain holds and occurs rapidly when it is suppressed.
options.changes: Ties the two halves together elegantly and makes Silence or Domain suppression the trigger for the failure rather than time; a strong and findable counter.

options.option: Add Oblation's cavitation as the Drafted Vessel's self-repair failure: the conduit pits where the pressure term collapsed, and the repair degrades along those pits.
options.changes: Explains 'for as long as its own self-design stays coherent' mechanically and gives the vessel a slow decay the page currently only gestures at.

quote_a: The Black Mandate issues short fate-commands, and the cost rises with how abstract the command is.
quote_b: Cost · 2,800 to 8,900 EU per branch, drawn from Dougou's 92,000 EU reserve; Kokushin Gyuha costs 7,400 EU exactly per his sheet.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/The Iron Tree.md
why: Kurotana states a cost relation ('rises with how abstract the command is') with no scale, no anchor and no worked example, for five distinct capabilities. The Iron Tree, the neighbouring bloodline-apex page in the same section, prices every one of its eight branches to the hundred EU against a stated reserve. The two pages are the same kind of document about the same kind of thing and one is fully costed and the other is not costed at all.

options.option: Price the five capabilities on the Iron Tree model: a per-use EU figure for each, against a stated Septarch reserve.
options.changes: Makes the two apex pages comparable and gives Kurotana a Ledger presence; requires the Septarch sheet (SA-GAP-SEPTARCH-NO-SHEET) first.

options.option: State the Black Mandate's abstraction scale as a small number of named tiers with an EU figure each.
options.changes: Prices the one capability whose cost relation is already stated, and leaves the other four; a partial and cheap fix.

options.option: Rule the vessel's capabilities uncosted by design and state why on the page.
options.changes: No numbers; consistent with SA-PHYS-KUROTANA-UNBILLED option four.

quote_a: The completed Domain, Murder of Crows, Cathedral of Unchosen Futures, marks each significant choice with a crow
quote_b: Domain · Murder of Crows — seed, partial active. 40m warning field / 18m active pressure. ... Maintenance 8,400 EU/s at full · Collapse: eleven+ simultaneous threats, Stage IX+ Domain invasion, triplanar Ketsumyogan overload
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Niran Yukari.md
why: The partial seed of this Domain carries a precise upkeep (8,400 EU/s), a radius (40m warning, 18m pressure) and three stated collapse conditions. The completed Domain, four Stages higher and carrying a Nihiloth null field, carries none of the three. From the card's figures the seed sustains for about fifty-two seconds from a full 485,000 EU reserve; the completed Domain's endurance is unknowable, which means the single most important tactical question about the corpus's most developed Domain cannot be answered.

options.option: State the completed Domain's upkeep, radius and collapse conditions on the Kurotana page, scaled from the seed's figures.
options.changes: Makes the apex Domain playable and gives the vessel a clock; scaling from a seed to a completed Domain has no stated rule, so the multiplier would need ruling.

options.option: Rule the completed Domain upkeep-free, as the standing structure of the vessel rather than a sustained working - Monolithion 'becomes the standing structure of the crow-Domain itself', per the page's own line.
options.changes: Consistent with the page's own Wellspring assignment and with the vessel being a state rather than a working; removes the exhaustion counter entirely and makes Silence the only field answer.

options.option: Rule the completed Domain sustained by the crows themselves - each marked choice funds its own mark - so upkeep scales with the number of significant choices in the field rather than with time.
options.changes: A new cost shape, strongly thematic, and it makes a quiet room cheap and a crowded decision expensive; needs a scale.

quote_a: Category: Conjunction, the same as Moetana's own "Conjunctia-class transformation state." Craft: the vessel itself is a standing state rather than a cast working ... Stage floor XI, Dissonance; Grade SS.
quote_b: FOW line — Governing Primary Harmonics and Gnosis, per Limina's Stat Affinity, with Dominion from Spatium; Sub-Stats Harmonics Suppression, Gnosis Cognition, Dominion Sense, Resilience Nullity and Warding from Oblivara.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Antinomy.md
why: Kurotana carries no FOW line: no governing Primary, no Sub-Stats, no Path gate and no Resonant Pair, while its own derived technique Antinomy carries a complete one on the facing page. Without a governing Primary, Part Seven's gate table cannot be consulted at all, so unlike every other page in this section the Path requirements cannot even be derived. Six of the twenty pages in this section carry a FOW line and Kurotana, the section's largest working, is not one of them.

options.option: Write a FOW line for Kurotana from its four Wellsprings' Stat Affinities, as the Antinomy page does from its three.
options.changes: No invention beyond following the registers; makes the Path gates derivable and puts the working on the same footing as its own derivative.

options.option: Rule that a Conjunction-class transformation state has no FOW line by definition, because it alters the sheet rather than being cast from it, and state that convention.
options.changes: Establishes a category rule that would also cover Moetana and Gisei; makes transformation states a different kind of document from techniques.

options.option: Inherit Antinomy's FOW line upward, since Antinomy is the vessel's technical expression.
options.changes: Cheapest; risks understating a working that spans four Wellsprings against a derivative that runs three.

quote_a: Vantabriel combines them: what strikes the practitioner is kept rather than reflected, and the Crystal's condition is a function of everything it has ever absorbed. Endurance here is carried loss, not replaced loss.
path_a: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md
quote_b: The remainder leaves as heat, sound, and structural bleed, which is why a low-efficiency practitioner is loud, warm, and easy to find, and why the highest Bands run quiet.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: The system's account of efficiency assumes the wasted fraction leaves: it becomes heat, sound and structural bleed, and that is why a low-eta practitioner is loud, warm and easy to find. A Vantabriel practitioner's bleed does not leave - absorption without emission is the Wellspring's defining property. So the standard diagnostic inverts (such a practitioner runs cold and quiet regardless of eta) and the retained fraction accumulates with no stated term, no unit and no threshold. Dougou Ozumu Zettari's card states the same architecture in different words ('external leak near-zero by design', 'internal cycling immeasurable'), which is why his AU/s could not be recomputed under R44-2 (CONFLICTS.md C-054).

options.option: Add a retained-bleed term to the Core Vocabulary alongside eta: the fraction of waste a Crystal keeps rather than radiates, with saturation as its failure.
options.changes: Gives Vantabriel and sealed-architecture practitioners a proper accounting, explains why such practitioners are hard to locate, and connects directly to C-054's unresolved question about Dougou's output.

options.option: Rule that retained bleed is why such practitioners read as low-output externally while cycling far more internally, and state that as the reading rule for sealed architectures.
options.changes: No new unit; makes external AU/s and internal cycling two different measurements and would inform the C-054 ruling.

options.option: Rule the retained fraction lost to the structure permanently, as accumulated damage rather than stored energy.
options.changes: Makes Vantabriel endurance genuinely costly over a career, which matches 'carried loss, not replaced loss', and gives the Wellspring a long-run price.

quote_a: Grade required · A-Grade minimum; X-Grade at Dougou's personal apex.
quote_b: Numerical Effect · Per the Physical Benchmarks table and Dougou's own sheet, output at apex reaches 12,000,000 N and 8 to 20 MJ, at the boundary between D-Grade and low C-Grade force
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/The Iron Tree.md
why: One page states both. Part Four puts X-Grade attack output at 4.184e21 to 1.24e29 J and D-Grade at 1.5e4 to 2.092e7 J. The page's stated apex output of 8 to 20 MJ (8e6 to 2e7 J) is D-Grade, which the page itself correctly identifies, and is fifteen orders of magnitude below the X-Grade band it simultaneously requires. Part Four does supply a partial reading, since Grade is read off a Sub-Stat's raw value rather than off a technique's delivered output, so an X-Grade practitioner may throw a D-Grade blow; but the page says 'output at apex reaches', which is a ceiling claim about the technique, and a ceiling fifteen orders below the stated Grade is a contradiction rather than a spread.

options.option: Keep the output and drop the Grade line to what the output supports, stating that the Iron Tree is a D-to-C-Grade technique wielded by an X-Grade practitioner and that this is deliberate - it is a concentration weapon, not a magnitude one.
options.changes: Makes the working's whole point explicit and unusual: a Stage XIII practitioner whose signature discipline delivers building-scale rather than country-scale force, because the mechanism concentrates rather than scales. Nothing else in the corpus reads this way.

options.option: Keep the Grade and raise the output into the X band.
options.changes: Turns every branch into a planetary event and destroys the shaped-charge reading, the 12 MN figure, the card's own 5-12 MN line and the behind-armour effects that make the technique interesting.

options.option: Rule that 'Grade required' names the Sub-Stat Grade a practitioner must hold, not the output Grade delivered, and state that convention on every technique page.
options.changes: Resolves this and any similar mismatch corpus-wide, and makes the Grade line a gate on the caster rather than a claim about the effect; the cleanest general fix.

options.option: Split the line: A-Grade minimum to perform, D-to-C-Grade delivered output, X-Grade the practitioner's own standing.
options.changes: Three figures where there was one, all of them true, and it makes the page a model for how to state the distinction elsewhere.

quote_a: Crystal State. Sealed near-total. Whatever answer he found about being reached, he found it holding almost nothing back
path_a: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Dougou Ozumu Zettari.md
quote_b: Crystal States · The three conditions a Soul Crystal can occupy. Fractured ... Refined ... and Overgrown ... Crystallized is not a State
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: 'Sealed near-total' is not one of the three Crystal States. Unlike Niran's 'Harmonic-Emergent', which is a Developmental Tier in the State field, this one is a description of architecture rather than a mislabelled axis - but it still leaves the State field unstated on a card that every system account of the Iron Tree has to read.
