The same card's Aether Class line ('Closed-World Compression Anchor - external leak near-zero by design') already carries the architecture, so the State field is doing duplicate work instead of its own.

options.option: Set the State to Refined and let 'sealed near-total' stand in the Aether Class line where the architecture already lives.
options.changes: One field; no information lost, since the sealing is stated twice on the card.

options.option: Set the State to Overgrown, on the reading that a containment which never resolved is power exceeding architecture.
options.changes: Changes the card's account of him from a man who succeeded at sealing to one who was failing at it, which bears directly on the page's open question about whether the seal was killing him.

options.option: Add 'Sealed' to the Core Vocabulary as a fourth State for closed architectures.
options.changes: A new mechanic; the Core Vocabulary's sentence about Crystallized suggests the list is closed deliberately.

quote_a: Each release draws down Dougou's 92,000 EU reserve and the vented chamber cannot be re-loaded until the seal recompresses on its own schedule.
quote_b: Passive Recovery 28% EU/min · Active 8%
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Niran Yukari.md
why: The Iron Tree's true rate limiter is not the EU cost but the recompression schedule, and the page states no schedule: no time, no rate, no condition. Seven chambers vented once each is a count the page implies and never gives. Another card in the corpus (Niran Yukari) states recovery as a percentage of reserve per minute, so a format exists; Dougou's card states none. Without it, 'how many branches can he throw in a minute' - the only question that matters in a fight against him - is unanswerable, and the Starvation margin computed from reserve alone (nine to twenty-nine branches) may be far more generous than the real limit.

options.option: State a per-chamber recompression time on the page, and a passive recovery rate on the card in the format Niran's card already uses.
options.changes: Gives the working its real clock and makes a fight against him a resource-management problem in two currencies rather than one; two figures, both new.

options.option: Rule that recompression is tied to the Sevenfold Seal being held closed, so he recharges only while not attacking - which the page's own mutual-exclusion clause already implies.
options.changes: No new numbers, uses a rule the page already states, and produces an elegant rhythm: he must stop to reload, and stopping is when he is armoured.

options.option: Rule that the EU cost is the whole limiter and that recompression is instantaneous with expenditure, striking the schedule clause.
options.changes: Simplest; makes the computed Starvation margin the true one and removes a stated limit, which is the wrong direction for a working this strong.

quote_a: Category · Arts (Body-Aligned: structured, discipline-based styles blending movement, form and Essence flow). Craft · Magicraft.
quote_b: Spellcraft migrated from the old Trello board. See build/publish_imports.py. - [The Iron Tree](Spellcraft/The Iron Tree.md)
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/Spellcraft.md
why: Four of the twenty pages filed on the Spellcraft shelf declare a Craft that is not Spellcraft: The Iron Tree and Mugen no Hatsurugi are Magicraft, Precept is Runecraft, and Kami no Kobushi declines the Four Crafts altogether ('Not clearly one of the Four ... reads nearest to Magicraft where a Craft label is forced on it'). Kurotana states its durability is 'closest to Runecraft'. The shelf is a migration artefact from the Trello board rather than a Craft classification, and the Spellcraft discipline page says so in its first line - but nothing on the individual pages warns a reader that the section name is not a claim about the Craft.

options.option: Add a standing note to the Spellcraft discipline page that the shelf is a migration grouping and each page's own Craft line governs.
options.changes: One sentence; stops every future reader and every future account from having to rediscover it.

options.option: Re-shelve the four pages under their declared Crafts.
options.changes: Moves five documents and breaks existing links and the system-accounts directory structure; the tidiest and the most disruptive.

options.option: Rename the shelf to something that is not a Craft name, since it is not a Craft grouping.
options.changes: One page title and its inbound links; removes the ambiguity at the root rather than annotating it.

quote_a: One concrete data point is given directly: against a light-infantry line, arrivals come at a rate of roughly one weapon transition every two to three strides.
quote_b: Cost · Roughly 45,000 EU per arrival, rising toward 90,000 EU for a weapon named against a significantly higher-weight opponent
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Mugen no Hatsurugi.md
why: The page states a rate in strides and a cost in EU, and no page in the corpus relates a stride to a second. Taking a stride as about a metre: at a fighting pace of roughly half a second per stride, one arrival per 1.0-1.5 s is 30,000-45,000 EU/s, and his 1,850,000 EU reserve (less the ten-percent Starvation floor) supports 37 to 55 seconds of sustained line-breaking. At the card's own Mach 8 sustained, two to three strides pass in about a millisecond, giving roughly 4e7 EU/s and a reserve that empties in about forty milliseconds. The two readings differ by four orders of magnitude, both are supported by the documents, and the difference is between a sustainable battlefield technique and one that cannot be used twice. The same absence blocks every other working in this batch that states a tempo (SA-GAP-TURN-LENGTH).

options.option: State the rate in seconds on the page instead of in strides, and pick the reading that matches the stated cost against the stated reserve.
options.changes: Resolves the working; requires choosing which reading is intended, which decides whether Mugen no Hatsurugi is a minute-long capability or a single burst.

options.option: Define a stride, and an exchange, and a turn in the Core Vocabulary, as the corpus's standard time units.
options.changes: Closes SA-GAP-TURN-LENGTH as well and makes every stated tempo in the corpus computable; a system-wide addition.

options.option: Rule that arrival cost scales down with tempo - a rapid substitution during a single committed exchange is one arrival's cost, not many - and state the rule.
options.changes: Makes the fast reading affordable and turns the ledger into a per-exchange rather than per-weapon cost, which also fits 'the exchange proceeds as though Muken had been holding the weapon the entire time'.

options.option: Rule that Mach 8 sustained is a travel figure and not a fighting-tempo figure, so the slow reading governs in an exchange.
options.changes: Cheapest; keeps both numbers and states which one applies where, and gives 37-55 seconds as the working figure.

quote_a: EU Reserve · 1,850,000 EU · Flux Density 18,600 EU/g · Output 15,624 AU/s · η 0.84
quote_b: 6 · Master | VIII–X Transcendence to Realization | 0.70–0.80 | First true Domain, which provides a feedback loop recycling ambient bleed.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VII. Aether Class, Essence Typology, Aether Flow (Parts Seventeen–Nineteen).md
why: Muken's card states eta 0.84 at Stage X, and Part Nineteen puts Tier 6 (Stages VIII-X) at 0.70-0.80. The figure is above its band. Extends SA-NUM-ETA-TIER, which enumerates five other cards and does not include this one. The consequence is direct and awkward: under R44-2 (AU/s = Flux Density x eta governs and a card's stated AU/s is the error) this card currently needs no correction at all, since 18,600 x 0.84 = 15,624 exactly. Correcting eta into band would move a figure that is presently consistent.

options.option: Rule Tier of Standing eta bands typical rather than binding, so a card may state an out-of-band eta where its architecture warrants it.
options.changes: Resolves this row, SA-NUM-NIRAN-ETA-TIER and the five in SA-NUM-ETA-TIER together, and is consistent with Part Five's own note that two practitioners at one Tier with different eta are the same rank and not the same problem.

options.option: Correct the eta to 0.80 and recompute the AU/s under R44-2 to 14,880.
options.changes: Brings the card into band and moves a figure that currently satisfies R44-2; it would be the first R44-2 correction applied to an already-consistent card.

options.option: Rule his Stage understated rather than his eta overstated, since 0.84 sits between Tier 6 and Tier 7.
options.changes: Contradicts the card's explicit 'XI-XVI - Locked. Died at Stage X.'

options.option: Hold it with the other out-of-band etas pending one ruling on the whole set.
options.changes: Defers; nothing moves.

quote_a: Materia Primordia hosts the weapon's form the way a seed crystal hosts a lattice
quote_b: Failure · Phase locking. Under sufficient pressure the lattice commits to one allotrope permanently, and the practitioner keeps whichever form they were wearing when the pressure came.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md
why: The technique's load-bearing Wellspring has a documented failure that would end it, and the page does not carry it. Materia Primordia's whole gift is polymorphism - one substance, many lattices - and its failure is the loss of that polymorphism under pressure, permanently, leaving whichever form was current. For a practitioner whose armoury is exactly that polymorphism, phase locking means an infinite forge collapsing to a single blade and staying there. Anamnesis's failure is similarly unstated and similarly apt: 'a careless practitioner erases the record in the act of taking it', and his records are his weapons.

options.option: Add phase locking to the page as the technique's structural failure, triggered by sustained pressure - which also gives the working a reason to avoid long engagements.
options.changes: Gives the forge a catastrophic failure mode it currently lacks and makes attrition a real strategy against him rather than only an arithmetic one.

options.option: Add Anamnesis's thermal resetting as a per-use risk: each arrival carries a small chance of degrading the ledger entry it drew on.
options.changes: Makes the armoury a depleting resource across a career rather than a fixed asset, which fits 'the ledger is built across a lifetime'.

options.option: Rule that Fixatio's cure protects the ledger from both failures, and state that as the reason Fixatio is primary.
options.changes: Explains the Wellspring ordering the page already gives and closes both hazards with one sentence; also makes disrupting Fixatio the route to inducing them.

options.option: Adopt the general reading rule that every technique inherits its Wellsprings' documented Failures without restatement.
options.changes: Closes this class across the corpus rather than page by page; the same option appears on SA-PHYS-ANTINOMY-UNCARRIED-FAILURES.

quote_a: Wellspring · Fixatio (primary), Materia Primordia, Coagulatio, Anamnesis, Aurevane, Monolithion.
quote_b: Fractura Primary ... Petralon Secondary ... Coagulatio Tertiary ... Fixatio Active Support ... Judicium Active Support ... Resonance Developed Partial ... Balance-thread Developed Partial ... Mortalis-thread Awakening
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Muken Moto.md
why: The technique names six Wellsprings and the practitioner's card harmonises eight, and only two overlap (Coagulatio, Fixatio - and Fixatio is 'primary' on the technique and 'Active Support' on the card). Materia Primordia, Anamnesis, Aurevane and Monolithion appear nowhere on his card. The card's own five techniques do not include Mugen no Hatsurugi, and the page flags that discrepancy itself ('his later, ratified reign in Kharven, whose own sheet does not carry this technique'), but not the Wellspring mismatch, which is the larger problem: the Core Vocabulary makes harmonisation one of four conditions an Ability needs to develop, so a technique running on four unharmonised currents cannot develop at all as written.

options.option: Add the four missing Wellsprings to Muken's card as harmonisations, at whatever standing the technique requires.
options.changes: Four card fields; makes the technique performable and considerably widens his declared Wellspring stack, which has consequences for every other technique on the card.

options.option: Rewrite the technique's Wellspring line from the card's actual harmonisations - Fractura, Petralon, Coagulatio, Fixatio, Judicium - and rebuild the mechanism from those.
options.changes: Keeps the card and changes the technique; the seed-templating mechanism would have to be re-derived, since Materia Primordia is the Wellspring that supplies the polymorphism the whole working depends on.

options.option: Rule the technique a pre-Kharven working from an earlier harmonisation set, and date both documents, as the page's own Origin note half-suggests.
options.changes: Resolves the technique-not-on-sheet flag and the Wellspring mismatch together by making the card a later state; requires accepting that harmonisations can lapse, which the corpus does not currently state.

options.option: Write the earlier, Plane-of-Fate Muken as his own sheet, so the technique has a bearer whose harmonisations match it.
options.changes: A second sheet for one character, the same structural question SA-GAP-SEPTARCH-NO-SHEET raises.

quote_a: Path gate · Body Path, primary; Attraction Path, secondary, consistent with the 25% Attraction weighting on Muken's own sheet.
quote_b: Retention requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D, and Stage VI to exceed A for the number of complete workings held loaded.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The page's FOW line names Gnosis Retention among the technique's Sub-Stats and requires SS-Grade. Part Seven gates Gnosis Retention on the Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D and at Stage VI to exceed A for the number of complete workings held loaded - which is precisely what an armoury of ratified templates is. The card gives him Spirit/Mind 15%, so the Path exists but is the weakest of his three, and the page's two-Path line does not mention it. Milder than the 'None documented' lines on the four Design Chain pages, since this page at least derived its Paths from the practitioner's own sheet.

options.option: Extend the Path gate line to Body primary, Attraction secondary, Spirit required, per Part Seven.
options.changes: No invention; and it puts real pressure on the technique, since a 15% Spirit weighting is thin for a Sub-Stat gated at Stage VI to exceed A.

options.option: Rule that the Retention gate applies to the ledger's breadth rather than to any single arrival, so a low Spirit weighting caps how many templates he can hold loaded at once.
options.changes: Turns the gap into a mechanic and gives the armoury a stated size, which the page currently leaves unbounded.

options.option: Rule that a page's named dominant Paths govern and secondary gates are assumed met at the stated Stage.
options.changes: No page edits; a reading convention that would also cover the four Design Chain pages.

quote_a: Consequence · The exchange proceeds as though Muken had been holding the weapon the entire time. No tell precedes the arrival.
quote_b: It has a tell. A careful opponent can read it coming.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Fairness check 4 fails as written: the page states twice that there is no visible transition and no tell. A counter does exist and it is genuinely good - Aurevane's documented Failure is 'Glare. Coherent output is also a beacon, and Aurevane practitioners are the easiest people in any engagement to locate', so the practitioner is maximally visible even though the arrival is not - but that is in the Fulguria register, on a Wellspring the technique page names in passing, and nothing points a reader to it. As a result a player reading only the technique page sees an untelegraphed attack with no counter-observation at all.

options.option: State Aurevane's glare on the technique page as the practitioner-level tell, so the page carries both facts: the arrival cannot be read and the man always can.
options.changes: One sentence, no mechanical change, and it turns a fairness failure into a genuinely interesting asymmetry.

options.option: Give the arrival a one-beat tell of its own - the coordinate Fixatio anchors is fixed a moment before the lattice grows - so an opponent watching his hands gets a fraction of warning.
options.changes: Weakens the technique's defining property ('no visible transition to react to'), which is the thing that makes it different from every other weapon summon in the genre.

options.option: Rule that the absence of a tell is the point and that fairness is carried by the ledger limit and the reserve arithmetic instead.
options.changes: No change; puts the whole weight of fairness on 'be unprecedented' and on eighteen arrivals before Starvation, both of which are real.

options.option: Give the tell to a reader rather than to an observer: a practitioner with Anamnesis or Judicium can read which blade is coming from the ledger entry being ratified.
options.changes: Creates a counter that rewards a specific discipline and makes bringing the right diagnostician to a fight with Muken a decision worth making.

quote_a: It scales with the target's own history rather than the practitioner's output. Kings, gods and old practitioners are the easiest targets, not the hardest, since the richer the ledger, the more roses there are to raise.
quote_b: It touches the ledger of past holdings, honored relationships, paid debts, kept oaths, that a present coordinate is standing on, and it dilutes the target's claim on those holdings until the coordinate can no longer be sustained by them.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Saba no Rosa.md
why: The stated mechanism is load redistribution: a present coordinate stands on a set of past deposits, deposits are taken out of the load path one at a time, and the coordinate fails when the remaining members cannot carry it. Under that mechanism more members means more redundancy, which is the whole basis of alternative-load-path design after Ronan Point, and a rich ledger is therefore harder to collapse rather than easier. The page's scaling claim only follows if a long ledger's deposits are serially dependent, each standing on the one before, rather than parallel and independent. That is a substantive proposition about how standing works in this world and it is stated nowhere. It decides whether the discipline is a king-killer or king-proof, and it also decides whether the counter in option two below exists.

options.option: Rule that a ledger is serially dependent by nature - later holdings are granted on the strength of earlier ones - so a long ledger is a long chain and the page's scaling is correct.
options.changes: Confirms the page and makes the discipline genuinely terrifying to the old and the eminent; it also means no amount of standing is a defence, which removes the option-two counter entirely.

options.option: Rule ledgers redundant by default, correct the scaling, and make diversity of claim the counter: a coordinate standing on several independent holdings survives the loss of any one.
options.changes: Inverts the page's own headline claim; gives players a constructive defence they can build deliberately, and makes a narrow, single-patron career the vulnerable one.

options.option: Rule that both hold at different depths - a ledger is redundant near the surface and serial at its foundation - so the survey finds the chain beneath the truss, which is why the field must be raised across the whole ledger.
options.changes: Preserves both the scaling and a defence, and explains mechanically why the Shingan's ability to name the single correct rose is so decisive.

options.option: Strike the scaling sentence and leave the discipline scaling with unpaid debt alone, which is what the counter clause already implies.
options.changes: Smallest change; makes 'how much do you owe' the only variable, which is cleaner and loses the page's most striking line.

quote_a: every rose is paid from the practitioner's own Oblation reserve
quote_b: EU Reserve · 1,850,000 EU · Flux Density 18,600 EU/g · Output 15,624 AU/s · η 0.84
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Muken Moto.md
why: This is the only working in the Spellcraft section with a fully stated practitioner - Stage, reserve, Flux Density, eta, AU/s, Crystal State and Path weighting all on one card - and no cost at all. The page states the cost's shape precisely (per rose, from the practitioner's own reserve, scaling with field size) and gives no magnitude at any scale, so a 1,850,000 EU reserve sits there with nothing to divide it by and the Starvation margin is null. The same card yields eighteen to thirty-seven arrivals against Mugen no Hatsurugi and nothing at all against this.

options.option: State an EU cost per rose and let field size be the multiplier, so 'expanded only as reserves allow' becomes arithmetic.
options.changes: Makes the discipline's central scaling statement computable and gives Muken's reserve something to spend; one figure does the whole job.

options.option: State a cost for a field of a given radius, in the format the card uses for its other techniques.
options.changes: Matches the practitioner's existing technique format and makes the working comparable with his other five; requires choosing a reference radius.

options.option: Rule that the cost is the Oblation trade rather than an EU expenditure - pressure surrendered for velocity, with the total conserved - and price it in what is given up rather than in reserve.
options.changes: Fits Oblation's Core Law exactly and is the most in-character answer; it needs a unit for what is surrendered, which the system does not have.

quote_a: Stage floor and Grade are not stated on the source card; the discipline reads no lower than Stage VII Refraction (A-Grade)
quote_b: FOW line — Governing Primary · Resilience (Oath, Persistence), secondary Dominion (Sovereignty). Stage floor · Stage IX — Invocation. Grade required · S-Grade. Path gate · None documented.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Oathrend.md
why: Saba no Rosa carries no FOW line: no governing Primary, no Sub-Stats, no Path gate, no Resonant Pair, and a Stage floor and Grade the page derives itself and openly declares as derivations rather than sources. Six Wellsprings across five Families give Stat Affinities too broad to gate from, so unlike most pages in this section the Path requirements cannot even be derived from Part Seven. The page's honesty about deriving is exemplary and it still leaves the working ungated.

options.option: Write a FOW line from the six Wellsprings' Stat Affinities, choosing a governing Primary from the working's actual operation (reading a ledger and withdrawing answering is Gnosis and Dominion rather than Resilience).
options.changes: Makes Part Seven consultable and the working gateable; requires a judgement about which of five Families' affinities governs.

options.option: Confirm the page's derived Stage VII / A-Grade as canon and leave the Sub-Stats unstated.
options.changes: Ratifies a careful derivation at no cost and closes half the gap.

options.option: Rule that a cross-Family discipline carries no single FOW line by definition, as Kami no Kobushi also does, and state that convention.
options.changes: Covers both cross-Family pages in this section with one rule; it makes a whole class of discipline unpriceable against Part Seven, which may be the honest answer.

quote_a: until enough wrongful attempts exhaust the practitioner's own Oblation reserve at the threshold and the ledger the gardener stands on dilutes beneath his own feet
quote_b: Failure · Self-inspection. The Wellspring does not exempt its bearer, and a Fractura practitioner under strain reads their own flaw population with perfect clarity at the worst possible moment.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vectoria — Mechanics.md
why: The page's own stated penalty for wrongful use - the gardener's ledger diluting beneath him - is Fractura's documented Failure arriving on schedule, and the page does not cite it. Two further Failures from the working's own Wellsprings are also uncarried: Mortalis's equilibration ('sustained proximity to the boundary reduces the gradient the practitioner is themselves maintaining, and they cool toward it without noticing'), which is a career-length cost for a discipline that operates at a threshold; and Contrition's autoimmunity ('the record generalises past its target and the practitioner begins answering their own tissue as though it were the original insult'), which for a discipline built on surfacing unpaid weight is the obvious way it turns inward. Oblation's cavitation is half-present, as 'the sea turning brackish and the thorns turning inward'.

options.option: Cite Fractura's self-inspection on the page as the mechanism behind the stated wrongful-use penalty, and add Mortalis's equilibration as the discipline's slow career cost.
options.changes: Two sentences; connects a stated penalty to its stated cause and gives the discipline a long-run price that suits its subject matter.

options.option: Add all three uncarried Failures as standing risks with their trigger conditions.
options.changes: Gives the working a full hazard list and makes repeated use progressively dangerous in three different ways.

options.option: Adopt the general reading rule that every technique inherits its Wellsprings' documented Failures without restatement.
options.changes: Closes this class corpus-wide rather than page by page; same option as on SA-PHYS-ANTINOMY-UNCARRIED-FAILURES and SA-PHYS-MUGEN-PHASE-LOCKING.

quote_a: Each Labor-Form can do what its Work does: the Ruin Fist locates a structure's oldest failure and makes it arrive on schedule rather than creating new damage
quote_b: Tei no Kugi Pillar Nail ... 3.2 × 10¹² EU | Tetsubun Otoshi Iron Verdict Drop ... 8.7 × 10¹³ EU | Yo no Soko Floor of the Yet-To-Be ... 1.1 × 10¹⁴ EU
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Gimbzo.md
why: The discipline page names seven Labor-Forms and prices none of them, states no Stage, no Grade, no Path gate and no FOW line. The originator's card itemises three Works to two significant figures against a stated 4.8e14 EU capacity - and the card's three Works are not among the page's seven forms. So the best-costed practitioner in the corpus and the discipline he originated share no number, no technique name and no gate. The page and the card are documents about the same man that do not meet anywhere.

options.option: Price the seven Labor-Forms on the card's own scale, and state whether the card's three Works are expressions of particular forms.
options.changes: Connects the two documents and gives the discipline its Essence stratum; requires deciding how the card's Works map onto the seven Works of Hataraki.

options.option: Rule the card's three Works to be Gimbzo's personal expressions of three of the seven forms, and name which, leaving the other four unpriced.
options.changes: Cheapest bridge; gives three of seven a cost by inheritance and makes the mapping explicit.

options.option: Rule that a bloodline art is documented at doctrine level and costed only per bearer, so the page never carries figures and every practitioner's card does.
options.changes: Establishes a convention for bloodline and personal arts generally, which would also cover the Ketsumyogan and the Iron Bison discipline; it makes the discipline page a philosophy document by design.

quote_a: Craft · Not clearly one of the Four; Kami no Kobushi is closer to a martial doctrine carried in the body than to a spoken, written, or poured working
quote_b: Below Stage VII, Refraction, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary. At Refraction the practitioner can hold the Crystal as an object of study and the Glyph Roles compress into an internal chain that needs no material anchor at all.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: Kami no Kobushi is the only page in the Spellcraft section that states no Temperance Stage floor at all. Without one, Law V cannot be checked, the Tier of Standing cannot be read, the eta band cannot be assigned, the Developmental Tier cannot be given and Part Five's ceilings cannot be applied - so five rows of any system account of it are null for one reason. Every other page in the section either states a floor or, like Saba no Rosa, derives one and says it is deriving.

options.option: State a Stage floor for the discipline as a whole, and separate floors for the seven forms if they differ.
options.changes: Unlocks five derived rows at once and makes the discipline assessable; requires a judgement, and seven judgements if the forms differ.

options.option: Derive a floor from the mechanism, as Saba no Rosa's page does, and declare it a derivation: an anchor that treats position as law rather than ground is Domain-adjacent work and reads no lower than Refraction.
options.changes: Honest, cheap, and consistent with how the neighbouring page handled the same absence.

options.option: Rule that a bloodline art is gated by lineage rather than by Stage and that no floor applies, and state that explicitly.
options.changes: Turns the absence into a design statement; it also means a low-Stage heir could in principle hold a Work, which has consequences.

quote_a: Family and Wellsprings · Spans several Families rather than one, by design; each of the seven forms draws its own cluster.
quote_b: Aether Class · Fixator-Imposer — a Body-rooted Hataraki dialect that does not project outward but locks inward.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Gimbzo.md
why: The page carries no FOW line and no governing Primary, so Part Seven's gate table cannot be consulted. The card's Aether Class implies a Body Path, which would put Resilience Anchoring, Resilience Hardening and Vitality Fortitude in play with their stated Body gates, but the page supplies nothing to derive from and the seven forms each draw a different Wellspring cluster, so no single Stat Affinity governs. Shared shape with SA-GAP-SABA-NO-FOW-LINE: both cross-Family disciplines in this section are ungateable for the same reason.

options.option: Write a FOW line per Labor-Form rather than one for the discipline, since each form draws its own cluster.
options.changes: The most accurate and the most work: seven lines, each derivable from its own named Wellsprings' Stat Affinities.

options.option: Write one FOW line for the spine the page says never changes (the anchor, the load path, the verdict), which is Resilience and Vitality on a Body Path, and leave the forms to vary above it.
options.changes: Matches the page's own 'the spine never changes across forms' framing and gives one gateable line; a reasonable compromise.

options.option: Rule cross-Family disciplines exempt from the FOW line by convention.
options.changes: Covers this page and Saba no Rosa; makes a class of discipline permanently unassessable against Part Seven.

quote_a: Craft · Not clearly one of the Four; Kami no Kobushi is closer to a martial doctrine carried in the body than to a spoken, written, or poured working, and reads nearest to Magicraft where a Craft label is forced on it.
quote_b: Bodily · Martial integration. Corporis. A fist with combustion on it is Spellcraft with the body as the pen, and the sentence is still ephemeral - which is why the fist stops burning the moment attention lapses. It is not a separate craft and should never be written as one.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: The Four Crafts page treats its four as exhaustive and addresses the bodily case directly, ruling that a martial delivery is Spellcraft with the body as the pen and 'should never be written as one' separate craft. Kami no Kobushi declines all four and settles for 'reads nearest to Magicraft where a Craft label is forced on it'. Either the four are exhaustive and this discipline has a Craft it has not been assigned, or they are not exhaustive and the governing page overstates. The Craft assignment is not cosmetic: it decides durability (Spellcraft lapses with attention, Runecraft is fixed) and therefore whether an Anchor's coupling survives a broken concentration.

options.option: Assign Spellcraft with the body as the pen, per the Four Crafts' own ruling on martial integration, and accept that the coupling lapses when attention does.
options.changes: Follows the governing page exactly and gives the discipline a real and severe limit: break his concentration and the anchor is gone. It also contradicts the page's 'reads nearest to Magicraft'.

options.option: Assign Magicraft, as the page half-suggests, and state what Magicraft durability is - the Four Crafts page defines Magicraft as the theoretical study and does not give it a durability.
options.changes: Requires the governing page to say what a Magicraft working's durability is, which it currently does not for any working.

options.option: Rule that a bloodline art carried in the body is a standing state rather than a cast working, as Kurotana's page rules for its vessel, so it has Runecraft-like durability and does not lapse.
options.changes: Makes the Anchor genuinely unbreakable by distraction, which suits the doctrine, and opens the same durability question the Edictum conflict raises (SA-CROSS-EDICTUM-SPELLCRAFT-DURABILITY).

options.option: Amend the Four Crafts page to admit a fifth category for bloodline and personal arts.
options.changes: The largest change; the governing page is emphatic that the four are the four, and a fifth would reach the Ketsumyogan, the Iron Bison discipline and Moetana as well.

quote_a: Temperance Stage XII — Zenith, anchored permanently. His cultivation curve was severed mid-ascent and frozen by the Plane of Fate itself, refusing decay
quote_b: | XII | Emanation | SSS | 950 | 7 · Grandmaster |  ... | XIV | Zenith | EX | 1,500 | 8 · Archmaster |
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md
why: The card states a Stage number and a Stage name that belong to two different Stages. Part Five: XII is Emanation, Zenith is XIV. Which is intended decides his Tier of Standing (7 Grandmaster or 8 Archmaster), his eta band (0.85-0.90 or 0.95-1.2), his Max Grade (SSS or EX), his Sub-Stat ceiling (950 or 1,500) and his Developmental Tier (Sovereign or Crystallized Soul). His stated eta of 0.94 is outside the band on either reading, which is a separate row (SA-NUM-GIMBZO-ETA-TIER) and is also the best evidence that the two errors are one error.

options.option: Read the number as governing: Stage XII, Emanation, Tier 7 Grandmaster.
options.changes: Puts his eta 0.04 above band rather than 0.01 below, and caps his Sub-Stats at 950; the more conservative reading and the smaller edit.

options.option: Read the name as governing: Stage XIV, Zenith, Tier 8 Archmaster.
options.changes: Puts his eta just below band and raises his ceiling to 1,500 and his Developmental Tier to Crystallized Soul, which suits 'living infrastructure' and a curve frozen by the Plane; the larger character claim.

options.option: Rule that a curve 'severed mid-ascent and frozen' produces a non-standard reading - the number he reached and a standing that behaves as a higher one - and state that as a special case.
options.changes: Keeps both words on the card and makes him a documented anomaly; it also creates a precedent for Stage and Standing coming apart, which the Tier of Standing column currently forbids.

quote_a: Efficiency (η) | 0.94 — near-superconductor. The Plane reclaims most of his bleed; he wastes almost nothing
quote_b: 7 · Grandmaster | XI–XII Dissonance to Emanation | 0.85–0.90 ... 8 · Archmaster | XIII–XIV Principality to Zenith | 0.95–1.2
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VII. Aether Class, Essence Typology, Aether Flow (Parts Seventeen–Nineteen).md
why: Gimbzo's stated eta of 0.94 falls in the gap between two Tier bands and is therefore out of band on both readings of his Stage: above Tier 7's 0.85-0.90 if his Stage number governs, below Tier 8's 0.95-1.2 if his Stage name does. No reading of his own card places the figure in a band. Extends SA-NUM-ETA-TIER. Separately, the gloss describes something the system has no term for: the bleed is not merely small but reclaimed by the Plane he is coupled to, which is the same accounting problem as SA-GAP-VANTABRIEL-RETAINED-BLEED.

options.option: Rule Tier bands typical rather than binding, which resolves this row, SA-NUM-NIRAN-ETA-TIER, SA-NUM-MUKEN-ETA-TIER and the five in SA-NUM-ETA-TIER together.
options.changes: One ruling clears the whole class and makes eta a diagnostic axis rather than a lookup, which Part Five's own note already gestures at.

options.option: Set the Stage to XIV per the card's name and raise the eta to 0.95, the Tier 8 floor.
options.changes: Two small edits, both in band; it also changes his Grade ceiling and Developmental Tier, so it is a larger character decision than it looks.

options.option: Rule that reclaimed bleed is accounted separately from eta, so his effective eta is 0.94 and his apparent one higher, and add the term.
options.changes: Introduces the retained/reclaimed bleed term the corpus lacks; it would also give C-053 a route, since his AU/s discrepancy is an output-accounting problem of the same kind.

quote_a: refuse to move, and let the thing that is trying to move you discover it has not earned the right
quote_b: Failure · Tensile exposure. Load the structure in the one direction it does not answer and it does not deform gracefully. It parts.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vectoria — Mechanics.md
why: The discipline's two best-attested forms name Petralon and Cataclysm among their Wellsprings, and both carry documented Failures that bear directly on a doctrine of not moving. Petralon routes every load into compression and parts rather than deforming when loaded in tension - so an Anchor has, by construction, exactly one direction it cannot take a load in, and pulling or lifting is not what anyone instinctively tries against a man who refuses to move. Cataclysm's reflected overpressure returns the shock along its own path so that 'the practitioner standing at the origin receives the sum of the wave and its reflection', which for a man whose method forbids stepping aside is not hypothetical. Neither is on the page, and the page's own stated failure taxonomy is entirely about Obsession Force.

options.option: Add tensile exposure to the page as the Anchor's structural vulnerability, naming the direction.
options.changes: Gives the discipline a physical counter to sit beside its moral one, and it is a counter an opponent has to think of rather than stumble into.

options.option: Add Cataclysm's reflected overpressure as the Ruin Fist's specific hazard in confinement.
options.changes: Makes terrain matter to a discipline that currently has no terrain modifier, and punishes the doctrine precisely where it is most rigid.

options.option: Rule that the coupling to the Plane exempts an anchored practitioner from both, and state why.
options.changes: Preserves the discipline intact and requires a mechanism; it would also make severing the coupling the prerequisite for every physical counter, which is a clean design.

options.option: Adopt the general reading rule that every technique inherits its Wellsprings' documented Failures without restatement.
options.changes: Closes this class corpus-wide; same option as on three other rows in this batch.

quote_a: Mechanically this runs through Benediction, whose documented law is that bonds formed under it carry mechanical weight rather than merely social or narrative weight.
quote_b: Failure · Competitive inhibition. A rival ligand with higher affinity displaces the existing bond, and the displacement is silent, complete, and not felt until the bond is called on.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Vitalia — Biochemistry.md:37
why: The page cites Benediction's Mechanism almost verbatim as the rite's justification and does not carry Benediction's Failure, which bears on this working harder than on any other in the section. Competitive inhibition means a GENUINE Anointing can be displaced by a higher-affinity claim, silently, with the subject discovering it only at the moment of use. The page's entire account of failure is forgery - a rite performed with no current behind it - and it has no account at all of a true mark going quietly empty because something outbid it. A working whose subject is the reliability of a mark, whose Wellspring's documented failure is the silent displacement of marks, should carry that failure.

options.option: Add competitive displacement to the page as the second failure mode, naming the higher-affinity claim that does it.
options.changes: Gives Anointing a failure that needs no forger, makes rival orders' Anointings mechanically competitive with each other, and gives the section a betrayal that nobody has to lie to commit.

options.option: State on the page that an Anointing sealed with Fixatio is covalent rather than affinity-held and therefore not displaceable, with unsealed marks displaceable.
options.changes: Makes the Fixatio secondary harmonisation load-bearing rather than decorative, and splits Anointings into two grades of permanence that an examiner could tell apart.

options.option: Rule that the Traitus mark, once standing in the Essence Core, is no longer an Attraction-Layer bond and so is out of Benediction's Failure's reach.
options.changes: Closes the question by scope rather than by mechanism; the rite's window of vulnerability becomes the rite itself, not the years afterward.

options.option: Leave the page as written and record that Benediction's Failure is not carried by this working.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; the gap stays in the questionnaire and any scene that wants a displaced Anointing has no rule to stand on.

quote_a: The card names Lo (claimed: devotion/divine acknowledgment), Wy (claimed: grace/elevation), and Ka (claimed: destiny/chosen path). Wy and Ka are attested elsewhere in current canon in the Identity and Force strata respectively, as Truth and Cycle, not as the readings the card gives; Lo does not appear in any glyph fragment available to this conversion and is unverified rather than confirmed.
quote_b: A glyph creates nothing and carries no power. … A glyph is a boundary condition imposed on that law.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms.md
why: Three glyphs are named with readings the page itself says are wrong for two of them and unattested for the third, and none of the three is among the thirty entries of the Master Glyph Index the repo mirror carries, so this account cannot check them either. The page's own recommendation is that the chain be checked against the Index before being treated as final. This account proposes no substitute, because a proposal would be a third reading rather than a check.

options.option: Read the chain with the attested values: Wy as Truth, Ka as Cycle, and strike Lo until a fragment attests it.
options.changes: The rite's chain becomes a truth-claim carried on a cycle, which is a different working from devotion-and-elevation and would want the page's prose rewritten to match.

options.option: Mirror the remaining 106 Index entries and then check all three readings against them.
options.changes: Answers this row and roughly a dozen others in one operation; blocks nothing else in the meantime.

options.option: Rule the card's readings correct and record that Wy and Ka carry stratum-dependent readings.
options.changes: Makes glyph readings context-sensitive across the whole Index, which is a system-wide change and would need stating on the Index itself.

quote_a: Stage floor / Grade · Stage VI, Glory, A-Grade, for the officiant.
quote_b: Oath requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:138
why: The page states a Stage floor and a required Grade and names no Path requirement. Benediction's own Stat Effect names Harmonics Empathy, Harmonics Axis and Resilience Oath, and Part Seven gates all three on the Attraction Path: Oath and Axis at Stage IV to exceed B, Empathy at Stage III to exceed C. The rite requires A-Grade, which is above B, so an officiant must hold Attraction Path at Stage IV to express the working's own governing Sub-Stats at the Grade the page demands. The page's silence reads as 'no Path requirement' and there are three.

options.option: Add 'Attraction Path at Stage IV' to the page's Stage floor line.
options.changes: Narrows who can officiate to Attraction-Path practitioners, which is consistent with a rite of recognition and removes Body- and Spirit-Path officiants from the trade entirely.

options.option: State that the rite reads only Resilience Oath and gate it on that one Sub-Stat.
options.changes: One gate instead of three, and makes the officiant's stake the vow rather than the discernment.

options.option: Rule that a Ritus performed with a full apparatus reads the apparatus's Grade rather than the officiant's, which lifts the Path gate.
options.changes: A system-wide rule about Ritus and material anchors that would reach every rite in the corpus, not only this one.

quote_a: Stage floor / Grade · Stage VI, Glory, A-Grade, for the officiant.
quote_b: EU · Essence Units — the raw reserve. Scales with Temperance Stage, governed primarily by Tempering Yield.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The page states a Stage, a Grade and a permanence, and no quantity at all: no EU, no duration of the rite, no AU/s, no reserve. Because no formula anywhere in the system converts a Stage into an EU figure (SA-GAP-EU-FORMULA), the ledger for this working is null in every energetic row, and the only cost the account can state is the one the page states in kind - the officiant's own standing, staked on a claim about somebody else. That is a real cost and it is not in any unit the system defines.

options.option: State an EU cost on the page, in band for Stage VI per the Grade table.
options.changes: Fills the ledger and makes the rite affordable or not against the five attested reserves; also fixes how often an order can perform it.

options.option: Rule that a Ritus whose cost is a stake rather than an expenditure carries no EU figure by design, and say so on the page.
options.changes: Makes null the correct answer rather than a missing one, and creates a class of workings the essence ledger deliberately does not price.

options.option: Define a unit for staked standing - Tempering Coherence at risk, or a Resilience Oath charge - so the stake is billable.
options.changes: A new accounting quantity in the Core Vocabulary, which would reach Votia, vows and every other working priced in credit rather than energy.

quote_a: None of the four figures the card names, Aethelsige Moto, Seraphiel Moto, the Oracles of Vellsorea, or Caladriel of Highspire, have a card or page anywhere in current canon.
quote_b: AU/s = Flux Density × η.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: No Anointing officiant anywhere in the corpus has a character card, so Flux Density, eta and AU/s are null for this working by absence rather than by omission, and the Starvation margin cannot be computed for anyone. Every efficiency figure in the account is read off the Tier of Standing table at the Stage floor rather than off a practitioner, which is the weakest form the ledger can take.

options.option: Card one of the four named figures, rebuilt under the naming law their house requires.
options.changes: Gives the working a practitioner with numbers and makes the eta band checkable against a real sheet; the two Moto names need rebuilding first, which is itself an invention this account cannot make.

options.option: Attach the working to an already-carded Benediction practitioner as its worked example.
options.changes: Fills the ledger with attested figures and costs nothing in new canon; changes who the rite belongs to.

options.option: Leave the ledger null and record that this working has no carded practitioner.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; the account's efficiency rows stay bands read off a table rather than figures read off a person.

quote_a: The Order of Benediction, named as the central rite-keeping body, and the False Anointing Rebellion, named as a historical crisis triggered by a corrupted bishop of Lurien, are both unattested; Lurien itself is attested elsewhere in current canon as a Holy See that was struck from canon and replaced by the Holy Sea of Alabaster, so a rebellion anchored to Lurien is now anchored to a see that no longer exists in that form.
quote_b: The card's own citation, WOTR: Era of Grace, Volume I, is a Trello-era work title distinct from the current Volume I through V Character Card structure and is flagged as superseded.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Anointing.md:33
why: The working's only named institution, its only named historical crisis and its cited source are all unattested, and the crisis is anchored to a see that current canon has replaced. This matters more here than the usual unattested-colour case: the False Anointing tradition is the page's whole account of how the rite fails, so the mechanism's documented history rests on an event that has no home in current canon. Nothing in current canon says where an equivalent would sit under Alabaster, so the account flags it rather than relocating it.

options.option: Relocate the False Anointing Rebellion to the Holy Sea of Alabaster and name the see that holds it.
options.changes: Gives the rite's failure history a current home and makes Alabaster carry a scandal it does not currently carry.

options.option: Keep the event and detach it from any see, recording it as a crisis of the trade rather than of an institution.
options.changes: Preserves the mechanism's history at the cost of the politics; no faction gains or loses anything.

options.option: Strike the Rebellion and the Order of Benediction, and rest the failure account on the mechanism alone.
options.changes: Removes unattested history from the page; the rite keeps its forgery failure mode with no documented instance of it.

options.option: Card the Order of Benediction as a faction and let it own the event.
options.changes: Creates an institution, which the issue does not authorise, and would make the rite's keepers a faction other pages can reach.

quote_a: it cannot be undone casually, since a standing Traitus mark does not lapse the way a sustained working does, meaning a false Anointing left standing can misdirect a subject's Crystal for the rest of their Temperance path if nobody catches it.
quote_b: Rescind, the withdrawal-of-consent effect attested elsewhere in the corpus, is the clearest documented counter to a soul-bound Precept, and only when the Precept was never lawfully consented to in the first place.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Precept.md:40
why: The Precept page in this same section names Rescind as the documented counter to a soul-bound working imposed without lawful consent. An Anointing performed on an unwilling or deceived subject is exactly that: a standing Traitus mark, soul-bound, without consent. The Anointing page names no counter at all and says the mark cannot be undone casually, which leaves a deceived subject with no route on the page even though a neighbouring page names one. Whether Rescind reaches a Traitus mark, as against a Precept's clause, is not stated anywhere.

options.option: Rule that Rescind reaches any soul-bound working imposed without lawful consent, Traitus marks included, and name it on the Anointing page.
options.changes: Gives the deceived subject a route and makes consent the hinge of the whole rite; also reaches every other standing mark in the corpus.

options.option: Rule that Rescind reaches clauses only and that a Traitus mark requires Scission instead.
options.changes: Sends the remedy to a rite with a documented complication rate, which makes an unwanted Anointing genuinely expensive to be rid of.

options.option: State on the page that a false Anointing is removed by the officiating order's own correction and by nothing else.
options.changes: Makes the rite's politics its only remedy, which is a strong hook and leaves a subject whose order will not act with nothing.

quote_a: Craft · Spellcraft. The effect is spoken or otherwise sustained by active attention and collapses once that attention lapses or the working completes, matching the current Craft durability rule rather than a fixed inscription.
quote_b: the 'banned in most formal Ritus Orders' claim is consistent with Mechanica's own Statute XXVI, which exists because the category leaves scars the Continuum does not forget.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Fallacy.md:29
why: The page states no Temperance Stage, no Grade, no EU cost and no duration - the only entry in the Spellcraft section with no Stage floor anywhere in it. Because Max Grade, Sub-Stat ceiling, Tier of Standing, efficiency and Developmental Tier are all read from Stage (Part Five, Part Nineteen, Part Twenty-One), one missing field empties nine ledger rows and makes the Path gates untestable. The system therefore currently forbids a working it cannot price, gate or rank, and no scene can be adjudicated against it.

options.option: State a Stage floor on the page and let Grade, Tier, eta and the Developmental Tier follow from Part Five and Part Nineteen.
options.changes: Fills nine ledger rows at one stroke and makes the Path gates testable; fixes who can perform the working, which currently anyone can.

options.option: Rule that a Mechanica working carries no Stage floor by definition, because it skips the authorisation that Stages gate, and say so on the page.
options.changes: Makes the absence deliberate and gives Mechanica a system-wide property; also means a low-Stage practitioner can file a false axiom, which is a large change to the threat model.

options.option: State a Stage floor AND an EU cost that scales with the clause's load (see SA-GAP-FALLACY-COST-SCALES-WITH-LOAD), so the two missing quantities close together.
options.changes: Prices the working by consequence rather than by content, which is what the physics requires and what the page's own account of catastrophic uses implies.

quote_a: Craft · Spellcraft. The effect is spoken or otherwise sustained by active attention and collapses once that attention lapses or the working completes, matching the current Craft durability rule rather than a fixed inscription.
quote_b: Phenomena secondary for the self-sustaining collapse once the working is triggered and has outrun its own Attraction Layer.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Fallacy.md:25
why: The page asserts two incompatible accounts of the same collapse. The Spellcraft durability rule makes the collapse caster-held: it happens when attention lapses, which puts its timing in the practitioner's hands. The Phenomena tag makes it caster-independent, and the taxonomy is explicit about what that means - 'once triggered, Phenomena are no longer cast; they're lattice-position events on the Plane of Fate that have outrun any Attraction Layer. This is why Counter-Phenomena are so dangerous: the trigger has an author, but the Phenomenon itself does not' (Magical Categories:86). The physics agrees with the second reading: a nucleation event belongs to the interface, not to whoever seeded it. Which one holds decides whether a practitioner can schedule the shattering, which is the single most important tactical fact about the working.

options.option: Rewrite the Craft line from the Phenomena tag: the practitioner sustains the false clause, and the collapse once begun is not theirs to stop or time.
options.changes: Makes the working genuinely dangerous to its author, supplies the cost the fairness check finds missing, and matches the physics. Every school that plans its own withdrawal becomes wrong.

options.option: Drop the Phenomena secondary and keep the working wholly caster-held, collapsing on lapse.
options.changes: Makes Fallacy a controllable tool, removes the self-sustaining catastrophe the page's history rests on, and would want the 'corrupts what is near it indiscriminately' claim revisited.

options.option: Split the working: the false clause is Spellcraft and caster-held; the collapse crosses into Phenomena only above a stated load threshold.
options.changes: Gives the page a stated threshold it currently lacks and makes scale the hinge - small lies are recallable, large ones are not.

options.option: Leave both and record that the durability of a Fallacy is unruled.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; no scene can say whether the practitioner can stop it, which is the question a table will ask first.

quote_a: Wellsprings · Nihiloth, Dissolution, and Mirithane.
quote_b: Mechanica coerces transformation without lawful Wellspring participation, consuming Resonance and damaging the Continuum - the practice this entire taxonomy exists in opposition to.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:131
why: The page files Fallacy as Mechanica primary and then names three participating Wellsprings. Mechanica is defined by the absence of lawful Wellspring participation; that absence is the category's whole content and the reason Statute XXVI exists. A working cannot both be Mechanica-primary and run on Nihiloth, Dissolution and Mirithane as the page describes, and the choice matters well beyond filing: it decides whether the working has Wellspring Failures that bear on it (Nihiloth's symmetric cancellation is the practitioner-facing cost this account could otherwise derive), whether it can be performed inside a Silence, and whether it answers to the Four Theories at all.

options.option: Refile the working as Limina-with-Nihiloth primary and drop the Mechanica tag, keeping Mechanica only for uses that skip authorisation.
options.changes: The working gains three Wellspring Failures, including the symmetric cancellation that makes it dangerous to its author; loses the Statute XXVI standing that justifies the guild ban.

options.option: Keep Mechanica primary and strike the three Wellsprings, describing the working as extraction rather than participation.
options.changes: Justifies the ban and the scarring, and removes every Wellspring-derived mechanism this account uses - the page would then owe its own account of how the false clause is filed.

options.option: Rule that a working may name the Wellsprings it COERCES rather than the ones that participate, and say so on the page and in the taxonomy.
options.changes: A taxonomy-level change that would let every Mechanica entry name currents, and would need a way to tell a coerced current from a harmonised one.

options.option: Keep both and record the contradiction.
options.changes: Nothing; the account cannot say whether the working has Failures, and the Silence question in section 5 stays unanswerable.

quote_a: Wellsprings · Nihiloth, Dissolution, and Mirithane.
quote_b: A true mirror adds nothing. Angle in equals angle out, and fidelity is defined entirely by the absence of introduced distortion. … Mirithane makes the Shell such a surface, so what leaves the practitioner is what was in them, with no flattering correction applied in transit.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:40
why: Mirithane is the Wellspring of not lying. Its Mechanism is the absence of introduced distortion and its Failure is that 'the mirror does not discriminate. A practitioner in a state they would rather not broadcast broadcasts it perfectly.' Naming it as a component of a working whose entire operation is a false clause is either a deep reading - the lie must be a perfectly formed, distortion-free rendering of a false statement, which is exactly what makes it unreadable from inside - or a mis-assignment. The page does not say which, and the difference decides whether a Mirithane practitioner is Fallacy's natural author or its natural detector, which is a counterplay question as well as a filing one.

options.option: State the deep reading on the page: Mirithane supplies the fidelity of the forgery, not its content, and a Fallacy told badly is not a Fallacy.
options.changes: Makes Mirithane load-bearing and gives the working a craft standard - a false clause with introduced distortion is detectable, which is a findable counter.

options.option: Replace Mirithane with a current whose law fits a false statement, and record which.
options.changes: Removes the tension and loses the fidelity mechanism; the page would need another account of why the clause is indistinguishable.

options.option: Rule that Mirithane practitioners are Fallacy's natural detectors and cannot author one, and say so.
options.changes: Turns the current from a component into a counter and creates a named profession that beats this working.

quote_a: It cannot make the lie permanent. The shattering is built in, not an external correction, and everything the working achieves, it achieves inside that window and loses the instant the window closes, though the damage done while it was open does not repair itself along with the lie.
quote_b: a working's energy budget balances at the Aether stratum and not at the Essence one. The practitioner does not supply the joules. They supply the boundary condition.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Physical Account Two Sets of Books.md
why: Every other working in this section that supplies a boundary condition is downhill: the driving force was already there and the practitioner pays only for the route. Fallacy is uphill. Putting a region into a metastable state means supplying the free-energy offset between the true minimum and the false one, and that offset scales with how much structure the clause is load-bearing for - a false clause nobody reads is nearly free, a false clause a Wellspring path runs through costs in proportion to the path. So the cost of a Fallacy is a function of its CONSEQUENCE rather than of its content, and the page states no cost at all. This is the one place where the physical account bills the working and the stratal account does not.

options.option: State the cost on the page as scaling with the load the clause bears, with a band, and say that the practitioner pays going up and the region pays coming down.
options.changes: Prices the working by consequence, which makes the small lie usable and the domain-scale lie something only a named power can afford; also explains why the collapse is larger than the working.

options.option: Rule that the whole offset is paid by the region rather than the practitioner, so the working is genuinely cheap and the damage is entirely borrowed.
options.changes: Keeps the working affordable and makes it strictly parasitic, which strengthens the Mechanica reading and the guild ban.

options.option: State a flat EU cost independent of the clause's load.
options.changes: Simplest to adjudicate and breaks the physical account, since a flat price for an arbitrary offset is not a boundary condition.

quote_a: This is why it reads to witnesses as revelation rather than as trickery: for the working's duration, the false thing genuinely is true, in the narrow, load-bearing sense that everything downstream of it behaves as though it were.
quote_b: Every ability costs something that hurts, has stated limits, a Counterplay route that beats it, a tell, and numbers in band.
path_b: .claude/skills/wotr-write/references/fair-play.md
why: Two of the five fairness checks fail as written. COST: the page states no cost in any currency - no EU, no Stage, no Sub-Stat toll, no apparatus and no aftermath the practitioner pays - for a working it says can persuade a domain that its own god never existed. TELL: the page's stated experience of the working is that everything checks out, which is the absence of a tell rather than a subtle one. Both have fixes already implicit in the system rather than needing invention: Nihiloth's symmetric cancellation puts the practitioner's own path inside the null, and a metastable region is detectably QUIETER than it should be, reporting no anomaly where the cancelled law's absence ought to register - a tell for an instrument rather than an eye, which is the kind a player can look up.

options.option: Carry Nihiloth's Failure onto the page as the practitioner's cost: the clause cancels law the practitioner's own path also runs through.
options.changes: Supplies a cost that hurts without inventing a number, and makes the working self-limiting to the exact degree it is ambitious.

options.option: State the quiet as the tell: a region under a Fallacy reports no anomaly where the cancelled law should register, findable by Judicium or any externally calibrated instrument.
options.changes: Gives the working a fair, research-rewarding tell and makes the audit scene possible; costs the working its perfect invisibility.

options.option: State both, plus a Stage floor, and close the fairness failure completely.
options.changes: Fixes cost, tell and band together; the largest change to the page and the one that makes it usable at a table.

options.option: Leave it and record that the working fails two fairness checks.
options.changes: Nothing; the working stays free, silent and unbounded, which no other entry in this section is.

quote_a: Serenhal Caelmorne has no wiki entry. The surname Caelmorne belongs elsewhere in the corpus to a different, unrelated moon-aligned Anima Harmonist (Caelmorne Halvrein, of the Harmonic Arts), which makes the name plausible as a house name without making this particular bearer of it real.
quote_b: None of the four figures the card names have a card or page anywhere in current canon: Serenhal Caelmorne, said to have projected a corrupted version of himself during a Moetana trial
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Vainglory.md:32
why: Serenhal Caelmorne is unattested and appears on TWO pages in this section as the practitioner of two different unsanctioned workings - Fallacy and Vainglory - with no card, no page and no shared account between them. That makes him load-bearing across the section rather than colour on one page: whatever is decided about him decides who authored two of the section's forbidden disciplines. The surname collides with an attested and unrelated Anima Harmonist, Caelmorne Halvrein, so the name is plausible as a house without the bearer being real.

options.option: Card Serenhal Caelmorne once, as the figure both pages name, under the Caelmorne house.
options.changes: Gives two forbidden disciplines a single attested author and a history that ties them, and creates a character - which the issue does not authorise, so it needs a ruling.

options.option: Strike him from both pages and leave both workings without a named practitioner.
options.changes: Removes unattested history from two pages; both lose their only account of who performs them.

options.option: Keep him on one page only and strike the other mention.
options.changes: Halves the exposure and makes an arbitrary choice between two pages that both need him.

options.option: Keep both mentions flagged unattested, as they stand.
options.changes: Nothing; the section carries a figure across two pages who exists nowhere else.

quote_a: Razakiel is attested as a figure who imposed the Unlawful Acts of Order on at least one occasion, confronted and annulled not by force but by Dazkar's stillness, the mirror of consequence forcing the decree's own contradictions to erase it.
quote_b: AU/s = Flux Density × η.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The page's one attested figure, Razakiel, is attested for a RELATED act - an unlawful, false-premised order written into law and failing under its own weight - and not for this working; the page says so and keeps the Fallacy claim as originated. No Fallacy practitioner anywhere in the corpus has a character card. With no Stage stated either, the working has no eta from the Tier table and no eta from a sheet, so Flux Density, AU/s, bleed and the Starvation margin are all null for two independent reasons at once.

options.option: Attach the working to Razakiel properly by ruling that the Unlawful Acts of Order WERE a Fallacy, quoting the attested account.
options.changes: Converts the section's only attested anchor into a real practitioner and gives the working a documented instance and an outcome; needs a ruling because the attested text does not say so.

options.option: Card a Fallacy practitioner so the ledger has a sheet to read.
options.changes: Fills every null energetic row; creates a character, which the issue does not authorise.

options.option: Leave the ledger null and record that the working has neither a Stage nor a carded practitioner.
options.changes: Nothing; the account's ledger stays empty in every row, which is unique in this section.

quote_a: this is the conservative reading consistent with the card's account of mass casualties among summoners who lost control of multiple Inverted Eidolons at once.
quote_b: Essence Cost · 75,000 – 150,000 EU per eidolon depending on complexity, with a sustained cost of 10,000 – 25,000 EU per second. Multiple simultaneous constructs multiply strain on the Aether Shell and risk Essence depletion cascade.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Summoning Arts.md:42
why: The page's central historical event is multiple simultaneous Inverted Eidolons. At the Discipline's own sustain of 25,000 EU/s, two constructs cost 50,000 EU/s and three cost 75,000 EU/s. Muken's 1,850,000 EU is the largest reserve attested anywhere in this batch; after the 10 percent Starvation floor and one 150,000 EU fabrication that buys about 60 seconds for ONE construct and about 20 seconds for three. Dougou at Stage XIII (92,000 EU) cannot pay the upper fabrication charge at all and gets 0.31 s at the lower one. The Discipline says the strain multiplies rather than adds, which makes it worse. No practitioner in the corpus can produce the event the page rests its history on.

options.option: Lower the sustained cost for Animatria constructs, or make sustain scale with what the construct is doing rather than with its existence.
options.changes: Makes multi-construct operation possible for the largest reserves and reaches every Animatria page in the corpus, not only this one.

options.option: Raise the attested reserves, which is the same unresolved question as SA-CROSS-EU-STAGE-LADDER.
options.changes: Fixes this row and about a hundred others at once; needs the ruling on what a corrected EU figure becomes.

options.option: Rewrite the page's history so the mass-casualty event is many summoners with one construct each rather than one summoner with several.
options.changes: Keeps every number as written and changes the story to one the ledger can pay for; arguably a better story.

options.option: Rule that an Anti-Eidolon out of its summoner's control is no longer drawing sustain from them, which is why the event was survivable long enough to be a catastrophe.
options.changes: Explains the history and creates a class of construct that persists without payment, which would need its own limit.

quote_a: a sustained cost in the 10,000 to 25,000 EU per second range
quote_b: η · efficiency — the ratio of Essence spent to Essence that arrives as intended effect.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/VII. Aether Class, Essence Typology, Aether Flow (Parts Seventeen–Nineteen).md
why: At the Stage VIII floor the Tier of Standing is 6, Master, with eta 0.70-0.80, so 20 to 30 percent of expenditure leaves as heat, sound and structural bleed. Against the sustain that is 5,000 to 7,500 EU per second, continuously. Under R44-1 (1 EU = 1 MJ) that is 5.0 to 7.5 gigawatts of waste every second the construct stands. A human body at rest dissipates on the order of 100 watts, so the working requires a dissipation path about 5 x 10^7 times larger than the only one a practitioner has. The account cannot say this breaches an Aetheric Density ceiling because the system states no numeric ceiling (SA-GAP-AETHERIC-DENSITY); it can say the joules have no stated destination. This is the same structural failure imports/essence-ledger/physics-check.md found at the low end of the corpus, arriving at the high end.

options.option: State where a working's bleed goes - into the Aether stratum rather than through the practitioner's body - and say so in Two Sets of Books.
options.changes: Answers this row and every other waste-heat finding in the batch in one sentence; makes bleed an environmental quantity rather than a physiological one.

options.option: Rule that sustained costs are not subject to eta, because the bleed fraction applies to delivered work rather than to upkeep.
options.changes: Removes the gigawatt figure and creates two kinds of expenditure with different accounting, which would need stating across the Ledger.

options.option: Lower the sustained cost, which also answers SA-NUM-INVERT-MULTIPLE-CONSTRUCTS-UNPAYABLE.
options.changes: Fixes both rows with one number and reaches every Animatria working.

options.option: Record the figure and leave the constant, the eta and the cost all as written.
options.changes: Nothing; the largest unaccounted energy flow in this section stays unaccounted.

quote_a: It cannot be relied on to defend its summoner by default; per the mechanism, it inherits inversion of affinity as well as of function, and 'hostile unless bound or redeemed' is the honest baseline rather than a worst case.
quote_b: It maintains continuity through a tether back to its source, which is why Animatria summoning fails completely inside Silence Realms. Harmonic Silence severs the connection and the construct dissolves.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Summoning Arts.md:39
why: The stated effect is a construct hostile to its summoner. The stated mechanism is a construct whose existence depends on a tether back to that same summoner. Whether an Anti-Eidolon CAN kill the thing it is made of, and what becomes of it if it does, is not stated anywhere - and it decides a live tactical question, because an opponent who works out what is happening has the option of doing nothing and letting the working finish. As written the effect describes an attacker and the mechanism describes something that cannot complete the attack without ending itself.

options.option: State that the construct cannot act to end its own tether, so its hostility stops short of lethal against the summoner - obstruction, betrayal, refusal, not killing.
options.changes: Makes the discipline a liability rather than an assassin and makes waiting a genuine counter; removes the page's worst-case ending.

options.option: State that it can, and that summoner and construct end together, which is what the mass-casualty history describes.
options.changes: Gives the page's history its mechanism and makes the discipline straightforwardly suicidal at the failure point.

options.option: State that a construct that has reached code exhaustion (Oblivara's Failure) has substituted its own continuity for the tether and is no longer bound by it.
options.changes: Ties the escape to a named Wellspring Failure and a stated duration, so the danger has a clock an opponent can read.

options.option: Record the question and leave both lines.
options.changes: Nothing; the counterplay route of waiting cannot be adjudicated.

quote_a: The card's claim that he unintentionally triggered a fractured, refused construct during early trials has no confirmation anywhere else, and nothing on his sheet contradicts it either; it is kept here as an open, unattested thread rather than an established fact.
quote_b: Splinter Drift. Every Echo fielded is a live gamble against his own continuity, because his Class has not stabilised and stabilisation requires Stage VI. Sustained multi-Echo operation risks a fragment refusing recall - a piece of Karo that decides it prefers being someone else.
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Karo Venrik · The Foolish Magus.md:40
why: The page says Karo Venrik's involvement has no confirmation on his sheet. His sheet carries a named Limit, Splinter Drift, which describes this working's outcome mechanically and specifically: a fielded fragment refusing recall and preferring to be someone else, gated on the fact that his Class has not stabilised. That is closer to confirmation than 'nothing contradicts it' - it is arguably the same phenomenon under a different name, on the one card the page's practitioner actually has. Whether Splinter Drift IS accidental Invert Eidolon, or a neighbouring failure that must be kept distinct, is not stated and changes what the page may claim.

options.option: Rule that Splinter Drift is the accidental form of this working and cite the card on the page.
options.changes: Turns the page's unattested thread into an attested one at no cost in new canon, and gives the discipline a documented low-Stage accident pathway.

options.option: Rule that Splinter Drift is a distinct Animatria failure and say on both pages how to tell them apart.
options.changes: Keeps the two clean and forces the page to find its confirmation elsewhere or drop the claim.

options.option: Leave the page's wording and add a cross-reference to the card without ruling on identity.
options.changes: Makes the connection findable by a reader while deciding nothing, which is what a lookup trail wants and what an adjudicator does not.

quote_a: Stage floor / Grade · Stage VIII, Transcendence, S-Grade minimum.
quote_b: Retention requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D, and Stage VI to exceed A for the number of complete workings held loaded.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:126
why: The page states a Stage floor and an S-Grade minimum and names no Path requirement. The three Wellsprings it names gate on three different Paths at that Grade. Eidolyn's Stat Effect names Ardency Density, which Part Seven gates on Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B, and Gnosis Retention, gated on Spirit Path at Stage VI to exceed A. Nihiloth's names Dominion Sovereignty, gated on Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed A. S-Grade exceeds both B and A, so all three are live simultaneously, and the account cannot tell whether one practitioner may satisfy gates on three separate Paths at once - the system does not say.

options.option: State on the page which Path the working actually requires and drop the harmonisations whose gates cannot be met.
options.changes: Makes the working performable by a real practitioner and narrows who can do it; costs the page one or two of its three named currents.

options.option: Rule in Part Seven whether a practitioner may hold gates on multiple Paths, and at what cost.
options.changes: A system-wide answer that reaches every multi-Wellspring working in the corpus, which is most of them.

options.option: Rule that a Path gate is read against the Sub-Stat actually expressed in the working rather than against every Sub-Stat its Wellsprings strengthen.
