options.changes: Collapses most multi-gate findings in the batch and would need stating in Part Seven; changes how every account in this batch reads gates.

quote_a: Below that Gate, the working still produces an Anti-Eidolon, but not one stable enough to survive contact with anything actively opposing it, which matches the card's own description of summoners losing control.
quote_b: Temperance Gate · Stage VI (Glory) for basic eidolons · Stage VIII (Transcendence) for semi-autonomous forms · Stage X (Realization) for constructs capable of independent tactical action.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Summoning Arts.md:41
why: The page sets a Stage VIII floor and then says the working still produces an Anti-Eidolon below it, and its one attested figure is at Stage V - three Stages under the floor and, by his own card, unable to stabilise anything until Stage VI. So the floor gates the deliberate practice and not the outcome, which means it is not a floor in the sense the rest of the system uses the word: a player cannot rule out an Anti-Eidolon by checking a Stage. Whether an accidental Anti-Eidolon has its own lower gate, and what it can do there, is unstated.

options.option: State a separate lower gate for accidental production, with a stated capability ceiling at that gate.
options.changes: Makes the accident adjudicable and gives low-Stage scenes a real hazard with real limits.

options.option: Rule that below the floor the product is a Tier I ephemeral construct - the Discipline's own reflexive extrusion that dissolves in seconds - and not an Anti-Eidolon.
options.changes: Keeps the floor meaningful and removes the page's low-Stage catastrophe, which is most of its history.

options.option: Keep the floor for the deliberate working only, and say on the page that it does not bound the accident.
options.changes: Honest as written and leaves a working with no Stage bound at all on its dangerous form.

quote_a: The remaining figures and events the card names, Thessan and her bound Anti-Eidolon Vel-Muriah, Silvantes Mournthresh of a 'Riven Choir,' the Twilight Concord where the practice is said to have first surfaced, an 'Era of Calamity' and a mass-casualty incident called the Wellspring Fracture of Nalisem, and fringe preservationist cults called the Mirrorwake Ascetics and the Occultinarii of the Hollow Eye, have no page or card anywhere in current canon.
quote_b: this is the conservative reading consistent with the card's account of mass casualties among summoners who lost control of multiple Inverted Eidolons at once.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Invert Eidolon.md:28
why: Eight names and two events are unattested, and the page correctly flags them as colour a review may cut. One of them is not colour: the Wellspring Fracture of Nalisem is the event the page's Essence cost reading is derived FROM - the page says the upper end of the cost band is chosen because of it. So an unattested incident is currently doing load-bearing work in the ledger, and the same incident is the one SA-NUM-INVERT-MULTIPLE-CONSTRUCTS-UNPAYABLE shows cannot be paid for by anyone in the corpus. The 'Era of Calamity' also appears on the Vainglory page in this section, unattested there too.

options.option: Strike the Wellspring Fracture of Nalisem and re-derive the cost reading from the Discipline's table and the construct's complexity alone.
options.changes: Takes an unattested event out of the ledger; the upper-end cost reading then rests on the page's own argument rather than on a history.

options.option: Attest the incident as a named event in canon and let the cost reading stand on it.
options.changes: Creates canon history, which the issue does not authorise, and inherits the unpayability finding.

options.option: Keep all of it flagged as unattested colour and note that one item is load-bearing.
options.changes: Nothing on the page; a ledger reading continues to rest on an event that does not exist in canon.

options.option: Rule on the 'Era of Calamity' once for the whole section, since two pages name it.
options.changes: Settles a shared reference in one ruling rather than twice, and either creates an era or removes it from both pages.

quote_a: A Precept can found a standing law inside its declared sphere: a guild code, a spiritual compact, a geasa that binds a named party rather than the world at large. It can outlast its author, the way an inscription outlasts the mason, because Fixatio does not care who is still standing.
quote_b: EU · Essence Units — the raw reserve. Scales with Temperance Stage, governed primarily by Tempering Yield.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The page states no Temperance Stage, no Grade, no EU cost and no glyphs - the second entry in the Spellcraft section with no Stage floor anywhere in it, the other being Fallacy. Max Grade, Sub-Stat ceiling, Tier of Standing, efficiency, Developmental Tier and both of Fixatio's Path gates are all read from Stage, so one missing field empties the ledger and makes every gate untestable. That matters more here than for most entries because the working founds guild codes and dynastic law: a Precept is the instrument institutions are built on and there is currently no way to say who is able to file one.

options.option: State a Stage floor and let Grade, Tier, eta, the Developmental Tier and the Path gates follow from Parts Five, Seven and Nineteen.
options.changes: Fills the ledger and fixes who may found a standing law, which currently anyone may.

options.option: State a Stage floor that scales with the breadth of the clause - a sphere-wide Precept gated higher than a geasa on a named party.
options.changes: Ties the gate to consequence and makes the small binding accessible while the founding act is not; adds a rule the system does not currently have.

options.option: Rule that a Runecraft inscription is gated by the substrate and the drafting rather than by the inscriber's Stage, and say so.
options.changes: Explains how a guild clerk's seal outlives him and moves the gate from the person to the apparatus; reaches every Runecraft page in the corpus.

quote_a: Craft · Runecraft. Per the current Craft/durability split, Spellcraft holds only while attention holds and Runecraft is fixed and degrades like any inscription; a Precept that is meant to found a guild code or a dynasty's law cannot be an art that lapses when the caster looks away.
quote_b: Below Stage VII, Refraction, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: The page sits in wiki/Spellcraft/ and states in its own words, with a correct reason, that its Craft is Runecraft. The consequence is not cosmetic. Runecraft is beaten by damaging a substrate and Spellcraft by interrupting a chain, so the shelf decides which Counterplay route applies; and the durability rule decides whether the working survives the caster looking away, which is the page's entire argument for itself. The same shape was logged from Edictum (SA-CROSS-EDICTUM-SPELLCRAFT-DURABILITY) and The Iron Tree (SA-CROSS-IRONTREE-CRAFT-SHELF), so this is the third entry in one section whose stated Craft disagrees with its shelf.

options.option: Move the page to the Runecraft shelf and keep its Craft line as written.
options.changes: Puts the working where its own reasoning puts it and settles which counter applies; the Spellcraft section loses an entry.

options.option: Rule once, for the whole section, that the shelf records where a conversion landed and not the working's Craft, and say so at the top of the section.
options.changes: Answers this row and the two neighbouring ones together, and stops a reader inferring a Craft from a folder.

options.option: Keep the shelf and restate the working as Spellcraft, with a separate Runecraft form for the founding uses.
options.changes: Splits the working in two, which the durability rule arguably requires anyway, and would need both forms described.

quote_a: Category · Glyphica primary (the Authorization and Sealing glyph roles, spoken of in the Unified Taxonomy as the syntax by which the Continuum 'recognises and authorises transformation'), Votia secondary where the Precept functions as a binding compact between parties rather than a standing law.
quote_b: Workings whose operative currency is a declared and irrevocable price: an offering made before the effect, a restriction accepted permanently, a thing given up so that a law will answer more readily than the practitioner's Temperance should permit.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md:263
why: The page carries a Votia secondary tag. Votia's defining property in the taxonomy is a declared and irrevocable price paid before the effect - that IS the category, not a feature of it - and the page states no price at all, in any currency. Either the Votia tag is wrong or the page owes the declared price the tag promises. This is the same absence the fairness row records, arriving from the taxonomy rather than from the brief, which is why it is logged separately: the taxonomy makes the price mandatory rather than merely desirable.

options.option: State the declared price the Votia tag requires, for the compact form of the working.
options.changes: Closes both this row and SA-FAIR-PRECEPT-NO-COST for the soul-bound case, and makes a Precept-as-compact something both parties spend on.

options.option: Drop the Votia secondary and keep the working purely Glyphica.
options.changes: Removes the obligation and with it the account of a Precept as a compact between parties, which is the form Rescind is documented against.

options.option: Rule that Glyphica's Authorization role can itself be the declared price - the filing is the thing given up - and say so in the taxonomy.
options.changes: A taxonomy-level change that would let other Glyphica workings carry Votia tags without stating separate prices.

quote_a: This is why the older registers called the practice a kind of enshrining: the law is not enforced from outside afterward. It is load-bearing from the moment it is sealed.
quote_b: Failure · Irreversibility. The cure is not undone by wanting it undone, and a Fixatio binding placed in error is a permanent feature of whatever it was placed on.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Materia — Material Science.md:60
why: The working's standing cost is genuinely zero, and correctly so: a constraint does no work, which is why a Precept can outlive its author. That makes the sealing cost the only place a price can go, and the page states none - no EU, no Stage, no Sub-Stat toll, no material, no aftermath. A working that founds dynastic law, needs no upkeep and costs nothing to file fails the cost test completely. The cost that belongs here is already in the register: Fixatio's irreversibility means a clause written slightly too wide is a permanent feature of whatever it was written on, keeps costing nothing to be wrong, and will outlive everyone who could testify about what it was meant to catch.

options.option: Carry Fixatio's irreversibility onto the page as the working's stated cost, in its own words.
options.changes: Supplies a cost that hurts without inventing a number, and makes drafting - rather than power - the thing at risk, which is the right hook for this working.

options.option: State a sealing cost in EU that scales with the breadth of the clause.
options.changes: Prices the founding act and makes a sphere-wide Precept something only an institution can afford.

options.option: State the Votia price the page's own category tag requires (see SA-CROSS-PRECEPT-VOTIA-WITHOUT-A-PRICE).
options.changes: Closes two rows with one statement, and only for the compact form; the standing-law form still has no price.

options.option: Leave it and record that the working fails the cost test.
options.changes: Nothing; the section's only zero-upkeep working also remains its only free one.

quote_a: A Precept is not persuasion and it is not a threat. It is closer to a boundary condition. Other workings, other oaths, and in the right circumstance other people, do not defy a Precept so much as discover that the space it named will not hold the shape they were trying to give it.
quote_b: Knot and Lock. The only two Counter forms in the index, and they do not oppose a law, because laws cannot be opposed. They condition the conditioning. Knot entangles a path so it cannot be traced cleanly. Lock occupies a limit so no other limit can be set there. Every counter-working ever recorded is one of those two moves.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md
why: 'Lock occupies a limit so no other limit can be set there' is a standing prohibition described exactly, and it is the nearest form in the register to what a Precept does. But the Index files Lock as one of only two COUNTER forms, and a Precept is not a counter to anything - it is a first move, filed before there is anything to answer. Whether Lock is available as a standing form rather than only as a reply is not stated anywhere, and it decides which glyph this working is built on and whether a Precept is itself counterable by a second Lock.

options.option: Rule that Lock is available as a standing form and name it on the page as the Precept's glyph.
options.changes: Gives the working its glyph from the attested thirty rather than a proposal, and raises the question of what happens when two Locks are set at the same limit.

options.option: Rule that the Counter forms are replies only, and that a standing prohibition uses Boundary under Order.
options.changes: Keeps the Counter forms narrow and leaves this working on a proposed chain until the remaining 106 Index entries are mirrored.

options.option: State on the Index that Lock has both a standing and a counter use, with the difference in the Sealing role.
options.changes: An Index-level clarification that would reach every warding and prohibition working in the corpus.

quote_a: Lysandra Velkaris, said to have authored the Precept of Hierarchic Ascendance for Highspire's chain of command, has no current wiki entry.
quote_b: This is a plausible current-canon anchor for the card's claim, not an attested one-to-one match; no wiki entry states that Urion personally inscribed the Twelve Precepts of Fate.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Precept.md:33
why: The working has no attested practitioner. Its strongest anchor, Urion the Archon of Balance, is offered by the page as plausible rather than attested, and the page is explicit that no entry says Urion inscribed the Twelve Precepts of Fate; its named author of a specific Precept, Lysandra Velkaris, has no entry at all. Highspire itself IS attested, as the summit housing the Lawbell and the seat of the Highspire Choir, so a Precept of rank filed there is consistent without its author being real. The consequence for the ledger is that no Precept practitioner has a card, which - combined with the missing Stage - leaves every energetic row null for two independent reasons.

options.option: Rule that Urion's first act upon descending WAS the Twelve Precepts of Fate, and cite it on the page.
options.changes: Gives the working a founding instance and an attested author at no cost in new characters; the Twelve Precepts become canon law other pages can reach.

options.option: Card Lysandra Velkaris under Highspire and let her own the Precept of Hierarchic Ascendance.
options.changes: Creates a character, which the issue does not authorise, and gives Highspire's chain of command a documented legal basis.

options.option: Strike Velkaris and keep the Precept of Hierarchic Ascendance as an anonymous Highspire instrument.
options.changes: Removes unattested authorship while keeping the working's best example, which suits an instrument the page says outlives its author.

options.option: Keep both flagged as they stand.
options.changes: Nothing; the working keeps no attested practitioner and no card for the ledger to read.

quote_a: At its most developed it swaps a death for an echo, a memory for a physical object, or a soul for the housing of a mirrored construct, because 'position' under Transference's law is not limited to a point in physical space
quote_b: Two oscillators tuned to the same frequency and held near each other exchange energy without a conductor between them, and the coupling strength falls off sharply with separation.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Spatium — Spatial Geometry.md:26
why: The mechanism the page names requires DEGENERACY for complete exchange. Two coupled oscillators detuned by delta can transfer at most 4k^2/(4k^2 + delta^2) of the total: at a mismatch of 2k only half moves, at 10k only four percent. A like-for-like positional swap is degenerate and goes to completion; a memory traded for a physical object is maximally detuned, and the bound applies at every Stage, because no Temperance Stage closes a detuning. So the page's hierarchy is wrong in kind rather than in degree - it gates identity-trading one or two Stages above positional exchange as though it were a harder version of the same thing, when the mechanism it cites makes it a different regime that is bounded out rather than gated high. This is the page's largest physics finding and it bears on its most advertised uses.

options.option: Rule that identity trades are partial by law, and state the fraction as the rite's stated limit rather than as a failure.
options.changes: Makes the advanced uses honest and turns Spatial Disjunction from an accident into the expected residue of an ambitious trade; the soulguarding use becomes a partial occupation rather than a swap.

options.option: Supply a tuning step that makes unlike things degenerate - name the Wellspring or Sub-Stat that closes delta - and price it.
options.changes: Preserves the advanced uses and adds a stated, expensive preparation step that an opponent can attack; the Stage hierarchy then measures how much delta a practitioner can close.

options.option: Restrict the working to like-for-like exchange and move the identity trades to another discipline.
options.changes: Keeps the mechanism exact and removes the page's most developed uses, which are most of what makes it interesting.

options.option: Rule that Transmutatio's change of basis supplies the degeneracy, so the secondary harmonisation is what makes unlike trades possible.
options.changes: Makes the secondary load-bearing and gives the advanced uses a named requirement; would need a statement of what a basis change costs.

quote_a: Transposition can trade a caster's exposure for a decoy's, trade a memory into an object, or trade a caster's own body for the housing of a prepared construct, provided the coupling Transference requires can be established between source and target.
quote_b: The mechanism is Spatium's Transference read straight: two systems tuned alike exchange without a conductor between them, and the coupling falls off sharply with separation
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Transposition.md:20
why: The stated Effect is the exchange of unlike things - a memory for an object, a body for a construct's housing, a death for an echo. The stated Mechanism is that two systems TUNED ALIKE exchange. The mechanism as written does not produce the effect as written: a memory and an object are not tuned alike, and the page's own phrase 'read straight' forecloses the reading that would let them be. The page supplies the escape clause in the same sentence - 'provided the coupling Transference requires can be established between source and target' - without saying whether that coupling CAN be established between unlike things or what establishing it costs.

options.option: Rewrite the Effect from the Mechanism: the rite trades like for like, and everything else is a partial occupation rather than a trade.
options.changes: Makes the two lines agree and removes three of the page's four advertised uses; the remaining one is the strongest anyway.

options.option: Change the Mechanism to deliver the Effect by naming what supplies degeneracy between unlike things, and price it.
options.changes: Keeps all four uses and adds a preparation step; the same answer as one of the options on SA-PHYS-TRANSPOSITION-DETUNED-EXCHANGE, so the two rows close together.

options.option: State that the coupling between unlike things can be established but only through an Anchor Construct built for that pairing.
options.changes: Ties the advanced uses to a physical object an opponent can destroy, which is good counterplay and makes the anchor mandatory rather than advisable.

options.option: Record the mismatch and leave both lines.
options.changes: Nothing; a table cannot say whether a memory-for-object trade is a legal use of this rite.

quote_a: Stage floor / Grade · Stage VII, Refraction, A-Grade late push toward S, for a Transposition trading identity or fate-weight rather than mere position.
quote_b: Overchannel open, carrying inherent Overflow risk above D-Grade and Backlash risk above C, with no Path providing structural protection; recovery of rebound as usable output requires Body Path at Stage V to exceed B.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:122
why: The page states a Stage floor and an A-Grade requirement and names no Path requirement. Three gates are live at A-Grade: Transference's Stat Effect names Harmonics Projection (Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C for field weight, Stage VI to exceed A for reach) and Harmonics Synergy (Stage VI to exceed A for allied amplification) and Tempering Yield (Body Path at Stage III to exceed C). At the page's stated late push toward S, the Stage VI Attraction gates come in as well. Separately and more seriously, Transmutatio's Stat Effect runs through Ardency Overchannel, which Part Seven says carries Backlash risk above C-Grade with NO Path providing structural protection - so every A-Grade performance of this rite carries an unmitigable Backlash risk that the page's failure taxonomy (Spatial Disjunction, Wellspring Desynchronization) does not include.

options.option: Add the Path requirements and the Overchannel Backlash risk to the page's failure taxonomy.
options.changes: Gives the rite a third named failure mode that no Path commitment protects against, which is the cost the fairness check finds thin, and narrows who can perform it.

options.option: Rule that a Ritus reads its Path gates through the officiant's dominant Path only, and state which Path this rite needs.
options.changes: Collapses the multi-gate problem across this batch and would need stating in Part Seven.

options.option: Drop Transmutatio as a named harmonisation for the positional form, keeping it only for identity trades.
options.changes: Confines the unprotected Backlash risk to the advanced uses, which is where the page already puts the danger.

options.option: Record the gates and the risk without changing the page.
options.changes: Nothing; the rite keeps a stated Grade whose own Sub-Stat register carries an unmentioned unprotected risk.

quote_a: a lower-Stage attempt at pure body-swap positional exchange is plausible at Stage V, Splintering, B-Grade, since that is the first Stage at which a Crystal has enough Wellspring purchase to hold a second coordinate at all.
quote_b: Below Stage VII, Refraction, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary. At Refraction the practitioner can hold the Crystal as an object of study and the Glyph Roles compress into an internal chain that needs no material anchor at all.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: Two separate things called anchors are being conflated and the page's Stage V variant falls in the gap. The Anchor Construct the page requires is a COUPLING RELAY - it shortens each hop against a 1/d^6 falloff - and it is required by geometry, not by the Craft gate; at the stated Stage VII floor Law V requires no material anchor at all. But the page's lower-Stage variant sits at Stage V, below Refraction, where Law V DOES require voice, hand, ink or blood, and the page names no such anchor for it. So the low-Stage form of the rite is currently described as performable with no Law V anchor stated, while the high-Stage form is described as needing an object that Law V does not ask for.

options.option: State the Law V anchor for the Stage V variant explicitly, separately from the Anchor Construct.
options.changes: Makes the low-Stage form interruptible by the standard boundary route, which is the counter a player will reach for first.

options.option: Drop the Stage V variant and set one floor at Refraction.
options.changes: Simplifies the entry and removes the cheap body-swap, which is the rite's most usable form in a fight.

options.option: State on the page that the Anchor Construct is a coupling relay and not a Craft anchor, and that the two are attacked differently.
options.changes: Clears up which counter does what - breaking a relay restores the falloff, breaking a Craft anchor stops the sentence - and costs the page nothing.

quote_a: The card names Ci (claimed: mirror/duality), Th (claimed: threshold/crossing), and Ra (claimed: binding chain). Current attested readings give Ci as Order/Honor, Th as Foundation, and Ra as Transcendence, all in the Identity or Structure strata rather than a dedicated crossing register. The corrected readings are used above; the full sentence-order chain the rite would actually require is not attested and should be checked against the Master Glyph Index before this entry is treated as final.
quote_b: A glyph creates nothing and carries no power. … A glyph is a boundary condition imposed on that law.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms.md
why: Three glyphs are named with claimed readings the page itself corrects, and the corrected readings put none of them in a crossing register - so the rite's chain, as given, does not describe what the rite does. One of the three can be checked here: [Th] Foundation is among the thirty entries the repo mirror of the Index carries, and it reads Foundation, confirming the page's correction on that glyph. Ci and Ra are in the 106 unmirrored Notion sub-pages (SA-GAP-GLYPH-MIRROR), so the other two corrections rest on the page's own report. The page asks for the check itself and this account proposes no substitute chain, because the page has already named and corrected glyphs and a proposal would be a third reading.

options.option: Mirror the remaining 106 Index entries and check all three readings, then write the sentence-order chain.
options.changes: Answers this row and every other glyph row in the batch; blocks nothing meanwhile.

options.option: Build the chain from the thirty mirrored forms and record it as a filing decision.
options.changes: Gives the rite a usable chain now and risks being superseded when the Index is mirrored.

options.option: Strike the glyph line until the Index can be read, keeping the page's correction as a note.
options.changes: Removes an unverified chain from a page that says itself it should not be treated as final.

path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Transposition.md:33
why: Four practitioners, two places (Rovann and Ilcin'dor), one term (Echo Constructs as soul-lattice bodies preloaded with Transposition scripts) and the cited source are all unattested or superseded. None of it is load-bearing for the mechanism, which is why the page keeps it flagged. Two items are worth separating from the rest: the Great Spirit War IS attested, so the soulguarding claim attached to it stands as a plausible minor use of a known rite during a documented conflict; and Echo Constructs are the vessel the page's most ambitious use trades INTO, which makes an unattested term load-bearing for one stated capability.

options.option: Strike the four practitioners and the two places, keep the Great Spirit War claim, and rule on Echo Constructs separately.
options.changes: Removes unattested history while keeping the one claim anchored to attested canon, and isolates the term that a capability depends on.

options.option: Attest Echo Constructs as a named construct type so the soul-for-housing trade has something to trade into.
options.changes: Creates canon, which the issue does not authorise, and gives the rite's most ambitious use a real target.

quote_a: Stage floor / Grade · Stage VII, Refraction, A-Grade late push toward S
quote_b: AU/s = Flux Density × η.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: The page states two Stage floors, a Grade band, a glyph chain and a failure taxonomy, and no quantity: no EU, no duration, no range figure, no number of simultaneous couplings. The range limit in particular is the working's defining constraint and is stated only as 'falls off sharply' - the account can derive the shape (1/d^6 in transfer efficiency, so doubling the separation divides it by 64) but the system supplies no characteristic radius, so there is no distance at which a player can say the rite fails. For a working whose whole counterplay is standing further away, that is the one number the page most needs.

options.option: State a characteristic range for an unanchored Transposition and a per-relay extension for an anchored one.
options.changes: Turns 'stand further away' from a principle into a distance, which is what makes the counter usable at a table.

options.option: State an EU cost for the coupling and for the tuning correction separately.
options.changes: Fills the ledger and prices the difference between an easy trade and an ambitious one, which is where the physics puts the cost.

options.option: Rule that the range is set by the Dominion Radius Sub-Stat the practitioner already has, and say so.
options.changes: Derives the range from an existing figure rather than adding one, and makes a Dominion-heavy practitioner the natural Transposer.

quote_a: None of the four practitioners the card names … have a card or page anywhere in current canon
quote_b: η · efficiency — the ratio of Essence spent to Essence that arrives as intended effect.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: No Transposition practitioner anywhere in the corpus has a character card, so Flux Density, eta and AU/s are null by absence and the Starvation margin cannot be computed for anybody. Every efficiency figure in the account is read off the Tier of Standing table at the two stated Stage floors rather than off a sheet, and both of those figures now read eta 0.60-0.70: Stage VII under R44-4, and the Stage V variant under R44-7, the agent ruling of 2026-09-25 that reads R44-4's correction across the whole V-VII span of the single-cell row it edits (C-063, closed).

options.option: Attach the rite to an already-carded Spatium or Transference practitioner as its worked example.
options.changes: Fills the ledger with attested figures at no cost in new canon; changes whose discipline this is.

options.changes: Gives the working a practitioner and creates a character, which the issue does not authorise.

options.option: Leave the ledger null and record that the working has no carded practitioner and reads both of its eta figures off the Tier table.
options.changes: Nothing; both Stages' efficiency stays a table reading rather than a sheet figure.

quote_a: Primary Wellspring Mirithane, the Wellspring of Reflection, whose failure state is exactly this discipline's mechanism: what should be an honest reflection of internal state becomes a flattering or desperate one instead.
quote_b: Failure · The mirror does not discriminate. A practitioner in a state they would rather not broadcast broadcasts it perfectly.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Limina — Entropy, Void and Mind.md:40
why: The page says Vainglory IS Mirithane's failure state. Mirithane's documented Failure is the exact opposite: involuntary honesty, too much fidelity rather than too little - a practitioner broadcasting perfectly a state they would rather conceal. So Vainglory is not Mirithane lapsing, it is Mirithane being OVERRULED, which is a different and more expensive thing. The distinction is not academic: a lapse costs nothing extra, while overruling a convergent law means the working has to supply gain continuously, which is exactly why the page ends up with an 'unbudgeted drain' it cannot price and an instability that 'compounds rather than levels off'. Getting the attribution right is what makes the drain computable.

options.option: Restate the page: Vainglory overrules Mirithane rather than failing it, and the cost is the gain that overruling requires.
options.changes: Makes the unbudgeted drain a derivable quantity rather than a flourish, and explains why the construct diverges instead of merely drifting.

options.option: Keep the page's attribution and add Mirithane's real Failure as a separate hazard of the discipline.
options.changes: Gives the working a second failure mode - the construct broadcasting the summoner's actual state perfectly at the worst moment - which is a good scene and does not fix the cost problem.

options.option: Reassign the primary Wellspring to one whose documented failure IS flattering distortion, and record which.
options.changes: Removes the tension and loses the page's strongest mechanism, since Mirithane's convergence-on-honesty is what makes the instability compound.

options.option: Record the mismatch and leave the page.
options.changes: Nothing; the working keeps a cost its own page calls unbudgeted and the account cannot compute it.

quote_a: It can, given enough time active, develop enough independent coherence to attempt to displace the summoner it was drawn from, since its whole nature is competing with the summoner's honest self-image rather than extending it.
quote_b: Raziel Ados, said to have used the technique to impersonate himself across multiple Domains before being consumed by the result
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Vainglory.md:32
why: A feedback loop above unity has exactly two endings and the page asserts both without distinguishing them. If the pump keeps up with the growing intracavity energy the loop SATURATES: it settles into a steady state whose character is set by the cavity rather than by the original signal, which is a stable false self with real coherence - Yelara Vintress displaced and replaced. If the pump cannot keep up, the CAVITY takes the damage, and the cavity here is built on the summoner's own Shell and Core - Raziel Ados consumed by the result. Which ending arrives is set by whether the summoner's Core can sustain the exponential, and nothing on the page or in the Discipline says so. The two outcomes are the difference between a summoner who survives and loses their place and one who does not survive.

options.option: Rule that the ending is set by whether the summoner keeps paying: sustain it and it saturates into a rival, drop it and the backlash lands on the Crystal.
options.changes: Makes the ending a decision the summoner takes under pressure, which is the best version dramatically, and gives the discipline a real dilemma rather than a random outcome.

options.option: Rule that saturation is the only ending and that displacement is always the outcome.
options.changes: Removes the lethal version and makes the discipline reliably survivable but reliably ruinous; the page's own history would need one name struck.

options.option: Rule that the ending is set by Stage - a construct raised above the floor saturates, one produced by accident damages the cavity.
options.changes: Ties the outcome to the deliberate-versus-accidental split the page already relies on and makes the accident the dangerous one, which fits the page's history.

options.option: Record both endings and leave them unruled.
options.changes: Nothing; a table cannot say whether losing control of a Vainglory Eidolon kills the summoner.

quote_a: the conservative reading off The Spirit Summoning Arts' Animatria cost table is the lower end of the fabrication band, 75,000 EU, with the instability adding an unbudgeted drain rather than a higher headline cost
quote_b: Essence Cost · 75,000 – 150,000 EU per eidolon depending on complexity, with a sustained cost of 10,000 – 25,000 EU per second.
path_b: wiki/The Disciplines/The Spirit Summoning Arts.md:42
why: The page names an 'unbudgeted drain' and the phrase is exact: this is the only working in the section whose sustain is not a rate but a rate plus a growing term. Gain has to be pumped, and the pump must supply an intracavity energy that doubles on a schedule set by the excess gain - so the per-second cost climbs on the same exponential as the instability the page describes as compounding. The system supplies no excess gain, no round-trip time and therefore no doubling period, so the drain cannot be computed at all, and the working's duration bound - which the page says exists ('It cannot remain stable indefinitely') - cannot be computed either.

options.option: State a doubling period or a per-minute escalation factor for the sustain, so the drain and the duration bound both become computable.
options.changes: Turns 'unbudgeted' into a number and gives the working a clock a table can run; the clock is the whole of the exhaustion counter.

options.option: Rule that the drain is flat after all and that the instability costs coherence rather than Essence.
options.changes: Keeps the ledger simple and moves the price onto Tempering Coherence, which is where the Counterplay register already puts the consequence.

options.option: Rule that the escalation scales with how far the construct's projection departs from the summoner's actual state, and say what measures that.
options.changes: Prices the working by how big the lie is, which is the right shape, and needs a stated measure of the departure.

quote_a: Most who produce one do so by accident, during a failed ascension attempt, a Temperance collapse, or a Trait that overreached its own Stage.
quote_b: Below Stage VII, Refraction, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary.
path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Four Crafts.md
why: The page sets the floor at Stage VI, Glory, which is below Refraction, so Law V requires an external anchor - voice, hand, ink or blood - and the page names none. That matters because 'Take the anchor and the sentence does not complete' is the cheapest counter in the register and a reader will reach for it first. It matters twice over because the page's own account is that most Vainglory Eidola are produced BY ACCIDENT during a collapse or an overreaching Trait, and an accident has no deliberate anchor at all. Either the accidental form is not a Law V working, or Law V has an exception for workings nobody intended, and neither is stated.

options.option: State the anchor for the deliberate form and rule that the accidental form is a Structural fault rather than a working, so Law V does not reach it.
options.changes: Makes the deliberate form interruptible and the accident uninterruptible, which is honest and gives the two forms different counters.

options.option: State an anchor that both forms share - the summoner's own held self-image, treated as the external anchor.
options.changes: Keeps one working with one counter and stretches what Law V means by an external anchor, which would need stating in The Four Crafts.

options.option: Raise the floor to Refraction so no anchor is required, and lose the low-floor reasoning.
options.changes: Removes the page's best argument - that the floor should be one a practitioner can cross without meaning to - and makes accidental production impossible.

quote_a: Stage floor / Grade · Stage VI, Glory, A-Grade.
quote_b: Cascade requires Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B for spread, Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed S for range.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:122
why: The page states a Stage floor and an A-Grade requirement and names no Path requirement. Three are live at A-Grade across the three Wellsprings it names. Mirithane's Stat Effect names Harmonics Attunement, which Part Seven gates on Attraction Path at Stage II to exceed D. Eidolyn's names Ardency Density, gated on Body Path at Stage IV to exceed B, and Gnosis Retention, gated on Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed D. Oneirion's names Ardency Cascade, gated on Attraction Path at Stage IV to exceed B for spread. A-Grade exceeds both D and B, so Attraction Path IV, Body Path IV and Spirit Path II are all required simultaneously, and whether one practitioner may hold gates on three separate Paths is not stated anywhere - the same general question logged from Invert Eidolon at SA-CROSS-INVERT-THREE-PATH-GATES.

options.option: State which Path the working requires and drop the harmonisations whose gates cannot be met.
options.changes: Makes the working performable by a real practitioner; costs the page one of its three currents.

options.option: Rule in Part Seven whether a practitioner may hold gates on multiple Paths and at what cost.
options.changes: One system-wide answer that closes this row, the Invert Eidolon row and the Transposition row together, and reaches every multi-Wellspring working in the corpus.

options.option: Rule that a Path gate is read against the Sub-Stats a working actually expresses rather than against every Sub-Stat its Wellsprings strengthen.
options.changes: Collapses most multi-gate findings in this batch; changes how every account here reads gates and would need stating in Part Seven.

quote_a: None of the four figures the card names have a card or page anywhere in current canon: Serenhal Caelmorne, said to have projected a corrupted version of himself during a Moetana trial; Yelara Vintress of a 'Rose-Glass Order,' whose Vainglory Eidolon is said to have stolen her original Pneuma and taken her place; Raziel Ados, said to have used the technique to impersonate himself across multiple Domains before being consumed by the result; and the guild named as still teaching a controlled form of the rite, the Order of the Hollow Veil.
quote_b: The founding text the card cites, a Tome of Lurid Echoes, and the mass-casualty event it names, a Lament of the Nine Mirrors during an unattested Era of Calamity, are likewise unattested.
path_b: wiki/Spellcraft/Vainglory.md:32
why: Four figures, one guild, one founding text and one mass-casualty event are all unattested, and the page correctly flags them as colour a review may cut. Two items are not merely colour. Yelara Vintress and Raziel Ados are the page's ONLY evidence for which of the two possible endings the working has - displacement and consumption respectively - so the physics question at SA-PHYS-VAINGLORY-SATURATION-OR-DAMAGE currently rests entirely on two unattested people. And Serenhal Caelmorne appears on the Fallacy page in this same section as the practitioner of a second forbidden working, which makes him load-bearing across the section (SA-UNATT-FALLACY-SERENHAL); the 'Era of Calamity' likewise appears on Invert Eidolon.

options.option: Rule on the two endings directly (SA-PHYS-VAINGLORY-SATURATION-OR-DAMAGE) so the mechanism no longer depends on two unattested figures, then strike or keep them as colour.
options.changes: Separates the mechanism from the history; the figures become droppable without losing anything mechanical.

options.option: Card Yelara Vintress and Raziel Ados as the discipline's two documented outcomes.
options.changes: Creates two characters, which the issue does not authorise, and gives the working an attested pair of case histories.

options.option: Rule once on the 'Era of Calamity' and on Serenhal Caelmorne for the whole section, since two pages name each.
options.changes: Settles two shared references in two rulings rather than four, and either creates an era and a figure or removes them from both pages.

options.option: Keep all of it flagged as unattested colour.
options.changes: Nothing; the working's mechanism keeps resting on two people who do not exist in canon.

quote_b: AU/s = Flux Density × η.

This is worth logging on this page in particular because the page carries the one EU figure in the section that lands inside its Grade band under the ruled constant and eta (reports/eu_band_sweep_2026-09-25.md:61) - so the entry is unusually well-numbered on the cost side and has nobody to spend it.

options.changes: Fills the ledger with attested figures at no cost in new canon; changes whose discipline this is.

quote_a: This page has been retired. Its unique content was merged into the governing entry on 2026-09-15.
quote_b: The Veil is not a place. It is a condition — the state of being between planes, the moment of transition where the ordinary separation between matter, soul, and fate becomes navigable.
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:13
why: The issue's page list names wiki/Spellcraft/The Veil.md, which is now a redirect carrying no content: the definition, structure, access table and merged Practitioners section all live at wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md. This account is therefore written against the governing entry and says so at its head. Recorded rather than silently substituted because the section's page count and any later review pass both need to know that one of the twenty Spellcraft pages is a retired redirect, and because a reader following the issue's own list would find nothing.

options.option: Accept the account as written against the governing entry and note on the section index that the Spellcraft Veil page is retired.
options.changes: Keeps the count at twenty and points future readers at the live page; nothing mechanical moves.

options.option: Drop The Veil from the Spellcraft section's page list, making it nineteen.
options.changes: Removes a redirect from a list of workings; the Veil then has no system account in this batch unless one is filed under Cosmology.

options.option: File the account under Cosmology & Metaphysics instead of Spellcraft, matching the governing page's section.
options.changes: Puts the account where its source lives and breaks the one-account-per-listed-page correspondence this batch otherwise holds.

quote_a: The Veil is not a place. It is a condition — the state of being between planes, the moment of transition where the ordinary separation between matter, soul, and fate becomes navigable.
quote_b: The Transference Wellspring governs lawful passage through this medium. Every Veil Step (short liminal crossing through a thin boundary), every Essence Relay (transfer of energy, memory, or consciousness between vessels), every Echo Binding (temporary stabilization of a fragmented spirit), and every Soul Preservation (holding dying Essence in harmonic stasis) operates within the Veil's liminal space.
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:87
why: Every other entry in this section is a working with a caster, a cost and an effect. The Veil is a condition - a medium with properties - and the four sections of the account standard (physical, stratal, mechanism, ledger) assume a working. This account resolves it by accounting for the operations performed IN the medium (Bifold Perception, the four named Transference crossings, rupture containment) and for the medium's own measurable properties, and says so at its head. But that is a decision this account made, not one the system states, and it affects what the ledger means: the cost rows below price a crossing rather than the Veil, and the Veil itself has no cost because nothing casts it.

options.option: Confirm that a condition's account prices the operations performed in it, and state that convention in _method.md for any future condition or terrain entry.
options.changes: Makes the decision explicit and reusable; the Aether Shell, the Realms and the Domains would all get accounts on the same footing.

options.option: Rule that conditions get a different and shorter account - physical and stratal only, no mechanism or ledger.
options.changes: Keeps the working format clean and loses the gate ladder and the Drift accounting, which are the most useful things this page has.

options.option: Split the entry: one account for the Veil as medium, separate accounts for Bifold Perception and for Transference Crossing as workings.
options.changes: The most accurate shape and the largest amount of new work; each working then gets its own cost, tell and counterplay.

quote_a: Soul Drift is not immediate. It accumulates over repeated crossings. Each entry into the Veil loosens the practitioner's connection to Physical Plane sensation by a small increment. Each return requires the practitioner to re-establish connections that the Veil's liminal state had temporarily dissolved.
quote_b: The Veil Pilgrims, ethereal monks who never fully returned from repeated crossings, are the endpoint of this trajectory: entities patient enough to guide the lost but too thin to remember why they once wanted bodies.
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:125
why: The page states that Drift accumulates per crossing, in increments, without recovery, and names the endpoint of the accumulation. That is cycle-counted irreversible damage, so by the page's own description there is a number of crossings at which a practitioner becomes a Veil Pilgrim - and the system states no number, no increment size, no scale and no marker between the first crossing and the last. The consequence is that the section's most interesting cost cannot be spent: no scene can say whether this is the crossing that matters, no player can weigh going in against staying out, and the Drift counter that section 5 identifies as the working's best counterplay route cannot be run.

options.option: State a crossing count or a Drift scale with named thresholds, with severity per crossing set by depth and duration.
options.changes: Makes the cost spendable and the counter usable; turns every Veil crossing into a decision with a visible price.

options.option: Rule that Drift is tracked as a Ledger entry per practitioner rather than by a fixed count, with thresholds ruled case by case.
options.changes: Keeps the number out of the rules and puts it in the campaign record, which suits a cost that is meant to creep up on people.

options.option: Rule that severity scales with the gate used - a Veil Step costing less than carrying another person - and state the relative weights.
options.changes: Ties the increment to the page's existing seven-gate ladder rather than adding a new scale, and makes the Stage XII gate properly expensive.

options.option: Record the gap and leave Drift qualitative.
options.changes: Nothing; the working's only irreversible cost stays unspendable and its best counter stays unusable.

quote_a: Major cities, where overlapping ward-networks, alchemical residue, and competing Aether fields create dense metaphysical noise, tend toward Thick Veil despite (or because of) their high Essence traffic. The noise itself acts as insulation: so many competing signals that the Soul Plane's deeper frequencies are drowned out.
quote_b: Locations where the boundary between planes is reinforced. Heavy material density, artificial Essence suppression (ward-networks, Silence Realm effects, anti-Harmonia fields), or natural geological features that insulate against spiritual energy all produce Thick Veil conditions.
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:63
why: Two physically different mechanisms are filed under one heading and given one list of consequences. Barrier THICKNESS raises the cost of transmission exponentially and leaves detection alone; a raised NOISE FLOOR destroys detection and leaves transmission alone. So a practitioner in a granite vault should be able to read and not cross, and a practitioner in a noisy city should be able to cross and not read - and the page gives both the same four consequences (crossings cost more, Mnemata readings muddy, Harmonia degraded, entities invisible, dreams shallow). Three of those four are detection effects and one is a transmission effect, which means the noise case is being credited with a cost it should not carry and the geological case with a blindness it should not suffer.

options.option: Split the Thick Veil entry into Thick (barrier, transmission cost) and Loud (noise floor, detection cost), each with its own consequence list.
options.changes: Makes terrain genuinely tactical: a city becomes a place you can cross from and cannot read in, and a vault the reverse. Reaches every Transference and Mnemata page.

options.option: Rule that noise raises the effective boundary thickness as well, so the two collapse into one quantity.
options.changes: Keeps the page as written and requires a stated mechanism by which competing signals thicken a barrier rather than merely masking it.

options.option: Keep one heading and correct the consequence list so transmission and detection effects are attributed separately.
options.changes: The smallest change that fixes the error, and leaves the single Thin-to-Thick scale the page's diagram relies on intact.

quote_a: Soul Drift. The condition in which a practitioner's awareness becomes more anchored to the Veil's liminal medium than to their Physical Plane body.
quote_b: Failure · Reverse coupling. A gradient runs both directions, and a Transference practitioner beside a depleted ally will empty into them without deciding to.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Spatium — Spatial Geometry.md:26
why: The page describes Soul Drift in detail and never cites the Wellspring Failure that produces it. Transference's coupling is symmetric by its own register - a gradient runs both directions and the practitioner empties into the other side without deciding to - so every operation the page lists (Veil Step, Essence Relay, Echo Binding, Soul Preservation) opens a route INTO the practitioner at the same rate it opens one out. Soul Drift is reverse coupling measured over years instead of minutes. This closes the account rather than breaking it, and it is logged because it is load-bearing in two directions: it explains why Drift is irreversible (nothing runs the gradient backwards) and it means the Drift increment should scale with how depleted or how hungry the far side was, which nobody has said.

options.option: Cite Transference's Failure on the Veil page as the mechanism of Soul Drift, and scale the increment with the far side's gradient.
options.changes: Gives Drift a mechanism and a variable: stabilising a badly fragmented spirit costs more Drift than a routine crossing, which is both fairer and better drama.

options.option: Rule that Drift is a separate structural accumulation unrelated to reverse coupling, and say what causes it.
options.changes: Keeps the two apart and owes the page its own mechanism for an irreversible per-cycle loss.

options.option: Record the identification without changing either page.
options.changes: Makes the connection findable and leaves the increment unscaled, so a routine Veil Step and a desperate Soul Preservation cost the same.

quote_a: Transference's core law — "What must pass onward may remain itself through motion" — is a law of continuity rather than of ending. It teaches Essence how to survive transition.
quote_b: Mechanism · Two oscillators tuned to the same frequency and held near each other exchange energy without a conductor between them, and the coupling strength falls off sharply with separation. Transference makes the Attraction Layer such an oscillator.
path_b: wiki/The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings/Spatium — Spatial Geometry.md:26
why: The page attributes a core law to Transference in quotation marks. That sentence appears nowhere in The Eight Families & the Sixty Wellsprings, which is the register of core laws; the Transference entry there gives the coupled-oscillator Mechanism and no aphorism, and a grep of the mirror returns the sentence only on this page. It may be quoted from an older register the mirror does not carry - which would be consistent with this page's own note that older registers 'were sorted by feeling and do not map onto the eight Families' - or it may be an unattested formulation. The two statements are not contradictory in content, but one of them is being called Transference's core law and the other is what the register of core laws actually says.

options.option: Add the sentence to the Transference entry in the Sixty Wellsprings register as its stated law, beside the Mechanism.
options.changes: Makes the quotation attested and gives every Wellspring entry a precedent for carrying an aphorism alongside its physics.

options.option: Mark the sentence on the Veil page as an older-register formulation rather than the current core law.
options.changes: Preserves the line as in-world literature without making it the register's, which suits a page that already reads older registers as historical.

options.option: Strike the quotation and read Transference's law from the register.
options.changes: Loses a good sentence and removes an unattested quotation from the page that is otherwise the corpus's best defence of a Family assignment.

quote_a: Controlled Bifold Perception | Stage VII · Refraction | Loss of coherence across two perceptual grammars
quote_b: Projection requires Attraction Path at Stage III to exceed C for field weight and Stage VI to exceed A for reach.
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:134
why: The page carries seven Temperance Gates with a named principal risk each - more attested gating than any other entry in this section - and states no Grade at any of them. Because every Path gate in Part Seven is expressed as a Grade threshold ('to exceed C', 'to exceed A'), no Path requirement for any Veil operation can be tested, even though Transference's own Stat Effect names three gated Sub-Stats: Harmonics Projection, Harmonics Synergy and Tempering Yield. So the page passes the Stage check completely and cannot be run against the Grade bands at all, which is the one check an entry this well gated ought to pass.

options.option: Add a Grade to each row of the Access table, so the Path gates become testable.
options.changes: Completes the best gate ladder in the corpus and fixes which Paths a Veil practitioner must hold at each gate.

options.option: Rule that a Temperance Gate implies the Max Grade of its Stage per Part Five, so Grades need not be stated separately.
options.changes: Derives every Grade from the existing Stage column at no cost in new text, and reaches every page in the corpus that gates by Stage alone.

options.option: Record that the gates are Stage-only and that Path requirements for Veil work are unruled.
options.changes: Nothing; the page keeps seven gates that cannot be checked against the Sub-Stat register.

quote_a: Rikudoku Moto carries the most striking tradition attached to the Veil: that he manipulated deep Veil layers to fracture spiritual continuity across battlefields, and that his soul was rumored to drift between folds even after death. The name is genuinely attested in current canon, named a philosophical ally on two other characters' sheets, but the wiki mirror flags him as needing re-identification before anything about him hardens into fact.
quote_b: Eremund Vellsore, credited with developing the first known method of Veil-thread weaving through song, and the Bound Watchers, Veil-bound entities said to sit at the outer edge of the Astral Fold in judgment over oaths and Temperance rituals, have no matching record anywhere in the wiki mirror.
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:139
why: The Veil's practitioner record is one attested name flagged for re-identification and two unattested entries, so no Veil practitioner is available as a worked example and the ledger's Flux Density, AU/s and Starvation rows are null by absence. Rikudoku Moto is the interesting case rather than the others: he IS attested, named a philosophical ally on two sheets, and the tradition attached to him here - fracturing spiritual continuity across battlefields, a soul drifting between folds after death - is the corpus's clearest description of advanced Drift, which makes him the natural worked example for the page's own central cost and unusable until the re-identification is settled.

options.option: Settle the Rikudoku Moto re-identification, then card him as the Veil's worked example and advanced-Drift case.
options.changes: Gives the page's central cost an attested face and the ledger a sheet to read; the re-identification is a prerequisite and is not this issue's.

options.option: Attach the account to an already-carded Transference practitioner for the numbers and leave the traditions as they stand.
options.changes: Fills the ledger without touching the re-identification; the Veil's history and its numbers then belong to different people.

options.option: Strike Eremund Vellsore and the Bound Watchers and keep only the attested name.
options.changes: Removes unattested history; the page loses its account of who judges crossings, which it says reads thinner without them.

options.option: Keep all three flagged as they stand.
options.changes: Nothing; the working with the section's most interesting cost keeps nobody to spend it.

quote_a: What changes · Bifold Perception occurs spontaneously in practitioners of even moderate Temperance. Transference crossings require less Essence. Mnemata readings are sharper.
quote_b: What changes · Transference crossings require significantly more Essence. Mnemata readings are muddy.
path_b: wiki/Cosmology & Metaphysics/The Veil.md:65
why: The page states the cost of a crossing only comparatively - 'less Essence' in a Thin zone, 'significantly more' in a Thick one - with no EU figure at any gate, no baseline, no range and no duration. The physical account says the dependence is exponential in local boundary thickness rather than proportional, so the two adverbs are the ends of an exponential and the gap between them is not a modifier but a multiplier of unknown size. Since the whole economy of every Veil-working order in canon (maintained nodes, sacred groves, deliberately sited chambers, cities avoided) follows from that multiplier, it is the number the page most needs and the one it is furthest from having.

options.option: State a baseline EU cost for a Veil Step at Baseline thickness and a multiplier for Thin and Thick.
options.changes: Prices every operation on the page at once and makes terrain a calculable decision rather than a described tendency.

options.option: Rule that Veil crossing cost is derived from Aetheric Density at the site, which would first require Aetheric Density to have a numeric scale (SA-GAP-AETHERIC-DENSITY).
options.changes: Ties the page to a quantity the system already names and closes the batch's largest gap as a side effect; blocked until that scale exists.

options.option: State costs per gate rather than per zone, so the seven-gate ladder carries the prices.
options.changes: Uses the page's existing structure and makes carrying others properly expensive; leaves terrain qualitative.

quote_a: Governing Titan | Sylorin, the Ferryman of Etherea

path_b: wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md
why: No Veil practitioner has a character card, so Flux Density, AU/s and the Starvation margin are null and every efficiency figure in the account is read off the Tier of Standing table at the page's stated gates rather than off a sheet. That is a weaker position here than on most pages in this section, because this page's gates span Stages V to XII and therefore three Tiers of Standing with three different eta bands, none of which can be checked against a practitioner who actually works the Veil.

options.option: Card a Veil practitioner at one of the higher gates, so at least the Tier 6 or Tier 7 band has a sheet behind it.
options.changes: Gives the upper gates an attested efficiency; creates a character, which the issue does not authorise.

options.option: Attach the account to an already-carded Transference or Spatium practitioner.
options.changes: Fills the ledger at no cost in new canon and checks one Tier band rather than three.

options.option: Leave the ledger null and record that a seven-gate ladder spanning three Tiers has no carded practitioner at any of them.
options.changes: Nothing; the account's efficiency rows stay table readings across three bands.

quote_a: Level / Stage | 195 / 500 · Band II — Disciplined Foundation · Stage VII — Emanation · Tier of Standing 5, Expert
quote_b: Temperance Stage · X, Realization
path_b: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Muken Moto.md:30
why: Niran Yukari's card states 18,400 EU/g, eta 0.89 and 16,376 AU/s at Stage VII. Muken Moto's card states 18,600 EU/g, eta 0.84 and 15,624 AU/s at Stage X. Both satisfy R44-2 exactly (18,400 x 0.89 = 16,376; 18,600 x 0.84 = 15,624), so neither is under an open AU/s conflict and neither can be dismissed as an arithmetic slip. The practitioner three Stages lower therefore has 4.8 percent MORE output than the one three Stages higher. Their Flux Densities are within one percent of each other, so the whole difference is eta, and eta falls as Stage rises across this pair because Muken's 0.84 is above his Tier 6 band while Niran's 0.89 is above his Tier 5 band by more. This is not the same finding as SA-CROSS-AUS-LADDER, which says the system states no scaling rule: this says that any monotone Stage-to-AU/s rule is now arithmetically impossible to fit to the attested cards without editing one of them, which removes 'anchor the ladder on the figures and interpolate' from the options. Serenyra Vaelith is the extreme case in the same direction - 22 AU/s at Stage VIII against Niran's 16,376 at Stage VII - but her figure comes from a technique page rather than her card and her eta is itself derived under R20C-34, so the clean pair is the one quoted here.

options.option: Rule that AU/s is a per-practitioner sheet value with no Stage relation, and that Flux Density and eta are the only quantities Stage constrains.
options.changes: Closes this row and the second option of SA-CROSS-AUS-LADDER together, and makes AU/s a diagnostic rather than a rank; every page without a card keeps a null AU/s permanently.

options.option: State an AU/s progression by Stage and rule both cards' figures corrected to it.
options.changes: Gives the batch the ladder it most needs, and edits two cards that currently satisfy R44-2 exactly - the first corrections applied to internally consistent cards.

options.option: Rule that eta governs output per character (as R44-5 already does for the three Stage VI cards) and that non-monotone AU/s across Stages is therefore lawful and expected.
options.changes: No numbers move and no card is edited; it makes AU/s formally useless as a measure of who is stronger, which several technique pages currently lean on.

options.option: Rule that Flux Density rather than AU/s is the Stage-scaled quantity, and read AU/s as instantaneous throughput only.
options.changes: Preserves a Stage ladder on the quantity that is nearly equal across this pair (18,400 against 18,600, which is monotone-compatible) and reframes every output comparison in the corpus; needs a stated Flux Density band per Stage, which does not exist.

quote_a: Level / Stage | 195 / 500 · Band II — Disciplined Foundation · Stage VII — Emanation · Tier of Standing 5, Expert
quote_b: | VII | Refraction | A, allocation stops at 400; late push toward S entry | 475; 401–475 under strain only | 5 · Expert |
path_b: wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four–Ten).md:70
why: Niran Yukari's card states a Stage number and a Stage name belonging to two different Stages, which is exactly the defect logged for Gimbzo as SA-NUM-GIMBZO-STAGE-NAME. Part Five: VII is Refraction; Emanation is XII. The card's own cells split on which is meant. Its Tier of Standing cell reads '5, Expert', which Part Five assigns to Stage VII - so the number governs. Its eta of 0.89 sits in the Tier 7 Grandmaster band 0.85-0.90, which Part Five assigns to Stage XII - so the name governs. This is the third reading of SA-NUM-NIRAN-ETA-TIER, which currently treats the eta as simply out of band: if the name governs, the card is internally consistent on eta and inconsistent only on its Tier cell. Which is intended decides his Tier of Standing (5 or 7), his eta band (0.60-0.70 under R44-4, or 0.85-0.90), his Max Grade (A or SSS), his Sub-Stat ceiling (475 under strain, or 950) and his Developmental Tier (Resonant or Sovereign), and it bears directly on SA-CROSS-SEPTARCH-STAGE-VERSUS-CARD, which quotes this same card line for a different reason and does not notice the name. Reading the name as governing would close four of the five Stages between his card and Antinomy's Stage XI floor.

options.option: Read the number as governing: Stage VII, Refraction, Tier 5, and the name on the card is a slip.
options.changes: Smallest edit, and it keeps the card's detailed Stage VII architecture and its Tier cell; it leaves eta 0.89 far out of band at SA-NUM-NIRAN-ETA-TIER and leaves the four-Stage gap to Antinomy's floor at its full width.

options.option: Read the name as governing: Stage XII, Emanation, Tier 7, and the Tier cell is the slip.
options.changes: Makes the card's eta lawful without any numeric edit and brings him within one Stage of Antinomy's XI floor, which nearly closes SA-CROSS-SEPTARCH-STAGE-VERSUS-CARD; but it contradicts the card's Level 195 in Band II and its Stage VII Confluence and partial Domain seed, and Part Five's Stage XII requires passage through Dissonance.

options.option: Rule the two Yukari-and-Gimbzo cases together as one class of card defect, stating which of number and name governs for all such cards.
options.changes: Closes this row and SA-NUM-GIMBZO-STAGE-NAME with one ruling and sets the reading for any future card that splits; it decides Gimbzo's Tier, ceiling and Developmental Tier as a side effect, which that row treats as the substance of the question.

options.option: Rule that the card is a snapshot of a practitioner mid-transition and that both words are recorded deliberately, naming the reached Stage and the emerging one.
options.changes: Keeps the card as written and gives the corpus a stated form for a practitioner in transit, which would also serve Kurotana's rebuilt-vessel account; it creates a precedent that Stage number and Stage name can disagree lawfully, which the Part Five table currently forbids.
